a16_0000015.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0000015.text: : Roger roll. You have good thrust in all five.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0000015.text: It sure ain't what I expected.

a16_0000015.speaker: Duke
a16_0000015.text: Me, neither. It's like a freight train.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0000015.text: That's what everyone said. Quiet as [garble].

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: [Apollo] 16 now maneuvering to its proper flight path attitude.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: 36 seconds. Roll program completed, pitch profile still in progress. 40 seconds.

a16_0000015.speaker: Duke
a16_0000015.text: Man, look at this thing go! What are the g's, John?

a16_0000015.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0000015.text: Through 10K [10,000 feet altitude, 3,000 metres]. Must be coming up on a little Q here.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Mark. 50 seconds. Cabin pressure relieving, adjusting now from sea level to a space environment; two nautical miles in altitude.

a16_0000015.speaker: Duke
a16_0000015.text: Tower [sic] system's relieving - Tower's rel - cabin's relieving...

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: That callout from CapCom Gordon Fullerton says Apollo 16 now capable of water landing. Mark. One minute, 12 seconds. Coming up on period of maximum aerodynamic pressure on the vehicle.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: One minute 22, seconds; 6 nautical miles in altitude [11 kilometres]. Looking good.

a16_0000015.speaker: Young
a16_0000015.text: Coming up on max Q, Charlie.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Mark. One minute, 30 seconds; 8 nautical miles [14.8 kilometres] in altitude.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Mark. One minute, 41 seconds. Passed through max Q, still looking good.

a16_0000015.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0000015.text: Okay; you're through max Q, and everything looks good. [Pause.]

a16_0000015.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0000015.text: It does indeed. I believe this baby's gonna go up.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: 16 now 12.5 nautical miles [23.1 kilometres] in altitude. Young, Duke, Mattingly moving out to the outer traces of the Earth's atmosphere.

a16_0000015.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0000015.text: Stand by for Mode I Charlie.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Mark. Two minutes, 3 seconds. The status check in Mission Control by Flight Director Gene Kranz. The Go/No-Go for staging. Coming up on center engine shutdown.

a16_0000015.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0000015.text: Roger; inboard. You're Go for staging. [Long pause.]

a16_0000015.speaker: Young
a16_0000015.text: Right now, that [garble] only [garble] for staging. Watch it.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Two minutes, 28 seconds; 26 nautical miles [48 kilometres] in altitude, 32 nautical miles [59 kilometres] downrange.

a16_0000015.speaker: Young
a16_0000015.text: Okay, I'll count you down to it. 30, 31, [garble] 32. Those are good numbers, Ken?

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Two minutes, 35 seconds - 2 minutes, 40 seconds. Coming up on staging.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Two minutes, 53 seconds; a normal staging. Young, Duke, Mattingly now riding on five good second-stage engines.

a16_0000015.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0000015.text: Thrust is Go on all five on the S-II. [Long pause.]

a16_0000015.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0000015.text: Three minutes, 2 seconds. The giant first stage falling away now, its day's work completed. Apollo 16 now 46 nautical miles [85 kilometres] in altitude, 80 nautical miles [148 kilometres] downrange. Coming up on skirt sep and tower jettison.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0000015.text: Want me to go on time, John?

a16_0000015.speaker: Young
a16_0000015.text: Second plane Sep light's out. We'll go on time.

a16_0000015.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0000015.text: All right. I got the register...

a16_0000015.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0000015.text: Roger. And we confirm your skirt Sep. You're Mode II now.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Three minutes, 28 seconds. The Launch Escape Tower is ejected on time. Its surveillance [sic] role no longer required.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Oh, Charlie, look at that horizon. Can you see...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay. Okay, what - how's the steering?

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: Roger. Steering has converged. The CMC is Go.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Three minutes, 45 seconds. Apollo 16 now 62 nautical miles [115 kilometers] in altitude, 135 nautical miles [250 kilometers] downrange. Apollo 16 now 33 feet [10 metres] shorter and 9,000 pounds [4,000 kg] lighter. Unencumbered now for its mission in space.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Four minutes. We should be sitting at 21 degrees. [A flight angle of 21 degrees to the launch pad's horizontal.]

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: I'm going to look out a little bit.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, we're only pulling three-quarters of a g.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. Four minutes. Everything looks great down here.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Roger. It looks good up here, too.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Hey, Gordy, you ought to see that horizon. Just gorgeous.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Four minutes, 10 seconds. 70 nautical miles [129 kilometres] in altitude, 170 nautical miles [315 kilometres] down-range. Velocity now reading 10,600 feet per second [3,230 metres per second].

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Look at that stuff out your left window. What the heck is that?

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: That's just stuff from the tower.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Four minutes, 30 seconds. In Mission Control, trajectory data [is] driving right down the middle of our plot boards as expected. Right now, flight path data is Go.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: 04:30. Just a little low on the - the altitude. Velocity's looking good.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay. Let's see - you got - How about let's clean up the rest of the things we didn't do, like attitude, the rate command.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Four minutes, 45 seconds. 76 nautical miles [140 kilometers] in altitude, 220 nautical miles [407 kilometers] downrange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: P c . Turn on our gimbal motors here at 6 minutes, Charlie.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay. I'm ready; about a minute to go.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Well, you even remembered the - you remembered to do the water, Charlie.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Yeah, I got the water and everything going.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: We ought to give you an award for that.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Man, I was watching those gauges at S-IC and they were really jumping. That steam pressure the secondary read out. Man, was that a ride!

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Five minutes, 10 seconds. Still good performance on all five of the second stage engines. Second stage shutdown predicted at 9 minutes, 19 seconds.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: It was that staging that's thrilling, ain't it?

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: You ain't kidding! I was real glad someone warned us.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo]16, Houston. Times are nominal, level sense will be 8 plus 37, and cut-off at 9 plus 19.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. 5 minutes, 40 seconds. Another status check in Mission Control by Flight Director Gene Kranz. His console is coming up all greens. Looking good at this time.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: You'll get a little buzz now.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: Stand by for S-IVB to COI capability.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Coming up on 6 minutes. With th - CapCom Gordon Fullerton reporting that [Apollo] 16 [is] capable of reaching a minimum orbit with a good third stage and Service Module engines. We're at 6 minutes, 8 seconds. Apollo 16 [now] 88 nautical miles [163 kilometres] in altitude, 380 nautical miles [704 kilometers] downrange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, stand by. Go ahead on the Ones.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Yaw 1. Did you get it?

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: No, I couldn't see it. Okay. Go ahead.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay. You can't see that on the fuel cells, Ken.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: It's all on the batteries here.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Six minutes, 30 seconds. Velocity now reading 14,880 feet per second [4,535 metres per second]. Altitude, 90 nautical miles [166 kilometres] for Apollo 16. Downrange distance of 440 nautical miles [814 kilometres].

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Yeah. I saw that. That's really strange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Got a minute to go to inboard shutoff.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Man, it looks like a champ. [Garble] get Omni Delta.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: Stand by for S-IVB to orbit.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Young, Duke, Mattingly now told that they can reach orbit if given a good third stage. Mark. Seven minutes. Ninety-one nautical miles [168 kilometres] in altitude, 496 nautical miles [918 kilometres] downrange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. Seven minutes, 15 seconds. [Apollo] 16 flying almost parallel over the ocean now with the Young crew in a pitched down position. Really moving out now for downrange distance. We show Apollo 16, 551 nautical miles [946 kilometres] downrange. Velocity now reading 17,527 feet per second [5,342 metres per second].

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Coming up on center engine shutdown.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Center engine shutdown on time. Seven minutes, 50 seconds. Ninety-two nautical miles [170 kilometres] in altitude. 620 nautical miles [1,148 kilometres] downrange. Still showing stable thrust on the other 4 engines. They've got about a minute to go in burn time remaining.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. We saw the PU shift. Thrust looks good, and you're Go for staging.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Eight minutes, 35 seconds. Apollo 16 now 93 nautical miles [172 kilometres] in altitude, 756 nautical miles [1,400 kilometres] downrange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: You have level sense arm now.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: That terse response from Apollo 16 Commander John Young. We're at 8 minutes, 52 seconds. Apollo 16 now 807 nautical miles [1,494 kilometres] downrange, 92 nautical miles [170 kilometres] in altitude. Velocity now reading 21,642 feet per second [6,596 metres per second].

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: Stand by for Mode IV capability.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. You have Mode IV now.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: And your thrust looks good on the S-IVB.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: The Young crew has used up two-thirds of their Saturn stages on the way to orbit. We see good performance on the third stage, the S-IVB. That Mode IV report says Apollo 16 can achieve orbit on spacecraft power only. 9 minutes, 50 seconds. Apollo 16 [is] 93 nautical miles [172 kilometres] in altitude 1,011 nautical miles [1,872 kilometres] downrange. Velocity now reading 23,654 feet per second [7,210 metres per second].

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. 10 minutes, 18 seconds. A status check in Mission Control for orbit.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Everything's in great shape up here, you guys.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, we're gonna back this guy up, and we've got...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. You're Go for orbit. Predicted cut-off, 11 plus 49.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, now, you're gonna shut this guy down with the hand controller if it overspeeds?

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Yep. But we're going to see 20...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. 10 minutes, 40 seconds. The predicted time of shutdown, 11 minutes, 49 seconds. Apollo 16 now 93 nautical miles 172 kilometres] in altitude, 1,192 nautical miles [2,207 kilometres] downrange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: That's right. We want - Let's see. 25.6 is normal, so we go to 25.7 to back it up.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. 11 minutes. Showing a buildup in velocity, now reading 24,621 feet per second [7,504 metres per second] and accelerating.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Eleven minutes. Look at that. Minus 60, and it says it's gonna be 69. It's got a little buzz of its own.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. 11 minutes, 10 seconds. Velocity now reading 24,887 feet per second [7,585 metres per second], 98 per cent of the desired speed for insertion into orbit. Less than 20 seconds now from time of shutdown.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Nm-Bmm. Here's another one. A little rumble.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: ...11:20. Okay, 25.1, 25.2, 25.3. Look at it pitch back up and kill that altitude. 25.4...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Should have about l0 seconds - to shutdown.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark. 11 minutes, 40 seconds. Apollo 16 now 1,400 nautical miles [2,592 kilometres] downrange.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: I'm turning off the pyro arms, you guys.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay. Gimbal Motors. Let's go, Gimbal Motors.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: That was shutdown, right on the money.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. The range safety system is safe. The orbit is Go.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Roger. Boy, it's just beautiful up here, looking out the window. It's just really fantastic. And the thing worked like a gem.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: Sure did. We copy Noun 62, and your orbit by radar is 95 by 90 [nautical miles, 176 by 167 km]. [Long pause.]

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0002758.text: Mark, 12 minutes, 54 seconds. That enthusiastic report from orbit was from spacecraft Commander John Young. Apollo 16 in what appears to be a safe orbit. Preliminary numbers show 95 nautical miles by 90 nautical miles. The Saturn V, once again, an apparent victor in its tug-of-war struggle with the Earth's forces of gravity. We're at 13 minutes, 20 seconds Ground Elapsed Time and Apollo 16 is in orbit.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. The booster looks good. It's reconfigured for orbit. [Long pause.]

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0002758.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. The Z-torquing angle will be plus 0.06. Over.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: ...[garble] breaker and install the COAS. Okay, we just...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: That's okay. I just pushed the breaker in.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, Gordy; we're on page 2-11 [of the Launch Checklist] down through - We're getting to installing the COAS. That MA (Master Alarm) was the Transducer, ECS.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Oh, look how easy it is! Okay, Service Module...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Yeah, I did that, but I'm sorry (laughter). Okay, Waste H 2 O/Dump; Fuel Cell's going Normal; Purge Line Heater's on.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Let's see, [garble] got the torquing angles. You got...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: And I made it up with a clean window.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Yeah. Okay, going to Command Module...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Listen to that tone. Barely audible.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Young
a16_t-0002758.text: Shoot. I don't have any trouble hearing it. Hatch Gear Box is Latch; Actuator Handle is going to neutral [garble]...

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: I'm gonna leave the nitrogen in the - in the hatch. We're gonna pump that when we get back. I talked to the guys about that.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Mattingly
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, and I've got a note in the Flight Plan that says we're to vent it later on.

a16_t-0002758.speaker: Duke
a16_t-0002758.text: Okay, we just had loss of comm.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Apollo 16, Houston. [Long pause.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: Okay. Ohhh.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Ohhh. Is that ever nice! Look at that [garble]...

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Look at that view out there, you guys!

a16_0001618.speaker: Someone
a16_0001618.text: (Laughter)

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Oh, is that ever pretty.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Hey, it's b - blacker than pitch out this window five.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Supposed to be, Charlie. That's the rule of it.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: [Garble.] Yeah.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: Okay, I got your Verb 83 up there. I don't know what you're gonna do with it. I [garble] just buy it for you.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: That really is nice, that Verb 83 (laughter).

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Okay, I'm gonna start in on the...

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: If you'll get me a camera, I'll take a nice picture.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: I'll go get those in just a minute, babe.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Okay.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: It looks like those clouds are right on top - right down there. You could reach out and touch them.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: They are. We're coming up over the Africa, Charlie, and...

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Where's Africa? I don't see it.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: Okay, I've got eight grays. That all looks like a champ. Okay, cabin pressure's good.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Well...

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Is it - maybe I can just look...

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: This is just - these little old - It's clouds like this or like it...

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Apollo 16 through Canaries. How do you read?

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Okay, you're 5 by, Gordy.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Okay; we're noticing a possible blockage in the primary coolant loop. Would you have John check the Glycol Reservoir Bypass valve to be sure it's Open?

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Roger. [Garble].

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Hey, Gordy, do you want us to go ahead and - and - put the radiators on?

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Charlie, this is Houston. Whatever you just did up there got the coolant loop flow back. We'd like to watch it for a minute before proceeding. Over.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Okay, we're at step 12, page 2-13, configuration now with radiators at bypass. We've got the - the Reservoir Bypass Open, and the Outlet and the Inlet [valves] Closed.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Okay, let me tell you what it was, Gordon, I think, is the - the Outlet [valve] was - was accidentally Open, probably at - at some other time, and the - the Bypass [valve] was Closed and the Inlet [valve] was - was Open. That's probably been the indications you were seeing.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Roger. Understand. [Pause.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: We're coming up over Africa now, Gordon, and it really is a spectacular view.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Roger. I wish I was there with you.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: I guess we're - we're just over the Canaries looking down at those little islands, and that sure is something. [Long pause.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0001618.text: Apollo Control Houston. 20 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. That again that was John Young, commander of Apollo 16, appraising the view over this Canary Island pass. We're at 21 minutes Ground...

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: 16, Houston. You can proceed with the rest of the normal ECS configuration.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Roger. That's in work. [Long pause.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: 16, Houston. We're having a - kind of intermittent data down here due to a problem with Canaries antenna. [Long pause.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Okay, we're gonna put the glycol to the res - to the radiators now.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Roger.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0001618.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. 22 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We show a present orbit of 96 nautical miles by 91 nautical miles [154 by 146 kilometres].

a16_0001618.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0001618.text: About a minute to go until Loss Of Signal with Canary.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Okay, I'm going to unhook and stow - unstow the helmet bags.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Hang on a second. Let me get that circuit breaker for you.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0001618.text: A quick status check being taken at Mission Control Center by Flight Director Gene Kranz with his flight control team to try and pass up a final few words with the 16 crew before we have Loss Of Signal. We're at 23 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: [Apollo] 16, Houston. Data is back now good, and everything looks fine as we come up 20 seconds to LOS (Loss Of Signal). We'll see you at Carnarvon at 52:39.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Roger; 52:39, Gordon.

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Enjoy the view there.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: All right. We're just starting to come into darkness now, and the sunset is...

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Look - look at that. Look out there...

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: ...just as beautiful as always in this space business.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: [Laughter.]

a16_0001618.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0001618.text: Roger.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Oh, would you look at all that. We could use some helmet stowage bags.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Well, I'm getting them now.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: I'll get them. I'll get you the Tool E down if you kind of watch your feet for a second.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: I don't even know - I know - What am I kicking?

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: Well, in just a minute, it'll be me.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Okay.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Yeah. I don't know where I'm moving it to. [Laughter.] I must - Somehow it's ... Holy smokes, it's as bad as I thought it would be.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: No, they're over here, Charlie.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: No, they're over here. The helmet stowage bags?

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: Yeah.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: You're dreaming.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: No. They're in U-1.

a16_0001618.speaker: Young
a16_0001618.text: Yeah, but here's the...

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: You got - you've got both TSBs [Temporary Stowage Bags] and helmet stowage bags to get out, guys.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Yeah.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: That's all I need.

a16_0001618.speaker: Duke
a16_0001618.text: Okay.

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: John, could you move this foot?

a16_0001618.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0001618.text: If you put your feet down, I'll get it out of your way somehow. Hang on a second - let me get this flashlight here and see what the heck that is. [Laughter].

a16_0001618.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0001618.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We've had Loss Of Signal over Canary with the Apollo 16 spacecraft. They will be reacquired at 52 minutes, 39 seconds Ground Elapsed Time. We'll pass along at this time, peat - peak heart rates during the launch phase of flight. Peak heart rate for Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly, during the powered flight phase of flight, read 115. For spacecraft commander John Young, 108; and for Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke, 130. At 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: In here somewhere is a Tool E.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Yeah. Is all the rest of that stuff coming out? We don't [garble] it.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: I'd have sworn he was gonna unpack the whole spacecraft. [Laughter]

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Okay, I'm going to lower my seat.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Hey, listen, you gonna have to just take it easy; we ain't really in no hurry.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, I don't - I think this is absolutely the greatest, but if you [garble] you torque your platform.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: I'm gonna keep my plat - platform way over standard.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Okay. The [oxygen] flow is less than 0.2 [pounds per hour] or something like that?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Okay, and how's the cabin pressure?

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Cabin pressure's holding at 5 - about 5½ (psi, 34-38 kPa). Okay, let me get that. We have the Canaries LOS . Let me do what I'm supposed to do here at Canaries. Getting ready to flow.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Okay, the emergency regs I'm going to put on. They is on Both.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: John, can you get the Suit Circuit Return Valve Open?

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, I can if I can get back to it.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Suit Circuit Return Valve is coming Open. Nyuh-nuh-nuh-nuh.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Felt like it took a little Delta-P.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Here we fly in comfort though. My - is my hand controller [garble] ...

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, [garble] the RCS Command is Off, too.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Let me do that one more time. The aft is fine, that's for sure.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, there's some - there's some Delta-V in here.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: You want your old hat back?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: That's all right. Have you got the Suit Circuit Return Valve Open?

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, the Suit Circuit Return Valve is Open.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Okay, and don't want to forget our Window shadem Number 5 there.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Oh, yeah. Am I supposed to put that in right now?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: ...I'm gonna turn the flows off if you want to come out of the helmets and gloves.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Okay, could you put my seat [garble].

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Have you done the main reg [regulators] check?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Let me see. No, we do the main regs afterwards, don't we?

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Oh, okay. Oh, I don't know...

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Okay. What could make my feet want to climb up to the...

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: You want me to get it for you, Charlie?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Okay. You want this thing down, John, or like this?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: I do the main regs next, Charlie. We can go ahead and take helmets and gloves off.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Okay, if you'll tell me when you want to - when you want your flow off, I'll turn it off for you.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Okay. And the Window 5 cover's the one in the bag?

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: You just st - stuff the bag back in there?

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Huh? Stuff what bag back in there?

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: I didn't know they had a bag with it.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Yeah. It's so it won't get scratched [garble].

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: [Laughter] Hey, if you pull your helmet off, it's gonna go.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Did you shut your air off?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, but there's still just as much Delta-P in [garble] [laughter] it [garble] my nose, I couldn't even see it.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Well, pull your glove off first.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Can you - can you shut my flow off [garble], Ken?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Yes, sir. Here comes your flow off, now.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Man, that do make a difference. Okay, turn it back on, Ken.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: I don't know what I'm kicking down there.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: I can't believe it but I got her.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Now - Well - well, be careful you don't hit the thrust switch, Charlie.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, I know it. I'm trying to avoid that, John.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: I keep forgetting you have to hold things.

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: Well, for some reason, I want to float right up against the instrument panel. Maybe my - maybe it's my helium in my suit.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: You want your old dinner bag there, Ken?

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Isn't that neat, the way stuff just floats around?

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: That's got to be the world's greatest thing.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: I hate to tell you this, you guys. John's got to go potty.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: Oh, you're kidding me - I hope.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: I guess I'd better get on with that P52.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Yeah, I guess - Have you jettisoned the covers, Ken?

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: No. I - I was trying to move too slow, I think.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: I'm gonna do that next, and then I'll get this stuff. I'll do it.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: It's 29 minutes, so we got plenty of time.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: What - what all is in the checklist to do between now and tonight? Anything?

a16_0002400.speaker: Duke
a16_0002400.text: No. No, wait a minute. Let me get this thing. There you go [garble] it back, naturally.

a16_0002400.speaker: Young
a16_0002400.text: Oh, come on. My goodness sakes.

a16_0002400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0002400.text: I figured I was gonna - I stuck Tool E in here where I've been keeping it. And it floats out. I thought I'd just started off the mission by losing Tool E.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, well. There's still [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mission Control
a16_pao_agnew.text: This is Apollo Saturn Launch Control in the Launch Control Center at Kennedy Space Center. The successful launch of Apollo 16 took place at 12:54.00569 seconds, that is, 569 milliseconds past 12:54. Following the successful launch, the Vice President of the United States came into the firing room and had the following to say to the launch team.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mission Control
a16_pao_agnew.text: That was the Vice President of the United States speaking to the launch team in the Firing Room - Firing Room 1 at the Kennedy Space Center. Now Dr. Debus has a few words.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mission Control
a16_pao_agnew.text: That was Dr. Kurt H. Debus, Director of the John F. Kennedy Space Center.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, here's yours, Charlie.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I - I think it's looking for TSBs out of yours, Charlie, and...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, wait a minute, John.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, just leave it.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: It won't go nowhere.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: I know it.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: That's nice.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, Ken. You can cut my flow off.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: All right; stand by. Hey, John, if you want to put your hoses on, I'll cut this baby off again for you.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: No, that's all right. I'll leave them where they're at.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, cut it back on, Ken. I've got a glove popped [?] yet.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: : All right, sir; you're on.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay. I'm sorry, but the evil winds are blowing again, you guys. [Laughter.]

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: [Garble.]

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Ain't nothing you can do that's evil right now, babe.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: You just got to [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: You know something, I never did like this, and I like it even less in zero gravity. I don't know why anybody ain't squawking.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: What's that?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, I got a - a caution and warning on the PGNS . I don't know what that was. Must have been taking it out of the - [Optics] Mode is Manual. Optics Coupling is Direct, Speed [is], Hi[gh]. Now if [garble] up there. The [Optics] Zero's Off. Go Max speed to the right. The first one [ie cover] that comes off is the sextant at 40 degrees [shaft angle].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: I don't believe those [garble].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Ha-ha.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Ha-ha-ha-ha.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: What's that, John?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Looky here. Well, why don't you get your - well -

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, darn it. I didn't hear anything come off of the telescope.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Did you see out of it?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: No.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, keep going.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I was going all the way to the Sun. Shoot. Oh, well...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Maybe you can run it back again.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Maybe you ought to go the other way.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, I don't know. If I could ...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Are you seeing anything out of the telescope?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: No, sir.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, but that's going to take awhile. You want to turn down the lights, Ken?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah. I got my lights down here. I'm going to go ahead and do a P52.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, but - okay, but...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: You think there is anything wrong with turning the other way if they didn't - if the cover didn't come off?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, I think you ought to wait and ask them.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I hate to mess up 52. Let's see - let me - let me get myself good and light adapted.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, that's the problem.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: You want me to turn the lights down?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: You want to turn down some of the lights?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I got my eye closed and...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: I forgot, the flood's turned all the way up in here. Stars are out there, Ken, I can see them.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, I don't see a thing. I heard the sextant go.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Can't you go back to Zero and try it again?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I'm going to. I'm going to Zero and [garble].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: We're 90 by 95, you guys.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: That's neat.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, you don't see anything wrong with trying to - to do a - Oh, hey, I think I do see some stars now.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: There you go.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, thank God. [Laughter.]

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: It takes awhile.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, boy, you do have to be light adapted, I tell you.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, yeah.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Where? I don't see them. Oh, yeah. There's some, I think...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Hey, I can - They're off because I saw our thruster fire.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: I did, too [laughter]. Hey, that's a thunderstorm down there.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Was it?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah. Must be that.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, those are down [garble].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I'm looking in the other direction though.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, I'm looking on the ground...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...and that's - that's a thunderstorm.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, I'm going to do a [P] 52 if that's all right.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: [Garble] have to do a 52. That's a [garble].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: : Okay. I'm gonna ...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: I haven't got ORDEAL set up, but I got it laying here.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Can I get rid of your thing for a minute?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Sure.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, there's your flow. The Optics Zero is Off...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: What's the - what's the - what should we be doing?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...[Optics Speed Controller] Speed should be Lo[w]; [Optics Zero?] Off.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: I'm gonna turn the page here, and...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I tell you one thing you can do is - I'm going to stay in the dark here, so I can see.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Would you copy these numbers for me?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, I'll get them for you. John, we're up to speed, as far as I know.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I haven't started unstowing stuff.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, at 35 minutes.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, we got to do the - we got to do the Main Reg Check, and the secondary Accumulator Quantity.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Man, I tell you what, I - There's another thruster fire.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay. John, you want to go to Secondary Glycol?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, would you record star 23?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Denebola.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I don't - I flat don't think I can see a star pattern at all.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, I can out the front here, out the rendezvous window.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: But I got a star in the sextant.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: What's the name of it?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: You didn't see Denebola out the big [garble].

a16_pao_agnew.text: Good, Charlie.

a16_pao_agnew.text: That's magazine AA.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Magazine AA is what's on there. How about that? Another new [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.text: You're kidding me.

a16_pao_agnew.text: It's really there?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yep.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: [Laughter] Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Can't believe it.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: [Laughter] Okay, you got the [Hasselblad] EL, John?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: The what?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: How about an f/8.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, f/8.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: : Reads 250th.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: And...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: And infinity?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, why don't you take it about ten feet and go - well, put it on infinity for the time being. We might...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, because as we come across the [garble], we might see something. Yeah.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, and that thing just gets stowed out here. Here, I - I put up my little...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: : I can't do it; they put velcro right here.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...[garble] my goody bag.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: You don't want to do that.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: It can't get loose unless somebody bumps it.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, where did you put it?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Right there. See?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Isn't that neat?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay. I've got to...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: I could have nailed it right up here to this Velcro, but I don't think [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, here, I've been using this little goody bag and getting my stuff emptied out of it.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, here come the TSBs you guys.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Old TSB Charlie.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: It is so white and pretty.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Kind of like our suits.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: : Who wants one? Ken, there's one for you.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, I'll be with it in a second, as soon as I get my things put in here.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: (Singing) I'll be dancing [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: [Garble] be right in front of us on these, are there? They're all the same.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...before I leave.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I don't think there's any difference. I think it's like - like ... Okay. Oh, [garble] I was gonna put this thing back once you get the CMC up.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, John, here's one for you.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, that's sure nice, Charlie. I'm sure glad you gave me that TSB.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: I thought you'd like that.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, how about the...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: : Aren't - aren't I supposed to put some cameras and mags back in here? In U-l?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, I think that's [garble] yet, Charlie.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay. I'll leave it [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I'm taking one last look at my sextant - my telescope here...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Leave it at [garble]...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...before I screw up on it.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, ho.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I got a star in it now.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Hee, hee. Hee, hee, hee. It got away from me. Come back here, you [garble] [laughter].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Gosh, this is mag - Oh, look at those pretty stars. Look at that. Oh.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, GDC Align is all we got left.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, Charlie. I'll align the old GDC. That'll be roll 180...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I know, I couldn't be looking at Denebola again, but...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Can you see a pattern?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Yeah, I don't recognize it. It's brighter than heck. It looked like Denebola, but...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: [Garble] constellation is [garble].

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: I bet it is.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: See, the horizon is beginning to light up.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, and I just won me a beer.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: What's that?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Well, maybe I didn't here. What's going on?

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: I'm turning up S-band volume for the...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: : Oh-oh...

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Duke
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...Canaries [sic - means Carnarvon] check.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: ...I wonder.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Okay, Charlie. We got a little roll drift in the GDC and a little yaw drift, but we don't have a heck of a lot of other, and it's - Goldang, it's been running for 50 minutes, and it's off 5 degrees in yaw - 5 degrees in yaw - and we're on Rate 2, so you don't really know. And two degrees in pitch - Heck, I'll take that. And - and 8 degrees in roll for 50 minutes. That's with the BMAG s [garble]. That ain't really all that bad.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: Oh, I can even see stars now with the reticule turned on. Is it - guess what I got? Antares!

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Young
a16_pao_agnew.text: Beautiful.

a16_pao_agnew.speaker: Mattingly
a16_pao_agnew.text: : [Laughter] It even looked like Scorpio [laughter]. Oh.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: Okay, the GDC's aligned behind - to behind you at 51:05.

a16_0005100.speaker: Duke
a16_0005100.text: Mark that down.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: So I get a - then I have that we're on Rate 2, BMAGs.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: Yeah, I'm gonna do some scientific research on this thing with my little pen - unless some dingaling give me a [garble] pen [garble].

a16_0005100.speaker: Duke
a16_0005100.text: Okay, I - do you want to do this reference comparison - SCS attitude reference comparison check, John?

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: Yeah, but I - can we do it until after we've had some...

a16_0005100.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005100.text: You've got to compile them.

a16_0005100.speaker: Duke
a16_0005100.text: Oh, okay. That's right. [Garble] be sure.

a16_0005100.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005100.text: Oh, you beautiful [garble]. You little beauty. Hoo, hoo.

a16_0005100.speaker: Duke
a16_0005100.text: Okay, there's the comm coming up.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: What's that?

a16_0005100.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005100.text: I said that if I went from Manual, that the optics would drift.

a16_0005100.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0005100.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 51 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We're standing by. We have begun to acquire data over the Carnarvon pass. We presently show Apollo 16 with an orbit of 97 nautical miles by 91 nautical miles. We'll stand by now for conversations that will transpire between the CapCom Gordon Fullerton and the crew of Apollo 16.

a16_0005100.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0005100.text: That data being received was Instrument Unit data. We now have Acquisition Of Signal with the Command Module.

a16_0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005100.text: Apollo 16, Houston through Ca - Carnarvon. Over.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: Hello there, Houston. Read you loud and clear.

a16_0005100.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005100.text: Tell them where we are.

a16_0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005100.text: You're loud and clear also.

a16_0005100.speaker: Duke
a16_0005100.text: Okay. Okay, Gordy. We're down through - on page 2-17, Ken's done the P52, and everything is copacetic on all the steps up to that point, and I'll let Ken - Well, I've got the numbers here. He marked on stars 23 and 30. It was - Noun 05 was all balls. Torquing angles were plus 040, plus 031, plus 045, and we torqued them at 38:40. Over.

a16_0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005100.text: Okay, Charlie. We got that. [Pause.]

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: And that torquing angle was just super. [Pause.] And you can even see stars.

a16_0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005100.text: Very good. [Pause.]

a16_0005100.speaker: Duke
a16_0005100.text: Man, this is really something, Gordy.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: Hey, Gordon. Let me tell you a little bit about the ride.

a16_0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005100.text: Okay, stand by one, John. We're discussing the booster data here.

a16_0005100.speaker: Young
a16_0005100.text: Okay. Pressures look good up here.

a16_0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005100.text: Roger.

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Okay, I - No, there's nothing really spectacular different to report on the ride. We'll hold off on that.

a16_0005615.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0005615.text: Okay.

a16_0005615.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0005615.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. The rate pressure referred to there was on one of the attitude control engines. Readings here on the ground indicated it's about 100 psi [pounds per square inch, (690 kPa)] above the normal. We're at 57 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, continuing to monitor on this pass. This is Apollo Control Houston.

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Can you handle this, Charlie?

a16_0005615.speaker: Duke
a16_0005615.text: Yeah. Yeah, I can handle one of them.

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Want me to unstow your panel here?

a16_0005615.speaker: Duke
a16_0005615.text: No, no. Huh-uh. I don't [garble]...

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: [Garble] do that.

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: [Garble] as crummy in zero g as they are on the ground ....

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: John?

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Yeah.

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: Got a [garble] that's coming up by your sh - [garble] that's your shoulder. Your [garble] right? No, [garble] going the wrong way. That'll get it. Okay, and here's the UV magazine. It goes over by Charlie.

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Okay. What was that? I just keep handing them to Charlie. I don't know what he's [garble]...

a16_0005615.speaker: Duke
a16_0005615.text: Well, wait a minute, now. I'm getting my hands full here.

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: Okay. Well, the UV thing is the one that goes in - goes in that [garble]...

a16_0005615.speaker: Duke
a16_0005615.text: Yeah. Okay, John. You hold the camera and pass me the UV thing.

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: John, you got your hands full?

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Yeah. I'll take it.

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: Okay, I'll wait.

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: What do you need?

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: I got two TV cables here.

a16_0005615.speaker: Young
a16_0005615.text: Oh, heck. I can take the...

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: All right. The rest of this stuff I'm going to just go ahead and put up in the - in - my little stowage place up here, I think - while I'm here. Don't see any reason why not. Why not? Oh, you're gonna earn your pay today. I know you do good work ...

a16_0005615.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0005615.text: [Singing] De-de-dum-dum. Do-bee-do-dah-do-beedo - bee-do. (whistling) You're right. That camera did very well without practice.

a16_0005615.speaker: Duke
a16_0005615.text: [Laughter]

a16_0010000.speaker: Young
a16_0010000.text: [Garble] could have gone all day without telling about that.

a16_0010000.speaker: Young
a16_0010000.text: That ain't no problem, but [garble] those dingalings.

a16_0010000.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010000.text: Oh? Why do you say that, John?

a16_0010000.speaker: Young
a16_0010000.text: Well, I mean, I don't want to know there's a APS overpressure rate. What the heck can I do about it?

a16_0010000.speaker: Young
a16_0010000.text: But I - I don't have no gauges to be alert for it, or what? Well, if they want me to take some positive action, like putting on my helmet and gloves, why - they ought to say so, don't you reckon?

a16_0010000.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010000.text: Yeah, but I think we - at least, I have badgered them so much about - you know - just [garble] looking at something, that maybe...

a16_0010000.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0010000.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. One hour Ground Elapsed Time, continuing with the pass over Carnarvon and Honeysuckle.

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Well, Ken, you might have your work cut out for you.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Well, shoot. Now I've got to set up ORDEAL. Can I call Verb 83?

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Look at that sunrise coming up, you guys.

a16_0010203.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0010203.text: : [Apollo] 16, we're just about to LOS. The pressure shows right - in fact, a little bit above the relief pressure. We'll have to wait 'til the States to get a real good handle on how it's gonna deplete. Over.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Roger. [quoted as Duke in Tech transcript.]

a16_0010203.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0010203.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 1 hour, 4 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We've just had Loss Of Signal with Honeysuckle. The problem discussed between CapCom Gordon Fullerton and the crew of Apollo 16 was one relating to the APS, the Attitude [means Auxiliary] Propulsion System aboard the S-IVB and it deals with the regulator pressures on one of the - one of the APS, APS number 2. The normal reading is around 190 psi [1310 kPa]. We've shown an increase in the range of 320 psi [2,200 kPa]. This system relieves at 325 psi [2,240 kPa] and reseats once the number backs off to 225 psi [1,550 kPa].

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Yeah, it's coming up. See it. On the horizon.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Oh! Oh, look at that! Isn't that - Holy smokes. Have you ever seen anything like that?

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Hey, what does that mean to us now, is this - on this APS module.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Data [garble]. Get a hold of the - [laughter] It doesn't need APS for - it needs its attitude control.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Yeah. It doesn't have anything to do with TLI. How do we get our LM? You got your UV shade in the window, have you, Charlie?

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Did you have any trouble getting it in?

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: You said something about getting it in.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Okay. Because that UV is - is a-coming at us. Okay, I'm gonna start unstowing some Flight Data File stuff - PAD updates.

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Man, I think we've had sunrise.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: You're right. Look how pretty it is. Now, how do we [garble]...

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Hey, Ken, where can we put this - the cover for the TV lens? It doesn't have a piece of velcro.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Oh, okay. I'll - I'll put it down here with my optics cover - where I keep my optics in this little [garble] pouch.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: All the time we saved with that, I thought we would [garble].

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Well, I got an idea. We could get - we could do Verb 46, pitch it out of attitude, so it'd have to fire that APS module, and get back in.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Trouble is, there's too much backing up [garble] determine [garble].

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Well, the pressurization looks good. We got to get it down. What - what he's saying really is, we got to empty some of that fuel out of there. Right?

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Well, like he says - it seems to me what he means is that - is that the thing's just going to deplete the helium in there.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: That's [garble]. It do seem like helium did that.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Okay, get to those procedures on that page, and tell me what they are.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Okay, that - that would be where? In what?

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Flight Data File plus Dr. Spock's baby book.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Would I be allowed to take a picture out here? (Laughter )

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: No, I'll Just use it 250 , f - f/8 and [garble]...

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Flight Plan, Volume 1, [garble] Data Book. Data we essentially won't need for a while.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: I got the dark slide in.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: [Laughter.] Oh, you're off to a good start, leader.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: I got an Earth orbit chart here, but I don't think anybody really cares. Do you?

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: There's one over there that's supposed to be [garble].

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Okay, Charlie. I'm going to give you R12.

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Yeah, wait a minute. I got to get this...

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Okay. You want me to get that? The last three times, I've been able to just walk up there and put it in.

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Yeah, naturally, the flight one doesn't have a color code on it. {Garble].

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Hey, that's a - we're not - are we up on the States yet?

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: No. We're at 01:09. Where does that put us, Charlie?

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Hey, your docking probe thing is out over here, your docking light.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: We couldn't be in the States, could we?

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: We're at an hour and 9 minutes.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: Isn't it? Well - didn't I see some land go underneath us?

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Okay, I'll get that out of my pocket in a little bit.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Where are we at, though, Charlie? Does it say?

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: He talked to us from Carnarvon a few minutes ago.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: We're about halfway across the Pacific.

a16_0010203.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0010203.text: I thought I saw - maybe that was Hawaii. Huh? I thought I saw some land down there.

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: What the heck? My checklist floated to the wrong page. U.S. AOS (Acquisition of Signal) 01:28.

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Yeah, we're a long way from [garble]. Is there any ship or anything that we'd be talking to between now and then?

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Att Set dials, null FDAI 1 error needle.

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Okay, key V - Null the needles. Key Verb when nulled. Freeze display. And then...

a16_0010203.speaker: Young
a16_0010203.text: Okay, key - key Verb when nulled. Freeze display. Okay -

a16_0010203.speaker: Duke
a16_0010203.text: Okay, give me from the DSKY roll, pitch, and yaw.

a16_0024342.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0024342.text: Roger.

a16_0024342.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0024342.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 2 hours, 46 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We're now receiving radar data through Hawaii. We presently show Apollo 16 at an altitude of 766 nautical miles [1,418 kilometres].

a16_0024928.speaker: Duke
a16_0024928.text: Okay, Houston. I'm going to Omni Charlie.

a16_0024928.speaker: Duke
a16_0024928.text: Gordy, you got Omni Charlie. Over.

a16_0024928.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0024928.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 2 hours, 51 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Our countdown clock at Mission Control shows the time of separation is less than 13 minutes away now.

a16_0024928.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0024928.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 2 hours, 54 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Coming up now on that time when the booster initiates its maneuver to separation attitude. We presently show Apollo 16 at 1,974 nautical miles [3,656 km].

a16_0025400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0025400.text: Okay, and we are maneuvering to the attitude right now.

a16_0025400.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0025400.text: 16, we see the cabin is up to 5.7 now.

a16_0025400.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0025400.text: We'd like Omni Delta, please. [Long pause.]

a16_t-0024556.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0024556.text: Seven minutes away now from time of separation. We presently show Apollo 16 at an altitude of 2,620 nautical miles [4,852 km]. We are at 2 hours, 58 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Flight director Gene Kranz, is taking a check with his flight control team, for a Go/No-Go for transposition, docking and ejection of the Lunar Module.

a16_t-0024556.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0024556.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 2 hours 59 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We presently show Apollo 16 at 2,800 nautical miles [5,185 km] and velocity at 26,931 feet per second [8,208 m/s].

a16_t-0024556.speaker: Fullerton
a16_t-0024556.text: 16, Houston. The booster is in attitude and stable. You have a Go for T&D.

a16_t-0024556.speaker: Young
a16_t-0024556.text: Roger. [Pause.] We'll give you a call just before we get off.

a16_t-0024556.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0024556.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours Ground Elapsed Time. Present altitude of Apollo 16, 3,004 nautical miles [5,563 km]. Velocity now reading at 26,408 feet [8,049 metres] per second. We're four minutes away now from time of - proposed time of separation. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_t-0024556.speaker: Mission Control
a16_t-0024556.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 2 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16's present distance away from Earth now 3,388 nautical miles [6,274 kilometres].

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: ... so we have some measure. Okay? Ready to start the clock?

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay, Houston. We're getting ready to arm the pyros. Are you ready? [Pause.]

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay; Pyro Arm A is Armed; and B is Armed.

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Okay, let's read it - you want me to read out the - the rest of it?

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Let's see, I want to get a Verb 62 in here. Is that - that should be about where we start the time, right?

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Yeah. We're right at where we start the DET.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay, now, what we're gonna do - is we're gonna start the clock, and I'll call times. At 50, I'll take the CMC Mode switch to Auto; at 58, I start hitting the Plus-X. And then at zero, I push this button.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: We ullage for three seconds, and I release it.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: I'll take my Accel Command; pitch up - in ten seconds, I'll pitch up, making sure this needle's positive.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: When it goes positive, you can go to ...

a16_0030208.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030208.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 4 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16's presently at a height of 3,703 nautical miles [6,858 kilometres].

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Okay. Yeah. EMS Mode to Normal.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay, I'm going to catch that at the last minute because it counts.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: You know, John, if you'll just notice what it is for me...

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Yeah. I want to get my countdown on time.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030208.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 4 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 presently at a height of 3,703 nautical miles [6,858 km].

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay, I'm going to hit Normal on the EMS. Eight - Auto.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: 1, 2, 3, release. It's off. Oh, boy. We're holding attitude pretty good. Pitch is - pitch up. Okay, Pro - John.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030208.text: 3 hours, 5 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We've had small sep[aration] burn.

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Pro's in; talkbacks are all gray.

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Okay. The Reactant Valve is going to [garble].

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: Okay; all the talkbacks are still gray, Houston. It's pitching around now.

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Okay, hit these four to Close.

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Okay, and I got a gray on ...

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Man, look at all the junk out there.

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: Let me look out here and see what that stuff looks like [garble].

a16_0030208.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030208.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 6 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 presently at a distance of 4,017 nautical miles [7,439 km].

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay, let's look for that booster. That's the guy I don't want to hit. Watch my - watch my hand controller, John.

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: There's a door out there by the Earth (cough).

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Okay. Did you get Direct Ullage Two, open?

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: There he is. He's right out there.

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: You're well clear, and you're about 60 feet out.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Not yet, we got to get ...

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Oh, okay. That's right. We got to go there.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay. Man, did you ever see so much junk?

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Oh, look at that. It's like a picture.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Wait, wait, wait - I'm not clear yet.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Yeah, let me get my ullage in here before you - before you change the DAP on me.

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: Okay. Is it going to stop by itself?

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Okay. Now you can change it.

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: Key Release. Verb - Verb what? Verb 48 ...

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: Enter, no, you got to Enter first. John, let's go back to your Release - Key Release - Key Release. There you go.

a16_0030208.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030208.text: 11102. Hey, how you doing with that TV?

a16_0030208.speaker: Duke
a16_0030208.text: Coming up on the - getting the - Antenna's going to Reacq right now.

a16_0030208.speaker: Young
a16_0030208.text: Looks like it's about 80 feet out.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Okay, Houston. You got the High Gain?

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: Well, I think you're closing, but I sure can't tell it ...

a16_0030736.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0030736.text: Roger, Charlie.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: You got the DAC started?

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Oh, I forgot! Ten feet, f/8, 12.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Okay.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: [Garble] turn the power on and I think I'm gonna hold it off for a second here [garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Yeah.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: [Garble] close [garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030736.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 8 minutes now on Ground Elapsed Time. We show Apollo 16 at a height of 4,435 nautical miles [8,213 km].

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Okay, did you get the DAP?

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: The DAP is set.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Man, that looks like I'm opening, doesn't it, John?

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: Yeah [garble] you [garble]. Whatever you [garble] it [garble] much to open it.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: I don't want to put in too much [garble] rate.

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: That's right [garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Hey, when that thing turned around, guys, the crosshairs in the COAS are within the docking target.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Well, I can't get - I - I got this half of a picture ...

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: It is close - closing, isn't it?

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Yeah, he is.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Okay, Houston, you ought to be getting some TV.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: I'm trying to get a mark on that.

a16_0030736.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0030736.text: I haven't got it yet; we're working on it.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Have you - how does the monitor look?

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: It looks great; but all I got is just this little picture - the cor - the corner of the picture. I can't ...

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Well, if you move the ...

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: You got to move the camera.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: ... camera?

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: That's what I've been trying to do, and I can't get any more [garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: [Garble]. That thing is maneuvering in attitude a little bit. I don't think I'm closing [garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: [Garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Let it ride?

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: [Garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Hmph, there we are - perfect picture.

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: I don't think you're closing.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0030736.text: Give me [garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Young
a16_0030736.text: [Garble].

a16_0030736.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030736.text: Apollo Control, Houston. 3 hours, 10 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The black and white picture is beginning to come in now. Television is now showing...

a16_0030736.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0030736.text: We got a picture now, Charlie, and it looks real good.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Man, it just looks like a picture book from up here, Gordo. We must have a zillion particles along with us. [Pause.]

a16_0030736.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0030736.text: Roger. We see the particles and - great picture!

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Hey, is the zoom in too much, Gordo? You - Let me take it out a little bit. [Long pause.]

a16_0030736.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030736.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 11 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 now 4,851 nautical miles [8,984 kilometres] away from the Earth.

a16_0030736.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0030736.text: That's just right, Charlie. That's a good zoom setting right now.

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Super! [Long pause.]

a16_0030736.speaker: Duke
a16_0030736.text: Gordy, looks like Orion is hanging in there pretty well. She looks great.

a16_0030736.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0030736.text: Looks the same to us.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030736.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 13 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 presently 5,195 nautical miles [9,621 kilometres] away from the Earth.

a16_0030736.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0030736.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 15 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 now 5,536 nautical miles [10,253 kilometres] away from the Earth.

a16_0031300.speaker: Young
a16_0031300.text: About a foot out now, Houston.

a16_0031500.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0031500.text: Roger. Looks like a real smooth join-up. [Long pause.]

a16_0031500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0031500.text: Apollo 16 reporting that they have captured the Lunar Module. We're at three hours, 16 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We show an altitude of 5,706 nautical miles [10,567 kilometres].

a16_0031500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031500.text: Well, I'm going back over them, and I can't see - Well, I don't know.

a16_0031500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031500.text: I tell you, it doesn't dress up very much - or even.

a16_0031500.speaker: Duke
a16_0031500.text: Looks like something in the [garble] or something.

a16_0031500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031500.text: Man, this patience biz is hard to take (laughter). We're dressing up in pitch now, John, and the yaw is, too. We're gonna have lots of time here.

a16_0031814.speaker: Young
a16_0031814.text: Ken's taking some time in dressing this thing up, getting these attitudes right.

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: ...quite a bit from the attitude that we had.

a16_0031814.speaker: Duke
a16_0031814.text: Look at that. Isn't that something else?

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: [Garble] fired it again, it looked like [garble].

a16_0031814.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0031814.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 19 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16's present distance from Earth, 6,246 nautical miles [11,568 kilometres]. Velocity now reading 21,466 feet per second [6,543 m/s].

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: My docking budget didn't allow for all this. But I get no prize if I break it.

a16_0031814.speaker: Young
a16_0031814.text: Yeah, I think it's probably Mylar. I think we got some gas [garble] trapped in those blankets maybe.

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: John, is it worth dressing up the roll, do you think?

a16_0031814.speaker: Young
a16_0031814.text: I don't think so. It looks like that's [garble].

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: Okay; we're about - I'm trying to guess what it is in degrees we're off. I guess we're still off maybe 3 or 4 degrees.

a16_0031814.speaker: Young
a16_0031814.text: Ain't supposed to be off that far.

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: Well, you know they don't tell you how to tell the degrees you're off. I - I guess I never worried about it except [garble].

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: Yeah. Okay; all we have to do in order to do it now is what?

a16_0031814.speaker: Duke
