a16_0031814.text: Put Docking Probe, Retract , to Prim[ary] 1. That's all you got to do.

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: We got both rates nulling at the same time.

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: Little more help here in pitch [garble].

a16_0031814.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0031814.text: I tell you what. We're within a width of a line.

a16_0031814.speaker: Duke
a16_0031814.text: Man, I think that was it.

a16_0032201.speaker: Duke
a16_0032201.text: Did you get a - a gray?

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: Roger, John. We saw it come in.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: And there is no question when you get the latches.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0032201.text: 3 hours, 22 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 at 6,845 nautical miles [12,677 km] away.

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: We'd like - We noticed the mixing valves cycling about once every 10, 15 seconds. We'd like to give you a mark, at which time we want you to put the Glycol Evap Temp In Valve in Manual and try to catch the flow rate at a - at a appropriate setting. I'll - I'll give you kind of a countdown and a mark here.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: I think we saw it before.

a16_0032201.speaker: Young
a16_0032201.text: Yeah, we've been noticing that ourselves. [Pause.]

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: Okay, Charlie. Let me - let me give you some numbers here before I get off. With it - When we were docked...

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: Okay, flow rate's high. It's starting back down. [Long pause.]

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: John, now all of a sudden we've stopped seeing it - that it has stopped cycling. You didn't throw the switch already, did you?

a16_0032201.speaker: Young
a16_0032201.text: That's negative. We're awaiting your mark there.

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: Well, it - (chuckle) it just hung up. Just as I said that. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: ...supposed to do that. Let me pull those docking probe circuit breakers.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: Okay, Docking Probe Main A and Main B are open.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: Hey, when that thing's lined up, it's one bar width - the target is one bar ...

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: We'd like you to cycle the Manual back to Auto and see if that starts it back down. Over.

a16_0032201.speaker: Duke
a16_0032201.text: Okay, you were in Manual for about two seconds and back to Auto.

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: Okay. [Pause.] Okay, it's coming down now. Stand by to put it in Manual.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: And the - it's over to the right one bar width and up one-half bar width.

a16_0032201.speaker: Duke
a16_0032201.text: Okay. Okay, you got it right there on the "now." [Pause.] (onboard): Okay; say that again, Ken.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: Okay. My - the cross is one-half bar width...

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: I was a little slow on the "now," but leave it there for now and press on with the normal procedures. [Long pause.]

a16_0032201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032201.text: ...and one bar to the right of the target. Right then - right here next to my docking [garble].

a16_0032201.speaker: Duke
a16_0032201.text: Okay. Tape Recorder's Off. Going Off.

a16_0032201.speaker: Duke
a16_0032201.text: Houston, before we turn the TV off, we gon - we want to give you a picture of the Earth.

a16_0032201.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0032201.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 27 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. That view of Earth from a distance of 7,500 nautical miles [13,890 kilometres].

a16_0032201.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032201.text: Very nice picture, Charlie. We can see Southwestern United States, Lower California. Very nice.

a16_0032201.speaker: Duke
a16_0032201.text: Good. Ken's doing all that good work for you. It's out his window. [Long pause.]

a16_0032700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032700.text: Gordy, is that color okay for you?

a16_0032700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032700.text: I bet it's good, but you just can't believe how beautiful it is. See the reds in the desert down there and the Southern United States and northern part of Mexico. And from here, you see the Great Lakes and the State of Florida out there. And it's just absolutely something. We're going to go back to work, but thought you'd enjoy that.

a16_0032700.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032700.text: Thank you for the picture. It's the next best thing to being up there. [Pause.]

a16_0032700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032700.text: And - and we might be able to get you an S-IVB later on. That's if you got room to get that kind of stuff.

a16_0032700.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032700.text: 16, Houston. We'll extend the time on commercial TV lines here if - if it looks like we'll get some good shots on the S-IVB.

a16_0032700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0032700.text: Okay. I really haven't worked out the angles to tell you exactly how the Sun's going to be, but I have an idea we'll see it pretty nicely from here.

a16_0032700.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0032700.text: Okay, we'll stand by for it. [Long pause.]

a16_0032700.speaker: Young
a16_0032700.text: Just went to Auto on O 2 Heater 3, Houston. We're down to that part in the post-docking checklist.

a16_0032700.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0032700.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 31 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 presently at a distance of 8,240 nautical miles [15,269 km] away from Earth. Velocity now reading 19,445 feet per second [5,930 m/s].

a16_0033319.speaker: Duke
a16_0033319.text: Okay, Gordy, we're down to 0.2 on the Delta - I mean, correction 2.0 on the Delta-P, and we're starting our leak check.

a16_0033319.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0033319.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 3 hours, 36 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We presently show Apollo 16 at a - a distance of 8,997 nautical miles [16,662 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reading 18,818 feet per second [5,736 m/s]. Very little conversation with the crew at this time as they're in the process of removing the tunnel hatch and going through their check list prior to separation and ejection of the Lunar Module. We are at 3 hours, 37 minutes; continuing to monitor. This Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0033600.speaker: Duke
a16_0033600.text: We're picking up again on the procedure, Gordy. Cabin pressure's down to 41.

a16_0033600.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0033600.text: 16, Houston. In about 30 seconds, a couple [of] non-propulsive vents will open on the booster.

a16_0033600.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0033600.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 40 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The Booster Systems engineer reports the S-IVB, a non-propulsive vent has begun. We're at 3 hours, 40 minutes; continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0034018.speaker: Duke
a16_0034018.text: Okay, Houston. The hatch is out.

a16_0034018.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0034018.text: 3 hours, 40 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. This is Apollo Control, Houston. Charlie Duke reports the hatch is out. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 9,739 nautical miles [18,036 km] from Earth. Velocity now reading 18,277 feet per second [5,570 m/s].

a16_0034300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0034300.text: Houston, it looks like Number 10 latch is indeed locked. Let me start by saying all the latches are locked. Number 10 is - is over the ring, but the handle isn't all the way up flush, and we're just going to leave it alone. Thought we'd just tell you about it.

a16_0034300.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0034300.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 46 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 presently at 10,617 nautical miles [19,663 km] away from the Earth.

a16_0034600.speaker: Duke
a16_0034600.text: Okay, Houston. The connectors are connected, and we got LM power to CSM, and the system test is okay.

a16_0034600.speaker: Duke
a16_0034600.text: And, Gordy, the old Rover's right where it's supposed to be.

a16_0034903.speaker: Duke
a16_0034903.text: The only reason we comment on it, it just seemed like there was a awful lot of them.

a16_0034903.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0034903.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Making that report was Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke. In his discussion with CapCom Gordon Fullerton here in Mission Control.

a16_0034903.speaker: Duke
a16_0034903.text: DAC six [garble] feet per second, six frames per second.

a16_0034903.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0034903.text: DAC's - was six frames per second, and what did you say - six feet?

a16_0034903.speaker: Duke
a16_0034903.text: No, just six frames per second. Okay, lo - DAP is - load the DAP, 21101.

a16_0034903.speaker: Duke
a16_0034903.text: And - Okay, that's go. And load Pitch trim a plus -

a16_0034903.speaker: Duke
a16_0034903.text: Okay, load Noun 22 attitude maneuver - monitor - Okay, it's a 90, 325 point - load Noun 22. Pro[ceed] on that one now.

a16_0034903.speaker: Duke
a16_0034903.text: Nine - plus 90 - 09000, plus 325.5 - zero, plus 355.90. Okay; Verb 60 - Verb 63.

a16_0034903.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0034903.text: That's affirmative. I got Secs Arm, two, close, verify.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Okay, Houston. We're ready to proceed with the Logic.

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Want me to hold the Flight Plan, Ken?

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Okay. All right, now. Yeah. Before we get ready to get off...

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: ...there's a couple of items we need to review, so...

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Okay; why don't we go down to that part?

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Okay. Have you armed the pyros?

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: TVC Servo Power, On - Power Number 1.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: TVC Servo Power, Number l, is AC1/Main A.

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Trans Control Power, On, Up; verify.

a16_0035632.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0035632.text: Okay, they look good. [Referring to the pyros]

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Okay, then call P47. Okay, what do you want to do?

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Let - let's review before we get into 47.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Okay. The - the thing we got to do when we get through here is I want to be sure that there's a - we're gonna come in the last thing we started and we said at the time we hit Sep, I start my clock, and - and then at...

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: ...three to five seconds, I thrust for three.

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: And you go to Auto - you go to - start your clock and go to Auto.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: And go to Auto. At the same time, John hits the Sep.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: And we'll [garble] all three of the [garble] on the line again.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Okay, and I'm going to hold my hand here. Okay; now the next thing is that I want to do this maneuver - is within 30 - at - any time after 30 seconds, I can start my maneuver.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Yeah, 30 seconds and clear. We'll go [garble] approximately a minute. Okay. They haven't clued us to get off. I guess that's all we're waiting on. Are there any questions?

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Houston, we got - We're ready to get off, if you guys are ready.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: [Garble] this display up here? Okay, at five, I go for three.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Okay. Are you all set? I'll give you a countdown. We'll go at zero. 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 -

a16_0035632.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0035632.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 3 hours, 59 minutes. That's Charlie Duke reporting they're off the booster.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: [Garble] 2, 3, 4 [garble]. Okay, now, in a minute, we're gonna...

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: I guess it's gone; I can't see it anymore.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: Okay, and [garble]. Okay and go to [garble] there.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Oh, oh, don't - Yeah, okay. Let's go to a minute. Can you see the booster anywhere in sight?

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Okay, I got my BMAGs caged. All off.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Enter. Pro[ceed]. Is that the right attitude?

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: Okay. SECS Pyro Arm, Two, Safe.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: Your Pyro Arms are Two going to Safe.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: SECS Arm, l, 2, Open. There's another strap.

a16_0035632.speaker: Duke
a16_0035632.text: I got them. Okay. The O 2 Tank Isol Valve is gray.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: Okay. It says O 2 Tank 3 Isol valve talkback gray.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: Mapping Camera On switch is supposed to go to Off.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: 21101. And it doesn't look like we're yawing enough. Oh, I know what it is.

a16_0035632.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0035632.text: We - we left it in the - no, you put a 63 in there. But, boy, that's [garble].

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: Mapping Camera On should be Off.

a16_0035632.speaker: Young
a16_0035632.text: Pan Camera Power should be Off. Service Module/AC Power should be Off.

a16_0040132.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040132.text: Okay, Houston. We're doing our maneuver, and we'll tell you as soon as we have a visual.

a16_0040132.speaker: Duke
a16_0040132.text: Which way should it come out of?

a16_0040132.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040132.text: Well, that's why I got this ....

a16_0040132.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040132.text: ...ball set here. We have to get rid of that thing.

a16_0040132.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040132.text: Okay; we have rolled right 20 degrees.

a16_0040132.speaker: Duke
a16_0040132.text: Man, we fired some jets, I'll tell you.

a16_0040132.speaker: Duke
a16_0040132.text: Yeah, you can see those Mylar particles getting blown off of the [garble].

a16_0040132.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040132.text: Rolling to 90 - Oh, you can feel this thing kind of ...

a16_0040343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040343.text: Okay, Houston. The post-LM injection - ejection checklist is complete.

a16_0040343.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040343.text: Roger. And, for your information, we're unable to get lines from Goldstone to Houston for live TV; however, we're going to record any TV you give us for later playback. Over.

a16_0040343.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040343.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 5 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Our displays presently show Apollo 16 at 13,310 nautical miles [24,650 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reading 16,083 feet per second [4,902 m/s].

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Houston, Casper is out of his bag; and we got the S-IVB in the window. And the TV is transmitting pictures of it now, and if you want to do your maneuver with it, we're well clear.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay, we copy a Go for the S-IVB maneuver.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: That's the attitude maneuver we're talking about. [Pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: They'll start the maneuver about 4:10 GET. [Pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Okay.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: 16, your TV down-link looks good out at the site; however, we can't see it here in Houston live.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Okay. Well we're still adjusting the - all those good things.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; we're 4 hours, 10 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. That was Ken Mattingly responding to CapCom Gordon Fullerton. We now show Apollo 16 at a distance from Earth of 14,005 nautical miles [25,937 km] with a velocity reading 15,751 feet per second [4,746 m/s]. Booster Systems engineer reports the yaw maneuver is in progress.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Rog. We can see it maneuvering. [Pause.] I tell you, they never make movies like these.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Gotcha. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: We'd like Auto Track on the High Gain, please. [Pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Duke
a16_0040744.text: You got it.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Gordy, we've - we lost the - the monitor picture, and we're gonna try to power the TV set down. We're gonna check all the connections, and it's got a lot of horizontal lines. And you really can't even make out the image. It started out okay, and then while John was taking a picture, it - the monitor picture went out. So we're gonna try to take a look at it. It's got a whole bunch of horizontal lines.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay, we'll go to...

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: It looks like maybe multiple images.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: We'll go to the site. Standby.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 14 minutes. That was Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly talking about the television. We now show Apollo 16 at a distance of 14,416 nautical miles [26,698 km]. Velocity now reads 15,543 feet per second [4,737 m/s].

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: 16, Houston. The maneuver is complete. We're standing by for your Go for the evasive burn.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Okay, stand by one. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Okay, Gordy, we're all set. It looks like it's almost 90 degrees to us.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay. On the TV problem, we had a good picture out at the site there at the first, but then we started losing signal strength, which would - doesn't really tell us whether anything is wrong with your monitor set or not.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Okay. Well, we're gonna take pictures like it's working, and you can check it out later.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: And we are all set.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Roger.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 16 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Booster Systems engineer reports he will start with the evasive burn of the S-IVB at 4 hours, 18 minutes Ground Elapsed Time.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: 16, Houston. Goldstone says they're getting a good picture, and so your trouble is worth the effort there, and we'll start the evasive burn at 4:18 even. [Pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Okay, Gordy, thank you. We got another spectacular view of the Earth down here. The polar ice cap. We can see the whole sphere, and the United States is absolutely spectacular.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: How about that. [Pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Young
a16_0040744.text: And out the other side, we've got a crescent Moon.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: In fact, you can see Lake Mead, Gordy; very clearly.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: No kidding?

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 17 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 now 15,039 nautical miles [27,852 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reading 15,272 feet per second [4,655 m/s].

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 18 minutes. Booster Systems engineer indicates he has initiated the evasive burn. That's 1 minute, 20 seconds in duration.

a16_0040744.speaker: Young
a16_0040744.text: We can see her moving away now, Gordon, and she's just slowly picking up a little speed there. Only way you can tell it's moving is against the - the particles in the background. I don't think you can see those on TV, but it's - it looks like there's a million stars out behind the S-IVB as it moves off.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Roger, John. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Now the evasive burn is complete, now.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay, John, I'll speak to them. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 20 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. That was spacecraft commander John Young expressing his appreciation of the Saturn V team.

a16_0040744.speaker: Young
a16_0040744.text: And you might relay to old Mike Wash, thanks a lot for his help. We know he's leaving, and we're sure glad we didn't have to use any of that training he gave us.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Okay, we'll sure do that. He's just about to walk out the door. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: 4 hours, 21 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Mike Wash has worked with the Apollo flight crews in the - in training these crews for the powered phase of launch and also...

a16_0040744.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0040744.text: Gordy, up off - looks like Alaska - up maybe a little farther north - is a pretty good swirl pattern. Looks like a pretty good storm up there.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: During the powered phase of flight, Mike Wash is always positioned right next to the Capsule Communicator.

a16_0040744.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0040744.text: Apollo 16, here is a word from the auxiliary CapCom here.

a16_0040744.speaker: Wash
a16_0040744.text: Good luck, you fellows. Take it easy, and hope everything works out all right.

a16_0040744.speaker: Young
a16_0040744.text: Kind wordks, Mike. Thank you.

a16_0040744.speaker: Wash
a16_0040744.text: Say again?

a16_0040744.speaker: Young
a16_0040744.text: Thank you for all your trouble. We sure enjoyed working with you.

a16_0040744.speaker: Wash
a16_0040744.text: Well, was sure my pleasure, John; thank you a lot. Good-bye and good luck.

a16_0040744.speaker: Young
a16_0040744.text: Thank you, now.

a16_0040744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0040744.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 22 minutes. The voice you just heard was Mike Wash who is being transferred to the Ames Research Center. We're at 4 hours, 23 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We show Apollo 16 at a distance of 15,707 nautical miles [29,089 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reading 14,972 feet per second [4,563 m/s].

a16_0042428.speaker: Young
a16_0042428.text: Okay and the - the S-IVB has drifted maybe half a mile away now, so we went ahead and turned off the tube.

a16_0042428.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0042428.text: John, just before you turned the mon - the TV off, was the monitor still giving you trouble?

a16_0042428.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0042428.text: I guess it's about time for a little Verb 49 to the P52 attitude. How's that suit you?

a16_0042428.speaker: Duke
a16_0042428.text: Gordy, the - I can't get over the view of that Earth. None of the pictures just do it justice. Absolutely beautiful.

a16_0042428.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0042428.text: We're kind of getting the idea that you're impressed.

a16_0042428.speaker: Young
a16_0042428.text: Man, the thing about it, Gordy, is that the whole Southern United States, Mexico, and that - and - and Florida and Cuba and the Virgin Islands down that way - they're all clear of clouds. It's just fantastic!

a16_0042428.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0042428.text: Did you take some good pictures?

a16_0042428.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0042428.text: The way we're going, we may have to get a reload before we get to the Moon.

a16_0042428.speaker: Young
a16_0042428.text: As a matter of fact, you can see as far north as Lake Michigan and Lake Superior.

a16_0042428.speaker: Duke
a16_0042428.text: And all the way down past the Yucatan and - and into the Central America.

a16_0043202.speaker: Young
a16_0043202.text: Houston, we've got the cabin back up some now, and our LM/CM Delta-P gauge is reading 0.6, and that's probably due to that Delta[-P] on the cabin. And the O 2 Flow Hi light has gone out, so things are getting back to normal.

a16_0043202.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0043202.text: And, Houston, we've done a LM/CM Delta-P; and at time four hours and 30 minutes, we had a plus 0.6.

a16_0043202.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0043202.text: Houston, we're going to take the Waste Stowage valve to Vent [at] this time.

a16_0043202.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0043202.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 4 hours, 37 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Our space digitals display in Mission Control [is] presently using the Moon as a reference and we show that Apollo 16 is 174,639 nautical miles [323,431 kilometres] away from the Moon. At 4 hours, 37 minutes, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0043952.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0043952.text: Ah, 16, Houston. Don't know if you can see it or not, but we've started the LOX dump on the S-IVB. [Pause.]

a16_0043952.speaker: Duke
a16_0043952.text: We lost it a little while ago, Gordy.

a16_0043952.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0043952.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 40 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The Booster Systems engineer reports that the LOX dump has been completed with the S-IVB. We're at 4 hours, 41 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0043952.speaker: Duke
a16_0043952.text: Houston, are you ready for us to start charging Battery B? [Pause.]

a16_0043952.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0043952.text: Okay, we're Go for the battery charge on B, and we'd also like you to dial in the Flight Plan High Gain angles, minus 47 and 98, and go to Reacq[uire].

a16_0043952.speaker: Duke
a16_0043952.text: Okay, you got the angles, and you're going to Reacq[uire].

a16_0044546.speaker: Duke
a16_0044546.text: Okay, we got Bat B charging, and it says volts should be 37½ to 39½, and I'm looking at 33. [Pause.]

a16_0044546.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0044546.text: Charlie, we got - we figured about 8 amp-hours out of that battery, so it'll be a while yet before the voltage gets back up, and EECOM thinks that's okay.

a16_0044546.speaker: Young
a16_0044546.text: Houston, we got 3.4 on 7A. We're gonna vent - we gonna vent the battery to zero, if that's okay.

a16_0044546.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0044546.text: We'd like you to hold on that a minute. [Pause.]

a16_0044546.speaker: Duke
a16_0044546.text: You're too late, we just vented it. [Long pause.]

a16_0044546.speaker: Young
a16_0044546.text: Okay, it's reading about two-tenths right now.

a16_0044546.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0044546.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The space digitals display is still using the Moon as a reference. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 172 - 173,082 nautical miles [320,548 km] away from the Moon. Continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0045000.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045000.text: Houston, got a couple of comments on the EMS for G&C, whenever he has a break.

a16_0045000.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045000.text: That must look funny. Okay. We been running null bias tests here for - well, since we got in orbit - each time the checklist calls for it. On the first one, we found that in our hundred-second check, it gained 2.5; then, just before docking, it got 2.6; and I just ran another one, and I have 2.8. And I don't really know what you can do with that, but I just thought I'd go ahead and tell you about that's the magnitude of what we're looking at.

a16_0045000.speaker: Young
a16_0045000.text: Okay, and our first rough guess as to how the SCS GDC system is performing, it looks like it's well within spec in pitch, yaw, and roll, as far as its drift measurements go.

a16_0045000.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045000.text: Okay, Ken and John, we got that.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: 16, Houston. Whenever you're ready, we're ready to load the PTC REFSMMAT.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: Okay, you have P00 and Accept.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Ken, sorry about that. We didn't get coordinated here. We don't have an uplink site, so go back to Block until after 5 hours, and we'll try it again then.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: All righty. We're back in UpTel to Block. And we're going to be kind of hanging up here for a while anyhow, while we get our suits off. It - it turns out to be a pretty interesting operation with these new B-suits.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Roger.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Oh, how about that. I haven't heard of that one before.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: Then when we - when we scooted out here and you started your nonpropulsive vent, we could see - First, it just looked like - like it was a little mist around the outside when you looked at the Sun. And then the Sun hit it at such an angle that you started getting a - a spectral reflection, and it looked like a rainbow out over the LM. And then after - after that, you could look out my Number 1 window, and apparently the lighting was just right so that it - it had the appearance of - of light streaming off to a point source at infinity. There was a little blank spot in it at the - at what looke

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Rog. Enjoying the description. [Pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: I'll tell you, you can't wait too many years to make this worth it.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Roger.

a16_0045315.speaker: Young
a16_0045315.text: Gordy, on that boost, that S-IC is a real freight train. I'll tell you, boy. I can't get over that.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Roger.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: Could you folks see that thing on the TV up through staging?

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: I didn't watch it all the way until it went out of sight. I'll have to check here. [Pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0045315.text: Apollo Control, Houston...

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Yeah, I guess we saw even [the LES] tower jett.

a16_0045315.speaker: Duke
a16_0045315.text: Good show. John's in the middle of his suit doff.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0045315.text: We're at 4 hours, 58 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Most of that long description coming from Ken Mattingly, how...

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: And thanks to good old Stu Roosa's suggestion, we wrote in the Flight Plan to be sure and take a look at the fires out there in Africa as we went over, which is something we probably would have forgotten or never even thought about. And they are just as beautiful as everybody's ever said they could be. They're just all over the place. All these little - little yellowish-red dots down there. And there was some - looked like some low overcast in parts of the area, or maybe it was - from our altitude, maybe it was a high overcast. But it just gave - It looked like looking at the lights of a city

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Roger. We'll be sure to remind Ron to look for that one. [Pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: I tell you, God didn't equip us with enough eyes to see everything that there is to see in the first hour.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0045315.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 4 hours, 59 minutes. That last remark coming from Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly. Our space digital display still using the Moon as a reference. We show Apollo 16 172,048 nautical miles [318,633 kilometres] away from the Moon.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: Gordy, it looks like this whole operation may take us longer than - than we had guessed. Is there any thermal constraint on getting a 52 attitude and going to those other attitudes? Looks like we got some time to go here...

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: I'll check on that, Ken. We're about...

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: ...but I just wondered if that's something we ought to keep in mind.

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Okay. We're about to a handover here. I'll check on that and come back to you through Hawaii.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: Okay, thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: 16, we're - through Hawaii now. And you're scheduled in this attitude through 7 hours or - at least, so no problem thermally, and you're not even due to do the P52 for another half hour, so you're plenty ahead.

a16_0045315.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0045315.text: Okay, that P52 - We're going to come to a decision point; here pretty soon, whether to - you want us to do that and then we'll pick up the suit doffing after that, or we - I'd just as soon go ahead and do the - get all the suits out of the way. And we can do the 52 on schedule, or we can do it after we get the suits off. Does it make any difference to you folks ?

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: Let me check. [Long pause.]

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: If that's what you'd like to do, why don't you go ahead with the - finish up the suits. No problem slipping the 52 a little bit. And we'd like P00 and Accept for that uplink.

a16_0045315.speaker: Young
a16_0045315.text: Okay, there's P00 and Accept. [Pause.] Is Fredo still around there?

a16_0045315.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0045315.text: No, he went home about a half hour ago.

a16_0050528.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0050528.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 5 hours, 10 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Our displays still show the Moon as our reference. We show Apollo 16 at a distance of 170,878 nautical miles [316,466 km] away from the Moon and we've had no conversation for a while with the crew of Apollo 16. We suspect that they're in the process of doffing their space suits and later preparation for their eat period which is scheduled to begin at six hours Ground Elapsed Time. Five hours, 10 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0050528.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0050528.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 5 hours, 30 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Our space digital display now using the Earth reference. We show Apollo 16 at 23,892 nautical miles [44,248 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reading 12,295 feet per second [3,747 m/s].

a16_0050528.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0050528.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston, at 5 hours, 44 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 25,488 nautical miles [46,204 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reading 11,945 feet per second [3,504 m/s]. Very shortly in Mission Control, we will have a change of shift - or shift changeover of the Gene Kranz team of flight controllers will be replaced by Pete Frank's team of flight controllers. We're at 5 hours, 45 minutes and continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0050528.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0050528.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 5 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 26,143 nautical miles [48,417 km] away from the Earth. And traveling at a velocity of 11,796 feet per second [3,595 m/s]. We're continuing with our shift turnover in the Mission Control Center at the present time. Pete Frank's team of Orange flight controllers coming aboard, replacing the Gene Kranz team of White flight controllers. We estimate the start time of our change of shift news conference at 6 to 6:15 pm Central Standard Time. The news conference will involve Flight D

a16_0060354.speaker: Duke
a16_0060354.text: Hello, Houston; 16. John and I are back up now.

a16_0060354.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0060354.text: Roger. That up-link is complete. In case you didn't hear me some time ago, the computer is yours.

a16_0060354.speaker: Young
a16_0060354.text: And it took us about an hour for me and Charlie to climb out of those suits and stow them. It's really something.

a16_0060354.speaker: Fullerton
a16_0060354.text: I'm going to hand over to Pete here. He's coming on with a good boost there. He's got a bunch of - P37 PAD and a bunch of Flight Plan updates for you when you get somebody free to do some stenographic work there. Enjoyed the first six hours. Hope the rest of it goes as well.

a16_0060354.speaker: Young
a16_0060354.text: Gordon, that was beautiful. Tell Flight and the guys down in the trenches, "Man, that was super!"

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Roger, 16. At 11 hours in the Flight Plan.

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Okay; go ahead.

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Roger. At 11 hours, we want to delete "Waste Stowage Vent valve, Close;" and, at 12:15, we will add "Waste Stowage Vent valve, Close." [Pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Okay; copy add at 12:15 "Waste Stowage Vent valve, Close."

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Roger. And delete it at 11. [Long pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Okay; go ahead.

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Roger. Then we've got the change to the CSM Experiments/EVA Checklist having to do with the ultraviolet filter. [Pause.] UV filter apparently did not meet the specs, and we're going to have to make some changes to the exposures at - on several different pages in the checklist. [Pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: We'll wait on that; we don't have that checklist out yet, Pete.

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Okay; and I've got P37 block data. [Pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Stand by.

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Okay, Pete, go ahead with the P37 block data.

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Okay. Lift-off plus 15. It's 015:00; 5493; minus 165; 046:40. [Pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Roger; copy. 015:00; 5493; minus 165; 046:40. Over.

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Rog. That's correct, Johnny. [Pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Is that all?

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Yeah [garble] that's all.

a16_0061301.speaker: Duke
a16_0061301.text: Okay. How's the midcourse [correction] looking? [Pause.]

a16_0061301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0061301.text: Stand by one. We're still looking at it; it looks pretty good right now.

a16_0061301.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0061301.text: This is Apollo Control. We've now completed our shift handover in Mission Control. Flight Director Pete Frank and the Orange Team of Flight Controllers. The CapCom on this shift is astronaut Donald Peterson. We have a change of shift press briefing scheduled to begin momentarily in the MSC News Center briefing room as is our normal practice during change of shift briefings, we will have the air to ground line down and we'll be recording any conservations with the crew for playback following the press conference. The coming eight hours or so should be a relatively quiet time for the crew. The b

a16_0061301.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0061301.text: The crew is scheduled to begin a eat period and as we passed up to Charlie Duke we do not expect to have Midcourse Correction 1 based on the current tracking data. At 6 hours, 19 minutes; Apollo 16 is traveling at a velocity of 11,159 feet per second [3,401 m/s]. Now 29,187 nautical miles [54,054 km] from Earth. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0063115.speaker: Duke
a16_0063115.text: Houston, now have Noun 93; are you happy?

a16_0063115.speaker: Peterson
a16_0063115.text: Okay, 16. You can go ahead and program.

a16_0063953.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0063953.text: This is Apollo Control at 6 hours, 41 minutes. During the change of shift briefing, we accumulated a small amount of tape conversations which we'll play back for you at this time. And then continue to stand by live following that tape playback.

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Pete, 16 here. Go ahead with the update. Give me a page number for the UV, and we'll update the filter settings.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Okay; we've got a whole bunch of pages. We'll start on 2-16. [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0064301.text: Okay; go ahead.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Under item 4, we want to change from "20 seconds - 2 frames" to "2 seconds - 2 frames." [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay; keep going.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Okay; on page 2-17. Item 4, "20 seconds - 2 frames," change to "1/15 second - 2 frames." [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Page 2...

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay; 2-16 - 2-16, line 4, "20 seconds" to "2 seconds," and 2-17, same line is "1/15" versus "20 seconds."

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: That's affirmative. And on page 2-19, we want to change shutter - under item 5 - we want to change "Shutter 1/15 - 2 frames" to "Shutter 1 - 2 frames." [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay; "Shutter 1/15" went to "Shutter 1 - 2 frames."

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Roger. On page 2-21, we have change from "Shutter 1/15 - 2 frames," to "Shutter 1 - 2 frames."

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay. That's item 2?

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Affirmative; that's item 2. [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay; that was "Shutter 1" vice "1/15."

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Affirmative. And on page 2-22, item 2, change "Shutter 1/15 - 2 frames" to "Shutter 1/2 - 2 frames." [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Copy; 1/2.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: On page 2-23, item 4, "20 seconds - 2 frames" to "2 seconds - 2 frames." [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay, copy.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: And on page 2-24, under "At T start plus 7 minutes", change "20 seconds - 2 frames" to "1/15 seconds - 2 frames."

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Can you say where that is again?

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Okay, it's on page 2-24, and it's under the heading that says "At T start plus 7 minutes."

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay. What was it? I'm sorry; I got all of that, but didn't get what it was.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Okay. It's change "20 seconds - 2 frames" to "1/15 second - 2 frames."

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay, copy.

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Okay, on page 2-36 [pause.] about 1/3 of the way down the page where it says "Configure lens f/8,1/30, 4" - We want to change that to "Configure lens 1/2 stop between f/5.6 and f/8, 1/15, and 4." [Long pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay, that's ½ stop between f/5.6 and f/8, and the shutter to 1/15?

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: That's affirmative, Charlie. [Pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: And on that same page, about 2/3 of the way down, under the step that says "Electrophoresis Power, On," we want to add a note to hold for instructions from MSFN. [Long pause.]

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay, understand hold for instructions from MSFN. Is that before the Power, On?

a16_0064301.speaker: Peterson
a16_0064301.text: Negative. That's immediately after Power, On, and I won't read you that instruction now; we'll wait until we get to that in the Flight Plan.

a16_0064301.speaker: Duke
a16_0064301.text: Okay.

a16_0065021.speaker: Peterson
a16_0065021.text: Right, John. This Verb 49 that's at seven hours in the Flight Plan, we want you to hold up on that so we can have a look at the attitude.

a16_0065622.speaker: Peterson
a16_0065622.text: 16, Houston. We had a temporary very short loss of comm there. Did you do anything on board to return comm?

a16_0065622.speaker: Young
a16_0065622.text: We haven't touched a thing there, Pete.

a16_0065622.speaker: Peterson
a16_0065622.text: Roger. Everything seems okay now. It was very brief, but we lost it for a while.

a16_0065622.speaker: Young
a16_0065622.text: Okay. We didn't even hear any squelch or any of that noise...

a16_0065622.speaker: Young
a16_0065622.text: ...like you usually get when you lose comm.

a16_0070300.speaker: Duke
a16_0070300.text: Okay, Houston. You have Omni Delta.

a16_0071629.speaker: Duke
a16_0071629.text: And that's the only surface we have that looks like that, and we continually get particles shredding off from that.

a16_0071629.speaker: Peterson
a16_0071629.text: Charlie, we're having a little trouble figuring out which surface you're talking about. Can you give us a little better description of what you were talking about there?

a16_0071629.speaker: Duke
a16_0071629.text: Okay. We - On the plus-X side - on Ken's side - the surface right below the docking target that runs parallel to the plus-X of the LM and right into the top of the APS propellant tank.

a16_0071629.speaker: Peterson
a16_0071629.text: Okay. Right below the docking target, and it runs right into the top of the APS propellant tank.

a16_0071629.speaker: Duke
a16_0071629.text: That's affirm, and that axis is almost - ia almost parallel to the plus-X axis.

a16_0071629.speaker: Duke
a16_0071629.text: And whatever that surface was, is all shredded, and - as I said, like shredded wheat, and it's continually spitting particles off.

a16_0071629.speaker: Peterson
a16_0071629.text: Okay. In other words, you can see it deteriorating now, huh?

a16_0071629.speaker: Duke
a16_0071629.text: That's affirm. It's spitting particles off - about five or ten a second.

a16_0071629.speaker: Peterson
a16_0071629.text: Okay, 16. We got it, and we're going to take a look at it now.

a16_0071629.speaker: Peterson
a16_0071629.text: And, 16, we've got a correction to the G&C checklist, page 9-4, whenever you get ready to copy.

a16_0071629.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0071629.text: This is Apollo Control at 7 hours, 22 minutes. At the present time the LM Systems Engineer is going through the handbook to try to pinpoint the precise location that Charlie Duke was describing on the Lunar Module. Charlie said that they appeared to have found the surface that is giving off the particles that were reported earlier. He said that they can see about five to ten particles per second, shredding off a surface where the coating appears to have degraded, as best we can tell from his description. He says the surface looks like shredded wheat and it's spitting off particles. At the pres

a16_0072200.speaker: Peterson
a16_0072200.text: Roger. On panel 382, the Primary Glycol Evap(orator) Inlet Temp valve, we want to adjust it slowly to get that temp to about - to Evap Out to about 45 degrees.

a16_0072200.speaker: Peterson
a16_0072200.text: And you'll have to go toward them.

a16_0072200.speaker: Young
a16_0072200.text: You want us to go into manual and set the evaporator - you want to set the temperature - to 45 with the manual while we have the waterboiler going, is that correct?

a16_0072200.speaker: Peterson
a16_0072200.text: 16, you can go ahead and set it. Move it toward Max, and you'll have to go pretty slow with it.

a16_0072200.speaker: Young
a16_0072200.text: Okay. Can we stand by just a minute?

a16_0072200.speaker: Young
a16_0072200.text: Thanks. I got to open up that panel and all that stuff.

a16_0073441.speaker: Peterson
a16_0073441.text: 16, Houston. Can you go Manual on the High Gain?

a16_0073441.speaker: Peterson
a16_0073441.text: Charlie, it was in Reacq, and it was drifting around. [LPause.]

a16_0073441.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0073441.text: This is Apollo Control at 7 hours, 38 minutes. We appear to have pinned down on the diagrams a little more precisely where the thermal skins that Charlie Duke described shredded and spitting off particles are located. Perhaps the best way to describe this would be to ask you to visualize the Lunar Module as if you were looking at the Ascent Stage of the LM facing the porch - the front porch - or the part of the LM that looks like a face, and visualize the docking target, which is on an upper surface slightly behind and to the left of the commander's position. The panels extend downward from th

a16_0073800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0073800.text: Houston, is that close enough on that evap temp? Looks like I can't hit 45; I can hit 43 or about 46 or 7. [Pause.]

a16_0074626.speaker: MCC
a16_0074626.text: Okay, we are considering the possibility of taking a look ...

a16_0074626.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0074626.text: I'm not sure. The picture that we're trying to paint here is like you had painted something and then all the paint started to peel off. It's all stripping up like an old, real - like you painted an old barn and had the paint come off of it. And it's all standing out. You can see it - kind of released from the surface. And I don't know if that fits your picture or not.

a16_0074626.speaker: Peterson
a16_0074626.text: Roger. I think that's the way we understand it. Are you still getting those particles coming off pretty fast there now?

a16_0074626.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0074626.text: They're not coming off as fast as they were a while back, but maybe that's our Sun angle has changed, making them not quite as obvious.

a16_0074626.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0074626.text: That last description came from Ken Mattingly. Ken describing the - the appearance of that thermal skin as looking like an old barn in need of paint, where the paint or whatever the coating is, is lifting up and kinda peeling back.

a16_0074626.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0074626.text: And our LM systems engineer, who has done a bit more digging into the nature of the skins at that portion - at that point on the LM, describes it as an aluminum skin about 4 mils [0.1 millimetre] thick and painted. So that would - would go along with the crew's description of paint peeling. This, as we mentioned previously, the skins at various portions on the LM differ. Typically they would be the Mylar type of material, but there are also skins that are aluminum.

a16_0075131.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075131.text: Hey, Don. We're ready to - looks like we ought to be deactivating the primary evaporator. Did you want us to keep it on for a while or something?

a16_0075131.speaker: Peterson
a16_0075131.text: Stand by a minute. Negative, Ken. You can go ahead and shut her down.

a16_0075347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075347.text: Okay, Don. We got the evaporator secured.

a16_0075624.speaker: Peterson
a16_0075624.text: 16, Houston. On that Panel 382, in the manual control, the mixing valve, looks like we are going to have to play with that valve every time we change attitudes. So you might just leave that panel open or closed, for the two of the fasteners, so it will be easy to get into.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Okay. Looks like that's going to be fun around the Moon, doesn't it?

a16_0075624.speaker: Peterson
a16_0075624.text: Rog. We are looking at that right now, Ken.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: All right.

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Supposed to. Trying to get it in the (garble)

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: I'll get the second one up. How about a - an antenna angle of minus 85 and Yaw 153. Minus 85 -

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: Okay.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Yaw 153. Is it (garble)?

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: No. We got comm.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Oh! I bet that's what I heard.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: (Sigh) Well, I can see I was wrong.

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: In what?

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: The only guys that don't understand space flight are not the flight planners (laughter).

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Yeah. The food people.

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: I'll say.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: [Laughter.] They is other folks in that operation that don't understand. Well, let's see. I guess you got to cut this thing first.

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Yeah.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Scissors, John?

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Yeah. I got them.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: The old head full again?

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Yeah. Really smarts. You want me to unloosen this down here? Put it right up here.

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: Okay, I've got one of those bags back here that you can (garble) orange juice in.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Put that in the trash?

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: The trash bag's done untied itself.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Yeah, I ain't sure that's going to be an acceptable solution. I'm afraid I - Maybe we ought to use one of those TSBs after all. Let's try that.

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Avoid that one.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Oh, here come de Sun. Order in the courtroom; here come de Sun.

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: What did you get, Ken?

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: I got one. Okay, didn't realize you had one that was empty. Excuse me.

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: (Garble).

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: That is obviously not one of the bags for me to fill up and use for my other water stuff.

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Thank you, sir.

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Guess we ought to tape the things. I don't know. Tape up the bags because if we throw them down in there loose, pretty soon we'll have so much stuff down in there we won't know what to do with them. What do you think?

a16_0075624.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0075624.text: Yeah. We ought to be able to make some kind of a lid to go over it. Tape a lid down or something? Don't you think?

a16_0075624.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0075624.text: This is Apollo Control at 8 hours, 5 minutes. Apollo 16, at the present time, is maneuvering to the proper attitude for calibrating the optics system that'll be used in a series of star sightings. These are taken routinely on the trans-Earth and translunar legs of the flight. The information is fed into the onboard guidance system and is used to update the onboard system's knowledge of so called state vector - the trajectory - that the vehicle is currently on. This data is then compared with the - with the ground figures. And as the spacecraft maneuvers into this attitude, we lose lock with th

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Sock me a pill. Is there any left?

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: Yeah. Here's one right here.

a16_0075624.speaker: Duke
a16_0075624.text: Here you go.

a16_0075624.speaker: Young
a16_0075624.text: Okay. What do you have to do? Take it loose, or just...

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Yeah. I guess. Take the paper off that thing?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: No, no. No. Just stick it in the way it is.

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Hmm; I took the paper off.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: No, you don't need to. You pull it out - just pull the thing out and stuff it in there and it'll be fine.

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: I'm thinking about sticking a window shade in over here.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Yeah, you ought to have a little Sun. Well, it's really - ought to end up in here.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Yeah. If you want to put that window shade in, it wouldn't be a - it would be an appropriate thing, I bet. Looks like we're about ready to - Well, we're on Omni B now (garble). maybe the high gain would pick up. Well, it's fluctuating back and forth.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Just leave those bags out until we get a whole mess of them, and then we'll put them all in the cupboard and stuff them in there.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: That is going to be a bright bear out there, isn't it?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: We're getting ready to go - do a P23. I - You trying to close it or open it?

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: I was trying to close it.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: I'll get it. Boy, that comm is less than optimum.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Okay, now. Looks like I'd better heat up that evaporator, huh?

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: That's falling off a little bit. See?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Okay. I hate to - (garble) if I put some Velcro on it - a little bit.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Okay, Ken. You want to get down here and P23 your way through this thing?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Yes, sir. I'll be down there in just a second.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Being a big manual guy, huh?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Okay, here's two (garble). You're gonna have to screw in this thing, it looks like. It's really bad that we have to play with that thing. Can you - did we stop it in the attitude?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Okay. Do you think we're gonna - you gonna be able to work on that food business while I'm down here?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: I can probably work on this thing by myself, if I - Darned umbilicals.

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Hey, Ken, could you put that in the jettison bag?

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Oh, yeah. I was gonna - you got to wrap up this tape hanging down.

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Well, you need - Here's two more that came off.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Oh, wait - wait a minute, I'll get some tape to hold it together.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: You've got - What? Is yours off over there, too, Charlie?

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Oh, just - is it just over here underneath the docking ring that it's off?

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Yeah. Well, I can see the edge of that panel over here and over there.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Yeah, it looks like some more of that gray stuff come off of it.

a16_0080500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0080500.text: 16, Houston. Give us a High Gain Antenna.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: Okay, John. I'm gonna see what I can do here. Let me see if I can find me a G&C Checklist, P23.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: By golly, it's right there. Some things we do pretty well, I guess. This program has figured out how to find stars.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Well, I'll tell you something, you guys. There may be a star out there, but I sure don't see it.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Oh, yeah, it's right in the middle of the sextant.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Sure ain't in the telescope, Ken.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0080500.text: But there's just - that telescope is just useless unless you want to look at the quad or the radar.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Yeah, but what star is it?

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Do you see anything leaking out over there, Charlie? Any particles coming off the LM?

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: You see any particles coming off?

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: There are a few out there.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: Whatever it is, it's up in the -

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: It looks like if it had been a leak - in a propellant tank, it would have - it would have - blown up. Blown the whole thing out of there instead of shredded it.

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Well, whatever it was coming out of there with full force, so it must have had some pressure behind it.

a16_0080500.speaker: Young
a16_0080500.text: It's still coming out of there?

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Does that look like particles to you, vapor - vapor or just a...

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: Is that what vapor particles look like?

a16_0080500.speaker: Duke
a16_0080500.text: We've got a pretty low signal here. Let me go to the High Gain [Antenna]. Okay. You got - put it in ReAcq. There you go.

a16_0080500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0080500.text: This is Apollo Control at 8 hours, 15 minutes. The LM systems engineer has...

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: Houston, this is 16. Over.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger, 16. You're loud and clear [garble].

a16_0081500.speaker: MCC
a16_0081500.text: Okay. Roger. Let's get in there and take a look at it.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger. I think we're going to have to get into the LM and take a look at the RCS system's gauges to tell what's going on here. Do you notice any color or anything more descriptive about that stream?

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: Well, my opinion of the color is that it's a brownish material.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger.

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: And it has long - some of it has long flakes to it, and - but some of it is just little particles.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: 16, we'd like to have a look at the LM/CM Delta-P before you start pressurizing it also.

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: Okay. Do you want us to stop the P23 and go in there right now? Over.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: That's affirmative, 16. [Pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Duke
a16_0081500.text: Do you want us to stay in this attitude, Pete? [Long pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Duke
a16_0081500.text: And, Pete, you might be thinking about what kind of a - where you want us to enter the checklist.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger. I understand. We'll get back to you in a minute, Charlie.

a16_0081500.speaker: Duke
a16_0081500.text: Rog. The Activation Checklist, I guess.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Duke
a16_0081500.text: We're up to 0.6 on the LM/CM Delta-P, which is what it was, due to our cabin pressure difference. I don't think it has leaked any.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger. We copied; and, Charlie, we want to start on page 2-1 in the Activation Checklist.

a16_0081500.speaker: Duke
a16_0081500.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0081500.text: Pete, how about if I go to a wider dead band?

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: We want to - first of all, Ken, we want to roll to 91 degrees, and that'll boresight the aft Omni toward the Earth, and also we want the Waste Stowage Vent valve, Closed.

a16_0081500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0081500.text: Okay, now. Take it a little slower here. You wanted to do a maneuver to a roll of 90. Is that affirm?

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: A roll of 91.

a16_0081500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0081500.text: Okay. You want the other attitudes to be the same as I have now?

a16_0081500.speaker: MCC
a16_0081500.text: That's affirmative.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: That's affirmative, 16. [Pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0081500.text: Okay, I have 91.00. And we'll use the present pitch and the present yaw, and you get the Waste Vent, Closed.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger. The Waste Stowage Vent valve, Closed.

a16_0081500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0081500.text: We've done that. Okay, we're starting our maneuver now.

a16_0081500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0081500.text: This is Apollo Control at 8 hours, 20 minutes and the import of that last series of exchanges with the crew, as we are instructing them to enter the Lunar Module. We'll power it up sufficiently to look at some of the systems and try to determine from the data what, if anything, out of the ordinary is happening. The additional description that we got a minute or so ago was from John Young. John described the particles coming off as, on further evaluation, to have the appearence of some sort of a vent. He said that the material appeared to have a brownish color, and appeared to be propelled away

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: Okay, Houston. We're opening the LM pressurization valve now.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger.

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: [Garble.] [Pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Young
a16_0081500.text: How's it look? [Long pause.]

a16_0081500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0081500.text: It appears at this point that the crew is opening the LM hatch. Total time probably would be around 15 minutes from the time they started the procedures of getting into the LM until they're in and began turning on some of the switches so that we can look at - look at those Lunar Module systems.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Ken, we're also thinking about trying to get some TV looks at that venting condition, if it doesn't interfere with the activation.

a16_0081500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0081500.text: Okay. I'll tell you what. We've stowed the camera aftwards. Wait until they get in the LM, and then I'll go down and get that thing out. I can do that while they're going in there.

a16_0081500.speaker: Peterson
a16_0081500.text: Roger; understand.

a16_0081500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0081500.text: Both Charlie Duke and John Young will be entering the Lunar Module. They're in the process of doing that right now. And at the present time, Apollo 16 is 41,141 nautical miles [76,193 kilometres] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 9,298 feet per second [2,834 m/s]. We have asked Ken Mattingly to get out the TV camera and we expect that once Duke and Young are in the Lunar Module, cleared out of the way so he can get to the area where it is stowed, that he will get it out and we would expect to get a TV picture hopefully showing the area of the Lunar Module where the particles are coming from.

a16_0082949.speaker: Peterson
a16_0082949.text: 16, can you Zero the Optics? All you have to do is hit the switch. It's within 10 degrees.

a16_0082949.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0082949.text: This is Apollo Control at 8 hours, 33 minutes and that last transmission from Charlie Duke indicates to us that Duke and Young are in the Lunar Module going through the Activation Checklist at the present time, getting the LM partially powered up so that we can get a look at some of the critical systems, and the pertinent systems in this case, in an attempt to determine what if anything out of the ordinary is happening. And, as we mentioned previously, we do expect to get some television from the Command Module. Ken - Ken Mattingly advised us that he would be getting the camera unstowed and in

a16_0082949.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0082949.text: Okay, Don. They're on their way into the LM now. And Charlie's in there and John's joining him, and I'll work on getting the TV camera out.

a16_0082949.speaker: Young
a16_0082949.text: Okay, Houston. We're going onto LM Power right now.

a16_0082949.speaker: Young
a16_0082949.text: Okay. We've gone to Reset and Off.

a16_0082949.speaker: Peterson
a16_0082949.text: And Ken, when you get the camera set up, ready to operate, we'll go to Medium beamwidth on the High Gain Antenna.

a16_0082949.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0082949.text: Okay, and it's going to be a few minutes.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Okay, Houston. You should have the data now, according to our checklist.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: We're down through Step 7 on Page 2, 3.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0083902.text: We have the data from the Lunar Module now. We're looking at it and we'll get an evaluation.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Houston, can we bring up our RCS quad A and B meter, take a look at them?

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: 16, I guess we don't need the - the heaters. We're looking at all the data now. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Okay, We didn't say "heater"; we said "meter." [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger; stand by. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: I guess we can take your word for it, that's for sure.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Rog. We're - we're looking at all the data now, I think.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Okay, fine. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Duke
a16_0083902.text: Our - our System A RCS meter, which is not powered, is at 92 percent quantity, and B is a little over 100.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger, Ken. Understand.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0083902.text: Our LM Systems Engineer's report, from the data we've seen so far, that everything looks good. Looks normal, no evidence of any propellant leaks or pressura - pressurization leaks and we're standing by now for television from the Command Module.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: 16, based on what we're looking at, the System A pressures look okay. We don't see any problem with the tanks. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Okay, but it - it sure is something strange coming out of that. I never saw anything like that on LM-4. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: I mean, I'm not normally a rabble-rouser; it - this just ain't - something - something funny going on here. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Would you like to have the TV with the wide beam outside? [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Yeah, Ken, I guess so. We haven't had a picture yet here.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: No, I was waiting for you. You said something about some High Gain things you wanted to do, and I hadn't done any of those things yet.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Oh, we wanted to go to Medium beamwidth on the High Gain, and we're ready for the pictures anytime. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Well, if it looks okay to you, Houston, do you want us to fire this thing down now? [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Stand by just a minute. We're - we're going to take one last long look here, but everything looks okay so far.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: That's great. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: 16, on Panel 16 in the LM, under the PQGS display breaker, and let's push that one in and we'll take a look at quantities. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay, Don. And do you have a picture now? I'm not going to zoom in until - until you've got a good picture.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Okay. That one's in, and the quantities went to 100 each. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Looks like the TV's in standby, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Does that help?

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0083902.text: And we are getting a black and white picture.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Quantities look good, 16.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: That's affirmative; they're both 100.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Okay, 16. We are ready to - to back out. You pull that breaker?

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: ...back down. We'll pull the breaker first and back down. Thank you.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay, Don. Can you see any picture yet? [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Negative, Ken.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0083902.text: At the present time we're looking at the picture in black and white waiting for the color converter to lock up.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Ken, we're still not getting a picture.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay: I'm in Transmit. [Pause.] Got a good monitor this time. I got FM transmitter. I got the S-Band Aux to TV.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Okay, Ken. I think the TV's okay. I think the problem is here. It will take us about another minute, I guess. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay, I'll stand by. I'm gonna have to show you the part we're looking at.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay. Can you see the docking target, and do you have a grid? I've got a grid on my monitor that you should be able to correlate with. Do you have that available? If you don't, I'll just try to talk you in towards the frame.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Stand by just a minute. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Ah, Ken. I guess we don't have a grid right now.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay. Right now, the center of my picture is just about on the center of the docking target. Does that look like your picture?

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Affirmative.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay, I'm gonna move the camera up and there is a flat surface which is now just about on the center of my picture, and it's pointing away from me. This is the one we can see it peeling off of.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: I'm gonna try to zoom in on it, and I'll see the best monitor picture I can get, and you may have to talk me in on some of the other.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Okay.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Houston. Our Activation Checklist says leave the Cabin Repress breaker, Closed, but we found it Open. How do you want to play that one?

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Stand by me a minute, John. [Pause.] Okay, John. We want that one Opened on the way out.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Open on the way out. Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: That's real good, Ken. Hold it right there.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: I can't hang on [laughter] I'm stuck here; I'll get back with you.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Okay. You had a real good picture there, where you were. [Pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Yeah, Ken. We're seeing the stuff coming off of there now. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Ken, while we are looking at it, we're trying to get a hack on whether or not there are any jets firing across that surface that would correlate with those particles coming off.

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Yes, sir; there are. My A thruster seems to bang on it quite a bit. And we put the LM Power back to CSM at 08:52; I'd say about 15 seconds ago.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger, copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: Don, are you guys through with this picture, or do you need something else?

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Hang on just a minute, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Ken, we see occasional particles come off, but we're not seeing a stream. Do you see any streaming like John was talking about earlier?

a16_0083902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0083902.text: No, sir. Well, maybe - Well, you know, we're in an entirely different Sun angle now, and it's not clear to me that we don't see different things. Maybe John can take this thing and show you where it was coming from, because I didn't see it.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Roger.

a16_0083902.speaker: Young
a16_0083902.text: Yeah, I'd be glad to - I'd be only too happy to point it out.

a16_0083902.speaker: Peterson
a16_0083902.text: Rog.

a16_0085634.speaker: Young
a16_0085634.text: Okay, Houston. On our monitor, the place where the stuff was coming out is at A and 1 on the grid. Over.

a16_0085634.speaker: Peterson
a16_0085634.text: Understand; it's A-1?

a16_0085634.speaker: Young
a16_0085634.text: Roger. It's the upper right-hand corner of that square, A-1.

a16_0085634.speaker: Peterson
a16_0085634.text: Roger.

a16_0085634.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0085634.text: Okay. He's going to put it right in the middle of the picture.

a16_0085634.speaker: Peterson
a16_0085634.text: Okay. Let's try that.

a16_0085634.speaker: Young
a16_0085634.text: And, Pete, I'll tell you, that Cabin Pressure Relief valve - I mean the Cabin Repress valve in the LM will really give you apoplexy, boy!

a16_0085634.speaker: Peterson
a16_0085634.text: Roger.

a16_0085634.speaker: Young
a16_0085634.text: Okay. It's right in the middle.

a16_0085634.speaker: Peterson
a16_0085634.text: Okay, understand. It's right in the middle of the picture now. Okay. I think we're seeing some of it now.

a16_0085634.speaker: Young
a16_0085634.text: No. No, you aren't, Pete. What you're seeing is particles that are floating off, drifting particles.

a16_0085634.speaker: Peterson
a16_0085634.text: Okay. Can you see the venting now?

a16_0085634.speaker: Duke
a16_0085634.text: No, it stopped. When we maneuvered it out of the Sun, it stopped peeling off.
