a16_0335831.text: You're loud and clear, Orion.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, we're coming down Downvoice Backup and - on a hot mike, and you're loud and clear to us. Over.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Roger.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, how does the Low Bit Rate look to you, Pete?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Looks good, Orion.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, I'm going up Bit Rate to High. [Pause.] Okay, how do you read now, Pete?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, you're 5 by also. You got High Bit Rate. [Pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Looks good, John.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, we're going Biomed, Right. How do you read now, Pete?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay. [Pause.] You want to - we can - we're down to step 5 on page 1-118 - 1-18. Do you want to look at the High Bit Rate some more? [Long pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Young
a16_0335831.text: Telemetry is Lo; perform voice and low-bit-rate check.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay. Do you want to - we can - we're down to step - 5 on page 1-118 - 1-18. Do you want to look at the bit rates some more?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Negative. We don't want to look at it anymore.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: You do not. Rog. We're going to Low Bit Rate. [Pause.] Okay, the book says "Perform voice and low bit rate check with MSFN." How do you read?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Same-o. [Long pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, Houston. Our Function - S-Band Function is in Voice now. How do you read?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Low Bit Rate looks good.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Houston, how do you read with the Function in Voice? Over.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: You're loud and clear.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, you're 5 by and Low Bit Rate. How does it look? [Pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Young
a16_0335831.text: How do you...

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, we're going to High Bit Rate. And we'll do the same thing with you - voice check and high bit rate check. [Long pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Houston, how do you read - now? Over.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: You're loud and clear.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, give me a short count please, Pete.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Rog; you're very good. Okay, we're going to - Bit Rate is going Low, and we're going S-Band Range to Ranging.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Roger.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, how do you read now? Over.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, how is the ranging check going?

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Ranging looks good, Orion. [Long pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, Houston, our ED bats are both Go at 37 volts and the sequence camera works.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Roger; copy. [Pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: And John's OPS was 5800 and mine was 6000. Over.

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Roger.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay. As far as we're concerned, the comm is just super, and we're ready to go on to page 1-20 and deactivate, if you guys are. [Pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Stand by 1, Orion. [Long pause.]

a16_0335831.speaker: Peterson
a16_0335831.text: Okay, Orion. You can deactivate.

a16_0335831.speaker: Duke
a16_0335831.text: Okay, deactivating.

a16_0335831.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0335831.text: Our LM controllers here in the Control Center report that all of the LM systems look good based on the telemetry data that we're receiving. Apollo 16 at this time is 128,138 nautical miles [237,313 km] from Earth traveling at a speed of 4,221 feet per second [1,287 m/s]. And Charlie Duke reported that he and Young are now ready to begin deactivating the Lunar Module in preparation for going back into the Command Module and closing up the hatch.

a16_0341922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0341922.text: Okay, Houston. Casper has the LM power back at 34:19.

a16_0341922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0341922.text: Hey, Don, if anyone wonders what I'm doing with 52, I just wanted to use Auto Optics to point at Jupiter.

a16_0341922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0341922.text: I'm not gonna take any marks.

a16_0341922.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0341922.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 35 minutes. John Young and Charlie Duke are apparently still in the Lunar Module, Orion. They're not scheduled to complete the close out and return to the Command Module for another 25 or 30 minutes. During the time that they had the LM partially powered up and we had telemetry data, all of the systems onboard looked normal, everything looked very good.

a16_0344320.speaker: Peterson
a16_0344320.text: Casper, we've got the LOI-minus-5 flyby PAD whenever you're ready to copy.

a16_0344320.speaker: Duke
a16_0344320.text: We got Casper's keeper over in the Lunar Module taking a peek, and we'll be closing it out and we'll get it in a minute.

a16_0344744.speaker: Duke
a16_0344744.text: Pete, you - really get to be a real believer in the heating capacity of the Sun. In the Lunar Module here, the commander's window is in direct sunlight, and it's almost too hot to touch it. My window's in the shade, and it's got fro - it's frosted over.

a16_0344744.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0344744.text: That was Charlie Duke reporting. He and John Young are going to close out the Lunar Module now, and get back in the Command Module. Duke also gave one observation of the effects of the Sun on heating the vehicle. He reported that the commander's window, which was in direct sunlight, was almost too hot to touch, and the Lunar Module Pilot's window on the other side of the vehicle was frosted over. That window, of course, not in the sunlight. And at this time Apollo 16 is 129,776 nautical miles [240,345 km] from Earth. The speed down now to 4,170 feet per second [1,271 m/s].

a16_0350353.speaker: Young
a16_0350353.text: Houston, the hatch is closed; the drogue is installed; the probe's installed; the hatch is installed on our side; the LM Tunnel Vent valve is in LM/CM Delta-P; the tunnel lights are off. Is it okay if we go to PTC; set up PTC now, or do y'all want to wait until 34?

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: 16, you can go ahead and do the PTC.

a16_0350353.speaker: Young
a16_0350353.text: Okay.

a16_0350353.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0350353.text: That was John Young reporting the probe and drogue assembly reinstalled in the LM tunnel, the hatch back in place, and a bit of what sounded like blue grass banjo music drifting in from the background. Apparently the music being played on the crew's onboard tape recorder. That report that Young and Duke had completed their activities aboard the Lunar Module and we're back in the Command Module with everything in the LM buttoned up. It came at about 35 hours, 5 minutes. We got the report at 33 hours, 14 minutes that Charlie Duke had entered the Lunar Module so...

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: 16, in addition to the LOI flyby PAD, we've got some cryo tank configuration changes for you. [Pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Young
a16_0350353.text: Okay. If you can hold up for a second on that.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Roger.

a16_0350353.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0350353.text: The total time that Young and Duke were in the Lunar Module Orion was about 1 hour, 45 to 1 hour, 50 minutes and we don't have a precise time on their reentry to the Command Module, but that would be a fairly good estimate.

a16_0350353.speaker: Young
a16_0350353.text: Hey, Houston; 16. You can go ahead with the cryo tank reconfiguration.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Okay. On the cryo tanks, we want H 2 Tanks 1 and 2 Heaters, Auto; and Tank 3 Fan, Off. Oxygen Tanks 1 and 2 Heaters, Off; Tank 3 Heater, Auto. [Pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Young
a16_0350353.text: Okay. Rog. Configuration now: H 2 Heaters 1 and 2, Auto; O 2 Heaters 1 and 2, Off; 3, we're in Auto. That's as we had it. H 2 Fans 1 and 2, Off; and 3, Off.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Duke
a16_0350353.text: Okay. [Garble] Houston, you can go ahead with the LOI-minus-5 PAD.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Okay, LOI minus 5 flyby, SPS/G&N; 66603; plus 1.24, minus 0.12; 069:28:26.27; plus 0039.8, minus 0118.9, plus 0422.9; 210, 193, 346; NA; H P is plus 0020.4; 0441.1; 1:07, 0436.5; sextant star 14, 124.8, 17.4; the next three lines are not applicable. Latitude, minus 23.03, minus 165.00; 1100.9, 36207; 142:23:42. Set stars Sirius and Rigel, 219, 166, 313. Ullage, none. Other: number 1, burn SPS docked; 2, PAD based on PTC REFSMMAT; 3, LM weight, 36287. [Long pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Duke
a16_0350353.text: Rog, Pete. LOI minus 5 flyby, SPS/G&N; 66603; plus 1.24, minus 0.12; 069:28:26.27; plus 0039. I missed Delta-V Y , Delta-V Z is plus 0422.9; 210, 193, 346; HA is NA; plus 0020.4; 4411, 107, 0436.5; 14, 124.8, 174; NA; latitude minus 23.03, minus 165.00; 1100.9; 362.07; 142:23:42. Sirius and Rigel; 219, 166, 313. Ullage is none. Notes are: 1, burn SPS docked; PTC REFSMMAT; LM weight, 36287, which is 30 pounds heavier than we had this morning.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Roger. We'll take a look at that, and the Delta-V Y is minus 0118.9. [Pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Duke
a16_0350353.text: Minus. Rog; minus 0118.9.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: That's affirmative. Gol.

a16_0350353.speaker: Duke
a16_0350353.text: Is that because we took the film over there? [Pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Say again, Charlie.

a16_0350353.speaker: Duke
a16_0350353.text: I said we took all that film over there, maybe that's the 30 pounds.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Affirmative, that's where it came from. [Long pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: And, 16, we still have this note to go on the Sun wheel. [Pause.]

a16_0350353.speaker: Young
a16_0350353.text: Stand by.

a16_0350353.speaker: Peterson
a16_0350353.text: Omni Charlie, 16.

a16_0354516.speaker: Peterson
a16_0354516.text: 16, your rates are okay, any time you want to go into PTC.

a16_0355026.speaker: Peterson
a16_0355026.text: 16, Omni Bravo, and then we'll take care of the antennas.

a16_0355026.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0355026.text: This is Apollo Control. 36 hours now into flight of Apollo 16. And the spacecraft is now in it's Passive Thermal Control mode. Rotating at the rate of three revolutions per hour. The crew is scheduled to be eating dinner and following that, they have a scheduled eight-hour rest period. Apollo 16 at the present time is 135,2 - rather 132,595 nautical miles [245,566 km] from Earth. And traveling at a speed of 4,084 feet per second [1,245 m/s].

a16_0355026.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0355026.text: This is Apollo Control, 37 hours now into the flight of Apollo 16, flight that has settled down into a steady, and at the moment, rather quiet routine. This is typically a quiet time of lunar missions with the crew using the time that they have available to review checklists and procedures that they'll be following during the very busy days ahead on the lunar surface and in orbit around the Moon. Also at the present time the crew is scheduled to be in the midst of a - an eat period, having diner prior to retiring for an eight-hour rest period. We've been watching all of the spacecraft systems

a16_0365646.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0365646.text: Hank, it's not clear, I'm gonna be able to find any stars with no closer alignment than I have on this thing. Looks like I'm gonna have to get a - a coarser alignment by using some big objects like Earth or something like that.

a16_0371909.speaker: Peterson
a16_0371909.text: Okay, just a last few words here. We don't have anything for you except one note to Ken. Earlier you asked about whether or not the PAD we read you contained the correct bias for the EMS; we told you it did, and we've looked at it a little more now, and actually it turns out it did not. The bias on that one was less than a foot per second, I guess. In the future, we will include that bias in the PAD.

a16_0371909.speaker: Peterson
a16_0371909.text: Rog and we're ready to copy any time you can give us the onboard read-outs and get into the Flight Plan here at about 37. [Pause.]

a16_0371909.speaker: Young
a16_0371909.text: Okay, Houston. Bat C is 37; Pyro Bat A is 37; Pyro Bat B, 37. [Long pause.]

a16_0371909.speaker: Young
a16_0371909.text: RCS A is readinkg 87; RCS B, 92; RCS C, 93; RCS D, 96. Is that what you wanted, the quantity of the RCS?

a16_0371909.speaker: Peterson
a16_0371909.text: That's affirmative. And we copied 37, 37, 37, 87, 92, 93, and 96. [Pause.]

a16_0371909.speaker: Young
a16_0371909.text: That's - that's correct, and Main Bus - Bus A is reading 29 plus volts. [Long pause.]

a16_0371909.speaker: Peterson
a16_0371909.text: Ken, for your information, the PTC looks beautiful; in fact, it was so good, it took some of us quite a while to realize you were in a PTC. [Pause.]

a16_0371909.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0371909.text: Gee, and my attitude hold looks a lot like that too.

a16_0371909.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0371909.text: All in the technique for the way you hit Proceed.

a16_0373702.speaker: Young
a16_0373702.text: Houston, let me read you this cryo tank configuration, and you tell me if that's what you want for the sleep period.

a16_0373702.speaker: Peterson
a16_0373702.text: Go ahead, 16; we're ready to copy the cryo configurations.

a16_0373702.speaker: Young
a16_0373702.text: Okay. H 2 Heaters are - 1 and 2 are in Auto. O 2 Heaters 1 and 2 are Off, 3 is in Auto. H 2 Fan 1 - 1 and 2 are Off, and 3 is in Auto. [Long pause.]

a16_0373702.speaker: Peterson
a16_0373702.text: 16, the H 2 tank 3 Fan should be Off. [Pause.]

a16_0373702.speaker: Young
a16_0373702.text: And, Houston, for your information, the LM/CM Delta-P gauge has not moved since we equalized the two vehicles.

a16_0373702.speaker: Peterson
a16_0373702.text: And, 16, would you verify optics power, Off? [Pause.]

a16_0373702.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0373702.text: No, sir; we aren't ready to turn it off just yet.

a16_0375015.speaker: Young
a16_0375015.text: Are you ready for a Verb 74? [Pause.]

a16_0375015.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0375015.text: Roger. We're standing by. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a16_0375015.speaker: Young
a16_0375015.text: What do you do on the graveyard shift, Hank?

a16_0375015.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0375015.text: Oh, that's lots of fun. Get to watch y'all snooze. [Pause.]

a16_0375015.speaker: Young
a16_0375015.text: Okay. Direct O 2 's on, the cabin's coming up now.

a16_0375518.speaker: Young
a16_0375518.text: Okay, Houston. Direct O 2 is off.

a16_0375518.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0375518.text: This is Apollo Control at 38 hours into the flight of Apollo 16. And we expect the crew will be beginning their scheduled eight-hour rest period shortly. Here in Mission Control, we're in the process of a shift handover. Flight Director Gene Kranz and his White Team of flight controllers are coming on now to replace the Orange Team headed by Flight Director Pete Frank. The Capsule Communicator on this shift will be astronaut Hank Hartsfield replacing astronaut Don Peterson in that position. And at the present time Apollo 16 is 137,239 [254,167 km] nautical miles from Earth. Traveling at a spee

a16_0375518.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0375518.text: This is Apollo Control. I would like to correct one portion of our last announcement on the shift handover. The Flight Director on this shift will be Phil Shaffer rather than Gene Kranz. At 38 hours, 4 minutes this is Apollo Control Houston.

a16_0380400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0380400.text: Casper, Houston. If you're transmitting, you're way down in the mud. I can't read you. [Pause.]

a16_0380400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0380400.text: Okay, Ken, go ahead with your film status, and we're looking at that stowing the optics. [Pause.]

a16_0380400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0380400.text: Okay, the magazine OO reads 26, magazine November November is either 33 or 34, depending on how you look at it. We finished up the 16-millimeter mag on Alpha Alpha by taking some pictures of the - part of the LM paint that we think is shredding. Magazine Oscar and November have been used just for the targeted pictures - no extras. And I guess that's - We didn't take any other original pictures today except for the AA frames on the LM. Tomorrow we'll try to get some interior photography. [Pause.]

a16_0380400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0380400.text: Okay. Copy 26 frames on Oscar Oscar. The November November report we got last night was 33 frames. You didn't use any of it today?

a16_0380400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0380400.text: Well, just for that UV. So whatever it was last night, it must be one more.

a16_0380400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0380400.text: And, Ken, it's okay to stow the optics.

a16_0380400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0380400.text: Okay, Henry, thank you. And I'd like to go ahead and take the voice comm down before I turn the optics power off. I wanted to try to take one last look and see if I can pick up one of the planets as we turn around, and I'd like to go ahead and knock off the voice. [Long pause.]

a16_0380400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0380400.text: Okay, Ken, get the voice down. Have a good night.

a16_0380400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0380400.text: Okay, Henry. See you in the morning. Good night, sir.

a16_0381955.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0381955.text: Okay, I'm not sure what just happened. I just saw - down looking at the optics and all of a sudden I saw a warning light and I got a No Attitude and a Gimbal Lock light. And my - my ball seems to, in fact - it looks like the platform may be frozen. [Pause.] Although we're still - still in PTC here.

a16_0381955.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0381955.text: Okay, we're seeing some telemetry. We saw something about the time you come on the line there.

a16_0381955.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0381955.text: Okay. And it shows the CDUs down there in Noun 20 as being gimbal locked. [Long pause.]

a16_0381955.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0381955.text: Stand by a little bit, Ken. We're taking a look at the telemetry.

a16_0381955.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0381955.text: This is Apollo Control at 38 hours, 22 minutes. That was Ken Mattingly reporting what appears to be a problem in the Guidance and Navigation System on the Command Module. His voice report came almost simultaneous with a warning light on the Guidance Officer's console and reports from the Guidance Officer to the Flight Director, Phil Shaffer, here in the Control Center. Mattingly's description of the problem was that they had a warning light in the Command Module indicating No Attitude. The gimbal platform frozen - we have an indication here of gimbal lock and coarse align and we're looking at

a16_0382519.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0382519.text: Ken, just so we can make sure we got it straight down here, could you run through again what you were doing, and then the sequence of events?

a16_0382519.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0382519.text: Okay, Hank, I'm not real sure when this happened. I was trying to see if I couldn't pick up one of the planets in the optics, and I was using P52. And I had gone in and I was calling Option 3 and then putting in planet vectors out of the Flight Plan and I tried - I thought I was going to catch, I guess it was Saturn and it looked like I had just missed it. And I was driving around just kind of looking around to see what I could see in the sky and waiting to try and pick up Jupiter. And somewhere in there, I guess I came down to zero the optics or do something, and then I looked down and saw I

a16_0382519.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0382519.text: I can't, think of any combination of DSKY inputs - I was trying to think if I could have made some combination of DSKY inputs that might have - Had I gotten in almost the right input that I could have caused the problem, but I don't see where I was using any verbs or nouns that could have done this. [Pause.]

a16_0382519.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0382519.text: Okay, you got a Gimbal Lock and No Att. Did you get an ISS warning?

a16_0382519.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0382519.text: Okay, You got a Gimbal Lock...

a16_0382519.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0382519.text: And the - the Noun 20s were approximately correct for both pitch and roll, although the - the middle gimbal angle was completely out to lunch.

a16_0383244.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383244.text: I'd like for you to think about the effects of having me go ahead and do a Verb 41 Noun 20 to match up with the SCS. That thing's been drifting a good bit, but, in this case, maybe I can get it close enough to have a starting point to try and pick up some things. I'd been looking in the - had been looking in the telescope just before this all happened, and there's so much of this - so many of these little particles out there that chances of recognizing a star pattern are extremely dubious, I'd like to try. And maybe we can work on something like the Earth, maybe the Sun, or something like that

a16_0383244.speaker: MCC [not CapCom]
a16_0383244.text: Okay. Do you want to stand by on this Verb 41 Noun 20 until you get your gimbal Lock removed? Okay, CapCom tell him we're working up - Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0383244.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383244.text: Casper, Houston. We'd like you to hold up on the Verb 41 Noun 20. We're working on a procedure to try to get rid of the gimbal lock.

a16_0383244.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383244.text: Okay. Did you have any data coming down at the time this all happened, or were you in the blind?

a16_0383244.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383244.text: Rog. We had good high bit rate data, and they're poring over that now.

a16_0383244.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383244.text: Okay. I'll sit tight then. Thank you.

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Casper, Houston.

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Go ahead.

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Okay. We want to try to get the platform inertial again, and what we'd like for you to do is a Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter, Enter, Verb 40 Enter. [Pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter. Then you want me to put plus Enter into that register. [Pause.] Okay, that got rid of the Gimbal Lock light. Now you'd like for me to do a Verb 41?

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Verb 40 Enter.

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Okay. Verb 40 Enter. [Long pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Okay. Our data shows the platform's inertial now, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Rog. And it appears that way from here, too. [Long pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Okay. Ken, you can go ahead now with you Verb 41 Noun 20. [Pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Okay. This will be a coarse align to the GDC angles, is that correct?

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Hey, Ken, hold up on that Verb 41 just a second.

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Wilco. I'll go ahead and load it but won't enter.

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Okay there. Guidance has got a little thing they're looking at and talking to people in the back room, little discussion going on here.

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Okay. I won't do a thing, then. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0383644.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 38 hours, 40 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. What you've been listening to is Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly talking back and forth with Mission Control. We had an earlier indication that the IMU platform appeared to be in a gimbal lock. Mission...

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Casper, Houston. Are the GDC ball and the IMU ball completely out of sync? [Long pause.]

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: Well, actually, they're not that far out. They're like ten degrees in outer gimbal and let's see the - I guess the middle gimbal is off by about two degrees, the inner gimbal no more than three, lots closer to two degrees.

a16_0383644.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0383644.text: Roger. Copy.

a16_0383644.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0383644.text: ...that close.

a16_0383644.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0383644.text: Mission Control has been going through a series of procedures with Ken Mattingly to alleviate the gimbal lock situation. Presently the platform is inertial. We'll stand by as series of Verbs and Nouns have been passed up to the spacecraft Casper. We're at 38 hours, 42 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 now 138,786 nautical miles [257,032 km] away from Earth. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0384745.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0384745.text: Okay, I think we got the agreed-on procedure here - is to go ahead with the Verb 41 Noun 20. That's procedure - in the G&C Checklist - 7-1. And reset the REFSMMAT - REFSMMAT flag and press on through that.

a16_0384745.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0384745.text: Okay. I guess, based on our drifts, I'm not sure that's any better, but I guess that's no worse, so I'll just go to that one, then.

a16_0384745.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0384745.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 38 hours, 54 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly now going through a series of Verbs and Nouns, trying to align the IMU platform to the Gyro Display Coupler. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 139,243 nautical miles [257,878 km] away from the Earth. Continuing to monitor, this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0385400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0385400.text: Okay. Are those particles out there giving you a lot of trouble?

a16_0385400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0385400.text: That's all there is. They're just everywhere. [Pause.]

a16_0385400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0385400.text: When you combine them with the limited area that you have to look in because of the LM reflections, you find the telescope's very unsatisfying. [Long pause.]

a16_0385400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0385400.text: Casper, Houston. Why don't you go ahead and try then, with the - the Sun and the Moon? You've got a filter for the Sun, right?

a16_0385400.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0385400.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 38 hours, 59 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. That was Ken Mattingly reporting difficulty sighting stars through the optics - those desired stars for alignment because of the vast number of particles. The update from CapCom Hank Hartsfield indicated a go-ahead to try the alignment using the larger objects in this case, the Sun and the Moon - for alignment. We show Casper's onboard computer program in Program 52 - this is the platform alignment program - as Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly presses on with his procedures. Apollo 16 is now 139,452 nautical miles [25

a16_0385400.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0385400.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 39 hours, 3 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Guidance reports that Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly is half way through his platform alignment. He has performed his mark on the Sun. He is now proceeding with his mark on the Moon. We're at 39 hours, 4 minutes; continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Houston, Casper.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Go ahead.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. I used the Earth and the Sun, and I got four balls 7, which I think is gonna be a significant improvement. I'd like to go ahead and see what those torquing angles turn out to be.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Roger. We concur.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. That looks about right for the amount that I had to correct for. It's - it's kind of hard to mark on the Earth because you have to guess where the - where the - the terminator really ought to be. [Long pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: and do you have those torquing angles?

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Roger, Ken. Go ahead and torque.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control Houston, 39 hours, 9 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We now show Apollo 16 at 139,788 nautical miles [258,887 km] away from Earth. Command Module [Pilot] Ken Mattingly, on using the Earth and Sun for platform alignment through the optics, reports significant improvement over his earlier attempt in the star sightings. We'll continue to monitor conversations between Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly and CapCom Hank Hartsfield here in Mission Control.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay, Henry. If you have those angles, I'll torque these. [Long pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Ken, what was your Noun 05?

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Four balls one.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Roger.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. I'll torque these at - on the minute, 11.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay, clear to torque.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 39 hours, 11 minutes. Mattingly doing a second P52 platform alignment this time using two stars for sighting and in this way the fine tuning - his earlier improvement if possible with the Sun and - Mo - Earth and Sun as reference. We're at 39 hours, 12 minutes Ground Elapsed Time and we now show Apollo 16 at an altitude of 139,907 nautical miles [259,108 km] away from the Earth.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. It looks like we're pretty much on target now, and I don't see any reason to torque these again - unless you particularly want to. [Pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay; we concur, Ken. Don't torque those. And we want to check a few switches. They're working on now getting a switch checklist, and then we're going to let you get some rest and smoke the data over during the night and have it stored for you in the morning.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. Can you give me any - Can you give me any cursory ideas of that, just the same - if there's any possibility I entered something inadvertently? Or that take too long to sort all that out?

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay. The preliminary look here - We think it's a hardware problem, Ken. Some sort of a transient problem...

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: ...and when we get the data in here, we'll be able to tell a little more about it.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. Guess I'm sorry to hear that.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: They - they don't think at this point that it's anything that you did, and it appears to be a transient problem, but we won't know until we take a look at it.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. Let me give you one other little tidbit that now seems to be somewhat more of - of interest than it was before, and that's that when I take this Optics Zero to Zero, the area around the shaft peapack [?] makes a lot of - a lot more noise than the one in the trunnion. It seems to me that it's making more noise now than it used to. When I say used to, when we first started out - when we first started out, they were very, very quiet and you couldn't even hear them running. And now they're getting noisier. And that may be typical, but it's just one more thing that - I guess we'll throw out a

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay. That only occurs when you're zeroing?

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.] Well, actually, Hank, I just tried it in Manual. It occurs when - the noise occurs whenever I'm in an extremely high rate. You know, like using high in a max shaft rate.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Roger; copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay, Ken. We'd like to check some switches up on Panel 1. [Pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Stand by a second. [Long pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. Go ahead, Hank.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay, we'd like to check position in FDAI Scale.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: The Scale is in 5/1.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay, Select.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Select is in 1 [garble], the Source is in Attitude Set, and the Attitude Set is in GDC.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay. That's what we wanted to know. Thank you. [Pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay, I think I'll go ahead and get some sleep then. Got any notes from [garble] yet?

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay, stand by one sec. [Long pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay, Ken. We don't have anything else [garble]. [Long pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Casper, Houston.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Go ahead.

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Okay. You caught us on the antenna switch. We don't have anything else for you. We'll look the data over, and try and get some word up to you tomorrow. It looks like to us now that you can get a full eight hours sleep. [Pause.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay. [Laughter.] Thank you.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0390649.text: Okay, Hank. How about - how about making it a duller shift?

a16_0390649.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0390649.text: Rog. [Laughter.]

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 39 hours, 30 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 140,597 nautical miles [260,386 km] away from the Earth. As you heard, Ken Mattingly has now been given the go ahead to start his sleep period. This being the case, we will go over and recount the activities that have just taken place regarding the Guidance and Navigation System. It - this activity was spurred when Mattingly saw a Gimbal Lock warning light on board and a No Attitude light on board. This was verified by the Mission Control team here on the ground. The first

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 40 hours, 35 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We presently show Apollo 16 at an altitude of 142,978 nautical miles [264,795 km], this from Earth, and traveling at a speed of 3,779 feet per second [1,152 m/s]. The crew is now sleeping after a flurry of activity related to a - the Guidance and Navigation system. Ken Mattingly, it appears, went to sleep at 40 hours GET, dozed off to sleep. At an earlier time - 38 hours, 22 minutes GET - the Command Module had a Gimbal Lock warning and a No Attitude light on board. This was verified by the flight controllers here in

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 41 hours, 30 minutes into the mission. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 144,956 nautical miles [268,548 km] away from Earth. Velocity now reads 3,724 feet per second [1,135 m/s]. We've had no conversation with the crew of Apollo 16 since our last report. The crew is presently in their rest period. Our Flight Director for this shift is Phil Shaffer. It is his first stint in the role of Flight Director. Until this mission, Shaffer has worked as Flight Dynamics Officer in the Mission Control Center. He's one of the new Flight Directors designated for

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 42 hours, 30 minutes since lift-off. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 147,092 nautical miles [272,414 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now shows 3,665 feet per second [1,117 m/s]. We've had no conversation with the crew of Apollo 16 over the past hour. There are some five minutes remaining on the sleep period. We're at 42 hours, 30 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 42 hours, 32 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We have a correction to our last report. A sleepy commentator reported five minutes remaining on the sleep period for the Apollo 16 crew. That should have been stated five hours remaining. I repeat, five hours remaining of crew sleep. We're at 42 hours, 32 minutes into the mission and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 43 hours, 30 minutes into the flight of Apollo 16. We now show the Apollo 16 spacecraft at a distance of 149,191 nautical miles [276,302 km] away from the Earth and now traveling at a speed of 3,608 feet per second [1,100 m/s]. At the present time, the crew of Apollo 16 is asleep. Also, at the present time, the Mission Control Center here in Houston is receiving periodic data from the Apollo 16 spacecraft due to an inability to switch antennas by ground command. At present, here in Mission Control, we're receiving 11 minutes of data, and seven and a half minu

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 44 hours, 30 minutes into the mission. We presently show Apollo 16 at a distance of 151,216 nautical miles [280,052 km] away from the Earth. Velocity now reads 5,353 [should be 3,553] feet per second [1,083 m/s]. Flight Director Phil Shaffer has decided to update the crew wakeup time by one hour. This being one hour earlier because of the work day. This one hour will allow spare time for troubleshooting associated with the antenna switching. There will be a change of shift briefing at 9:30 am in the News Center Briefing Room. Participants will include Flight

a16_0390649.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0390649.text: This is Apollo Control; 45 hours, 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time in the mission of Apollo 16. Spacecraft, at the present time, is 153,107 nautical miles [283,554 km] out from Earth. Velocity, 3,504 feet per second [1,068 m/s]. Here in the Mission Control Center, the Gold Team of flight controllers taking over headed up by Gerry Griffin, from the off-going shift of flight controllers headed up by a new Flight Director named Phil Shaffer. Phil Shaffer's press conference will take place in the News Center Auditorium, the Houston News Center, in about 10 minutes. The crew of Apollo 16 will be wake

a16_0455911.speaker: Young
a16_0455911.text: Houston, how do you read Apollo 16? Over.

a16_0455911.speaker: Peterson
a16_0455911.text: 16, you're loud and clear. How me?

a16_0455911.speaker: Young
a16_0455911.text: I read you the same. Good morning to you.

a16_0455911.speaker: Peterson
a16_0455911.text: How are you doing this morning?

a16_0455911.speaker: Young
a16_0455911.text: I guess that sort of depends on what y'all can say about the old platform.

a16_0460100.speaker: Young
a16_0460100.text: Now you're talking. That's the best news I've heard today, so far. [Pause.]

a16_0460100.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460100.text: Okay. And, John, we've had some problems here getting commands up to the bird - real-time commands. And we've got a command test we want to run. And - we'll be standing by. As soon as you can get ready, let us know and we'll get into it.

a16_0460100.speaker: Young
a16_0460100.text: Okay. We've got some seat swap to do and we'll let you know.

a16_0460100.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0460100.text: This is Apollo Control; 46 hours, 1 minute Ground Elapsed Time, and about 30 minutes early, the - or ahead of the scheduled wakeup time, the crew has called Mission Control. We have a few seconds of accumulated tape caught unawares. Then we will rejoin the conversation with the crew of Apollo 16 live. Let's roll the tape.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: 16, in the situation we're in now, we've only got one omni that we can read, and we can't command. So we're only getting about 11 minutes of low-bit rate data out of every 18 while you're in PTC. It's possible - we might lose you; if so, just stand by and we'll pick you up again.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Okay. We're ready for that command test, Pete.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Okay, Charlie. We're gonna go one step at a time. First thing we want to do is Up Telemetry, Command Reset and then Normal. [Pause.]

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Okay. I can give you - You want a Command Reset and then Normal?

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Charlie, we want the Up Telemetry Command switch to Reset and then Normal.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Roger. It's Reset, Normal.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Okay, Charlie. Stand by. We're gonna try some command. [Long pause.]

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Okay, Charlie. That apparently didn't work. We're going on in. But we want to cycle the Up Telemetry switch, Off, for three seconds and then back to Normal.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Rog. In work.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Okay, you're back to Normal.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Okay. We're trying commands now, Charlie. Stand by.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: Okay, Charlie. That apparently cleared it up.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Okay.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: And, Charlie, we've got commands again. We'll handle the antenna and the bit rate for you now.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Okay, fine.

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: To repeat an old phrase, Charlie, we had a lot of people down here turning blue on this - until that - until that last little situation got cured there.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Was that that IMU problem?

a16_0460236.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460236.text: No, the - the - comm problem.

a16_0460236.speaker: Duke
a16_0460236.text: Well, you could put Fendell in the backup mode and just put him up on top of the building.

a16_0460601.speaker: Peterson
a16_0460601.text: We may have to put him up there anyway, Charlie.

a16_0461850.speaker: Peterson
a16_0461850.text: 16, Houston. I've got about three - a couple, three updates to the Flight Plan. Whenever you're - it's convenient for you, we'll read them up.

a16_0463608.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0463608.text: Don, you about ready for a little status report?

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Okay, Ken. We're all set. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper, Houston. How do you read me? [No answer.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper, Houston. How do you read me? [No answer.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper, Houston. Do you read? [Long pause.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper we read you loud and clear. Do you read me? [No answer.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper, Houston. How do you read? [Long pause.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: Casper, we read you. Do you read us? [Long pause.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0463608.text: Houston, if you're reading Casper, we're transmitting in the blind. We have a signal strength on the meter of about 60 percent. We're not receiving you and, based on your comment about the antennas, we'll wait about five minutes and then try again before we change the configuration. [Long pause.]

a16_0463608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0463608.text: 16, you're loud and clear. Do you read Houston? [No answer.]

a16_0464608.speaker: Young
a16_0464608.text: Rog. We lost you there for a while there, Don.

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: Roger. You're loud and clear now. You read me okay?

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: Roger. You were loud and clear all the time. Apparently, you just lost us. [Long pause.]

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: And, 16, the comm problem may have been on the ground. We'll try to find out and let you know in a minute. [Long pause.]

a16_0464608.speaker: Young
a16_0464608.text: The background tone at the - the background noise that the system is making right now is a little different than it was making before, if that would help you figure out what the problem was. It's almost like it wasn't up-linking, maybe.

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: Stand by just a minute, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: Okay, Casper, go ahead with your status report. [Pause.]

a16_0464608.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0464608.text: Okay. I'm using that famous old trick on how to get someone to talk to you, but every time I pick up a juice bag and get halfway down, why it seems like we are able to establish comm. So I'll start with the Commander's list and I'll go through and I'll skip the menus since they're on separate pages and come back to them. So let's start with A-1: 22035; Alpha 3: 7, good; Alpha 4: none; Alpha 5: 19, 15, 18; Alpha 6: 6, 5, 6, and 3. That's a total of four. Going to Bravo. [Pause.] Bravo 1: 15035; 6: good - that's on Bravo 3. Bravo 4: none; Bravo 5: 10, 30, 25; Bravo 6: 2, 2, and 5. [Pause.] Charl

a16_0464608.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0464608.text: Okay. For John, and that's day 2, Meal B, scratch the bread and peanut butter. [Pause.] On Meal C, scratch the frankfurters; add an orange drink. [Long pause.]

a16_0464608.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0464608.text: Okay, on Bravo 2. Are you still there, Don?

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: Affirmative; we're getting a lot of background noise. 16, hold off a minute...

a16_0464608.speaker: Peterson
a16_0464608.text: ... we'll switch omnis [garble]. [Pause.] Hold off a minute, 16; we'll switch omnis.

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: Okay, starting on - Where did you copy last?

a16_0465419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0465419.text: Okay, we got John, day 2, Meal Charlie complete, and we're ready, I guess, for Bravo.

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: Okay, Bravo 2. On Meal A, you can scratch sausage patties and - orange juice - and fruit cocktail. [Long pause.]

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: On Bravo, that's Meal B, you can scratch turkey and gravy, vanilla pudding, bread, peanut butter. Meal C, you can scratch the chocolate pudding. [Long pause.]

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: On meal A, scratch the sausage patties. Meal B, you can scratch the bread and peanut butter. Meal C, you can delete two of the frankfurters and scratch the chocolate pudding.

a16_0465419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0465419.text: Okay, Casper, we copied all that. [Pause.]

a16_0465419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0465419.text: Okay, Ken. We'll - we'll think on that a little. And also, I've got a note on the Nikon camera light meter here in connection with the ALFMED photography. [Pause.]

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: Okay, stand by another second. [Long pause.]

a16_0465419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0465419.text: Ken, you don't really need to copy much, I think. If you've got the camera handy there where you can look at it, I can give it to you in a few words.

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: You know one of the things we need in this program is some octopuses.

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: Okay, Don, I don't have the camera out, but how about just reading to me whatever it is you want to say, and I'll write it down here.

a16_0465419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0465419.text: Okay. It's not - it's probably not worth writing down except maybe a little note to remind you the - the camera was observed to hang up in the Battery Check position full down, when you hit the camera light meter On, Check. And what we want you to do is - the little button on top of the camera there has a while band around the base of it - they want to make sure that white line is visible on the light meter switch button. If it's not visible, you can take your fingernail and catch the top of that button and pull out on it until the white line is visible. And then, verify that the meter is oper

a16_0465419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0465419.text: Rog. We'll make sure it works before we use it.

a16_0465419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0465419.text: Okay, Ken. That's all I've got on that one.

a16_0470244.speaker: Duke
a16_0470244.text: Rog. Flash, with a hot report here. Pass on to the chefs that the grits were delicious.

a16_0470244.speaker: Peterson
a16_0470244.text: Say again, Charlie. I didn't copy that.

a16_0470244.speaker: Duke
a16_0470244.text: I say, pass on to the chef that the grits were delicious.

a16_0470244.speaker: Peterson
a16_0470244.text: Roger; will do. [Pause.] And for Ken's information, the status report that we just got was excellent as far as format, readability, and everything. The - Doc said he really appreciates it.

a16_0470244.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0470244.text: This is Apollo Control; 47 hours and 27 minutes into the mission of Apollo 16. Crew awake now, presumably conducting either the ALFMED experiment or beyond the eat period. As a matter of fact, part of their first activities after wakeup was the status report, which [lists] all the parts not eaten; in other words, negative reporting on the meals for the three crewmen are read down. Also the problems with the commanding through the omni antennas have cleared themselves up, with the crew cycling a switch Off, back On again, which cleared the logic in the switching circuit. And everything is prope

a16_0473332.speaker: Duke
a16_0473332.text: Houston, 16. Over.

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Go ahead.

a16_0473332.speaker: Duke
a16_0473332.text: Okay, Pete, I'm up on biomed. How does it look?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Okay, the biomed data looks good.

a16_0473332.speaker: Duke
a16_0473332.text: Okay, thank you. [Pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: You can tell Charlie's still breathing, huh?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: It looks that way. [Pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: We've been suspecting it up here all along.

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Houston, based on the burn yesterday, is the data you gave us for the SPS burn card still going to hold for LOI?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Stand by a minute.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: And the other question is, does it look like we're going to have another midcourse, and which one and how much is it?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Okay, we'll get back to you in a minute.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Okay, thank you, Pete. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Okay, 16. On the burn card, we will probably have to do some more updating, we'll get to that tomorrow. And on the midcourses, Midcourse 4, right now, is - looks like it's less than one foot per second. If it gets much bigger, we'll probably do it. But we'll advise you. [Pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Houston, 16. You're breaking up badly. How do you read us? Over. [Pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0473332.text: [Garble], Pete, you probably read us loud and clear in the [garble] mode [garble]. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0473332.text: Go ahead, Houston, [garble]. Say again on all [garble] on the burn card. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Okay, 16, if you read. We probably will have to do some updating on that - on that PAD. And we'll let you know on that and we'll update it tomorrow. And on the Midcourse 4 - Midcourse 4 is looking pretty small, less than one foot per second now. If it gets larger, we'll probably go ahead and do it, but we'll keep you advised on it. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Houston, your up-link keeps fading in and out on you. [Pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Roger, 16, We're switching on you.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: [Garble] fading [garble]. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Houston, 16. Do you read us now?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: I read you loud and clear. Do you read me?

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: And I read you same. You faded cut on your last transmission again.

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Okay, hang on a minute until the comm clears up a little bit and then I'll come back to you.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: Okay, 16. Let's try it again. On that updating the PAD, we'll get that to you tomorrow. And right now, Midcourse 4 looks very small, less than one foot per second. If it gets larger, we will probably do it, but we'll keep you advised on that.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Outstanding. [Long pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Just to review that SPS pressure system - as near as I can make out, it's purely - we don't actually have a Delta-P. It's just - of about more than five psi. What we do have is a gauge difference. Is that not correct?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: That's affirmative, John. There's a - there's a chamber in there - a reference chamber that's supposed to be at atmospheric pressure. It has apparently vented to a vacuum condition, which brings in about - about a 14.7-psi bias. Then there's a 5-psi meter bias on top of that.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Okay, so actually, the two meters, as we look at them now, are actually balanced. Is that not correct?

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: I believe that's correct.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0473332.speaker: Peterson
a16_0473332.text: John, the actual pressures on both meters - the actual pressures are the same, although the meters are reading differently.

a16_0473332.speaker: Young
a16_0473332.text: Okay, we got the message.

a16_0474401.speaker: Duke
a16_0474401.text: Houston, 16. Will we need to charge Battery B, just looking ahead in the Flight Plan a little bit?

a16_0474401.speaker: Peterson
a16_0474401.text: Okay, Charlie, you can go ahead and start charging the battery now. [Pause.]

a16_0474731.speaker: Duke
a16_0474731.text: Okay, Pete, Bat B is on charge now.

a16_0480025.speaker: Duke
a16_0480025.text: Okay, Pete. We got you. Finally had time to look out the window and you're just coming into view again and just as pretty as ever.

a16_0480025.speaker: Peterson
a16_0480025.text: Very nice. What you looking at right now? [Pause.]

a16_0480025.speaker: Peterson
a16_0480025.text: Can you tell what part of the Earth?

a16_0480025.speaker: Duke
a16_0480025.text: We've got a half-Earth. Say again?

a16_0480025.speaker: Peterson
a16_0480025.text: Can you yell what part of the Earth you're looking at?

a16_0480025.speaker: Duke
a16_0480025.text: Well, we got a half-Earth, and we see a land mass - see the North Pole - the north polar cap with two big swirls coming out off of it to the southwest. I can see the subsolar point very distinctly. It's a big white dot in the center towards the LM, away from the terminator. And there's a big land mass that's visible in the center. And can't really make out exactly what it is. It's clear of clouds, though. It's the only place that's fairly clear.

a16_0480025.speaker: Peterson
a16_0480025.text: Okay, we show you directly over North Africa. [Pause.] And that's just about the terminator. [Pause.]

a16_0480025.speaker: Duke
a16_0480025.text: Okay, you got North Africa at the terminator?

a16_0480025.speaker: Duke
a16_0480025.text: Okay, that's what it is, then, looking at it, yeah. It's - it's Africa. [Pause.] Looks like a good storm system up in the Atlantic Ocean and above the subsolar point.

a16_0480025.speaker: Duke
a16_0480025.text: The blue color and the white of the clouds and the blue of the ocean, Dick. Things just stayed pretty constant as we move out - still really a spectacular sight.

a16_0480622.speaker: Young
a16_0480622.text: What do they think of this PTC down there in the trenches?

a16_0480622.speaker: Young
a16_0480622.text: It really does look good. I don't know who to congratulate, Ken or the computer. [Long pause.]

a16_0480622.speaker: Peterson
a16_0480622.text: I guess we'll give Ken credit for that one. [Pause.]

a16_0480622.speaker: Peterson
a16_0480622.text: 16, let us know what you think about the number of light flashes and whether or not it's feasible to try the ALFMED.

a16_0480622.speaker: Young
a16_0480622.text: Okay. That's in work right now.

a16_0480622.speaker: Young
a16_0480622.text: That is, if you can work on seeing flashes.

a16_0481949.speaker: Peterson
a16_0481949.text: Okay. And you think you are seeing enough light flashes to make it valid?

a16_0481949.speaker: Young
a16_0481949.text: They haven't gotten around to doing that yet, but we're working on it.

a16_0481949.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0481949.text: Don, Charlie saw some this morning when he got up. And so we're going to put the ALFMED on Charlie. And we will not turn it on until we start to see some flashes, and if we don't see any, we'll just terminate it. We'll wait some reasonable time. We'll talk it over with you. We'll tell you when we're ready to go through it. That's our present plan.

a16_0481949.speaker: Peterson
a16_0481949.text: Okay, Ken, we'll be standing by. And, Ken, while I'm talking to you, we've got a little more information on this platform problem and its a fairly big mouthful, so, sometime when you get a chance where you can copy some information, give me a call.

a16_0481949.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0481949.text: Okay. It looks like it'll be a couple of hours.

a16_0481949.speaker: Peterson
a16_0481949.text: Roger. We don't want you to get into another P52 before we have time to talk about it.a16_0480622

a16_0481949.speaker: Duke
a16_0481949.text: Pete, (clear's throat) a little background on these flashes [garble].

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: 16, Houston. We missed your comments on the light flashes. You'd started to give them to us, and you were blocked out by noise.

a16_0482402.speaker: Duke
a16_0482402.text: Rog, Pete. I was just telling you - the first night - during the first sleep period, whatever that was GET, I saw numerous light flashes before going to sleep, probably a - as freq - as high as three or four a minute. The next morning, they were not as numerous as that, and then last night still not as numerous. This morning, I was perhaps seeing maybe one every couple of minutes or so. If that frequency repeats itself during this test, is that good enough to go ahead?

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: Stand by one, Charlie. [Long pause.]

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: Okay, Charlie. If you see one every minute or so, that's enough to go ahead.

a16_0482402.speaker: Duke
a16_0482402.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: Affirmative. Call us when you're ready.

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: And, 16. At 48:30 in the Flight Plan, there's a line that says "Synchronize mission timer to CMC clock," and it is not required.

a16_0482402.speaker: Duke
a16_0482402.text: Okay.

a16_0482402.speaker: Young
a16_0482402.text: Oh, that's great. Thank you.

a16_0482402.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0482402.text: Hey, Don, is our comm gonna be good enough the way we're going here now for you to get the marks or are we gonna - can we count on recording them on board too?

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: You better record on board as well.

a16_0482402.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0482402.text: Okay. You'll start the tape recorder, is that affirmative ?

a16_0482402.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0482402.text: Or you want us to do that?

a16_0482402.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0482402.text: Okay. We'll do that; thank you. [Pause.]

a16_0482402.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0482402.text: Okay, if at any time, the voice quality goes down, our procedures, as I understand them described, will - I'll knock off or I'll take Charlie's place here, and I'll knock off the observations and go to recording. And other than that, Charlie will be doing all the things that I was going to be doing. But, if you want us to record them in pen and ink at the same time, just give us a call.

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: Roger.

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: 16, Houston. Voice check.

a16_0482402.speaker: Young
a16_0482402.text: Loud and clear there, Pete.

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: Roger. You all were so quiet, you scared us.

a16_0482402.speaker: Duke
a16_0482402.text: Okay, Pete. I just got the ALFMED on and in position, and we're gonna see if we see anything.

a16_0482402.speaker: Peterson
a16_0482402.text: Okay.

a16_0485333.speaker: Duke
a16_0485333.text: Okay. I've seen five in 15 minutes.

a16_0485333.speaker: Peterson
a16_0485333.text: Okay. Stand by a minute; we'll look at that.

a16_0485333.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0485333.text: Okay, Don. We were just about ready to call this thing off and try it another day. And then looked like Charlie was starting to see them at - at a pretty fair rate. That five in 15 minutes was like four in the last minute or two. And John has seen one; I have not seen any yet. But sounds like Charlie is gonna be able to see these and I'm gonna go ahead and take the photographs and get - get all set and wait for your answer.

a16_0485333.speaker: Peterson
a16_0485333.text: Okay. We've been advised that we do want to go ahead with the ALFMED experiment.

a16_0485333.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0485333.text: Okay. It's in work. I'll tell you when we're ready to start timing.

a16_0485333.speaker: Duke
a16_0485333.text: Okay, Pete. They seem to come in clusters. You get one or two right after - and then - then nothing for a while.

a16_0485807.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0485807.text: Hey, Don. Can you help us [garble] record our [garble] 12 [garble] 0.15, 1.2, [garble] at three feet shows Charlie in the ALFMED with his face sticking out. I'm taking a picture from the LEB looking up towards the center couch.

a16_0485807.speaker: Peterson
a16_0485807.text: 16, that was so garbled we didn't copy, so you're gonna have to say it again.

a16_0485807.speaker: Peterson
a16_0485807.text: Negative, Ken. We were in - had a lot of background noise, and we didn't get any of that.

a16_0485807.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0485807.text: Did you copy comments about the film?

a16_0485807.speaker: Peterson
a16_0485807.text: Negative; we did not. We had too much background noise. Can you say again?

a16_0485807.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0485807.text: Okay. I guess I'll write it down. I think that's faster after all.

a16_0490842.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0490842.text: Okay, Houston. We're ready to start. Could you make sure the tape recorder's running? [Long pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: Ken, it's been running awhile. We're going to rewind it, and I'll get it back to you in a minute. [Pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: In the meantime, Ken, if you've got comments we'll take them on air-to-ground. [Pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0490842.text: Does that mean you want us to go ahead and start?

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: Affirmative. [Pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0490842.text: Was that Roger or Stand by?

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: Affirmative; go ahead and start. [Long pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0490842.text: Okay, Don. We're running at 49:10.

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Mark. Okay, a bright dot in the - in my right eye in the upper - upper left center.

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Mark. Bright dot in the left eye, upper left - right center. [Long pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Mark.

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Mark. The first one was a fuzzy dot in the right eye - the left eye. The second one was a bright dot in the right eye, lower left center. [Long pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: You copying, Houston?

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: Affirmative. We're copying. [Long pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Peterson
a16_0490842.text: DSE - DSE is now running.

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Mark. Light streak - white streak in the right eye, upper center - moving from up - bottom to up - top.

a16_0490842.speaker: Duke
a16_0490842.text: Mark. Faint left - faint white dot in the left eye - extreme left.

a16_0491547.speaker: Duke
a16_0491547.text: Mark again. Same spot. That was a bright dot. [Long pause.]

a16_0491547.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0491547.text: Mark. Bright flash in upper left eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0491547.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0491547.text: This is Apollo Control. Apollo 16 crew now conducting the Apollo light flash experiment, using the blinders. The Apollo ALFMED, Apollo Light Flash in Moving Emulsion Detector, is the acronym, ALFMED. At 1:30 today, Central Standard Time, in the small briefing room in the Apollo News Center, MSC, there'll be a briefing by a panel of several scientist. The topic is "Magnetic Enigmas of the Moon". Spacecraft distance at the present time, 160,746 nautical miles [297,702 km]. Velocity 3,307 feet per second [1,008 m/s]. At 49:17, still up live air-to-ground, this is Apollo Control.

a16_0491547.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0491547.text: Mark. Flash across the bottom of right eye - white dot - from right [garble] left to right but I doubt it. [sic] [Long pause.]

a16_0491547.speaker: Duke
a16_0491547.text: Mark. Simultaneous white dots in the right eye, upper and lower center.

a16_0492005.speaker: Duke
a16_0492005.text: Mark. Right eye center. A - just a bright flash.

a16_0492005.speaker: Duke
a16_0492005.text: Mark. A bright flash in the lower center of the right eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0492005.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0492005.text: Mark. A little light dim streak in the lower right eye - lower left. [Long pause.]

a16_0492005.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0492005.text: Mark. Lower left - left eye, in the outboard, and it was a bright flash - looked like a streak - probably going from right to left.

a16_0492005.speaker: Duke
a16_0492005.text: Mark. Bright dot, upper right, outboard, right eye.

a16_0492741.speaker: Young
a16_0492741.text: Mark. Dot - bright dot in the upper right eye, center.

a16_0492741.speaker: Duke
a16_0492741.text: Okay, Houston. I've also had some very subtle things that - just very - looks like little dim flashes that I haven't been calling. They're just so subtle, I've been afraid to call them a definite mark.

a16_0492741.speaker: Peterson
a16_0492741.text: Okay, Charlie. We copied that. [Long pause.]

a16_0492741.speaker: Duke
a16_0492741.text: Mark. Upper right eye going from left to right. [Pause.]

a16_0492741.speaker: Peterson
a16_0492741.text: Okay. And, Charlie, if you see any more of the subtle marks, how about calling them and just call them a subtle mark. We'd like to record that information.

a16_0492741.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0492741.text: This is Apollo Control. The mysterious comments and singing and frequent repetition of 'hello, hello' on the Public Affairs broadcast line a few moments ago has been identified by the Network controller as a telephone company technician in Spain who inadvertently somehow got patched over onto the network line coming from the tracking station on the air/ground circuit. He has been isolated, electronically that is; and hopefully, we shouldn't have anymore of that sort of thing. Continuing with the ALFMED experiment at 49:31.

a16_0493316.speaker: Duke
a16_0493316.text: Mark. Bright dot, right eye, center, upper. [Long pause.]

a16_0493316.speaker: Duke
a16_0493316.text: [Garble] Left, right, the last one, I got the impression it was moving toward me. Why, I don't know, but it didn't - didn't [garble].

a16_0493316.speaker: Duke
a16_0493316.text: Mark. Subtle one, very subtle on the left eye, outboard, upper. [Long pause.]

a16_0493316.speaker: Young
a16_0493316.text: Mark. Flash in the lower right eye, sort of a distant lightning flash. [Long pause.]

a16_0493316.speaker: Young
a16_0493316.text: Mark. Upper center of upper right eye - bright light flash.

a16_0493958.speaker: Duke
a16_0493958.text: Mark. Faint dot, lower left eye, inboard.

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Flash, a - a light streak in the left eye, starting at the center going to the bottom right from upper - from upper - center down to right in movement.

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Bright dot, center, right eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Left eye, sort of subtle, towards inboard center, a white flash. [Long pause.]

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Subtle dot - white dot - in the inboard center of the right eye.

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark again. That was the left eye. That was the center upper, white dot, left eye; both of those were in left eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0494204.speaker: Young
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Upper right - part of right eye, white flash, small. [Long pause.]

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Subtle white flash, inboard upper right eye, inboard corner, that was.

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Same spot. A white streak.

a16_0494204.speaker: Young
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Right eye, center, white dot.

a16_0494204.speaker: Duke
a16_0494204.text: White dot, center - center right; lower of the left eye.

a16_0494204.speaker: Young
a16_0494204.text: Same here. All at the same time Charlie did. Only mine were in the lower left side and not the right.

a16_0494204.speaker: Young
a16_0494204.text: Mark. Flash across the bottom of the left eye, high speed.

a16_0494911.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0494911.text: Hey, Don. Can you tell us how we're doing on time?

a16_0494911.speaker: Peterson
a16_0494911.text: Stand by one; I'll let you know.

a16_0494911.speaker: Duke
a16_0494911.text: Don, this thing was made for about a size 6¼ or something head. It's really tight on me.

a16_0494911.speaker: Peterson
a16_0494911.text: Okay, Charlie. We'll make a note of that.

a16_0494911.speaker: Duke
a16_0494911.text: I'm not complaining, it's just a little tight.

a16_0494911.speaker: Young
a16_0494911.text: Mark. Bright flash down at the right center of the right eye. White flash [garble]. [Long pause.]

a16_0494911.speaker: Duke
a16_0494911.text: Mark. A dull fuzzy spot in the outboard center of the left eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0494911.speaker: Young
a16_0494911.text: Mark. Flash in the center of the right eye - sort of like a small flash.

a16_0494911.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0494911.text: Mark. Flash in the center of left eye, just a faint flash - much more like a dot.

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. White dot, outboard, right eye, center. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Young
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Small flash in the lower center of the right eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.text: Mark. Very tiny flash in the lower center of the left eye. [Pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Young
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Streak across the lower left of the left eye, on the inboard side. The light was going to left - from right to left. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Young
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Two little dot flashes in the upper right center of the right eye - left eye, excuse me. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Young
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Small flash in the upper right center of the [garble]. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. My last mark was the upper center right eye, little flash.

a16_0495636.speaker: Young
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Small flash in the left center of the right eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Mark. A - one - the first one was right eye, a streak going from inboard center to the upper right. Left one was a streak, pencil shaped - a pencil line, left eye from center to upper right. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Very subtle flash in the light - right eye, upper cen - upper right.

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Another subtle one just below that, center right, right eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Left eye, a streak starting in the center.

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Right eye, dot, center. The left eye was a streak starting in the center going out to the right. It increased in size as it went from right to left. [Long pause.]

a16_0495636.speaker: Duke
a16_0495636.text: Mark. Subtle dot, outboard side, center left eye.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Mark. Faint dot in the right eye, center, upper, and the inboard side is a white dot in the left eye - and the second one - was in the inboard side, center. [Long pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Dot, right eye, outboard center. [Long pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Young
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Streak in the lower left of - left eye, moving from top to bottom. [Long pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Simultaneous white dots, right and left eye. Left one was in the upper right, inboard center. Left - right one was in the inboard bottom, left. [Long pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Subtle flash in the right eye, upper inboard.

a16_0500626.speaker: Young
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Flash in the right eye, right side.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Houston, 16. How's the time? [Pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Peterson
a16_0500626.text: 16, we figure the time's about up on the ALFMED experiment. We'd like to know if the motor's stopped. [Pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0500626.text: No, it's still running.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. A streak in the lower left side of the left eye, moving down.

a16_0500626.speaker: Peterson
a16_0500626.text: Okay, Ken. Keep going until the motor stops. [Pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0500626.text: Okay.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Thin white dot upper right, inboard, left eye.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Lightning-flash-type phenomena, lower right, inboard, left eye.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. White dot, center, left eye. [Long pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. White dot, left eye, outboard, center.

a16_0500626.speaker: Young
a16_0500626.text: Mark. White dot, left eye, center. [Pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. Right eye, center, inboard, a white dot.

a16_0500626.speaker: Peterson
a16_0500626.text: Okay, Ken, we've got all the ALFMED data we need. We want you to give us a mark when you shut the motor off. [Long pause.]

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Okay, Pete.

a16_0500626.speaker: Duke
a16_0500626.text: Mark. ALFMED is off.

a16_0500626.speaker: Peterson
a16_0500626.text: Roger.

a16_0501837.speaker: Peterson
a16_0501837.text: 16, Houston. Whenever you can copy, I've got some words on the IMU problem that we had. Also some - an entry to the G&C Checklist.

a16_0501837.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0501837.text: Okay, Don. How about standing by, would you? Stand by until we clean up all the [garble].

a16_0501837.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0501837.text: You're cutting out pretty bad, Don.

a16_0502805.speaker: Peterson
a16_0502805.text: 16, the PI advises on the ALFMED experiment that we got about 70 counts, and he's very happy with the results, and he wants you to verify that the clutch is in the Stow position.

a16_0502805.speaker: Duke
a16_0502805.text: Okay, great. Those things - those things are really something, Don. There were a couple of the phenomena that I had seen previously that I didn't see today, but there were some other ones today that were different too. The phenomena - the flashes leave no afterglow and they're - they're just instantaneous. All the colors are white - were all we saw. We saw no colors at all; neither John nor I. It was - every one we saw was white.

a16_0503216.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503216.text: Okay, Don. I'm ready to copy some things now.

a16_0503216.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503216.text: Before we get into copying stuff, let me confirm what Charlie said about that clutch. Now I listened to that thing retract before, and as soon as we went to the mid-position on the clutch - why, you can hear the plates come down. And we went ahead and rapped it once, anyhow, just to be sure, but I didn't hear anything jiggle. And we cycled it to Operate and then back to Stow, and it all felt normal and the - the plate travel sounded proper.

a16_0503216.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503216.text: Okay, and I guess my only comment on ALFMED is that I think those light flashes are made by the same guy that makes the emperor's clothes.

a16_0503216.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503216.text: I think they're made by the same guy that makes the emperor's clothes.

a16_0503216.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503216.text: Hey, Don, I'm standing by to copy whatever words you got about P52s and G&N and any of those other subjects pertaining to our operation.

a16_0503216.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503216.text: Okay, Ken, I'll - we'll talk about the platform problem first, and I'm gonna back up and talk about the original data that we passed up because there are some small corrections to that.
