And then I'll - I'll try to break it down into about four shovelfuls here for you, because it's a fairly big mouthful if we try to do it all at once.

a16_0503216.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503216.text: Okay. You have some stuff that I probably should copy, huh?

a16_0503216.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503216.text: Yes, I will have some items for you to copy.

a16_0503216.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503216.text: Hold off a minute, 16. We're coming up on an omni switch. [Pause.]

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Okay, 16. How do you read now? [Pause.]

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay, is it important for me to copy those things that cause this, or are you going to give me a way to prevent it?

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Negative. You don't have to copy those. That's just background. Now we're going to talk about what you can do here in P52s and maybe subsequently in - for the LOI and for P40s. There are two ways to approach the P52. There's a - there's a quick and dirty way which is to simply go to SCS Control, because with SCS control, the TVC relay is not enabled. And, by doing that, you don't run the risk of generating this glitch. That's not the way, however, that the guys are recommending, because they have a procedure that they think will handle not only the P52, but the burn cases. And they'd like you

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay. How about running down that list of things that causes the TVC enable to change state again? Let me - let me copy those this time.

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Okay, will do. And - now - these cases are not all inclusive. These are just some examples that - that we can bring up to you. First of all, the TVC relay is enabled when you select Manual Optics. It is then subsequently disabled if you go from Manual to Auto or if you go to zero the Optics with Manual selected, or if you go with Manual - with the Manual Optics selected, if you go from P52 to P00. But these are probably not the only cases; they're probably just some examples that we know of. [Pause.]

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay.

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Another important point, Ken, is that it changes state during the TVC gimbal drive check.

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Yeah, that's what I was afraid of. Okay.

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Okay. We're going to - this next procedure that I have to read up to you is probably going to be the one that we'll use to try to get around that. And also, we'd like you to use it in the P52s because it allows us to monitor for the glitch, and at the same time prevents the glitch from bringing your platform down.

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay.

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Okay, if you're ready to copy...

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: [Garble]...

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: ...I'll read you up the procedures.

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: ...[garble] copy this or - Okay, I'll just copy this on a scratch pad, and we'll put it in the appropriate place, if that sounds reasonable.

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Roger. That sounds real good. Number 1, we want you to key Verb 48 Enter and load Noun 46, Register 1. The first digit should be loaded as a 3. The rest of the numbers can be left as they are. [Pause.]

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay, why don't you read on at about that pace, Don, and I'll just copy, and then I'll read it back to you?

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Okay, the second step is key Verb 25 Noun 07 Enter, 75 Enter, 1 Enter, 1 Enter. That sets the Average g flag, but does not turn Average g on. The combination of those two will prevent the CMC from going into coarse align. [Pause.] After you've done that, you can select P52 and use your normal alignment procedures. [Long pause.] And, when you've completed the P52 to terminate this - EMP, we'll have you key Verb 48 Enter, load Noun 4 Register 1 with its original value, whether that was 2 or 1 in the first digit. Step 2, we'll have you a key Verb 25 Noun 07 Enter, 75 Enter, 1 Enter, Enter. [Pause

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay, that - that was, in Verb 25 Noun 07, that was a 75 Enter, 1 Enter, and then zero Enter or a 1 Enter?

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Zero Enter.

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay.

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: Okay, that's the whole procedure.

a16_0503653.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0503653.text: Okay, let me look it over here for a second. At first glance, the first thing I see here looks like - do I - should I [garble]? [Pause.]

a16_0503653.speaker: Peterson
a16_0503653.text: 16, we're switching omnis; hold off a minute.

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Okay, 16. How do you read now?

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Okay. We lost comm there temporarily. You can go ahead now with the readback on that any time you're ready.

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay. Did you get my question about the Verb 46?

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Negative, but we have a caution note that says, "Do not key Verb 46 Enter while this EMP is in to prevent Sap - Saturn DAP actually coming on."

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Okay, thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay, what you would do then is - we're gonna set Saturn DAP in Average g in order to prevent coarse aligning in the event the middle gimbal picks up spurious signals. And to do this, we set Verb 48 with a Noun 46. Digit A is set to a 3, and we set the Average g flag with a Verb 25 Noun 07, address 75, bit 1, set it to a 1. Then we should call P52 normally, and if the glitch occurs, it'll be ignored. I assume from this that if the glitch occurs sometime while we're in the process of taking marks, that we get some kind of garbage out of P52, but it should be obvious. And from what you gave me o

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: That's affirmative, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay, do you - do you have some words on how - on how we handle the P40? [Pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Okay, Ken, and - in the P40 is what we're thinking about, and we haven't completely decided now, is that we'll probably use this EMP before and after the TVC gimbal check, and we may move the TVC gimbal check earlier or before the burn so that we have plenty of time to get this thing in and out. [Pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay, that sounds like a good plan.

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Okay, now I've got the last shovelful here if you're ready to copy.

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay, I've got my bucket out.

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Okay, if you should lose the platform alignment, we'll do the same thing we tried last night, a Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter, Enter, Verb 40 Enter, and then go to the checklist, G/7-1, and do the rapid IMU realign. [Long pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay, Don. If we - if we tumble the thing again, we're gonna release the platform by setting Noun 20 to - to zeros, and we do that with the Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter, Enter. Then we release the platform with the Verb 40 Enter, and then we go through page G/7-1 and get a rapid alignment to the GDC. Now that - that assumes that what happened to us was the glitch in the middle gimbal. If I understood your conversation, it's possible to have a glitch in one of the other gimbals. Is that correct?

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: That's correct. That will not, however, get you into the - into the problem that causes the platform to go into coarse align. And also, we were advised that while this EMP is in, you shouldn't have the problem with losing the platform alignment. [Pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay. If we - if we get this glitch in one of the other axes - I - and we have the controls enabled, I assume one of the things we would - we'd see would be some unusual thruster activity.

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: That's affirmative, and in that case I guess all you need...

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: [Garble] proper correction. Well, I'm trying to figure out what we'd do if we have a - say we're in attitude hold. If we have that glitch occur right now and - with our engines disabled, I don't think there would be any way I'd see it until I went to use some auto optics or something. And that - if we were in an attitude hold, it appears to me that I would see a - a DAP that appeared to be unstable in the axis that it was going for, or at least it would take off for some place other than where it is. And we would go to SCS momentarily, and the proper response would be a Verb 40, Enter, and all

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Right on. [Pause.]

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: This TVC enable that we're talking about that's used for the gimbal drive test - now that's a function only of the gimbal drive test and not a function of the setting of the trims in P40. Is that correct?

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: That's affirmative.

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Okay, so, our P40 then would be something like we would go out and we'll get a gimbal drive check to you folks early, then we'll turn the gimbals back off probably, and I'm just reiterating what I'm [garble].

a16_0504550.speaker: Peterson
a16_0504550.text: Omni switch coming up, 16. Stand by. Stand by, 16; we're switching omnis.

a16_0504550.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0504550.text: Roger.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: 16, how do you read now?

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Loud and clear, Don.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Okay. Go ahead with your question.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: I'm trying to give you my impression of what we're gonna be - the general approach to the burn - and we check out the gimbal drives and the gimbal trims, then when we come into P40 to do it for the actual burn, we would go ahead and use the SCS gimbal checks to verify all the gimbals are properly hooked up. Then we would bypass the flashing 202 with an Enter, and we'd just let the gimbals go to trim, and everything else would be done nominally. [Pause.]

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Ken, I think your general impression's right. I guess we're not yet ready to commit ourselves to a - a set of procedures. We're going to have Stu take a look at it in the simulator here, and we'll come up to you later with some detailed procedures specifically for the burn.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Rog. I understand that; I just wanted to make sure I had a general understanding in case we had to do some original thinking.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Rog. I think we concur with what you said so far. [Long pause.]

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Okay. And the other thing, that's out of curiosity - if the guys in the back rooms, after they get through getting all the important things squared away, that they could kind of think some more about their list of things that causes this enable relay to change state. I'll compile a list of those things in case we come across something later on that we hadn't thought about.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Okay, Ken, we'll do that for you. And there's one last note here, that, prior to your P52s, it'd be a good idea to align the GDC just prior to going in.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Yes, sir. I don't think I'll let that guy get very far away from us.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Okay, pencil in hand.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Okay, on Page 9-4, line 07, column A ...

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Yes, sir.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Column A, line 07, should read '76747.' Line 11 should read '77552.' Line 12, '77756'; line 13, '77307.' [Long pause.]

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Okay, I 'm on page G/9-4, reading down column A. On line 7, I replace '77426' with '76747.' On line 11, I replace '00214' with '77552.' On line 12, I replace '77714' with '77756.' Line 13, I replace '77446' with '77307.'

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: That's correct, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: And we've got, Ken, here some notes on this jet-on monitor EMP. We'd like to do a check on it at 54:25, and I can read you up the procedure for that any time you're ready to copy.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Go ahead.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: Okay, at 54:25 in the Flight Plan, we would like to add 'P20 option 5,' in the 'LM checkout attitude', Noun 78, minus 09000, minus 03000, plus 25500; Noun 79, plus 00050; Noun 70, plus 00047. We will up link the jet-on monitor loads and, when the P20 maneuver's complete, you can do a Verb 74 Enter. [Pause.] And the P20 attitude that we've selected will be the attitude that you're already in, so there is actually not a maneuver involved here.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Okay, when you say when maneuver complete, - does that mean that you would want us to maneuver to the LM checkout attitude using P20, or are you going to let us go to Verb 49 to that? And then, I'll call it up and bypass the maneuver, is that correct?

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: You can use a Verb 49 for that, Ken.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: Okay, I understand. A Verb 49, and then we'll call P20, and then you can command the same attitude I'm in.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: That's affirmative.

a16_0505419.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0505419.text: In other words, I've got the 50 18 the second time. Then you want the Verb 74, Enter.

a16_0505419.speaker: Peterson
a16_0505419.text: That's affirmative. Coming up on an omni switch, 16. Stand by.

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: 16, how do you read now?

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Loud and clear, Don.

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Okay, the only other thing is at 56 hours, that's 56:00, we want you to terminate the jet-on monitor EMP. [Long pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay, can you tell me what deadband you're gonna be setting in there?

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Okay, Ken, it'll be a one-degree deadband. [Long pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay, you're setting me in the EMP at one-degree deadband; is that affirm?

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Ken, on the Noun 70, I read you a - a plus 00047. You actually don't need that plus; that's an octal number.

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Rog. I understand.

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay, it's not clear to me - if we're going to exceed this or not; we normally would not. Do you want to try letting us drift out of the deadband and see if the monitor works?

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Negative; that's - that's not the intent, I think. They just want to get the program in and look at it. [Long pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay. Well, sometime before we get through, would you ask them if they would object to letting us see if that thing triggers the same response that we're used to?

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Okay, Ken; we'd like to think that over. We'll get back to you on that.

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay, fine. Thank you.

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Okay. Now I've still got this note that we've had since about 24 hours ago on changing the angle on that Sun wheel and if you have that out now, we can clean that up otherwise, I'll hold it a while.

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: I don't have it out, but why don't you tell me what it is. I think I know what you're talking about. It's due to the REFSMMAT angles on there being changed.

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: That's affirmative. And we [belch] inked '27 degrees' on it. We should have written in '37 degrees'. [Pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay. It turns out we're at - is inked in at 27 and it should be 37.

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.]

a16_0510324.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0510324.text: Okay, thank you. I'm glad you remembered that.

a16_0510324.speaker: Peterson
a16_0510324.text: Roger.

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: 16, terminate battery Bravo charge.

a16_0511012.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511012.text: Okay.

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: Okay, it's in work.

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: What's the probability of this - glitch happening? Is it about one in a million?

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: Stand by 1. [Long pause.]

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: Say again, Pete. You cut out.

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: 16, I guess we really don't know the answer to that. That's one of the reasons we want to get this EMP in to kind of watch for it and see if it's occurring frequently or infrequently. [Pause.] Omni switch, 16. [Long pause.]

a16_0511012.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511012.text: Okay, Don, we're going to go ahead and punch through this P52 and we'll start with our little procedure here, and you might kind of watch us through and make sure we do it right the first time.

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: Will do.

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: Okay, Houston. You're watching this, right?

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: That's affirmative. We're watching and you can go ahead.

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: Okay, and what did you say the probability was of this thing happening?

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: I think we don't know the answer to that, John. That's why we want to load this software program so we can monitor to see if that glitch is occurring frequently - or it may never occur again, we really don't know.

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: Understand.

a16_0511012.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511012.text: Okay, I've got it in. I'm going to call P52.

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0511012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511012.text: And you got the GDC aligned there?

a16_0511012.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511012.text: Oh, yeah.

a16_0511012.speaker: Young
a16_0511012.text: You better believe it.

a16_0511723.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511723.text: Houston, how do you like those angles? [Pause.]

a16_0511723.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511723.text: Do you want us to torque some that small? [Pause.]

a16_0511723.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511723.text: Okay. We'll do it at 17 minutes. [Pause.] Yeah, I guess that's 51:18, excuse me.

a16_0511723.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0511723.text: Okay, would you like for me to return it to zero with the switch in Manual this time, just to see if you get that glitch?

a16_0511723.speaker: Peterson
a16_0511723.text: And, 16, we didn't see any glitch. [Pause.] There, we're coming up on an omni switch.

a16_0512219.speaker: Peterson
a16_0512219.text: And, 16, that EMP that we loaded to protect the platform - we'll refer to it as EMP 509. [Pause.]

a16_0513032.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513032.text: 16, if you'll go Accept, we've got an uplink for you. And I've got news, if you're interested.

a16_0513032.speaker: Young
a16_0513032.text: Okay, here's P00 and Accept. And, yeah, we're interested.

a16_0513032.speaker: Young
a16_0513032.text: Charlie wants to know how (laughter) - how Consolidated Jack Pine is doing.

a16_0513032.speaker: Young
a16_0513032.text: Probably lost 3 or 4 points again yesterday.

a16_0513032.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513032.text: Rog. [Pause.] Charlie, I guess I haven't got those figures handy. We'll see what we can do. [Pause.]

a16_0513032.speaker: Duke
a16_0513032.text: If you can find out, Pete, you're a better man than I am. I've been trying to find it for 10 years.

a16_0513032.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513032.text: Okay, Charlie, And you can have your computer back, 16. [Long pause.]

a16_0513032.speaker: Young
a16_0513032.text: Yeah, that compensation you guys put up there really fixed that baby.

a16_0513742.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0513742.text: Don, we're gonna put off the Skylab [garble] until our [garble] and take the time to do it right. And we're gonna - gonna mix up [garble] snacks and try to get back [garble].

a16_0513742.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513742.text: We've got an omni switch, 16. Stand by.

a16_0513742.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0513742.text: Houston, do you read Casper? [Long pause.]

a16_0513742.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0513742.text: Yeah, I read you now. Did you copy when I commented about the Skylab food?

a16_0513742.speaker: Duke
a16_0513742.text: Pete, I'm back on the Biomed. How does it look?

a16_0513742.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513742.text: Charlie, they're just now starting to get it. They'll take a look at; I'll let you know in a minute. [Pause.]

a16_0513742.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513742.text: Okay, you want to go ahead with your comments on the Skylab food, now? [Pause.]

a16_0513742.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0513742.text: The comment I made, Don, was that, because we're behind the time line here, we - we thought we would put the Skylab food off until tonight, so we have time to do it right. And we're just going to eat snacks for now and try to get caught up a little bit.

a16_0513742.speaker: Peterson
a16_0513742.text: Okay; we concur with that, Ken.

a16_0514315.speaker: Peterson
a16_0514315.text: 16, we'd like to get the High Gain up on this next rev. You're about ten minutes away from it now. Do you think you can make that? If not, we can wait another rev.

a16_0514315.speaker: Peterson
a16_0514315.text: Okay, it's Pitch, minus 40; and Yaw, plus 90, 90. [Long pause.]

a16_0514315.speaker: Peterson
a16_0514315.text: And, Ken, you can go on; your - in your checklist there down to the MSFN cue any time, you're ready. [Long pause.]

a16_0514315.speaker: Duke
a16_0514315.text: Okay, Pete, I hit a Command Reset there. I went to the - went to High Gain too soon; and we're operating now in Omni Bravo. And give me a Mark. The High Gain just didn't seem to work; it looks like I ought to be able to get High Gain now. I'll try it.

a16_0514315.speaker: Peterson
a16_0514315.text: Negative. You won't be able to get it yet.

a16_0514315.speaker: Duke
a16_0514315.text: Okay. Okay, you're on Omni Charlie now. [Pause.]

a16_0514315.speaker: Peterson
a16_0514315.text: 16, we'll handle the omnis until we're ready to go to the High Gain, and we'll tell you when to go to High Gain at the angles we just gave you.

a16_0514315.speaker: Duke
a16_0514315.text: Okay, we're all set, and you're on Omni Charlie. Will you want me to reconfigure?

a16_0514315.speaker: Duke
a16_0514315.text: Okay, back to - back to Bravo. [Pause.] Okay, you're in Omni Bravo.

a16_0515257.speaker: Duke
a16_0515257.text: Houston, how much longer until we get the High Gain? [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: Okay, 16, you can bring up the High Gain.

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: 16, bring up the High Gain now, please. [Long pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: Okay, there you go. You got Reacq and Narrow on the High Gain.

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: 16, we're ready to proceed with the film cycling. [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Mapping Camera Image Motion is Off.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: That darn [garble] Data System is On. PCM Bit Rate, High?

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: System - S-Band Aux TV to SCI?

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay, the Mapping Camera is coming on to Standby.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay, you ready for Mapping Camera and Pan Camera operations?

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: 16, stand by. We're checking a couple of temperatures. [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay. The Mapping Camera is coming On. [Long pause.] And the Pan Camera Self Test has been hit. [Long pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Young
a16_0515504.text: I just might eat the peanut butter with no bread. How would that be?

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: And the Pan Camera Self Test is completed..

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: Well, I - I saw the [garble] around here - this morning.

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: Yeah. They're good. Want a bite?

a16_0515504.speaker: Young
a16_0515504.text: No, I just had some peaches. I had to throw mine in the jett bag [garble].

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: What are you waiting for, a word from them?

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: No. Waiting for the time to run out.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay, the Pan Camera Mode barber pole has gone back to gray. That took about 40 seconds.

a16_0515504.speaker: Young
a16_0515504.text: Now I lost my peanut butter [garble] I lose some of my peanut butter.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: I was only kidding. If you find it floating around, I bet you'll have a hard time finding the guy who hid it.

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: It's really good. Peaches is one of the best things we have.

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: How did you cycle the film?

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: The - was there something you wanted to say at the end of this thing, Charlie?

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: Huh? No. I just wanted to be sure at the end of this thing that the Mapping Camera to Standby Mode...

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: That's after - after you've cycled the Pan Camera switch.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Yeah. Well, let me see the Flight Plan. Thank you.

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: Read you loud and clear, Casper, Go ahead.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay. The next item here is to take the Mapping Camera to Standby mode, and I assume I should do that before I turn the SM/AC Power Off. [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: Can they see that down there? ...

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Yeah. Well, [garble] they can tell it, too.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Could it take the cassette? Will it sit one place and still - corners it has to go around and [garble] cassette?

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: Alright, Casper, after you turn the Mapping Camera to the Standby mode, we want you to add Pan Camera Self Test to Heaters. [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay, you've got Heaters now. And we're in Standby, and I'm about to turn the SM/AC Power Off unless you want me to hold it.

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: Leave it on, Casper. Leave that Power on.

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: [Garble] he say [garble] Standby Mode that I leave it? [garble]

a16_0515504.speaker: Young
a16_0515504.text: Number 2, a 3, a 4, a 5, a 6, [garble] all be [garble].

a16_0515504.speaker: Duke
a16_0515504.text: John, I tell you what I'll do [garble].

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: 16, go Omni Bravo. You can stow the High Gain.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay, after the film cycling, it normally calls for our taking the SM/AC Power Off, and you asked that we hold there. Do you want us to complete the rest of that powerdown, or do you want to just stop there and you're going to pick it up later or - what would you have in mind? [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: We want to leave the Heaters on for a while and the Power on. And we'll pick it up again later at about 58 hours, but we'll call you. [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: Okay. We'll leave that in your care.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: And, if you're ready, Houston, we'll go ahead and stop PTC and go over to the UV attitude.

a16_0515504.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0515504.text: It's really a shame to kill a PTC that looks as nice as this one.

a16_0515504.speaker: Peterson
a16_0515504.text: Casper, you might try killing this roll at 208, which is your next roll attitude. [Pause.]

a16_0515504.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0515504.text: This is Apollo Control; 52 hours, 17 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 now being maneuvered into a High Gain Antenna attitude leaving the Passive Thermal Control after all night and most of the day. Midcourse correction 3 will not be performed and it's likely that Midcourse 4 will not be either, in as much as the present calculations show that the correction would about 1.4 feet per second [0.4 metres per second] at the present time. We should be getting some improvement in communications when we do get locked up on the High Gain Antenna. And we're continuing to stand by at 52:18.

a16_0522619.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0522619.text: Hey, Don.

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Go ahead, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0522619.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0522619.text: Let me tell you, all our plans for peanut butter were - were correct. That's the ideal space food.

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Rog. [Pause.] You guys gonna do the Skylab thing tonight? [Long pause.]

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: 16, Houston. How do you read?

a16_0522619.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0522619.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0522619.speaker: Young
a16_0522619.text: Loud and clear.

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Okay, we're just doing a subcarrier voice check. [Pause.]

a16_0522619.speaker: Young
a16_0522619.text: Your sub - your subcarrier has good voice...

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Right.

a16_0522619.speaker: Young
a16_0522619.text: ...and Ken's right about that peanut butter sandwich. It's like when we were aboard ship, we can get that peanut butter sandwich when we're in too much of a hurry to do something else - to do anything else, and it works!

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Okay. We'll pass that along.

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Casper, I've got that list of TVC relay set and reset conditions anytime you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0522619.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0522619.text: I'm all pencil.

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Okay, the conditions that set the relay are: one, Spacecraft Control switch, CMC; Optics Zero switch, Off; and Optics Mode switch, Manual.

a16_0522619.speaker: Young
a16_0522619.text: What to Manual?

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Optics Mode switches Manual. [Pause.] And number two, another way to set it, is start a CMC TVC gimbal drive check in P40. [Long pause.] Okay, the different ways that it can get reset are: number one, Optics Zero switch, Zero; [pause.] number two, Optics Zero switch, Off and the Optics Mode switch to CMC; [pause.] number three, Spacecraft Control...

a16_0522619.speaker: Young
a16_0522619.text: Hey, Don, would you stand by for a minute, please?

a16_0522619.speaker: Peterson
a16_0522619.text: Sure will.

a16_0522619.speaker: Young
a16_0522619.text: Let's get our UV. Give us a rough on that time and I'll come back with you.

a16_0523751.speaker: Young
a16_0523751.text: Okay. On your plot board, Pete, what do you show us over now?

a16_0523751.speaker: Peterson
a16_0523751.text: Just about over Florida. [Pause.] Kind of down over the tip of ...

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: 16, could you verify the position of the S-Band Aux TV switch? [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Yeah, it's still in SCI, waiting for you guys to tell us to finish up our film cycling checklist.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Understand; it's in SCI?

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Affirmative. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: You can take that switch to Off, but leave the Pan Camera Heaters and stuff on.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. Well, since we - you don't want us to do the exact checklist, we'll - we'll turn the SCI, Off and the Data System, Off, or do you want the Data System On? You're not reading anything now, I don't think.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Just leave the Data System, On. We've commanded it Off on the ground.

a16_0524104.speaker: Young
a16_0524104.text: Okay; Data System, On.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Duke
a16_0524104.text: Houston, with the binocs out looking at the Earth, we can see Florida and the - the real blue water around the Bahamas. On around the Gulf of Mexico, looks like you might have some clouds near Houston and on down into Mexico and the Great Lakes up in the North, where there's lots of clouds on up north of that.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Roger. It is overcast here, Charlie.

a16_0524104.speaker: Duke
a16_0524104.text: [Garble] and up in the polar icecap, there is a big broken line; it looks like a river or something running down off to the southwest. Wonder what that feature might be?

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Does it look like - Is it a feature on the ground or a feature in the clouds? [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Duke
a16_0524104.text: Well, I cau - I thought the whole thing was just snow and ice up there; maybe it is the clouds up in - it looked like to me it's - it's just up at the North Pole in the icecap area.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Roger; understand. I don't...

a16_0524104.speaker: Duke
a16_0524104.text: And it's been there since we laun - it's been there since we launched.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Roger.

a16_0524104.speaker: Duke
a16_0524104.text: What it appeared to me to be was some places thawed out up there, but - and I was looking at water, but that might be the clouds actually.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay. Tony's sitting here. I'll see if he knows anything about it. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Duke
a16_0524104.text: Okay, and that storm system that was out west of Alaska or thereabouts appears to be still there.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, Don. I'm ready to copy the rest of those things that reset the TVC [garble].

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay, stand by just a minute. They're adding a couple of notes to it.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Sure thing. [Pause.] Can I read back the other things when I read back the ones that set it?

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Say again, Ken.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: I'll just wait until you get it all; I was going to read back the one that set it. Everybody's talking about those binoculars. We pulled those things out in Earth orbit as we were going over the States, and it's pretty impressive. It works out well in other places; it really does enhance things you can see.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, all set.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay. The note they added was back up on the very first thing I gave you: the number 1, conditions to set the relay. Those conditions only work in certain programs or extended verbs, and those are P20, 22, 23, 24, 52, or Verb 41 Noun 91. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay, and I believe we'd gotten down through numbers...

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Is it all options to P20? [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Stand by a minute, Ken; we'll get you an answer on that.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay. While we're waiting for them to decide whether it's all options or not, I believe we got down through number 2, reset conditions.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. I copied the Optics to Zero and the Optics Zero to Off when in CMC Mode control.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay, and that was number 2. Number 3 is Spacecraft Control switch, SCS. [Pause.] Number 4 is THC, clockwise. [Pause.] Number 5 is Verb 37 Enter, XX Enter. [Pause.] Number 6 is fresh start, Verb 36. [Pause.] Number 7 is Verb 34 or Pro in the sighting mark routine, R53 display. [Pause.] And number 8 is Auto Enter RCS DAP at SPS cut-off plus 2.5 seconds in P40. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. I didn't understand that one, Don.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay. It's the - it's what happens to you immediately following the burns. The SPS cuts off, and then 2.5 seconds later in P40, the TVC relay gets reset. [Long pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay, and on the question of options, back up under set condition number 1, it's all options except number 2 in program 20. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: And that's all of them. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, and I understand that this - this can happen when you either set or reset the enable relay, is that correct?

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: That's affirmative. They say it can happen going - any change of state on the TVC relay. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. Can you tell me if it's the change of state of the relay, or just the command to change? For instance, if we already had it in some of these things like a Verb 37, any program resets it; but if it's already in the reset position, is that a condition that's likely to trigger one of these things, or is that one of the safe conditions?

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: We - we think, Ken, it's the actual relay set/reset changing, not - not the command.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Don, let me read back what you read to me, and then I'll want to mull that over for a while and see if I have any other questions.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, and I think that, except the TVC enable [garble].

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: 16, you're fading out. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: 16, we are unable to read.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, the things that will set the TVC enable are the Spacecraft Control switch to CMC, the Optic Zero to Off, the Optics Mode to Manual, and the CMC TVC gimbal test in P40. These things occur only if I'm in P20 options 0, 1, 3, 4; P22, P23, P24, P52; and a Verb 41 Noun 91.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay, Ken. On that, the first three of those constitute one set of conditions; and the last one, that is, the start of CMC thrust vector control, is another condition that is sufficient by itself. [Pause.]

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, understand. The first three go with those programs, and the CMC thrust vector control is sufficient by itself.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Did you - I don't remember if we concluded whether that was when it - the CMC sets the gimbal in preparation for the burn or only during that test.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: I don't think that's - at least, I haven't been advised as to which set of conditions we're talking about there.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: Okay, now I'll read you the reset ones.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay.

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: It's Optics to Zero, Optics Zero to Off when in CMC Mode, Spacecraft Control to SCS, Translation Hand Controller to clockwise, any Verb 37 Enter to XX Enter, a fresh start, a Verb 34 or Pro when in the sighting mark display, and the Auto engine off or Auto TVC reset after a burn in P40.

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.] There are eight different reset conditions; number 2 actually contains two separate items [Pause.].

a16_0524104.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0524104.text: That's affirmative. Thank you...

a16_0524104.speaker: Peterson
a16_0524104.text: Okay.

a16_0525611.speaker: Young
a16_0525611.text: Okay, Houston. We're starting the fuel cell purge and waste water dump.

a16_0530552.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0530552.text: Okay, we've got a LM/CM Delta-P of 0.6. We'd like to go ahead and pressurize the cabin and get ready for the LM entry.

a16_0530552.speaker: Peterson
a16_0530552.text: Okay, Casper. We copied, and you can go ahead.

a16_0530700.speaker: Duke
a16_0530700.text: Okay, Houston. The waste water dump is terminated at about 12 percent.

a16_0530700.speaker: England
a16_0530700.text: Okay, Charlie. We copy that. [Long pause.]

a16_0530700.speaker: Duke
a16_0530700.text: And, Tony, we're into the - equalizing the pressure CM/LM at this point.

a16_0530700.speaker: England
a16_0530700.text: When you're working up there in the hatch area, I've got a test for you on that Docking Latch 10, when it's convenient. You might let me know when you can work on it.

a16_0530700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0530700.text: Okay, well. Why don't we wait 'til the guys get in the LM, then I'll work on that while they're doing that.

a16_0531751.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0531751.text: This is Apollo Control at 53 hours, 28 minutes. The LM TELMU, one of the Lunar Module flight controllers here in Mission Control, has just reported that from his telemetry data it looks as if the crew has opened the hatch preparing to enter the Lunar Module at this time. They're scheduled to spend about 50 minutes to an hour in the LM on housekeeping activities, in what will be the third entry into the Lunar Module Orion during the course of this mission. A change of shift press briefing is scheduled to begin shortly in the MSC news center briefing room. During the course of that briefing, we

a16_0532800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0532800.text: Okay, Houston. The Orion is on internal power at 53:28:34.

a16_0532800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0532800.text: This is Apollo Control. The change of shift press briefing is ready to begin. We'll switch at this time to the MSC news center briefing room.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Houston, 16. We're in Orion now, and you - you've got the comm on; you should be getting high bit rate momentarily.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay, and we'd like to go to the High Gain. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. You mean over on Casper's side? Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: That's signal strength for them.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Houston. Okay. We just got the signal strength on Orion. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. We have LM data.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Hey, Tony, ask TELMU about this 192 package lanyard. I looked at it yesterday, and I could see red and green. It's way out and looks okay to me. Is that copacetic?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Charlie, Houston.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. TELMU says that's okay; no problem. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: That's fine, and what did you want to update? What checklist?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay, your Lunar Surface Checklist and your LM Cue Card for EVA prep. [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay, Tony. I have the Cue Cards. Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. On the Cue Cards, it'll be all of them, EVA-1, -2, and -3; and I have one here for post-EVA. Okay. On the EVA-1, -2, and -3, after the sentence 'Read PLSS O 2 quantity to Houston,' we'd like to add the line...

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Wait, wait a minute, wait; hold on.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Rog.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. I've got EVA-1 prep; now which column? [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. It's on the left-hand column, right at the bottom line; it says "Read PLSS O 2 quantity to Houston."" [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. I've got the "Read PLSS O 2 quantity to Houston"; the next one is a note, "If Comm is No Go." Is that the one you want?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Rog. We'd like to put a line in between "Read PLSS O 2 quantity" and the note.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. "Squelch VHF B [pause] (LMP) - full decrease."

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. I got it.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. And now the EVA-2 prep Cue Card.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. This is the left-hand column and this is - at the bottom, and we'll add the same line there, "Squelch VHF B (LMP) - full decrease." [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. On the EVA-3 prep, the same as EVA-2 prep. [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Now this is on the post-EVA-3 Cue Card. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: I got it. Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. On the third column, one-third of the way down, it says, "Audio circuit breaker - Close."

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Got it.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. We'd like to add a line right after that. "Squelch VHF B (LMP) - noise threshold, plus 1½." [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. The point of all of this is to increase the range of PLSS to LM, in case you're having a crew failure.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: What else you got?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. It's the same sort of changes to your Lunar Surface Checklist, and I'll read them to you when you're ready. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay, Tony. We never use that checklist in this time frame. We'll copy it in, in a little bit, okay?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. That's fine.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Houston, 16.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Go ahead, Charlie.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. I'm a little confused about your terminology, I guess. It says "Squelch VHF B (LMP) - full decrease." We only got one VHF B to squelch.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Roger; I understand that. The "LMP" was just a cue that you're the only one on the comm at the time, so you'll be the one to - to have to listen and get it down.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Charlie, Houston.

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Go ahead.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. When you get a chance there, we'd like you to read the ED Voltage, both A and B. [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Exactly the same thing as yesterday, 37 volts, Tony, both of them.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Good show, and verify Off. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Duke
a16_0533058.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay, Apollo 16. I guess that's all they need in the Lunar Module. At your convenience, you can power down. And could you read that tunnel index as you go through, the docking index? [Long pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: Strange to say, it hasn't changed any.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: All right.

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: It's still minus three and a half.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. We copy.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay.

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: Do you want us to do that now?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Yeah, it'd be a good time, if you're ready.

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: I'm sitting here looking at it.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. On that docking latch Number 10, depress the yellow auxiliary release button, noting that the button will depress and whether it stays snapped in after being depressed. Now, the interest here is if the button will not depress, the latch mechanism is either stuck or broken. If the button stays snapped in, this indicates - or probably indicates that the latch was only partially cocked at launch...

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: [Garble]. It's in...

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: ...and stayed in.

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: It's in, and it stayed in.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Then, the indication there is that it was only partially cocked at launch. [Pause.]

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: Well, do you want me to re-cock it and fire it?

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: No, they had just as soon you leave it the way it is, because if it's broken, you may not be able to - to get it off again, and then that would foul up the undocking.

a16_0533058.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0533058.text: Sounds like a reasonable plan. Okay. I've got the Aux Release Button pushed in, and it stayed there, and the rest of it's gonna be left as is.

a16_0533058.speaker: England
a16_0533058.text: Okay. Good show. That's it.

a16_0534920.speaker: Duke
a16_0534920.text: Okay, Tony. We're going to get our suits on.

a16_0535547.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0535547.text: And, Houston, we brought LM power back to the CSM at 53:49.

a16_0535547.speaker: England
a16_0535547.text: Okay, we copy that. And Ken, we have a correction to that TVC relay set condition. [Pause.]

a16_0535547.speaker: England
a16_0535547.text: Okay, on the set in program P20, we read up previously that it wouldn't set in option 2. We've got a correction to that. It sets only in Options 0 and 4.

a16_0535547.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0535547.text: Understand; it sets in only Options 0 and 4.

a16_0535547.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0535547.text: Tony, I'm gonna try to get some pictures of selected portions of the suit donning on 16 millimeter. And I just checked here on the spotmeter, and it looks like the CIN is going to be marginal for this, and I'm looking at the - the BW that's available. And I wonder if anyone would object if I put it on magazine Hotel Hotel.

a16_0535547.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0535547.text: Okay; I - I'm in P00, and I'll give you Accept.

a16_0540000.speaker: England
a16_0540000.text: Okay, and I guess you'll have to go to P20 for us to load it. [Pause.]

a16_0540000.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0540000.text: Okay, you want me to be in P20 first.

a16_0540000.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0540000.text: Well, that was almost right. [Long pause.]

a16_0540000.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0540000.text: This is Apollo Control at 54 hours. During the change of shift briefing, John Young and Charlie Duke entered the Lunar Module, Orion. They powered it up, checked the communications system, completed their housekeeping activities aboard the LM and are in the process of returning to the Command Module. The total time from the time the LM was switched to its own power until they were back on the Command Module providing power to the Lunar Module was about 21 minutes. Again, as on the two previous occasions when we've had a look at the Lunar Module systems, when the data has been transmitted back

a16_0540437.speaker: England
a16_0540437.text: Okay. We've got an answer here on this Hotel Hotel. You have about ten percent available to use now if you like, and if you use the spotmeter inside, you'll have to set it for an ASA of 4000.

a16_0540437.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0540437.text: That's affirm, thank you. I can use ten percent.

a16_0540437.speaker: England
a16_0540437.text: Okay. We've got your program loaded. You can press on with the Noun 26.

a16_0540437.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0540437.text: You're gonna have to stand by a minute.

a16_0540437.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0540437.text: Okay, Tony. What did you want? Noun 26 loaded up?

a16_0540437.speaker: England
a16_0540437.text: Right. You can go ahead and call your Noun 26. [Pause.]

a16_0540437.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0540437.text: Okay. I was - We're in the LM trying to get some pictures of their suit zipping up.

a16_0540437.speaker: England
a16_0540437.text: Rog. I'll bet that's a real hassle.

a16_0540437.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0540437.text: This is Apollo Control. That completes our playback of the accumulated tape. We'll continue to stand by now and monitor the conversations live.

a16_0541447.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0541447.text: Okay. Tony, does that - does that look right for a Noun 26?

a16_0541447.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0541447.text: Thank you. The thing that I was questioning was the R36 not sliding over to the end.

a16_0541447.speaker: England
a16_0541447.text: Okay. If you'll call up Verb 05 26, it'll slide over. Right now you're not reading the third register. [Pause.]

a16_0541447.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0541447.text: Thank you. Okay. You want me to do a Verb 31?

a16_0541447.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0541447.text: Okay, and are we gonna check out the alarm function, or are we just gonna check out the loading capability?

a16_0541447.speaker: England
a16_0541447.text: I think they've got something in mind for alarm function later, but nothing right now.

a16_0541447.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0541447.text: Okay, thank you. I'm gonna go back over and see if I can get some pictures from the LM then. [Long pause.]

a16_0541447.speaker: England
a16_0541447.text: I guess they'd like an E-Mod now. [Pause.]

a16_0541447.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0541447.text: Anything else before I go over to the LM? [Pause.]

a16_0541447.speaker: England
a16_0541447.text: Everybody is shaking their head; I guess it's okay. About the time you get to the hatch, we'll think of something. [Pause.]

a16_0543016.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0543016.text: And, Tony, we used only five percent on - it went from ten to 15 percent on magazine HH.

a16_0543016.speaker: England
a16_0543016.text: Okay. We copy that. [Pause.] And when you get back in the Command Module there, we'd like for you to go to Block on the CM. [Pause.]

a16_0543016.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0543016.text: Okay. I'm Block, and Charlie's coming up on the comm, and I'm going to don my suit.

a16_0543016.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0543016.text: This is Apollo Control at 54 hours, 44 minutes. The Apollo 16 crew at this time is in the process of donning their Pressure Garment Assemblies, without helmet and gloves. Young and Duke are then scheduled to re-enter the Lunar Module and return to the Command Module. The exercise is part of a check of the procedures that the crew will be using on the day that they perform the landing on the Moon in suiting up and entering the LM. Following this exercise, the crew is scheduled to eat. During the eat period, they will be running the Skylab food test. There are several Skylab food items packed in

a16_0550603.speaker: England
a16_0550603.text: Okay. Sounds good. [Pause.] And there's no hurry on this, but when Ken gets all comfortable, we've got that Jet Monitor test.

a16_0550603.speaker: Duke
a16_0550603.text: Okay. Ken's busy. We'll give you a call.

a16_0550603.speaker: Duke
a16_0550603.text: Okay. I'm not even sure that would help, but it felt - it feels like it would to me.

a16_0550603.speaker: England
a16_0550603.text: Charlie, I guess that gives us a data point...

a16_0550603.speaker: Duke
a16_0550603.text: Tony, there was no - yeah, there was no trouble at all with the - with the pressure sealing zipper, it - or the pressure seal. It was just the - the restraint. And that was just in that one place in the small of my back.

a16_0550603.speaker: England
a16_0550603.text: Okay. We copy that. I guess that gives us a data point. You grow in zero g.

a16_0550603.speaker: Duke
a16_0550603.text: That's what it feels like - that I stretched out an inch or so.

a16_0550603.speaker: England
a16_0550603.text: You better watch that; you're pretty close to your six feet.

a16_0550603.speaker: Duke
a16_0550603.text: Okay. Tony, the hatch is back in.

a16_0551534.speaker: England
a16_0551534.text: Oh, yeah, Ken, we're still here. How are you doing?

a16_0551534.speaker: England
a16_0551534.text: Okay. We'd like you to disable all the B/D roll jets, and you're cycling against the stops about once every ten minutes, and so expect that you'll get your ISS light some time in there, and when you get it, we don't - you can turn back on the jets; we'd just like to look at it a while. [Pause.]

a16_0551534.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0551534.text: Okay. How about if I just go Free? [Pause.]

a16_0551534.speaker: England
a16_0551534.text: Okay. I guess the Free kills the Jet Monitor.

a16_0551534.speaker: England
a16_0551534.text: Ken, Just to verify that, if you go Free - CMC Free - the program doesn't monitor; if you go back to Auto, it does. You don't have to put the program back in.

a16_0551534.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0551534.text: Rog. I understand that. I guess I just wasn't thinking then. What I - what I did, Tony, was, rather than leave - leave two axes in control and one of them free, I put all the Manual Attitude switches to Accel Command, and we're still in CMC Mode, Auto.

a16_0551534.speaker: England
a16_0551534.text: Rog. We saw that down here. It looks good.

a16_0551534.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0551534.text: Okay. You can - you know, you can watch it all day long - whatever you want there.

a16_0552611.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0552611.text: And, sure enough, just like advertised, there's no status lights on - DSKY warning panel. And I'm gonna go ahead - if it's okay with you, I'll turn off the Channel 11, Bit 1.

a16_0552611.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0552611.text: While we're still outside the deadband, that's not going to work unless I cycle it Free and back to recenter the deadband. You folks want to watch it outside the deadband for a while? [Pause.]

a16_0552611.speaker: England
a16_0552611.text: That's okay. I guess we're happy with it, and we'd like to go ahead and terminate it - terminate the...

a16_0553046.speaker: England
a16_0553046.text: And, Ken, I guess you can go on to PTC at your convenience.

a16_0553046.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0553046.text: Okay. Just getting ready to ask you about that. Thank you.

a16_0553046.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0553046.text: Do you folks have me to continue using B/D roll? [Pause.]

a16_0553046.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0553046.text: This is Apollo Control at 55 hours, 35 minutes. A short while ago Ken Mattingly reported that the tunnel had been closed out, indicating that Young and Duke had completed their suit exercise, were back in the Command Module. The tunnel hatch replaced after all of the probe and drogue assembly equipment had been reinstalled. And we heard Charlie Duke report that his suit, when John Young attempted to zip it up across the back, appeared to feel tighter than he was used to feeling in that suit. Charlie said he didn't feel this would cause him any particular problems, but he was concerned that per

a16_0555026.speaker: Duke
a16_0555026.text: Well, it was a little - little tight launch day. We'd - you know, fitted it pressurized, Tony, and it felt okay then. Launch day, I thought the legs were a little tight but not much. [Pause.]

a16_0555026.speaker: Duke
a16_0555026.text: Once we get it zipped, Tony, it feels a little tight, but pressurized it's okay. It's just the zipping part that was worrying us.

a16_0555026.speaker: England
a16_0555026.text: Well, everybody's thinking about it, and we'll come back with an answer on it later. Right now I think the general feeling is that most people'd just as soon you not tamper with it unless you feel very strong about it. [Pause.]

a16_0555026.speaker: Duke
a16_0555026.text: Well, that's our opinion, too. Our next solution, or our next question is - is maybe breaking out with the LCG and putting all the gear on and seeing how it goes with all of the gear. Our question there is, if we break into one of the LCGs right now, will it affect - get any gas in the tubes; would it affect the startup on the PLSS?

a16_0555026.speaker: England
a16_0555026.text: Okay, we'll work that one. [Long pause.]

a16_0555026.speaker: England
a16_0555026.text: Okay, Charlie, we've looked at that LCG problem and you're right. If you break it out early, we'll probably get gas in there and never be able to get it out, and it will affect your cooling. [Pause.]

a16_0555026.speaker: Duke
a16_0555026.text: Okay. John and I were going to break into those LCGs and sleep in them the night prior to PDI. What do you think about that idea, then? [Pause.]

a16_0555026.speaker: England
a16_0555026.text: Okay; they're over there scratching their head again.

a16_0555924.speaker: England
a16_0555924.text: Okay; your rates are low enough for the PTC.

a16_0560650.speaker: England
a16_0560650.text: Okay, we'd like your onboard reading, the H 2 tank 1 pressure. [Long pause.]

a16_0560650.speaker: England
a16_0560650.text: Okay, Ken. That's - that transducer problem, probably - they've had that history of problems with that transducer. Prelaunch.

a16_0560650.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0560650.text: It was glitching launch day, but it looks like now it's sort of stabilized.

a16_0560650.speaker: England
a16_0560650.text: Okay. We'd like you to go to Omni Bravo, and stow the High Gain. And we'll handle the switching.

a16_0561922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0561922.text: Houston, 16.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Go ahead.

a16_0561922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0561922.text: Okay; we're getting reader to go to work on this Skylab food preparation bit, and we're trying to check out some camera settings and all. We've got 16-millimeter magazine allocated for this with CIN film in it, and by checking the most light that I can get on most objects, it looks like we'll be running with the lens wide open aperture at about 1/60 of a second. And I guess I'd like to know if you want to do that, or if you'd like to use a higher ASA and process the film differently.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Okay; we'll talk about that. [Long pause.]

a16_0561922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0561922.text: Tony, I was just looking here, and if we go to the 18-millimeter lens, we can open it up to a - to a T-1. And that gets our speed up to about 1/250. It looks like a lot better way to operate. [Pause.]

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Ken, the comm's pretty bad right now. We're having a hard time getting that. We understood that the light meter indicates that the film that was indicated to use here probably isn't going to be fast enough, and you're asking to use a faster film. But we didn't und - get there, how severe the problem was.

a16_0561922.speaker: Duke
a16_0561922.text: Houston, 16.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Go ahead, Ken. The comm's still pretty bad, though.

a16_0561922.speaker: Duke
a16_0561922.text: Okay, we were going to get started on the bistatic radar frequency check, if you're ready. [Long pause.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Okay, Charlie, I guess we'd like for you to hold off for a minute on that VHF test.

a16_0561922.speaker: Duke
a16_0561922.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Ken, Houston. The comm may be a little better now, if you'd go through the problem again.

a16_0561922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0561922.text: Okay, Tony. It looks like it's not as bright in here as we'd like to be able to get it, and we'll try - try timing it with some of the window shades up to see if we can get it a little brighter. With the cabin floodlights, it looks like 1/60 of a second is about the max I can get off of the 10-millimeter lens. And I was going to suggest either going to the 18, which will give me a little faster shutter speed because it's got a wider aperture, or we'll take a little less photography and just do it when the Sun gives us good illumination through one of the windows.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Okay, we copy that. We'll work it. [Pause.]

a16_0561922.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0561922.text: I think we can get more uniform photography if we did it with the window shades up and with all our lights in one fixed position. That way, we'll get a lot more photography done rather than having to wait. I really don't think you can afford to wait until the Sun's in just the right place to do your eating.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Rog. Understand.

a16_0561922.speaker: Duke
a16_0561922.text: Okay, Tony, we're going to restow my suit, if you guys don't want us to touch it.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Right, we're not gonna worry about it tonight. We'll have some sort of an answer tomorrow. So you go ahead and stow the suit.

a16_0561922.speaker: Duke
a16_0561922.text: Okay. And our H 2 tank pressure just went back - dropped back down to 240.

a16_0561922.speaker: England
a16_0561922.text: Okay. We saw that. [Pause.]

a16_0561922.speaker: Duke
a16_0561922.text: Hup! It's back up to 270.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Ken, Houston. [No answer.]

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Ken, Houston.

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: Go ahead.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Okay. After much debate, I guess we can have you go ahead and use the 18 millimeter. [Pause.]

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: Okay; thank you.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: All right. If you're not already done with it.

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: I really think we'll get the - We're - we're stowing one of our passengers here back in his suit bag.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: [Laughter.] All right.

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: And...

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Okay, I - We're...

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: We're having - You'd be surprised just how long those kind of things take. You know, you start on something like that, and then it almost fits and you refold it, and it almost fits again, and it's only because you know it fits that you keep trying with it. Because you sure couldn't prove it by us.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Understand. It doesn't sound like too much fun. We'd like to reverse ourselves...

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: No, I didn't say that.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Right. We'd like to reverse ourselves on something I sent up awhile ago. It doesn't seem to be any problem with breaking out the LCGs early. They were thinking about a Skylab situation. So that won't be a constraint. As far as whether we want you to try it tomorrow, we'll work that and send it up tomorrow. But there'll be a...

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: Okay, I guess the only thing on that is that we've got a busy day coming, and these things just really take a long time by the time you put on the suit, and then you play with it and then if we have some adjustments to do, too, why, it's going to take a block of time.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Right. Understand.

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: So the sooner the better, I guess, which I know you know already.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Rog. But I particularly wanted to let you know there was no problem with sleeping in it that night before.

a16_0563145.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0563145.text: That's a big help. Thank you.

a16_0563145.speaker: Young
a16_0563145.text: Yeah, I didn't think there was. That's what they did on Apollo 10.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a16_0563145.speaker: Slayton
a16_0563145.text: Remember Apollo 12, guys, before you do too much with that suit.

a16_0563145.speaker: Young
a16_0563145.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0563145.speaker: Young
a16_0563145.text: Of course, the problem is going to be if we can't get it on at all. That's going to be a real problem.

a16_0563145.speaker: England
a16_0563145.text: Rog.

a16_0563145.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0563145.text: This is Apollo Control at 56 hours, 46 minutes. The crew should be shortly beginning their dinner which will include Skylab food items that they'll be evaluating. At last report, Ken Mattingly mentioned that they were busily involved in restowing the suits and when that was completed, they would be scheduled to begin their eat period and to give us an evaluation of the Skylab food packets that they'll be trying out at this time. We've also had some additional reports, primarily from Charlie Duke with some comments from John Young, on the tight fitting suit. Duke first reported the suit appeare

a16_0564600.speaker: England
a16_0564600.text: Okay. We'd like to start with the VHF test when you're ready.

a16_0564600.speaker: Young
a16_0564600.text: Okay. Give us a couple of minutes here.

a16_0564600.speaker: Duke
a16_0564600.text: Okay, Tony. We have - VHF Antenna's on Left, B is in Duplex, and the Ranging is On.

a16_0571554.speaker: England
a16_0571554.text: Okay, We're gonna drop your S-band up-link for a little while. We'll be back in about ten minutes. [Pause.]

a16_0572214.speaker: England
a16_0572214.text: Okay, we're back early. We'd like you to go ahead and terminate the VHF, and, while you're over that way, we'd like you to switch the High Gain to Wide Beam.

a16_0572214.speaker: Young
a16_0572214.text: Roger, High Gain going to Wide, and terminate the VHF.

a16_0572214.speaker: Young
a16_0572214.text: Okay. The VHF is terminated and you got Wide on the High Gain.

a16_0572214.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0572214.text: This is Apollo Control at 57 hours, 24 minutes. The series of checks that we've been performing with the spacecraft using the onboard VHF and S-band systems are a preparation for an experiment that'll be performed in lunar orbit, the Bistatic Radar experiment which uses the spacecraft's communications equipment in a passive experiment to determine something about the electromagnetic properties of the lunar surface. These radio signals are reflected off the Moon, and the Moon affects the way in which they are reflected, and these characteristics are measured on Earth in an experiment performed

a16_0580735.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0580735.text: We're trying to work on the presleep checklist, and this little part about the Optics to Zero and then the - Optics Power Off. Will any of that do these things we don't want to do with our TVC enable? How about just leaving it all like it is?

a16_0581201.speaker: Young
a16_0581201.text: Okay; Houston, you ready for the onboard readouts?

a16_0581201.speaker: England
a16_0581201.text: Go ahead, Apollo 16. We're ready to take the readouts. [Long pause.]

a16_0581201.speaker: England
a16_0581201.text: Okay. I guess we had a - a weak period there. Yes, we're ready for your readout.

a16_0581201.speaker: Young
a16_0581201.text: Okay, Battery C is 36.7. Pyro Batteries: A, 37; Pyro Battery B, 37; RCS A, 87; B, 90; C, 92; and D, 96. We're on Main A, 29 volts.

a16_0581201.speaker: Young
a16_0581201.text: However, it took a lot longer than we allowed for it.

a16_0581201.speaker: England
a16_0581201.text: And, Apollo 16, I guess it's okay to go to that Optics Zero in Zero, which you are, and G&N Power Optics, Off. [Pause.]

a16_0581906.speaker: Young
a16_0581906.text: Okay. Houston, are you ready for the E-memory dump? Over. [Long pause.]

a16_0581906.speaker: England
a16_0581906.text: Okay, I guess we'd just like you to skip the E-Mod.

a16_0581906.speaker: Young
a16_0581906.text: Houston, you ready for a good old E-memory dump?

a16_0581906.speaker: England
a16_0581906.text: Okay, John; do you copy us now?

a16_0581906.speaker: England
a16_0581906.text: Okay, I think we'd like you to just skip that E-Mod tonight. We do have a couple of changes to Panel 230 when you get down that way. [Pause.]

a16_0581906.speaker: Young
a16_0581906.text: Oh yeah; we plumb forgot about that. [Pause.] Okay, go ahead.

a16_0581906.speaker: England
a16_0581906.text: Okay. We'd like to - Pan Camera Self Test, Off.

a16_0581906.speaker: England
a16_0581906.text: And then down there below, the Service Module/AC Power, Off. [Pause.]

a16_0584409.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0584409.text: Hi, 16. Can I talk to somebody about chlorine injection?

a16_0584409.speaker: England
a16_0584409.text: Roger; we'll talk about that. I know all about those two holes in that adapter. [Pause.]

a16_0584409.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0584409.text: Okay, these are the two on the outside now.

a16_0584409.speaker: England
a16_0584409.text: Rog. I know exactly which ones you're talking about.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Ken, Houston.

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Okays, when you put that buffer in, would you verify that you left the nut all the way screwed down for the ten minutes and that's the period when the water was coming out the two holes. [Pause.]

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: No, the water comes out of those holes - Let's see now. I put the buffer in, I put it into the injector and then I put the injector into the adapter, and when I went to screw down on the injector, it looked like it was starting to seep fluid around the injector again. So I stopped, and it didn't look like it was doing any more, and I thought I would look and see. By this time, I was getting suspicious that maybe the needle wasn't open. So I decided to take the injector off of the needle adapter. I took it off, and everything looked okay. And it was when I went to put it back on, when I depress

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Okay, we copy that. [Pause.] Was the nut snugly against the ampoule when you tried to put it back on? If you backed off on the nut, it may have allowed the - it may have allowed the ampoule to slide back up in the compartment there and then you were just opening up the needle. [Pause.]

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Well, I - I thought it was down snug. If it wasn't snug, would have - would it push water out of those two side ports?

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Yes, it sure would. I had that happen in the prechlorination there on the pad before launch. I had backed off on the nut and, instead of just filling up that ampoule, the water pushed the ampoule off the needle and then, once it's done that, the water just goes back around and comes out those two holes. [Pause.]

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Well, I can't say that didn't happen. The first problem occurred with the chlorine injection.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Right, I didn't see that on the pad. [Pause.]

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Yep. My first problem was when I went to put the chlorine ampoule in. And at some point in there when I went to take it out, I tried to get it in and it didn't look right. When I went to take it out, it started bubbling all over, and I couldn't tell where it was coming from then. And whether it came from those two holes or not, that's quite possible. I'm not sure. When I looked at the ampoule itself, after I opened up the injector, you could see that the - the bottom lug had broken, the little sliding plug in there.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Right. Once that thing isn't watertight anymore, you'll get leakage into that container and that'll all come out those holes.

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Okay. Then perhaps the only problem was the - was the one with the first ampoule breaking.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: All right, we'll try to get you a procedure here and go back and try that buffer again.

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: The rest of it...

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Say again.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: I was going to say we'll try to get you to agree on a procedure here and then go back and try the buffer again.

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Okay. I guess - yeah, we could do that.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Okay. Hold off on that. We'll - we'll get a procedure.

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: Okay. Is that something you want to do tonight or do it tomorrow?

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: You want that buffer in there tonight, don't you? [Pause.]

a16_0585059.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585059.text: I don't know. It's a - I - I can't vouch for how much chlorine went in. Perhaps - very little. It's up to the - the guys who have plumbing responsibilities. I - I just can't tell you how much chlorine may have gotten in.

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Okay, we understand. [Long pause.]

a16_0585059.speaker: England
a16_0585059.text: Okay, Ken. I - I guess we'd like you to take that buffer ampoule again and screw the nut down on it so that you think it's - it's good - good and snug in there, and then put it on the adapter and see if you can - see if it'll take the buffer.
