[Pause.] Before you - you close it all up again, you might look at the ampoule to make sure it hasn't cracked.

a16_0585821.speaker: England
a16_0585821.text: Did you get that about going ahead with the buffer?

a16_0585821.speaker: England
a16_0585821.text: Oh, okay; we probably had some bad comm there. We'd like you to take a look at that buffer ampoule and make sure it isn't cracked and, if not, then to go ahead and put it in that little container and screw that nut so you feel it's good and snug and then go ahead and see if it will take the buffer. [Pause.]

a16_0585821.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585821.text: Okay. How about if I just take a brand new one? Don't we have a couple spares?

a16_0585821.speaker: England
a16_0585821.text: Okay. Yeah, they agree. Why don't you take a brand new one.

a16_0585821.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585821.text: Okay. And while I'm doing that, I'm just looking over the gauges, and I know our onboard gauging isn't the greatest thing in RCS. Could you tell me how we stand on RCS?

a16_0585821.speaker: England
a16_0585821.text: And, Ken, at 54 hours, you were two percent ahead of your RCS budget - that's 25 pounds to the good. [Pause.]

a16_0585821.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585821.text: [Garble] I guess we have a low bias in quad A and just kind of looks bad. [Long pause.]

a16_0585821.speaker: England
a16_0585821.text: Okay. We - our bias is that you're reading 2 percent low on that. [Pause.]

a16_0585821.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0585821.text: Okay. Tony, I've got the buffer in, and I noticed just a slight little spit when I put it in. That's probably residual. So I'll wait ten minutes and then suck it out.

a16_0590605.speaker: Young
a16_0590605.text: Okay, Houston. The O 2 Flow High and the cabin is pumped up to 5.7.

a16_0590605.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0590605.text: This is Apollo Control at 59 hours, 9 minutes. The crew at this time completing the items on their checklist prior to getting an eight-hour rest period. And we had a description from Ken Mattingly of some problems he was having getting the chlorine and buffer injected into the drinking water system. This is done with a syringe-type device which injects the chlorine and the buffer alternately through a diaphragm in the waste - in the water management panel of the spacecraft. This is injected through with a hypodermic needle arrangement. And from the descriptions given by Mattingly and the discu

a16_0591633.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0591633.text: Okay, Tony, got that buffer in and out, and all looks normal now.

a16_0591633.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0591633.text: Okay. Looks like we've got the buffer in and water back out, and everything looks normal now.

a16_0591633.speaker: England
a16_0591633.text: Good show. If - if you didn't get much chlorine in the buffer, won't hurt anything, but it would have hurt the other way if you'd put the chlorine in without adding the buffer, so - either way, we're in good shape now. [Pause.]

a16_0591633.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0591633.text: Okay. Then I guess our only problem then was just the fact that I probably broke that first chlorine ampoule some way.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Rog.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mattingly
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay, Tony. I guess I'm ready to give you a film status report. [Pause.]

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay. Go ahead.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mattingly
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay. On magazine Victor Victor, we're on frame 21; magazine Hotel Hotel, frame 85; magazine Oscar Oscar, frame 34; November November is also 34; Juliet Juliet is 50 percent.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Was that 50 percent?

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mattingly
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: That's 50 percent. That's affirmative.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay. [Pause.]

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay. We copied all those. [Pause.]

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mattingly
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay, I guess we're about ready to sign off. Do you folks have any last words or any questions? [Long pause.]

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Young
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Houston, we're about ready to go to sleep. You got any questions or anything you want to tell us before we shut down the comm system?

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay. We're running around here to make sure there's nothing. I just read through your last system report that came around here, and everything looks nominal. Everything really looks great. [Pause.] Okay, I guess there's...

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Young
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: ...looks good to us, too.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Young
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Tony, even that won't keep me awake.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: [Laughter.] Oh, yeah, it would. I'll see y'all on the Moon. I've got a day off tomorrow. [Pause.]

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Young
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Good show.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mattingly
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Okay.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Young
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Sounds good. See you tomorrow.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: England
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Rog.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Young
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: Good night.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control. While we were in the process of completing those last few items with the crew before saying good night, Apollo 16 crossed into the Moon's sphere of influence, and we're now showing the spacecraft at an altitude of 33,680 nautical miles [62.375 km] from the Moon and traveling at a speed of 3,482 feet per second [1,061 m/s], and that velocity is increasing. The time again of that sphere crossing was 59 hours, 19 minutes, 45 seconds. At 59 hours, 24 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control at 60 hours, 3 minutes. At the present time, we're in the midst of a shift handover in Mission Control. Our Flight Director Phil Shaffer is coming on to replace Flight Director Pete Frank. The spacecraft communicator on the oncoming shift will be astronaut Hank Hartsfield replacing astronaut Tony England. And at the present time, Apollo 16 is 32,321 nautical miles [59,858 km] from the Moon. Traveling at a speed of 3,492 feet per second [1,064 m/s]. During this past shift, the major activities for the crew included another activation and checkout of the Lunar Module. At 5

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 60 hours, 51 minutes since lift-off. Phil Shaffer's again the Flight Director for the White Team of flight controllers who are now on duty in the Mission Control. As previously reported, the crew of Apollo 16 is in their sleep period. Right now, we expect that Young, Duke and Mattingly will be allowed an extra hour of sleep, making the wake-up time at 67 hours Ground Elapsed Time. At 61 hours

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 61 hours, 51 minutes into the mission. The crew of Apollo 16 continuing with their rest period as Apollo 16 continues on course toward lunar orbit. We presently show Apollo 16 at 28,605 nautical miles [52,976 km] away from the Moon; velocity now reads 3,520 feet per second [1,073 m/s]. Very little conversation over the Flight Director's loop in the Mission Operations Control Room. One of the items to be decided on this shift however, is the requirement for Midcourse Correction Number 4 prior to a Lunar Orbit Insertion. If it is decided to do it, MCC-4 will be

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 62 hours, 51 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Our displays in Mission Control now show Apollo 16 26,522 nautical miles [49,119 km] away from the Moon and traveling at a velocity of 3,540 feet per second [1,079 m/s]. Meanwhile in the Control Center, we continue in our systems monitoring mode as the White Flight Control Team continues to maintain their logs and update their planning notes for handover to the next team of flight controllers. The next team will be on duty when the Lunar Orbit Insertion burn occurs. This morning, the Surgeon is monitoring Commander Jo

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 63 hours, 52 minutes into the mission. We now show Apollo 16 at a distance of 24,470 nautical miles [45,318 km] from the Moon and traveling at a velocity of 3,567 feet per second [1,087 m/s]. Our CapCom Hank Hartsfield has not spoken with the crew on his shift yet this morning. However, he will place the wake-up call and the wake-up call is now scheduled for a bit over three hours from this time. We're at 63 hours, 53 minutes and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 64 hours, 51 minutes into the mission. We now show the Apollo 16 spacecraft at 24,237 [means 22,237] nautical miles [41,183 km] away from the Moon. We've had no contact with the crew of Apollo 16 for the past hour nor do we expect contact with the crew for a bit more than two hours. Crew wake-up time is now two hours and eight minutes away. We'll stand by however, and continue to monitor our conversations within the Mission Control Center and the various displays. At 64 hours, 52 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.speaker: Mission Control
XXXXXXXXXXXXXX.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 65 hours, 51 minutes into the mission. We now show Apollo 16 at a distance of 20,195 nautical miles [37,401 km] away from the Moon, and traveling now at a velocity of 3,626 feet per second [1,105 m/s]. The crew of Apollo 16 can expect their wake-up call in a bit over an hour. Our countdown clock in Mission Control shows one hour, eight minutes remaining until time of wake-up. The Flight Plan for the upcoming day for the crew, is essentially unchanged. However, one item is still open, this being the decision on whether or not to do Midcourse Correction 4. We'r

a16_0661600.speaker: Young
a16_0661600.text: Morning, Houston. How do you read? Over.

a16_0661600.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0661600.text: Good morning, 16. How are you this morning? [Pause.]

a16_0661600.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0661600.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 66 hours, 20 minutes into the mission. Apollo 16 now 19,161 nautical miles [35,486 km] away from the Moon. Velocity now shows 3,646 feet per second [1,111 m/s]. We heard that brief exchange between Apollo 16 Commander John Young and Hank Hartsfield who's manning the Capsule Communicator's console here in Mission Control. The first activity scheduled in the Flight Plan for this morning for Apollo 16 is a - a breakfast, or eat period. Presumably they - if they have not already started, they will be pressing on in their first bite of the morning very shortly. We'r

a16_0662733.speaker: Young
a16_0662733.text: Okay, Houston. The LM/CM Delta-P is about one [pound per square inch]. [Pause.] And, the cabin pressure being what it is, I guess that means that we really don't have any leakage up there much.

a16_0662733.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0662733.text: Apollo Control, Houston, at 66 hours, 29 minutes. Apollo 16 is now 18,839 nautical miles [34,890 km] away from the Moon, and now traveling at a speed of 3,652 feet per second [1,113 metres]. This is Apollo Control, Houston, continuing to monitor.

a16_0662733.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0662733.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 66 hours, 47 minutes into the mission. We now show Apollo 16 at a distance of 18,243 nautical miles [33,786 km]; this is the distance away from the Moon. We now read Apollo 16's velocity at 3,664 feet per second [1,117 m/s]. At 66 hours, 46 minutes continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0662733.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0662733.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 67 hours Ground Elapsed Time. Our displays now show Apollo 16 at a distance of 17,704 nautical miles [32,787 km] from the Moon, and we show a speed of 3,676 feet per second [1,120 m/s]. We've had no further communication with the crew of Apollo 16 since that original greeting from spacecraft Commander John Young. But we will continue to monitor and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0662733.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0662733.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 67 hours, 10 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We show the spacecraft Apollo 16 presently at a distance of 17,350 nautical miles [32,132 km] away from the Earth - away from the Moon, and traveling at a speed of 3,684 feet per second [1,123 m/s]. Meanwhile in the Mission Control Center, Flight Director Phil Shaffer has just decided that a Midcourse Correction Number 4 burn will not be required. We're at 67 hours, 11 minutes continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, we're waiting. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: You're all 85-foot dishes, right? Ears, I mean.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. [Laughter.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: All right, Henry. We'll start here on A section. [Long pause.] A-1, 22041; Alpha 3, 6½, outstanding; Alpha 4, none; Alpha 5, 27 and 5; Alpha 6, 7, 10, and 5. [Pause.] Bravo 1. [Pause.] Bravo 1, 15039; Bravo 3, 5, good; Bravo 4, none; Bravo 5, 37, 25; Bravo 6, 5, and 5. [Long pause.] Charlie 1, 21075; Charlie 3, 6, good; Charlie 4, none; Charlie 5, 15 and 15; Charlie 6, 5 - and - 5 and 7. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, was Charlie 6 just two entries, 5 and 7? [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: That's affirm. Okay, make that 5, 5, and 7.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: And off the gourmet sheet [garble]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Stand by, Ken. We're coming up on an antenna switch and we'll lose comm for a few minutes.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0671505.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 67 hours, 18 minutes into the mission. What you just heard was Ken Mattingly passing along the crew's biomedical report following a convenience format using letters and numbers for speed in reporting. For example, A is the Commander, B is the Command Module Pilot and C is the Lunar Module Pilot. The six pieces of data reported on were radiation dosimeter readings, food, this is a negative report when the crew member followed the planned menu, amount of sleep, medication, urine, and water consumed. At 67 hours, 19 minutes we show Apollo 16 at 17,033 nautical m

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: 16, Houston. [No answer.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Apollo 16, Houston. [No answer.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Apollo 16, Houston. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Young
a16_0671505.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. We're so far - You're so far out now that when we get close to antenna switching, we lose comm there for about a minute, a minute and a half. We're ready to copy the menu now; food. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Young
a16_0671505.text: Okay, our menu reporter is stealing a cup of coffee. He'll be with you in a second.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. And the Surgeon compliments the reporter on the way he reads the report down. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Young
a16_0671505.text: Yeah, when you've got a college education, you learn to read, and boy anything can happen after that. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, Henry. [Pause.] The happy gourmet says that for the Commander - Well, we'll start with meal A. And, stand by one. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, on the Commander, you can delete the grits. On Meal B, we - we skipped the Skylab meal as Meal B and then ate it as Meal C. And on that, we skipped the peanuts. [Pause.] And for the second meal on the day, John had a grapefruit drink, bread with peanut butter, and [pause] I guess that's it.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. On mine, you can start on Meal A. Scratch the peaches, the scrambled eggs, four bacon squares, grits. My Meal B: I had the bread and peanut butter and the grapefruit drink. On the Skylab meal, I had one of the two rye breads and - out of all this chicken spread, no one ate a third of it, that's - we probably ate a tenth of it apiece. [Pause.] And for Charlie, he's been good. He eats everything. None of us ate the peanuts on the Skylab meal. [Pause.] And for the second meal of the day, Charlie had an orange-pineapple drink with potassium, and peanut butter. And you'll be happy to know tha

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. Copy. That sounds kind of like it didn't work out too well. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Young
a16_0671505.text: There's a lot of peach still on Casper's face, I'll tell you that. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Duke
a16_0671505.text: Hank, when you open that can, you get them all at once. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Charlie, you're going to have to work on those guys about the grits.

a16_0671505.speaker: Duke
a16_0671505.text: Grits are good. I can't get them to eat them, though. They - I sur - ate part of John's. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, Hank. And maybe I missed it here, somewhere, but could you give us some words on what you plan to do about Midcourse 4? [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. No Midcourse 4. And, I got a couple items of news here, if you're interested in that. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. Is that general interest news, or like how we handle our relay setting and so forth?

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Oh, it's just general interest stuff on - We're coming up on antenna switching.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, we'll catch you after that.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0671505.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 67 hours, 27 minutes into the mission. As you heard, the crew of Apollo 16 sounds fresh and ready this morning. The principal spokesman for the crew thus far has been Ken Mattingly who provided the status reports. We show Apollo 16 at 16,736 nautical miles [30,995 km] away from the Moon. We now show the velocity of Apollo 16 at 3,699 feet per second [1,127 m/s]. At 67 hours, 28 minutes continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: 16, Houston.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Houston, you up yet?

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, 16. How do you read?

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, Henry. How about if we stop PTC right here at this 144-degree pass? [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Henry, did you copy that?

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, repeat no MCC-4 is required, and for your information, the data there for the UV photos is good for an hour after the Flight Plan time. So there's no real rush on that one. If you're ready to copy, we'll just charge right into these Flight Plan changes. The first one is at 70 hours and...

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, go.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: ...70 hours and 40 minutes. We want to write in there, "Charge Bat A," and that's, for your information, for about three hours and 20 minutes. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. At 70:40 we'll charge Battery A, and that's roughly going to be in three and a half hours.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. And at 71:20, we want to enter, "Load DAP with the weights and gimbal trim from MSFN, and call EMP 509." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. At 71:20, we'll load the DAP with MSFN weight and gimbals and call EMP 509.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. The next thing occurs at 73:55, at the sextant star check. Want to add, in parentheses, "No Verb 41. Manually - manual only with Verb 16 Noun 91." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. I've got at 73:55, at the sextant star check, we'll do no Verb 41 and we'll do it manual with 16 91 as our check.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That is affirmative. And EECOM advises you can...

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: While we're on that, Henry [pause] while we're on that one, Henry, I didn't see where we terminated 509. Do we keep it running all this time?

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That is affirmative. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Thank you.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. And EECOM advises you can go ahead and start that battery charge now, if you want to get Charlie started on that. And, next thing occurs at 74:08. And there we do the "Do SPS cue card through gimbal drive." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, that's at 74:08. It's SPS cue card through gimbal drive.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. And LOS - MSFN LOS time will be 74:18. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, 74:18 is LOS. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, that's the Flight Plan changes. I have some notes now. I don't know where's the best place to copy these. I've got about nine or ten of them here. Well, take it back. I got two notes on the use of EMP 509, and they read as follows.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, let me get my scratch pad out and I'll copy those first. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, Henry. I'm ready to copy your notes.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. Number one: the TVC DAP is unstable with EMP 509. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, understand. The TVC DAP is unstable with 509 running.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That is affirmative. And number two is, "At SPS cut-off plus 2.5 seconds, the TVC enable is de-energized." The EMP is off; thus, the platform alignment could be lost. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, and I have some Flight Plan changes now that are concerned with DOI. The first one occurs at seven...

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Stand by a second.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, Henry. I'm ready. These are comments, or these are things to go into the Flight Plan?

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. These are Flight Plan changes, Ken. I'm sorry I didn't get this in order a while ago. It was buried in the bottom here. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, at 77:57, there's a group of CSM systems checks. Move those up to 77:20. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, we take the CSM systems checks and move them from 77:58 over to 77:20.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. Now at 77:50, "Verb 48 21101 01111." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. At 77:50, that's "Verb 48 and 21101 01111."

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative, and immediately following that, "Start EMP 509." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, Henry. I guess I don't quite understand the loading the - the Verb 48 into 21101, and then the next thing we do is to load a three in there. Could you have someone give me some rationale on that?

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: The difference there, Ken, is you, once, when you're loading that Verb 48 for the - the EMP 509, you don't Pro on that one and activate that DAP. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, I see what you're saying. Alright.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: In other words, we have to get the right DAP in there before we do the EMP 509. The next item is the activities that are located between 78:03 and 78:08, we want to move back to just following the P52 at 77:53. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. How about giving me the first line and last line on the block you're talking about.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, that's "P30, verify DOI T IG and Delta-Vs" through "Acquire MSFN Omni D." Move all of that back to just following the P52, or "landing site orient" at 77:53. [Long pause.] And in that group of activities, we want to delete that Verb 48. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, now what I have is - have you got any more changes to this area, and then I'll read you what I have sequentially.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: There's nothing more on that particular page, 77 through 78 hours. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. Maybe I missed something here, but I have - I have not seen us - terminate 509. I'm sure we did somewhere before the LOI burn...

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Uh [garble].

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: [Garble] and we'll do it again.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: We're going to get to do - in that Ken, we're going to have that on your cue card. I've got cue card change coming up for you.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. All right, let me give you what I have here and then - At 77:20, I do all the CSM systems checklist items that are listed now at 77:58. At 77:50, we do a Verb 48 21101 01111. We start EMP 509. Then, at about 77:55, we do all the steps which are presently listed at 78:03 down through 78:08.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: And that's with the exception of the Verb 48.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: That's right; with the exception of Verb 48.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, that's all correct. Now, the next item is, at 78:22, we delete the sextant star check and move it back to 78:15. And it carries the same warning as we had before. No Verb 41, manual only with the Verb 16 Noun 91. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, that's a sextant star check at 78:15 with no Verb 41, doing it manually and deleting the star check at 78:22.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. And the last item for this is, at 78:18 add "Do SPS cue card through gimbal drive." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay; that's at 78:18, it's "Do SPS cue card through gimbal drive."

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. And the cue card that you'll use is the same for LOI and DOI. We're going to read you those changes.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. Just as a note here for yourself. You load the DAP before starting the card, and you do not change Verb 48 after starting EMP 509. Now, we tried to indicate that in the Flight Plan, and I explained that to you while ago. Okay, first step: at the top of the card, the very first item, add "EMP 509 called." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, at the very top of the card, it's "EMP 509 is called."

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. And down at the fifth item, where it says "Load DAP," delete that. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, we'll delete "Load DAP."

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: At where it says "Boresight & sextant star check," delete the "Verb 41 Noun 91 Enter," and make the comment: "No Verb 41, manual only with Verb 16 Noun 91." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, we delete "Verb 41 Noun 91," and we say "No Verb 41, manual Verb 16 Noun 91."

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. At the left of the card opposite "Main bus ties," where it says "54 minutes," change that to "40 minutes," and in parentheses "Minus 20 minutes." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, we've changed "54 minutes" to "40 minutes," and "Minus 6" to "Minus 20."

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Roger. And down a little further where it says "55 and 5," we want to change that to "41 and minus 19." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. We've changed "55" to "41" and "minus 5" to "minus 19." [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, on the back side of the card - Let me read you the whole thing we want to get in there, Ken, so you'll know how to squeeze it. Right after it says "Accept parentheses Pro," we want to get in there, "If glitch occurs, use RHC to stop maneuver, Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter Enter, Verb 40 Enter, Verb 62 Enter. Manual maneuver to attitude," so you have to kind of squeeze that in there a little bit. I'll read it to you slowly now. "If glitch occurs...

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, stand by a second. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, go ahead, Hank.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay. "If glitch occurs, use RHC to stop maneuver. Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter Enter. Verb 40 Enter. Verb 62 Enter. Manual maneuver to attitude." [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0671505.text: Apollo Control, Houston; 67 hours, 50 minutes into the mission. We're listening to CapCom Hank Hartsfield pass along Flight Plan updates to the crew of Apollo 16.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, now, this says that - this is after the Pro on gimbal test, and we're saying that if we - you get one of these glitches, use the RHC to stop the rates. Would there be any objection to just switching to SCS while we do the rest of this, and that's my question. Now I'll read on. It's "Verb 23 Noun 20 Enter Enter," and I have a question there, is that - I got the impression from what we were saying in our previous discussion that this wasn't restricted just to the middle gimbal; it's a possibility for - for the others. And then a "Verb 40 Enter," which will release the platform. Verb 62 wil

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Okay, I - I'm a little puzzled about the Verb 62 needles. However, on the other item, the reason you only need a Verb 23 is that the - that zeros that CDU, which is the only one that locks you up in coarse align, and the others will reinitialize when we do the Verb 40. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, I guess my question, though, is that, if it can happen in each of them, the only time you do the Verb 23 Noun 20 would be in the event that it did lock into the coarse align. [Pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. Guido was just saying you cover all bets when you do this, and you don't have to stop and think about it.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay, but if you had moved off in yaw, it seems to me I would be possibly introducing more error. [Long pause.]

a16_0671505.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0671505.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 67 hours, 53 minutes into the mission. Apollo 16 now 15,800 nautical miles [29,262 km] away from the Moon, and now traveling at a speed of 3,723 feet per second [1,135 m/s]. Continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: Ken, would you - would you state your concern again so we've got a clear picture of it.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay - maybe I'm off on a tangent. What it looked to me like is that if you pick up one of these glitches, I'm not sure that the rates are all going to be confined to just - just one axis by the time it stops, and if you then take and load Register 3 and Noun 20 to zeros, you may, in fact be at some other middle gimbal angle than zero. So, once you do that - I guess that - that has no effect if I do a Verb 40, huh? I guess that's the - I missed that point. That merely gets me out of the coarse align, and...

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That - that's affirmative.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: ...Verb 40 will be initialized. Is that correct?

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: That's affirmative. The Verb 40 starts the whole thing running again.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay.

a16_0671505.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0671505.text: The Verb 23 Noun 20 gets you out of the gimbal lock, if that's to be - if that's the case.

a16_0671505.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0671505.text: Okay. Now I'm with you. Now I guess the only other thing is that, in the event that we have the thing we had - that happened the other night and it did coarse align there, it seems to me that, before I do the Verb 40, I would want to fly back on SCS to zero middle gimbal angle.
