a16_0714622.text: Okay, Ken. Good enough; thank you.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay, Don. I'm - I got some free hands now, and got my little note pad out, and I'm ready to listen and copy and discuss anything you got on this stuff.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay; would you say again how we're gonna handle P - normally P20 option 5; we will not use 509. Is that correct?

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: That's affirmative. We will not use 509 during P20 option 5.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay. And when we come to do a P52, we will still not use the option - the 509 - we're gonna go to SCS control and use the Rate High and Max Deadband. Is that correct?

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Okay; Rate High and Max Deadband's okay, but the G&C tells me you really - that the Deadband - you don't need to go to Max, it's - it's kind of immaterial which position you put that switch in. You do need the Rate switch in High, and you need BMAG Mode, Rate 2. That way you don't have an attitude control situation. You have a rate control situation, but the level is high enough that it's well above the orb rate, and so the SCS will be equivalent to going CMC, Free.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay; I understand that. Thank you.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Okeydoke; and...

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: I'll leave it in Deadband, Min and Rate, High.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Roger. And we'll get more details to you later on the P24 and the rendezvous. [Pause.]

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay. Doing good work. [Long pause.]

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Ken, there's one other comment here. If you are gonna, at some point in lunar orbit, do quite a bit of Optics switching, like Manual and Automatic and that sort of thing, we would suggest in that case that you load EMP 509 before you start playing with the optics and take it out again when you're finished. [Pause.]

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay; anytime we're doing that - I assume that means like in - when we're doing the landmark tracking, both High and Low, and it's my understanding from the comments we got now that the only time 509 can get me in trouble is if I leave it enabled during thrusting.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: That in general is...

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: ...and also [garble] the automatic gimbal stop.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: That's absolutely correct, Ken. Those are the two cases.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: All right, sir. Thank you very much. Hey, you might tell Tom Holloway that his little note pad has really come in handy. That's super.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: He's sitting here smiling and giving me the thumbs up right now. [Long pause.]

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Charlie just asked that everybody lock the doors until he finds his pea soup.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0715423.text: This is Apollo Control; 72 hours, 1 minute Ground Elapsed Time. Two hours, 15 minutes prior to the time of Apollo 16 passes behind the Moon [on] the beginning of the first lunar orbit. The crew has moved up their meal period a few moments earlier than scheduled in the flight plan, and are now having their noon meal. Spacecraft presently 6,322 nautical miles [11,708 km] out from the Moon, approaching at a velocity of 4,281 feet per second [1,304 m/s]. Continuing to stand by as we approach lunar orbit. Maneuver for lunar orbit coming up in a few hours, about two hours and 26 minutes from now. [A

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Don, how about if I put off this scan ratio thing another ten minutes?

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Stand by one.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Okay, we're going ahead and get it out.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Okay.

a16_0715423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0715423.text: Shield is Off at this time; we'll turn back in ten minutes.

a16_0715423.speaker: Peterson
a16_0715423.text: Roger.

a16_0720531.speaker: Duke
a16_0720531.text: Okay, Pete. Go ahead with your P30 PAD.

a16_0720531.speaker: Peterson
a16_0720531.text: Stand by just a minute, Charlie. [Pause.]

a16_0720531.speaker: Peterson
a16_0720531.text: Okay, Charlie. TEI-4, SPS/G&N; 41534; plus 0.64, plus 1.35; 083:07:14.13; plus 3289.6, plus 1150.1, minus 0327.6; 181, 056, 022. The rest of the PAD is NA. Set stars, Sirius and Rigel; 131; 071; 014. Ullage, two jet, 17 seconds. Under Other: 1, burn undocked; 2, assumes no DOI; 3, assumes landing site REFSMMAT; [pause] 4, with LOI REFSMMAT; roll, 179; pitch, 183; yaw, 014. [Long pause.]

a16_0720531.speaker: Duke
a16_0720531.text: Okay, Houston. TEI-4 is SPS/G&N; 41534; plus 0.64, plus 1.35; 083:07:14.13; plus 3289.6, plus 1150.1, minus 0327.6; 181, 056, 022. Sirius and Rigel; 131; 071; 014; two jets, 17 seconds. One is burn is undocked; 2, assumes no DOI; 3, landing site REFSMMAT; 4, LOI REFSMMAT; 179; 183; 014. Over.

a16_0721302.speaker: Duke
a16_0721302.text: Pete, 16 here. Looking through the telescope at the Earth - It's sure apparent that we live on a pretty planet. The colors are just such, more such, more such - a lot more vivid [laughter] than any of the photographs. [Pause.]

a16_0721302.speaker: Peterson
a16_0721302.text: Roger. We understand. We were just sitting here enjoying some of the beauties of Earth ourselves. [Pause.]

a16_0721302.speaker: Young
a16_0721302.text: I'm wise to you new people. [Pause.]

a16_0721302.speaker: Duke
a16_0721302.text: How many pots has the MOCR gone through already?

a16_0721302.speaker: Peterson
a16_0721302.text: We'll have to get you a count, but Gerry says it's a new record.

a16_0723012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723012.text: Okay. Map update, Rev 1. LOS: 074:17:41; 180 degrees: 074:31:39. AOS with LOI: 074:50:05; without LOI: 074:42:08. [Pause.]

a16_0723012.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723012.text: That's affirmative. Okay. Now, Ken, on this other question. As we understood your question, you're concerned about what happens after - at 2.5 seconds after the burn when you switch back to the RCS DAP and cycle this relay. What happens if you get the glitch, and it looks like there are two cases. Either you get a - a yaw glitch of sufficient magnitude to put you into coarse align, or you get some kind of glitch that could be in roll, pitch, or yaw but does not put you into coarse align. If you go into coarse align, the nav is no good, and the Noun 85s are no good, and in that case, we'd like

a16_0723012.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0723012.text: Particularly in LOI, since there's no trim; that's only a problem for - for recording purposes anyhow.

a16_0723932.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723932.text: Okay. At 79:29 right at the bottom of the page there, we want to add "Load EMP 509," and at 79:3...

a16_0723932.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723932.text: That's affirmative. After. It should follow the "Load Noun 89." [Pause.]

a16_0723932.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723932.text: That's affirmative. And at 79:38, we want to delete the Verb 48 there, and that's not associated with the 509. That's simply because that's redundant. You're already in that DAP configuration. [Pause.]

a16_0723932.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723932.text: And at - 79:42 right after the MSFN update block there, add "Terminate EMP 509 after P24 completed." [Long pause.]

a16_0723932.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0723932.text: Okay "Terminate 509 after P24 is completed." Now let me - Is that the last one or you got some more?

a16_0723932.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0723932.text: Okay. Let me read them back to you where I've got them to make sure I have it all right. At about 79:29½ on the page, I've written "Load 509." I have deleted the Verb 48 which occurs at 79:38. At 79:41 - 42, I've got "Terminate 509 after P24 is completed."

a16_0723932.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0723932.text: And, Don, on this first rev, if we wanted to take some pictures or something, can we stick with magazine November November? I can't tell right now what that's scheduled for. Or should we use magazine Victor?

a16_0723932.speaker: Peterson
a16_0723932.text: Stand by. We'll let you know.

a16_0724438.speaker: Peterson
a16_0724438.text: Casper, November November looks pretty low on the PAD. You should go to magazine Victor.

a16_0724816.speaker: Peterson
a16_0724816.text: 16, Houston. We've got a couple more words on the LM paint-peeling problem. Apparently, it has been duplicated now in a vacuum chamber, and it does not appear to be any kind of a problem as far as the mission is concerned. [Pause.]

a16_0724816.speaker: Young
a16_0724816.text: Well, that's fine to hear. Thank you now.

a16_0724816.speaker: Peterson
a16_0724816.text: Rog. It's nothing leaking; it's just the paint itself. [Pause.]

a16_0725210.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0725210.text: Don, we're getting ready to start into the secondary glycol loop check. [Pause.]

a16_0725210.speaker: Peterson
a16_0725210.text: Okay. We're ready to follow. [Long pause.]

a16_0725210.speaker: Young
a16_0725210.text: Okay. The Secondary Cool Loop Pump is about to go Off.

a16_0725210.speaker: Young
a16_0725210.text: Pump AC1's On on the Secondary Loop.

a16_0725210.speaker: Young
a16_0725210.text: Okay. And we see the outlet temperature decreasing.

a16_0725628.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0725628.text: Houston, 16. Are y'all satisfied with the nitrogen pressures on the SPS?

a16_0730223.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0730223.text: Got so many [garble] You can see all the - you know, you can see all the prominent features and little sharp craters like - I think I'm looking at Kepler. It's out there in the middle of the mare. It's just beautiful. And that's all Earthshine.

a16_0730223.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0730223.text: Yeah, and it - it just about - it's like two-thirds of the window, and I've got my head no more than 6 inches from it. You know, the - on the dark side, you can see a big dark disk, and I think the reason I can see it is it's the solar corona that's illuminating around the back side. And I can see a star within - well, maybe it's within a degree of the Moon's disk.

a16_0730223.speaker: Peterson
a16_0730223.text: Could we have the LMP confirm that that's really the Moon and not the Earth you're looking at?

a16_0730223.speaker: Duke
a16_0730223.text: Hey, babe, this is really the Moon. It's the most awe-inspiring sight I've ever seen in my life. Looks like the door that just hung out there in the middle of blackness. It's really beautiful, Pete.

a16_0730223.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0730223.text: And you can make out all the features on the thing. I can see [garble], and you can see up into the Procellarum - and in the basins in there. You can even see the outer rings of Orientale. And you can't see the basin itself but you can see it's outer rings. [Pause.]

a16_0730223.speaker: Young
a16_0730223.text: And looking at our present orientation, I can tell that our new attitude will be perfect for LOI. [Pause.]

a16_0730223.speaker: Peterson
a16_0730223.text: Ken, just for your information - The reading that you got when you zeroed the optics on the Noun 91s there was considered normal, and it's like a single-bit - or less than a single-bit error. And the other thing I wanted to pass on was that this EMP 509 has been verified by MIT for use with P24 and during rendezvous.

a16_0730223.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0730223.text: Don, we're gonna waste the two frames of VHBW. Could you tell me if it's better to - to use SS or TT?

a16_0730223.speaker: MCC
a16_0730223.text: If you dial up channel 6, you can see a plot of the parameters on the primary coolant. [Long pause.]

a16_0731039.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0731039.text: Okay. I'm up to three exposures on magazine TT.

a16_0731039.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0731039.text: Houston, 16. Do you have any objections to our going to the burn attitude now?

a16_0731039.speaker: Young
a16_0731039.text: Was that affirmative or negative? Over.

a16_0731039.speaker: Peterson
a16_0731039.text: 16, give us P00 and Accept, and we'll give you your uplinks, and then you can maneuver. [Pause.]

a16_0731408.speaker: Young
a16_0731408.text: Okay, Houston. The reason we would like to go now is it looks to me like you can't get there without going through gimbal lock, but we want to see what the DAP wants us to do.

a16_0731408.speaker: Peterson
a16_0731408.text: Okay. LOI, SPS/G&N; 66314; plus 1.21, minus 0.14, 074:28:27.22; minus 2781.6, minus 0219.6, minus 0256.2; 000, 001, 000; Noun 44s, 0170.0, plus 0058.3; 2802.0, 6:14, 2794.7; sextant star 16, 242.9, 27.1. Rest of the PAD is NA. Set stars, Sirius and Rigel; 132; 196; 006. Ullage, none. LM weight, 36287. Single-bank burn time, 6:28. [Pause.]

a16_0731408.speaker: Duke
a16_0731408.text: Okay. We copy LOI, SPS/G&N; 66314; plus 1.21, minus 0.14; 074:28:27.22; minus 2781.6, minus 0219.6, minus 0256.2; 000, 001, 000; 0170.0, plus 0058.3; 2802.0, 6:14; 2794.7; 16, 242.9, 27.1. Rest of the PAD is NA. Sirius and Rigel; 132; 196; 006. No ullage. LM weight, 36287. Single bank burn time, 6:28. Over.

a16_0732832.speaker: Duke
a16_0732832.text: I read you five by. You're on Omni Delta.

a16_0733231.speaker: Duke
a16_0733231.text: Okay. We're going to the sextant star check.

a16_0733601.speaker: Young
a16_0733601.text: [Garble] sitting right in the middle there, Houston.

a16_0735655.speaker: Peterson
a16_0735655.text: 16, would you stow the High Gain Antenna, please?

a16_0741222.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741222.text: Houston, we're preparing for the gimbal drive check.

a16_0741222.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741222.text: Okay, we've completed the gimbal drive check. We're now going to terminate 509.

a16_0741222.speaker: Young
a16_0741222.text: Okay, 509's out of there. How's it look?

a16_0741543.speaker: Peterson
a16_0741543.text: 16, we're a couple minutes from LOS. See you on the next pass. [Pause.]

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Yeah. You can turn it on [garble].

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Hey, we got something in that kit that'll clear your sinuses up?

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Yeah, I need to do something; this thing's getting worse.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Well, we checked the switches three times. I guess it wouldn't hurt to check them again. (Laughter) Okay [garble]. Popped.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: It's on Panel 229 over there, Charlie. It's [garble]...

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: I ain't heard a thing pop.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Say that did kind of head out?

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Ooh. I think I was right.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: That guy had died. My nose ain't that stopped up. All that goes through is the odors, no oxygen.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Whew! I see what you mean. That was me.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Smells a long time [garble]. You guys are putting that on the tape, too [garble].

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Just be glad they don't have a gas inlet around here.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Oh, machine, do your thing. I won't badmouth you for being a marshmallow again.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: We going to burn, we come into daylight.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: No, don't look, we got too many - too many things going bad for us to look this time. Look after the burn. Get right there and then you get [garble]. Phew!

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Okay, gonna do it right in one minute [garble]. Stand by.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Translation Power, we don't need. The light is out. Delta-V Thrust A is coming on -

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Okay, average g is on. It's counting. Looks good, though.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: A's open. SPS - Okay, lights are out.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: I felt a - seemed like they dropped.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Pressure's looking great here. Helium valves are open. PUGS is looking good.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: I can feel that sucker bring that second bank on.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Okay. We - I see it in the reflection in the LM windows.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Keep your eye on them, babe.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: What was the alarm at the start?

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: I am. I got them, babe.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: It went out, whatever it was. I think it was a overpressure on the SPS; now it's back nominal.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Okay, fuel's running a little low. It's running about 165. Coming up on a minute.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Chamber pressure's staying, and - coming up a little bit, maybe. Up 92.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Okay. Doesn't register on the g meter (laughter). Okay, gimbals are still steady.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Chamber pressure's going up a little.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Yeah, I gave you bum dope. I was calling that 90, but it was 95.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: That's really 96 psi on the chamber pressure.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Attitudes are holding. How do the two Delta-Vs compare, John?

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Delta-Vs compare pretty close, as matter of fact.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Yeah, ten apart. Lot closer than in the simulator.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Yeah. You're gonna make me nervous [garble].

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: CMC's right on, with my time. PUGS is about 100, unbalanced, and holding. Decrease.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: [Garble]. Looks like it's working, doesn't it?

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Okay, we got 150 on the PUGS, unbalanced, decrease.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Okay. Don says that if we watch it go, it'll go down to about - almost 200 and then work its way back up.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: Okay. Three minutes. Right on time.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Man, that thing is - their prediction is right on this.

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: EMS and the Delta-V to go are right together. Perfect.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Stand by for the tight limits -

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Mark. Tight limits. We're at 200; unbalanced; jiggling around a little bit; decrease.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Coming up on 4 minutes. SPS pressures are rock solid.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: I'm not, I'm looking at the gages. I was having a little bias back there. Okay?

a16_0741700.speaker: Young
a16_0741700.text: EMS and this thing are right together. Couldn't be any closer.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: It looks like we've had crossover.

a16_0741700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0741700.text: Okay. My chamber pressure very smoothly increased to 100.

a16_0741700.speaker: Duke
a16_0741700.text: Okay, and the unbalance went a back - that's jiggling around on zero. Stand by.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0743300.text: This is Apollo Control at 74 hours, 33 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The Lunar Orbit Insertion burn presumably still underway at this time having a six minute, 14 second duration, an ignition time of 74 hours, 28 minutes, 27 seconds. And if the burn is successful, completely normal, the spacecraft will come around the east rim of the Moon in 16 minutes, 30 seconds. That would be at a Ground Elapsed Time of 74 hours, 42 minutes, 8 seconds. However, if for some reason, the burn is not successful or we have no ignition on the Service Propulsion System engine, the spacecraft will reappear much soon

a16_0743300.speaker: Duke
a16_0743300.text: Mark; five minutes. Unbalance is 150, decrease. Looking great.

a16_0743300.speaker: Duke
a16_0743300.text: Helium's down to 1800. Nitrogen's looking great.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Man, that time is gonna be 06:14.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Casper, you're gonna lose your bar [?].

a16_0743300.speaker: Young
a16_0743300.text: At shutdown, maybe we can get another light [garble].

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Not gonna get there early. Got ten seconds overburn to worry about.

a16_0743300.speaker: Duke
a16_0743300.text: Yeah. 100, decrease, unbalance, looking super, 40 percent. Six minutes...

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: ...four. Okay. We've done our thing. We didn't get anything here. You want to...

a16_0743300.speaker: Young
a16_0743300.text: Plus 0.2, minus one -minus zero, minus one. We got to look at 1620, right?

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Okay, get the - Delta-Vs now - I mean, Delta-V, 20.

a16_0743300.speaker: Young
a16_0743300.text: Okay. Enter. Okay, now let's - Roll's fine...

a16_0743300.speaker: Duke
a16_0743300.text: Good, yeah. Let's go with the gimbal motors.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Okay. Wait a minute now. Let me see if we got everything here. Gimbal Motors, four, Off. Okay. Main B.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Okay. Servo Power. Go ahead and go to P00. I'll do this one. Two, Off.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: Okay, hand controllers are locked. Directs, Off.

a16_0743300.speaker: Young
a16_0743300.text: Circuit breaker, Pitch 1, Yaw 1. I sure got that.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0743300.text: BMAGS, three, to Rate 2. Bus Ties are Off, Charlie?

a16_0743300.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0743300.text: This is Apollo Control at 74 hours, 41 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Less than a minute away from the time at which the spacecraft should come around the corner of the Moon assuming we had not a successful Lunar Orbit Insertion burn. The acquisition time with the normal burn would be at 74 hours, 50 minutes, 5 seconds; some eight minutes and eight seconds away from this point. Mark.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0743300.text: No noise on the down link. Apparently the spacecraft did have a successful burn. To repeat the acquisition time with a successful burn; 74 hours, 50 minutes, 5 seconds. At 74:42 Ground Elapsed Time, this is Apollo Control.

a16_0743300.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0743300.text: This is Apollo Control; less than a minute away from Acquisition Of Signal from Apollo 16, and it appears at least from the timing, that we have indeed had a successful Lunar Orbit Insertion burn, which according to pre-burn planning, should produce an elliptical orbit around the Moon, with a pericynthion of 58.3 nautical miles [108 km], [and an] apocynthion of 170 nautical miles [315 km]. We'll stand by here for the first words from the crew and the burn report. Displays being changed here in the Control Center from the Earth-Moon transit display in the center scribing plotter to the Lunar Or

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Roger, 16. Copy you loud and clear.

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Okay, Pete. Super double fantastic burn. If you're ready, I'll give you a burn status report.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Okay, go ahead, John.

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Okay, Delta-T IG was 0615 burn - 06:15.1 burn time, plus 2803.9, trim [garble]; residuals, plus 0.2, minus zero, minus 0.1. Delta-V C is minus 5.5; fuel, 376, Ox, 371; 150, unbalance, decrease. Okay, at ignition, we got a momentary SPS light; then it went out. During the burn, the Oxidizer pressure read 200. The Fuel side was a little bit low, and it was about 165 on my gauge. After shutdown, the Fuel side climbed to 170. The Oxidizer went to about 202 with an SPS light, and we've still got it. Over.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Roger. We copied everything except the roll, pitch, and yaw, which was blacked out by some noise.

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Okay, the trim attitude - we did not trim. The residuals were as we gave you after the burn. Our attitude was 005, 358, 002. Over.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Roger. We copy. [Pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: And it was a slight transient, when the second bank was lit, that I don't remember from previous burns. You might look at that data, but it was super.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Rog. Copy.

a16_0744912.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0744912.text: And it appeared to me that the chamber pressure had dropped off just as we brought the second bank on. [Pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: And as you can see, we're in 170.4 by 58.3 [nautical miles - 315.6 by 108 km] according to the old computer, and that baby just rifled it right down the line.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: All righty.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Roger.

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: You can see those little dark - those little dark - look like volcanic black spots up - up in the north sector of it, and you can see the central peaks with a - with a varied - very white central peaks covered by lighter gray - gray-brown material that sort of looked like somebody painted it on there with a - with a - with a paintbrush. [Long pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: And, Pete, your first view at Tsiolkovsky out of my window is pretty - it's a spectacular sight; the way that - looks like a marshmallow float - a central peak floating in the top of a hot chocolate.

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: Yeah, you - it - it's like - three guys - they've each got a window, and we're staring at the - at the ground. It's really - Boy, this has got to be the neatest way to make a living anybody's ever invented.

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Pete, 16 here. Another pretty sight we had before burn was the Earthset. It - really quite a view. [Pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: We're all sitting here listening, Charlie. Tell us about it. [Long pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Pete, you got - a - Mapping - or the Pan Camera Power's - is On?

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Okay, Pan Camera Power, On. [Long pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: How'd the S-IVB look? [Pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: It hadn't happened yet, John. It's about another - nine minutes or so. [Long pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: I - I trust we're not getting there the same time it does.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: I trust.

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: Okay.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: It - it's going to hit on the southwest corner of Reinhold, Ken.

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: Say again, Pete.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Tell Ken it's going to hit on the southwest corner of Reinhold. He should know where that is.

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: I'm sure he does.

a16_0744912.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0744912.text: Okay. Let me get the binoculars out here - playing with them there. It's pretty interesting. I tell you, all that time spent with Farouk sure is going to pay off, because it does look like old home.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: That's good, Ken.

a16_0744912.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0744912.text: The lawn needs mowing and all that. [Pause.]

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Okay, Casper, Pan Camera Power, Off.

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Rog.

a16_0744912.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0744912.text: This is Apollo Control; 75 hours, 1 minute Ground Elapsed Time. Completely successful Lunar Orbit Insertion burn, with a duration of six minutes and 15 seconds. Reported on board measurements on the lunar orbit; 58.3 by 170.4 nautical miles [108.0 by 315.6 km]. We'll continue to monitor this first front-side pass and Lunar Orbit Number 1. At 75:02, this is Apollo Control.

a16_0744912.speaker: Duke
a16_0744912.text: Pete, looking out at the horizon, you can really tell you're in the highlands. The horizon is really jagged looking.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Looks like coming up on the Rockies, huh?

a16_0744912.speaker: Young
a16_0744912.text: Of course, we're start - we're starting to come up over the flatlands now, over the Smyth Sea. I remember a landmarking track down there on Apollo 10. It's still there. You can't really tell by looking at it that the Smyth Sea is any - any deeper or lower than the data shows it is right in the surrounding terrain.

a16_0744912.speaker: Peterson
a16_0744912.text: Roger.

a16_0750617.speaker: Young
a16_0750617.text: The submerged craters in Smythii remind me a lot of a - coral atolls. They just got the ridges sticking up, you know, and the - and the bottoms of them appear to be flooded with the same material that's in Smyth. [Pause.]

a16_0750617.speaker: Peterson
a16_0750617.text: We're digging out a map now, 16, to take a look at it. [Long pause.]

a16_0750617.speaker: Young
a16_0750617.text: We're going to get a close-in picture of Humboldt here, as we come up, because we'll probably miss it on the next round.

a16_0750617.speaker: Young
a16_0750617.text: That's real - it's really a fascinating crater, the way the dark mare has got in - sort of like a path around the edges, and - and there's a fracture pattern running across it, and it has some very prominent central peaks that are very white. But it has every contrast and color on the Moon.

a16_0750617.speaker: Young
a16_0750617.text: Boy, those fracture patterns running down through it are white - appear to be white, layered fracture patterns. They look like somebody's drawn them on there with a piece of chalk. [Long pause.]

a16_0750617.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0750617.text: Seismograph traces beginning to show of the S-IVB impact at approximately 75:09, Ground Elapsed Time.

a16_0751315.speaker: Duke
a16_0751315.text: Houston, out my window is fine now. We got Petavius with it's central dome of - a whitish cap - dome, and it's a fairly subdued crater. The lineations running into it - the rilles or whatever they are - are just like it's drawn on the map here.

a16_0751315.speaker: Young
a16_0751315.text: Some of those central domes are exceptionally dark, and they have exceptionally dark material running down a white surface. You can see that.

a16_0751603.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0751603.text: With the binoculars, we passed over Langrenus, and you can see blocks on the tops of the central peak, and some features that probably are there that I just haven't noticed before in that central feature. You can see an awful lot of - looks like a - the demarcation where the central feature - looks like a crack in it - has a whole ring of craters that kind of dots that boundary. And then, you see some more of those little craters up along near the top of the central lineament also. And you just don't see those kind of things stand out at you without the binoculars.

a16_0751603.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0751603.text: I could also say that the binoculars at ten power is the maximum you can hold in your hand. You got to get yourself set up very nicely for it before you start.

a16_0751603.speaker: Young
a16_0751603.text: And we're coming up over the Messier A and B Craters.

a16_0751603.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0751603.text: This is Apollo Control at 75 hours, 18 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Crew of Apollo 16 still three tourists in their first lunar orbit observing the features of the Moon, calling out various craters as they pass over them. [The] S-IVB impacted the lunar surface at about 75:09. Signals are still coming to the ALSEP, coming out on the recording graph of the normal lunar seismic activity made rather straight line up until the time of impact and the strokes of the recorder are broadening continuously as the seismic waves travel through the Moon to the ALSEP site. Some 55 minutes until Loss of Signa

a16_0751603.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0751603.text: This is Apollo Control at 75:20. Apollo 16 Commander John Young becomes the first human to go into lunar orbit twice, having flown on Apollo 10 which is a precursor to the landing missions. [The] Apollo 10 mission descended to within about eight miles of the lunar surface and the, that is the Lunar Module did. Jim Lovell has been to the Moon twice, but the second trip, the first having been Apollo 8 the first manned lunar orbit mission. The second being in Apollo 13, which was an aborted mission and coasted past the Moon and, therefore, Lovell did not go into lunar orbit on his second trip. At

a16_0752326.speaker: Duke
a16_0752326.text: Houston, we're coming up on Theophilus now. Central peak's in the shadows, and the - As we approach the terminator, looking out towards the horizon, it really looks rugged.

a16_0752326.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0752326.text: This is Apollo Control. Members of the Orange Team of flight controllers under Pete Frank are beginning to drift into the room for the change of shift handover at 4 pm Central Time. We're estimating the change of shift press briefing in the Small Briefing Room, Building 1 Press Center, for 4 o'clock, somewhat earlier than would be normal, normally the case, with Flight Director Gerry Griffin.

a16_0752326.speaker: Peterson
a16_0752326.text: 16, if you'll give us the computer and go Accept, we'll give you a REFSMMAT. [Pause.]

a16_0752326.speaker: Young
a16_0752326.text: Just now looking at the Altai Scarp and, boy, it's well named in this lighting.

a16_0752326.speaker: Young
a16_0752326.text: Looks like the walls are vertical. I'll admit the lighting exaggerates it, but that's how it looks.

a16_0752326.speaker: Peterson
a16_0752326.text: And, 16, we're finished with the up-link. [Pause.]

a16_0752326.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0752326.text: You should be able to. Be right at the terminator.

a16_0752326.speaker: Young
a16_0752326.text: Trouble with the terminator, this Moon is so ragged, I can't - do it even. I'll get a decent terminator shot.

a16_0752326.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0752326.text: I'll take care of all that. Okay, there's Taylor, Taylor A [garble] Zöllner - then we have to have [garble] Descartes. That is Descartes, right there. See the - [garble]?

a16_0752828.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0752828.text: Right down - Here, let me - get to this window; I'll show you. Right there? The crater Descartes.

a16_0752828.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0752828.text: In this lighting, you can see the Crater Descartes, and it stands out much bigger than you would expect, because of the low Sun angle. And - in fact I had to look into my map in order to make sure that was what I was looking at. And the material that runs out of it - that - that's in the area, are the things we talk about as being that bright reflective area, in this low Sun angle, has a much blockier and jumbled appearance than it does on any of the high-Sun photographs.

a16_0752828.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0752828.text: It looks very much like looking down on a clinkery - a big clinkery cinder field, but on a much larger scale.

a16_0752828.speaker: Young
a16_0752828.text: Yeah, a big - a rounded surface of clinkers. It's fantastic. Boy, is that rough! [Long pause.]

a16_0752828.speaker: Duke
a16_0752828.text: Okay, Houston, as we look to the west and to past the terminator, there's - a couple of degrees past the terminator, there's one bright spot, a peak standing up which is west of [pause] well, west of Kant. [Pause.]

a16_0752828.speaker: Peterson
a16_0752828.text: Right after you started talking about this peak and you said something like "west of," you faded out. [Long pause.]

a16_0752828.speaker: Young
a16_0752828.text: Yeah, the general opinion here is that we may be looking at part of Smoky Mountain sticking up through some - through the shadows.

a16_0752828.speaker: Peterson
a16_0752828.text: Houston, 16, FAO advises you've got some extra film on Magazine UU - that's VHBW, and you can use it for targets of opportunity, and you can use the CEX exposure graph and stop down one stop from what you get off the graph. [Pause.]

a16_0752828.speaker: Peterson
a16_0752828.text: And, Casper, on that last transmission - As an example, f/11 for the CEX, you should go to f/16 to use with Magazine UU.

a16_0753652.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0753652.text: Don, I'd like to verify how we're going to do the P52 again now. Any ideas that we'll go to place the SCS Controls into Rate, High, and Deadband is Min. At the proper time, I'll - I've got the BMAGs in Rate 2, I'll go to SCS Control, and then I don't have to worry about loading 509. And I'll just go ahead and do the P52. And then when we're through, I can go back to CMC Control. Is that correct?

a16_0753652.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0753652.text: This is Apollo Control, at 75:39 Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 approaching the lunar terminator or sundown; in about four minutes. At the present time, the crew is conducting a Program 52 realignment of the Inertial Measuring Unit - Inertial Measurement Unit in the guidance system. To repeat again, the change of shift press briefing with Flight Director Gerry Griffin will be about 4 o'clock Central Time at the Houston News Center Briefing Room. At 75:39, this Apollo Control.

a16_0753900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0753900.text: Hey, Don, we're trying to set up the - the camera for the next terminator and sunrise, and I thought I understood what you told me about the settings, but I guess I don't. Can you run through that again? I guess I just as soon have you just give me the proper settings.

a16_0753900.speaker: Peterson
a16_0753900.text: You're talking about this Magazine UU that I just called up?

a16_0753900.speaker: Peterson
a16_0753900.text: Ken, they - they're get - looking that up for us right now. And in the meantime, I'll try to give you the rule again. Maybe that'll clear it up some. You can use that CEX exposure graph that you have on board, and take the readings off of that.

a16_0753900.speaker: Peterson
a16_0753900.text: And then simply increase the stop number one stop. For example, if the CEX exposure graph calls for f/11 and you're gonna use the Magazine UU, you should go to f/16.

a16_0753900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0753900.text: Yeah, okay. I - I thought - I - You used an example; I thought you meant that specifically, and I couldn't make that correlate. Okay. And Charlie says this magazine is HBW instead of VHBW.

a16_0753900.speaker: Peterson
a16_0753900.text: And, Casper, for the terminator photography on the next rev, we're recommending you go ahead and use Magazine SS. That's Sierra Sierra. [Pause.]

a16_0753900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0753900.text: Okay; use the one we had planned on.

a16_0753900.speaker: Peterson
a16_0753900.text: And, Casper, that call on Magazine UU; we meant to impart to you that you can use that for targets of opportunity.

a16_0755111.speaker: Peterson
a16_0755111.text: 16, put the High Gain on Auto.

a16_0760552.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0760552.text: Houston, did you copy our torquing angles?

a16_0760552.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0760552.text: Okay, Don; one comment. I'll try again and take a look at the optics in the - when we get out into the double umbra, but right now in that telescope, I - I can see the stars now, but I still can't see star patterns. Like we looked at - at Antares - and you just couldn't see the Scorpion at all. And that may be due to the extreme amount of Earthshine that's being reflected off of the LM. That LM is like looking at it almost in daylight, and, good gosh, the - the Moon looks like you can see everything on there just like - it's really bright.

a16_0760552.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0760552.text: This is Apollo Control. We're ready to switch now to the MSC News Center Briefing Room for our change of shift briefing. During the course of that briefing we'll be recording air to ground conversations with the crew for playback immediately following. At 76 hours, 9 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0761234.speaker: Peterson
a16_0761234.text: 16, we're about a couple of minutes from LOS. Everything's looking good, and while you're behind the Moon, we'll change shifts and pick you up on the next rev.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: Okay. We sure enjoyed it, and we really appreciate all of the things that you guys are doing to get us into orbit here. Man, I don't - That's the kind of help that really does it for us. Thank you much.

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Well, I guess that - that sort of makes six days of PTC not so bad.

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Let's see, I ought to be able to do both of these at the same time, or can I? Tsk, tsk, tsk, tsk, tsk, tsk, tsk.

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: What time was our - AOS - I mean, sunrise?

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Just look at the Flight Plan, there [garble].

a16_0761234.speaker: Duke
a16_0761234.text: We got to get going here, I'll tell you [garble].

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Well, we've got at least 20 minutes, Charlie.

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: No, no, no, no. Look at the Flight Plan where the column stops. It goes from black to white.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: Well, it - if it goes to black to some other squiggly line, what is that squiggly line? It goes from black to a squiggly line. Okay. And then it becomes full sunrise at 76:35.

a16_0761234.speaker: Duke
a16_0761234.text: Okay, what settings do I use on this color? I don't see how this can show that terminator with color film.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: No, you admit my ability to read the chart. It's wrong. (Laughter) One small step for mankind, here. What do you make it out to be, Charlie?

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: Is that when it gets daytime? Or get sunrise?

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: Our sunrise. Well, that can't be sunrise, man. He ain't gonna believe that. That's because you're looking at it [garble], which you ain't gonna ever see again [laughter]. Every time we did this on Apollo 10, a Fuel Cell light came on; every time we [garble]. And I was totally ignorant of what the fuel cell [garble], in here somewhere [garble].

a16_0761234.speaker: Duke
a16_0761234.text: I put both pair down there in the [garble].

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Okay. That's what we need to know.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: Did we stop logging our intake and all that stuff today?

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Yep. Did that this morning. I mean, after the first [garble]. What time did they say we get the AOS? About -

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: They're supposed to give us a Rev 2 update for that stuff, and they did, didn't they?

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: No, I don't think they're supposed to.

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: Yep. It's altered in the Flight Plan.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: I guess this is the real crux. If you don't get around on this rev, they've really screwed up.

a16_0761234.speaker: Duke
a16_0761234.text: We had [garble] terminator I'm supposed to take a picture of.

a16_0761234.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0761234.text: You want me to take a picture of Crookes or not? I - I...

a16_0761234.speaker: Duke
a16_0761234.text: I don't want you to take a picture of anything [garble] asked...

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: [Garble] asked us to ask you to take a picture of it.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: Please tell those guys - please tell Ken...

a16_0761234.speaker: Duke
a16_0761234.text: We're sorry he doesn't want to.

a16_0761234.speaker: Young
a16_0761234.text: What he said was, "I'd like to get a picture of Crookes." He said, "There's a possibility that you guys may be able to pick it up, depending on whose window you're sitting in at the time. I know Ken looks at it, but I don't know if you do or not; but if you happen to be sitting there and it comes around, why don't you get a picture of it?" That's what he said. On account of something, I forget what [garble].

a16_0761234.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0761234.text: This is Apollo Control at 76 hours, 27 minutes. During our Change of Shift Briefing, Apollo 16 went behind the Moon. Nearing the end now of their first revolution of the Moon. And we accumulated a small amount of taped conversation with the crew as they went around the corner on this first revolution which we'll play back for you at this time.

a16_0762700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762700.text: Now, how about putting the 250 lens on there?

a16_0762700.speaker: Duke
a16_0762700.text: Okay. Is that our waste water tank?

a16_0762700.speaker: Duke
a16_0762700.text: Still got 20 percent more to go.

a16_0762700.speaker: Young
a16_0762700.text: I'm not able to tell that they're doing any of that.

a16_0762700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762700.text: You're right. That's a - that's a rather startling sunrise, isn't it?

a16_0762900.speaker: Young
a16_0762900.text: You want to get over here, Ken?

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke
a16_0762900.text: It's out of this window. Crookes's supposed to be.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: It should be out - out of here or there, either one. This seems to be fine.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0762900.text: We'll be reacquiring Apollo 16 in about 30 minutes. At the present time, Flight Director Pete Frank is reviewing the mission status with each of his flight controllers. Our spacecraft communicator at this time is astronaut Hank Hartsfield. And our tracking data shows Apollo 16 to to be in an orbit with an apolune of 169.9 nautical miles [314.6 km], a perilune of 58.1 [nautical miles, 107.6 km]. At 76 hours, 29 minutes; this is Apollo Control.

a16_0762900.speaker: Young
a16_0762900.text: Okay, we got our fuel cell purge now?

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke
a16_0762900.text: No. I'm gonna start it right now.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: Okay. Let's see, get - get the - Suppose we could use Magazine SS? That other one.

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke
a16_0762900.text: That one's the magazine you want to use for this?

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: Okay, and this is gonna be [garble] seven [garble] six [garble]. Okay [garble] SPS pressure.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: I put it to acknowledge [?] because it was on continuously. Must be [garble]. It looks like it's gonna go higher. It's about 210 now.

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke
a16_0762900.text: Well - Yeah, if the light was on, though, it should come back on again.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: It may have gone off from being cooled down.

a16_0762900.speaker: Young
a16_0762900.text: Take a look in there. The condenser's normal [garble].

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke
a16_0762900.text: Starting to open the purge [garble]. Maybe we better turn off the waste water dump.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: Okay, I'll get it. What's that?

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: Oh. All right. Okay. Okay. This is off.

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke
a16_0762900.text: Man, we are streaming out a lot of particles with us. Okay, this terminator's coming up, Ken.

a16_0762900.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0762900.text: Okay. I'm coming. Well, we're not gonna be directly over it until about 34, which is two and a half minutes.

a16_0762900.speaker: Duke

a16_0773736.text: I have your map update Rev 3 whenever you're ready, Charlie. It's 79:05 in the Flight Plan.

a16_0773736.speaker: Duke
a16_0773736.text: All right, why don't you give me the map update and the Landmark PAD?

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: All righty. Map update: LOS: 78:23:17; 78:48:09; 79:10:25. Landmark PAD is T-horizon: 79:34:11; 79:36:22. [Pause.]

a16_0773736.speaker: Duke
a16_0773736.text: Roger; copy. Map update of 078:23:17; 078:48:09; 079:10:25. Landmark tracking is 79:34:11; 79:36:22.

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Good readback.

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: 16, the computer's yours, and I have your TEI-5 PAD for the updates book.

a16_0773736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0773736.text: Okay, Hank, before we do that - Looking at the change to the Flight Plan here, we got to load the Verb 48 to put in the proper DAP, and then start 509, and then go to the P52. Can we go ahead and stop the maneuver now and will this attitude clear enough things so we can get a P52 in here?

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a16_0773736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0773736.text: I'm sorry; I didn't copy that.

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Roger. Stand by a minute, Ken, I'll have FAO check.

a16_0773736.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0773736.text: Thank you. I was worried about getting in the same problem we get into after undocking tomorrow, where it might take a special angle.

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Apollo 16, Houston. FAO says this is a good attitude.

a16_0773736.speaker: Duke
a16_0773736.text: Rog; go ahead.

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Okay, PAD follows: TEI-5, SPS/G&N; 39838; plus 0.61, plus 1.19; 084:31:41:36; Noun 81: plus 3525.2, plus 1247.3, minus 0086.8; 182, 056, 022; the rest is NA. Set stars: Sirius, Rigel; 131; 071; 014. Two jets, 17 seconds. Other: 1, burn undocked; 2, assumes DOI; 3, landing site REFSMMAT. [Long pause.]

a16_0773736.speaker: Duke
a16_0773736.text: Rog. TEI-5, SPS/G&N; 39838; plus 0.61, plus 1.19; 084:31:41:36; plus 3525.2, plus 1247.3, minus 0086.8; 182, 056, 022. Rest of PAD is NA. Sirius and Rigel; 131; 071; 014. Two jets, 17 seconds. Other: 1 is burn undocked; 2, assumes DOI; 3, landing site REFSMMAT.

a16_0773736.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0773736.text: Good readback, Charlie.

a16_0773736.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0773736.text: This is Apollo Control at 77 hours, 54 minutes. During the last few minutes, among the sets of numbers passed up to the crew by CapCom Hank Hartsfield, were those they will use in performing the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver, and that burn is to occur at 78 hours; 33 minutes; 44 seconds. The maneuver will be performed using the spacecraft Service Propulsion System engine. It will be a - primarily a retrograde burn resulting in slowing the spacecraft by about 203.8 feet per second [62.1 m/s] or about 136 miles an hour [219 km/h]. And as a result of that, we expect the orbit to be changed to

a16_0775400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0775400.text: Houston, do you want to take a look at our rotated vector in P40 before we start our maneuver?

a16_0775400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0775400.text: Okay. The question was, do you want to take a look at the rotated vector in P40 before we start our maneuver, or can we go ahead and start the maneuver? [Long pause.]

a16_0775400.speaker: Young
a16_0775400.text: Houston, did you miss the question?

a16_0775400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0775400.text: Negative, but we're having trouble finding an answer.

a16_0775400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0775400.text: 16, Houston. Go ahead and call P40, then maneuver. [Long pause.]

a16_0775400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0775400.text: Okay. Have you got enough look now? [Long pause.]

a16_0775400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0775400.text: He's looking at it now, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0775400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0775400.text: You got a good vector, Ken. Go ahead.

a16_0775400.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0775400.text: This is Apollo Control at 78 hours, 2 minutes. At the present time the Apollo 16 crew is in the process of putting the spacecraft in its proper attitude for the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. That burn is to be performed in 31 minutes, 30 seconds with the spacecraft out of radio contact on the backside of the Moon. We have about 21 minutes remaining before we lose radio contact and in that amount of time we'll be monitoring spacecraft systems, Flight Dynamics Officer will be taking a last look at all of the numbers passed up to the crew to assure that the burn is the precise maneuver that w

a16_0780631.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0780631.text: This is Apollo Control, Flight Director Pete Frank has just gone around the room polling each of the flight controllers here, getting a status for the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. All the lights came up green, every one says we're Go and we'll be passing that Go up to the crew shortly.

a16_0780631.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0780631.text: This is Apollo Control, we're coming up now on nine minutes until loss of contact with Apollo 16. About 19½ minutes away from the time the crew will be performing the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. This maneuver, of course, performed behind the Moon. We'll be out of radio contact and we'll get our first look at the results of that maneuver when they come back around on the other side of the Moon on their third revolution. This burn is a very critical maneuver which must be performed with very preci - within very precise limits and particularly in the shutdown which the computer will

a16_0781411.speaker: Young
a16_0781411.text: Okay, Houston. The gimbal motors are on.

a16_0781902.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0781902.text: Okay, Houston. We're going to do the gimbal drive check.

a16_0781902.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0781902.text: 16, Houston. We're about two minutes from LOS. [Pause.]

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Oh, man, if I could just get my sinuses to stay cleared!

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: I just - yours ought to clear out on the ground, don't they? It sure is a pain in the neck.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Okay, nothing's hanging around the overheads anywhere that we've stuck out and we forgot to pick up? This burn occur in daylight or -

a16_0782500.speaker: Duke
a16_0782500.text: Boy, we'd use a lot of gas: 20,000 pounds' worth of fuel [garble].

a16_0782500.speaker: Young
a16_0782500.text: Huh? We used a lot, huh?

a16_0782500.speaker: Young
a16_0782500.text: I hope so. Never get it out of lunar orbit unless you do [garble]. Jettison.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Someday someone's gonna explain to me why that was a rational decision, to not have a dump [garble].

a16_0782500.speaker: Young
a16_0782500.text: Rational, I think, decision, that's because we couldn't get the SPS to burn or RCS to burn.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Two clocks that say it's two minutes.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: I don't - how you can get the - don't know how to put a bias in.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: With this kind of a burn - 20 seconds - it can't be more than a couple of tenths ...

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: ...plus the minute. So with a foot per second there - which might be significant -

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: I don't know how to do that.

a16_0782500.speaker: Young
a16_0782500.text: You got Trans Control Power and all that stuff?

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Comes on at - a minute. Okay. Okay, going to Normal, Trans Control Power, on. Delta-V Thrust A, coming on, no light.

a16_0782500.speaker: Duke
a16_0782500.text: Okay, everything looks good. Helium Valves are open. Pressures are great. Past the 10 seconds.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: I believe it was auto. Beautiful.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Okay, we had about - almost one of those before we started.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Okay, wait a minute now. That's - Okay, that's - We're not gonna trim. That's close enough.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0782500.text: Okay, let's look it up. Verb 6, Noun 20, 1.21, 272.7 - Yeah. Yeah, 3.44. That's good.

a16_0782500.speaker: Duke
a16_0782500.text: Okay, I'm ready on the gimbal motors.

a16_0782500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0782500.text: This is Apollo Control at 79 hours, 6 minutes. We're about four and a half minutes away from the expected time of reacquiring Apollo 16 on its third revolution of the Moon, at which time they should have lowered their orbit to about 10 by 58 nautical miles [19 by 107 km]. If, however, for some reason they did not perform that maneuver we would be reacquiring in about 30 seconds. The Service Propulsion System engine on this particular spacecraft is consuming about 66 pounds of propellant per second of burn; based on that, when next we see Apollo 16 they should be about 1,600 pounds [726 kilogra

a16_0782500.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0782500.text: This is Apollo Control. We should be coming up on Acquisition Of Signal now. And network reports that we have AOS.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger. That's great news.

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: At least in our training. [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Okay, we'll stand by for your burn report.

a16_0791028.speaker: Duke
a16_0791028.text: Okay, Henry. It feels like if we had - we're clipping the tops of the trees all through there - what it looks like. We got a burn report of a Delta-T IG , 0. Burn time we got was 24.4, plus two balls 06 - 2106 V GX . Trim attitude 001, 272, 003; so we did not trim. Residuals were plus 0.8, plus 0, plus 0.1; minus 2.3 Delta-V C ; Fuel 337, Ox 346. Over.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger, 16. Unbalanced? [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Duke
a16_0791028.text: Okay, it jumped up to 200 increase.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger; copy.

a16_0791028.speaker: Duke
a16_0791028.text: It never really stabilized though, Hank.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: And a Verb 82, last look, thought we were at 10.9 [nautical miles - 20.1 km] perigee.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger. Copy 10.9. [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: But I don't think it really knows. [Pause.] But the MSFN really knows. [Long pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0791028.text: That last comment was from John Young. Earlier we heard from Charlie Duke reporting a nearly perfect Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. Young reported that they're onboard readings show that they had an apolune of - rather a perilune of 10.9 nautical miles. The targeted was 10.3, but again that's an onboard reading and we'll be tracking and getting a reading here on the ground.

a16_0791028.speaker: Duke
a16_0791028.text: Houston, 16. it appeared to us that we got an auto shutdown.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger, Charlie. Copy auto shutdown.

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: You got any preliminary data, Houston?

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger, John. The Doppler says stay; we're waiting on the short arc.

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: Okay; thank you.

a16_0791028.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0791028.text: John Young's question is in reference to Stay/No-Stay - that we'll be passing up from the Control Center here in the event that tracking data - we've got about two minutes of it on which the Flight Dynamics Officer will make his calculations. In the event tracking data showed that we did not get the desired orbit and we're in an unsafe orbit, the crew has a maneuver on board that they would perform to raise their orbit to a satisfactory level. This is a so-called bailout burn which would be performed at 79 hours, 22 minutes, 8 seconds or about six minutes from now. All indications, preliminary

a16_0791028.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0791028.text: Assuming that maneuver went as planned, and the orbit is as we would expect, Apollo 16 should be at an altitude of about 19 nautical miles [35 km] above the lunar surface, accounting for Charlie Duke's earlier comment that it appeared to be right down among the tree tops.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Apollo 16, Houston. You're good on the short arc. You have a stay, and we show you 59 by 10.7. [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: Roger; 59 by 10.7. Thank you, sir.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: 16, Houston. Can you - could you give us Auto on the High Gain? [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Young
a16_0791028.text: Rog. You have it. [Long pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0791028.text: Henry, if you remember that little real bright crater on the northern rim of Chaplygin that Stu and Farouk were talking about the other day, we - we happened to see it right up close to us as we came by on this orbit, and we got a couple of pics for you on it, and that really is an unusual little guy. And it's really beautiful.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger; copy. [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0791028.text: Probably getting carried away with all of this, but we've - we've done all kinds of things to see back there. It would really be nice to fly that kind of an orbit down low.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_0791028.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0791028.text: And, we're pitching down to our landmark track attitude, and this is my first chance to point the sextant at the surface, and the sextant is just as clear as a bell. It's beautiful. You can pick out little bitty features. They're just - they're just as clear. There's no fuzziness. And the telescope's the same way.

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: Hey, that's great: We ought to be able to get some good use out of that.

a16_0791028.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0791028.text: This is Apollo Control. The landmark tracking Ken Mattingly is referring to is a procedure used on board the spacecraft to determine their orbit. It's also a procedure that'll be used by Mattingly from lunar orbit to track the spacecraft on the surface of the Moon, hopefully, and allow scientists on the ground to compute a precise location for the landing site for the touchdown part of the Lunar Module. We now show Apollo 16 at an altitude of 13.8 nautical miles [25.6 km], continuing to drop down towards pericynthion. And the preliminary tracking data the Flight Dynamics Officer reported, show

a16_0791028.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0791028.text: 16, Omni Delta.

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Hank, out to the - my side, out Window 5, there was one crater here that you could see in one section of it, it looked like some outcrop two-thirds the way up the crater wall, and some big blocks had rolled down the - into the crater floor, and you could see the boulder tracks all the way down.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger; copy. Can you locate that one?

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Wait a minute. No, I'm pretty lost right now. Let me see if I can figure it out. [Long pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Ken, while you're maneuvering there, we'd like to ask you what value did you put in your EMS, and what did you get on your EMS check?

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Houston, 16. That crater I had, I think was in a series around Maclaurin, maybe a little bit further west than that.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger; copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Hank, coming across the mare here, it reminds you of pitot static system cals at Edwards.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger. You're really down low, screaming across, huh? [Long pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: 16, Houston. Did you copy the question I had about the EMS Delta-V? [Long pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Houston, the Goclenius Rille looks like large grabens with very subdued sides to them; no outcrop at all apparent from my position. [Pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger; copy. [Pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: And looking on up into the Gutenberg Rille, you can see it cross one crater. Just climbs right across the crater wall.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger.

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: And that's Gutenberg C. That's Gutenberg C, Hank, and you can see the wall is down-dropped into the rille.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger; copy. How do you read, Charlie?

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: I'm reading you five by.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Okay. A littler earlier, I asked a question about the EMS Delta-V. Did you copy that?

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Negative; we did not.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Okay ...

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: It - it read minus 2.3.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger. We had a question here as to how the EMS Delta-V check came out, and which value you loaded into the Delta-V counter?

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Stand by.

a16_0792617.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0792617.text: Can I call you in a second on that, Hank?

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Sure thing.

a16_0792617.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0792617.text: It was like - it was like 1.8 at shutdown because of the drift in the EMS, and I did a check, and it came out to be normal and the bias was the same. I put in the Delta-V T , the same thing that we've used before, but then it looked to me like the bias was in - less than half a foot per second.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger; copy. We were a little confused here because the - the value that you had at the end there was somewhere in between what we thought it ought to be, depending on which setting you put in the Delta-V counter.

a16_0792617.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0792617.text: Rog. It was about 1.6 or something like that at shutdown. I'll have to look back at the Flight Plan.

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Okay, Houston. The walls - the north wall of Capella has striations that are dipping eastward about, oh, 60 degrees or so, all the way across the north face.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger. Copy, Charlie.

a16_0792617.speaker: Duke
a16_0792617.text: Okay, and also Isidorus, the same thing.

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0792617.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0792617.text: J-2 should be on the horizon now, Ken.

a16_0792617.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0792617.text: Rog. We got the - it's right on the horizon. Still haven't picked up the target yet. Looks like it's tracking just about right. I have Theophilus going out of the field of view now.

a16_0793609.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793609.text: Ken, you're coming up on about 30 seconds to TCA. [Pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0793854.text: Big old hill down the stream from where you're going [garble]? [Pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Young
a16_0793854.text: Guess who is sneaking in marks on Gator Crater right now?

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: I wonder who. [Long pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0793854.text: Gator crater is about 700 yards [640 metres] across, one of the craters at the Descartes landing site. Ken Mattingly obviously taking a landmark sightings on that crater at the present time as Apollo 16 passes directly over the landing site.

a16_0793854.speaker: Young
a16_0793854.text: Now that's what I call OJT right there.

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: How did the landing site look through the sextant? [Pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Young
a16_0793854.text: You have to do that with the telescope, Hank.

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Duke
a16_0793854.text: I think that was the best high-speed pass I've ever made.

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: Roger.

a16_0793854.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0793854.text: Okay, Henry; go ahead.

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: Roger. T-start, 080:38:01; T-stop, 080:46:04. And that same PAD is good for the Pan Camera.

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: Good readback.

a16_0793854.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0793854.text: That'll be the same PAD for both cameras. [Long pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: 16, Houston. We'd like for you to go on and get in the SIM bay attitude so we can get our DSE dump.

a16_0793854.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0793854.text: Wilco. [Long pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0793854.text: Hey, Hank, you want me to go ahead and do this Single Jet Authority, or use couples to go to the attitude?

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a16_0793854.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0793854.text: Ken, why don't you go ahead and go coupled, then we can go Single Jet.

a16_0793854.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0793854.text: Okay. Sounds like a good plan.

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: Hank, would you check on one thing for me? Would you find out if this method I've been using for reading out the maneuver times, Verb 4 Noun 1, is in any way affected by or affects the use of Program 509?

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: Thank you, sir. And I got a couple of minutes here, if you would like to go over some of those questions you had before now. I - I wasn't paying much attention. [Pause.]

a16_0794711.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0794711.text: Stand by, Ken. I think they got your answer awhile ago and it satisfied them, but I'll make sure.

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: Okay. I wasn't paying a lot of attention; I was trying to pick up that landmark.

a16_0794711.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0794711.text: Do you have any comments on the landmark tracking? Did it all go smoothly?

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: Well, except for the fact that those optics are perfect. That's really neat. The target area did not look as I anticipated. It's a - I think it's a function of the low Sun angle, but it looked to me like there were far more rims around the craters than - than what - the impression I had from looking at things on the - on the models. And I did not pick up North or South Ray; they still were in the shadows. So, I guess it's possible that I could have been on the wrong crater, but it sure looked like to me like I must have been on Gator.

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: It's still - still a problem in scaling when you look at something like that, until you're sure that you have the right feel for it. But I think it's pretty obvious, and I think picking it up tomorrow will be relatively easy.

a16_0794711.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0794711.text: 16, Houston. Could you bring up the High Gain, Pitch plus 35, Yaw 290. [Long pause.]

a16_0794711.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0794711.text: And, Ken, there's no problem in...

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: Okay, Hank, and we're about - Go ahead, Hank.

a16_0794711.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0794711.text: Roger. They say there is no problem in calculating maneuver completion time, and - and it does not interfere with 509.

a16_0794711.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0794711.text: Okay, thank you. I've been avoiding using that. All right. We're about ready to go through our solar monitor and tiedown release. You folks ready for us to do that? [Pause.]

a16_0794711.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0794711.text: Roger. We're ready to go, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0795423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0795423.text: Okay, Houston. We released the tiedowns and the door and heard just a very tiny little sound on each of those activities.

a16_0795423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0795423.text: Hank, another piece of questionable data that've collected today is - well, on our low pass on the back side there, we got our color wheel out. And we have two votes for Number 17, and one vote for Number 13.

a16_0795423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0795423.text: And that's over on the back side just past Chaplygin. And Number 17 really isn't quite right; it's just the closest thing we have. And the same comment applies to Number 13.

a16_0795423.speaker: Duke
a16_0795423.text: Well, I still say 13 was right on.

a16_0795423.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0795423.text: You'll never guess who voted for 13. [Pause.]

a16_0795423.speaker: Young
a16_0795423.text: The grits have affected his vision.

a16_0795423.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0795423.text: That's probably what it is, John.

a16_0795423.speaker: Duke
a16_0795423.text: Hey, Hank, ask Stu who he believes.

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Ken, you want to keep us posted on what you're doing there with the switches?

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay. I got the Mapping Camera Door Opens and the Alpha Cover Door Open, and the Mapping Camera's going out. And we've just gone through one minute of extend time, and I'm timing the first one.

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Roger; copy.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: I'll do the Gamma Ray and Mass Spec booms sequentially afterwards, so I can pay attention to the times. [Pause.]

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay. And I've got gray on the Mapping Camera, Extend, and that was at one minute and 20 seconds.

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Roger; copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay. Can you read me on vox, Henry?

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Roger.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay. That's the way we'll operate. I'm going to the Gamma Ray, Deploy at this time. Gonna to hold it for barber pole plus two seconds, then Off. Going to Deploy. Deploy. Barber pole now, 1, 2, Off; and it's gray. Gamma Ray is coming to Retract.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark. Barber pole, and it's gray. Okay. Going to the Mass Spectrometer. Deploy.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark. Barber pole, 1, 2, Off. Mass Spec to Retract.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark. Barber pole, Off. Okay. They're both in the Retract position, and everything looks normal. The X-Ray is coming On.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark. [Pause.] I've completed the Gamma Ray and Mass Spec Boom deployment and retraction, and I'm ready to go ahead with the Mass Spec, Deploy, if that's okay with you.

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Roger; go ahead. [Pause.]

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay; it's Deploy on the Mass Spec, and I'm timing it. [Long pause.]

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Give us Auto on the High Gain, 16.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Five seconds to stop. [Pause.] Okay, it's Off on the Mass Spectrometer, and you have Auto. [Pause.]

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay, Hank. You've got the Mass Spec out to 8.4 feet.

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Roger; looks good down here.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Laser Altimeter is coming On.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark. [Long pause.]

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: And can I go ahead and put the Mass Spec Experiment On without waiting the three or four minutes?

a16_0800201.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800201.text: Stand by. Roger. Go ahead.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Okay. Mass Spectrometer Experiment is coming On.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark. The Ion Source is going to Standby.

a16_0800201.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800201.text: Mark it.

a16_0800904.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0800904.text: Can you tell how the Laser's doing yet, Hank?

a16_0800904.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0800904.text: Stand by, Ken. We'll take a look. [Pause.] Laser looks good, Ken.

a16_0800904.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0800904.text: This is Apollo Control at 80 hours, 12 minutes. The Guidance and Control Officer reports that from looking at the replay of data from that Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver performed at the end of the second revolution, he reports that the engine appeared to perform normally in every respect and we're currently showing Apollo 16 in an orbit 58.6 nautical miles by 9.9 [108.5 by 18.3 km] and we expect that that will continue to be refined somewhat. Ken Mattingly has completed a series of exercises that deploy certain of the experiments in the Service Module Scientific Instrument Module Bay, the S

a16_0801225.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0801225.text: Apollo 16, Houston. We're about two minutes from LOS.

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: All righty. See you in a little while.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0801225.text: The Mass Spectrometer detects such things as the volatile products given off by volcanoes, should any of those happen to be active around this time. Would also detect water vapor should that exist in the lunar atmosphere. The other experiment activated by Mattingly was the Laser Altimeter. You heard him ask how that was performing. A report from the Orbital Science Officer here was that it appeared to be functioning normally. This device measures the spacecraft altitude above the lunar surface and is correlated with Panoramic Camera photographs obtained of the lunar surface. Putting these two

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: Okay, Hank. I'm up with the biomed. Take a quick look at it.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: And Power. Let's see. The V/H Override is not on.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Mapping Camera's Image Motion is coming - On -

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Mark. Barber pole. And it's gray. Image Motion is On.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Yes [garble]. That way if they get any unusual things in their signaling. Man, they sure need a timer over here. 38:01.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: No, sir. I'll take care of that. Thank you. Do you need to get in here?

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: Wanted to get a spoon is all.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: No [laughter]. Thank you. That timer is only good for telling me to not forget something. Huh? Yeah. That was so I wouldn't get hung up and forget to do what I'm doing.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. Man, that's gonna [garble] a crick in my neck before this is over.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Mark. Then that goes - Well, let's see, I'll come back and catch the Pan Camera, Operate.

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: Want me to take that stuff up for you, John?
