a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. Main B Undervolt; turning the Pan Camera back to Standby.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Yeah. Okay. Okay. Let's see if I can reiterate what happened. As soon as I turned it on, we got an Undervolt. Didn't happen to see how much it was ?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: That was Main B that gave us the Undervolt?

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: [Garble] about to eat the chocolate bar, huh?

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: You want to try it again, Ken, and let me watch it?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Oh, I don't really think there's any future in that.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Make sure the ground doesn't want to try it either.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Yep. Yeah, but the Pan Camera's on Main A.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Nope. Any conclusion they come to would be guessing anyhow. I suspect that Main B is running a little bit lower than Main A and they probably both got pulled down. You didn't happen to notice [garble]? I'm sure you didn't. I wouldn't have.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: No. All I saw was MA.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Let's see. We're running 38 - almost 40 on Fuel Cell 3; 24 and 22. That's 32, 64 - 100 amps. That 's a shame.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Main Bus B Undervolt; 27 volts? I don't understand that. Must have been a...

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: (Laughter) Well, John, I don't know what from. It's on 27 - 26½ volts. Main A is on 27½. Fuel Cell 3...

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: No, I think they're running - normal. It's only pulling 37 amps. Now it's something - just cycle it up to 40 amps.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: That's running about right. It must have been sitting right on the - I got some heater load on there. Main B. Those radiators couldn't be cycling, could they?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: No. What's the radiator outlet temperature? 25 - No, they're not on.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: What else did you shut off?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Well, we aren't running the thing.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Yeah, they're getting a pretty good spread there.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: I think there's something wrong with that oxygen regulator. The flows in that thing are very unstable.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Well - You know, I guess it really isn't bouncing that much more than the others. It's just that there's a bigger delta flow between the oxygen and the hydrogen here.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Charlie, can you hand me my - my spoon out of my temporary stowage bag over there?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. Well, we've got high bit rate data on all this. They can take a look.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Cryo 1 [garble] pressures are okay. Beats me [garble].

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Mapping Camera coming to Standby - Off. Image Motion is Off. Laser Altimeter is Off. Mapping Camera - Got a barber pole on Image Motion, and the Laser is Off. Mapping Camera's going to Retract.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Pan Camera shouldn't have anything to do with it, should it?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Mark. And a barber pole on the Retract, the Mapping Camera.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: I thought that stuff was on Main B...

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: I mean Service Module/AC Power is off of Main B, because ...

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Is it half and half? Because...

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Well, the reason I said so - the reason I thought it was - I mean - because I was reading the schematic somewhere and I thought you could lose - that they're in series and the fact that, if you lost this thing, it would cost you your B servo.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. I'm going to have to climb over where you are, John, for just a minute.

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: You want me to climb out of here? Where you want to go?

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: I don't know. Ken's got to be over here, and he's got to be over there.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Golly, there's some of those flows that go up the sides of walls.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Well, now. Guess who's got their next - next failure. A Mapping Camera that's out - to stay.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: (Laughter) I figured it would break, but I thought it would last more than one extension.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: There's 2 minutes and it hasn't come in.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: How long's it supposed to take?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Hey, John, can you - let me in there?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Is that - barber pole still on the Mapping Camera?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. It must have taken about - three minutes.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Watch the stick. I got it activated.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: You brute. Gol-dang-it. That thing went in before. There we go.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: I thought I put [garble] Ok, no, I did.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: You told me to put it back, so I did.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: I don't know. [garble] there. You only have [garble] then you gonna get that Main B Undervolt coming out on the front side [garble]

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Gol-dang-it. Once again. Didn't give me any pan. Set the High Gain at 0 and 170?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. How about Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover to Close? Let's see, verify that that Mapping Camera Retract barber pole is off and that the switch is in the Retract position.

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: Yeah. It was so fast I didn't [garble].

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: When am I going to eat?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: No, go ahead and finish your ...

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: ...and then I'll finish it up for you.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: No, go ahead and finish whatever you've got to do to get ready for tomorrow because the next thing I'm going to have to do is go to bed.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: That's how we figured these - Where those water bags at, Charlie? We ought to fill those, right?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: That's mine, too? In addition to this?

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: No, no, wait a minute [garble]. Couldn't [garble] chicken stew.

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: You want a wet pack? You sure?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Oh, oh. Let me. Let me do some more things here. This ain't going to work (laughter).

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: What do you want me to do?

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: There ain't no way to have an eat period in all this, isn't it?

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Looks like you can't have an eat period and see what's on the Flight Plan because you're gonna have [garble].

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Yeah. Except this is the first time to move the boom, and I'd like to move it. But I got to have the Flight Plan to see what time - Go ahead and finish your menu. No, it's on the other page.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Mass Spec and Gamma Ray to Deploy. Okay. Go ahead. Finish your Flight Plan.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: Okay. There's a barber pole on the Gamma Ray Boom.

a16_0801225.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0801225.text: And the Mass Spec was running - 15 seconds after that one.

a16_0801225.speaker: Duke
a16_0801225.text: Well, John, you want to put on the LTV - LCG [garble]?

a16_0801225.speaker: Young
a16_0801225.text: Yeah. After a bit - soon as I defecate [garble].

a16_0801225.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0801225.text: This is Apollo Control at 81 hours, 4 minutes. We're standing by now to regain radio contact with Apollo 16, now in it's fourth revolution of the Moon. This will be the last frontside pass prior to the time the crew begins their scheduled nine-hour rest period. And should be a relatively quiet period. And the Flight Dynamics Officer has just reported that their latest tracking shows the spacecraft to be in an orbit of 58.6 by 10.6 nautical miles [108.5 by 19.6 km] as a result of that Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. We're about ten seconds now from regaining radio contact.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Apollo 16, Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: You're five by, Hank.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. Our data down here we worked on during the back side shows you're in 58.8 by 10.6. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. Copy. You want to tell us about it? [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: Stand by. Yeah, it was when Ken was - messing around with the SIM bay, and he'll fill you in.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Okay.

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: Yeah, we got a little behind on this sequence already, Hank. But as soon as I turned the - had the Mapping Camera, On and it worked fine, I turned the Pan Camera,On, and as soon as I went to Operate on the Pan Camera, we got a Main B Undervolt. So I turned it back to Standby and left it there. Charlie said he saw about 25 volts on Main B, and concluded I'd wait and let you take a look at it. And then we got another Main B Undervolt some five minutes or so later, and it again was a momentary. By the time we looked at it, it all looked pretty normal. The only - We checked the fuel cell regulator

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Yeah. All the things we could check look okay.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Hank, we got a - it might not even be a small anomaly, but Fuel Cell 3, the H 2 flow's running a little bit higher than the O 2 flow, but the regulator pressure looks fine to me. But the other two fuel cells, H 2 and O 2 , match.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. We copy, Charlie. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: My guess is when you dump the DSE the whole story will be right on there probably.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Okay [garble]. John.

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: When you get the DSE translated, probably tell you what happened.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. We copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: Hank, you really can see both the Mass Spec and the Gamma Ray booms deployed.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. Understand you can see them both.

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: That's affirm. Looks like a couple of feet of the boom is about all you can see. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: You've really got us puzzled with this undervolt now, because the Pan Camera runs off from Main A.,

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: Yeah, we'd noticed the same thing. It - you know it may not be rational, but it just seemed like that was the - I touched one switch and got a Main Undervolt so I took it back off again. Decided to even let you think about it before I [garble] anymore.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Possible that it doesn't have any connection.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: I still have the power on it, Hank. I've got it in Standby and Power, On.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. Copy. [Pause.] And, Ken, I'd like to verify - is your Nonessential Bus on Main A or Main B?

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: That's Main A.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: And, Hank, last night we - I - think we got verification that we could wear the LCGs to bed tonight and be all ready to go by in the morning.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: That is affirmative.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Okay. Anybody thought any more about my suit?

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: We thought about it, and smoked it over, and we kind of think maybe we ought to do nothing unless you have some real bad trouble tomorrow. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Like if we can't get it zipped. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: Okay. Can we use my pliers on it to pull the zipper closed?

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: Houston. Houston, 16. Do you read? Over.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. Reading you 5 by 5, John. Go ahead.

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: Okay. If I have trouble closing it, can I use my pliers to get a better grip on it to pull it closed? Because it took me the better part of 20 minutes the other day to do it, and it usually takes about two. [Pause.] There's a place on there in the small of Charlie's back where that thing has just separated too far apart on the restraint zipper for me to pull it closed easily. When he gets on the LCG, the FCS, and the UCD bulk in there, the suit is going to be farther apart than it was - yesterday. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: John, we talked to Dave about that, and he said the big problem is that you can't arch your back in zero g as well. He had - he had a lot of trouble too, but on the Moon in one-sixth g he had no problem at all, because the gravity helped him arch his back. Does that sound like the problem - you just couldn't get arched back that far enough to do it?

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: Got me there. It looked like he was arched as much as he usually is. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: But you're saying that if I can't do it in - in zero g, we go on down to the Moon and try it in one-sixth g? [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. That sounds pretty good, John. We - we did look at a backup procedure here, but it's a long - looks like a long thing and involves using a needle and pulling things together like you're sewing. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Okay, Hank. I think to give us every benefit of the doubt that I will not - I don't plan to wear the - the FCS probably tomorrow, and I'll just use the LCG and UCD. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. Understand, and could you give us Auto on - the High Gain. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: There you go.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Hank, also we'd like to get permission to fill the drink bags tonight to save a few minutes also, if you think that's gonna be all right. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. That - Go ahead and do that, Charlie.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Ken, we can't find any connection between the Pan Camera and Main Bus A, and we were wondering - Main Bus B, and we were wondering if, when you got the second momentary one - undervolt - were you moving any switches at that time?

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: That's negative. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Young
a16_0810400.text: They were both momentary Main Bus undervolts.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger. The - the first one was momentary also?

a16_0810400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0810400.text: It - it could be, or it could be that the sensor is triggering at the wrong level. It could be that the sensor shifted up to something that looks reasonable. I wouldn't object - we still got the Pan Camera power on - I wouldn't object to, had it to operate for a second and back off - go ahead and use a couple of frames just to let you watch it. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Stand by, Ken.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Houston, 16.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Go ahead.

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: Is Tom satisfied with his Glycol Evap Out? We've got off scale, high here.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Stand by. Stand by a minute, Charlie. [Long pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: 16, Houston. EECOM advises that's the top of the scale. That you're still okay. You should now monitor Rad Out. [Pause.]

a16_0810400.speaker: Duke
a16_0810400.text: A Rad Out is 75.

a16_0810400.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0810400.text: Roger.

a16_0812817.speaker: Young
a16_0812817.text: I just used it to get a better grip with, not to pull the zipper, just to pull with. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Their concern is over side loads, John. They're afraid for you to use the pliers. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Young
a16_0812817.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0812817.text: This is Apollo Control at 81 hours, 30 minutes...

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Ken, Houston. We'd like to talk to you a minute about this docking latch, if you're free. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Go ahead.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Yeah. I'm not sure I know what you're looking for.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, when you look in the side there...

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: I'm not at all sure what the roller pawl is.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, the roller pawl is on the far left side of the latch, behind and above the Auxiliary Release Button. And it can be identified by the roller on the tip of the pawl. The pawl is just a little arm that sticks out, and it's got a little roller on the end of it that rides on the cam that has these detents in it.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Do you want to do this before we unlock it?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That's affirmative. And it best be done tomorrow, after - before you get your helmet and gloves on, of course. Just take a look at it while - perhaps while they're bringing the LM up. And if you - if you find, after we get the condition of that, if the roller's down in the detent like we suspect it is, when you remove the yellow probe umbilical cover on the right side of the latch, we'd like for you to look in the right side in there and at the bungee bell crank mechanism, and see if there's any foreign-object damage or anything wedged up in there. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: When you say remove the cover - do you mean physically remove it from the spacecraft, or just open it up and look underneath it?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Just open it up and look under there, Ken. And this is mainly - these two steps are just an inspection. We'd just like to verify the condition of the roller pawl and also the bell crank mechanism on the other side. Has nothing to do with the latch, but at least it'll give us an idea of what's wrong inside, if there is anything. It's not gonna help you in any way to prepare for unlocking it. To unlock it - after you've looked at these two things, we'd like to know if the latch handle requires force to cock the latch on the first stroke - and the second stroke, if required. In other words, if th

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay. So the kind of thing you want me to look for are information only. Is that affirmative?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Right. It would help the guys down here to try to understand what - what really happened to the latch. We kind of suspect it only got one cock. But if you look in there, and look for the roller pawl on the left side and look at the bell crank on the right side, at least that would tell us that nothing is jamming it, and that the roller pawl is in the right direction - right place. [Long pause.] Operationally though, to prepare for undocking, what it really amounts to, you just use the normal procedure. You pull the - pull the latch handle down and cock it if necessary, and if the - if the hook

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay. I just wanted to keep in mind what it was I needed if the time gets crowded.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Rog. The only this is - if there is any question on cocking, the only thing you have to do there is just pull it down and get the hook out of the way.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Do you have any questions on any of that?

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Ah, Hank, we just came ov...

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Not - not right now. Maybe you want to get in there and look at it. I'll call and ask you for some clarification or something tomorrow. But I think I know what you mean.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Hank, as we came up towards the landing site, in that terrain - the general terrain to the east of it appears to me to be frothy vesicular-looking type terrain, real craggy looking at this scale. Over.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. We copy, Charlie.

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: I'd say that was the Descartes. It has that appearance to it to me.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: And do you have this LM DAP load for us and TEIs?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. We're working on those PADs now. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Charlie, we'd like to get a Bat B charge going. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Okay, Bat B charge going on. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Bat B is charging. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Okay, stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay. TEI-12, SPS/G&N; 39817; plus 0.61, plus 1.19, 097:45:53.09; plus 3163.2, plus 1040.3, minus 0234.6; 181, 080, 020. Rest of the PAD is NA. The set stars are the same as for DOI. Won't repeat unless you want. Ullage; two jets, 17 seconds. Other remarks: burn undock, assumes no circ. Longitude Moon at T IG , minus 171.47. Landing site REFSMMAT. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Rog. TEI-12, SPS/G&N; 39817; plus 0.61, plus 1.19, 097:45:53.09; plus 3163.2, plus 1040.3, minus 0234.6; 181, 080, 020; NA; Sirius and Rigel; and information is same as DOI, two jets, 17 seconds; burn undocked, assumes no circ; longitude of Moon at T IG , minus 171.47; landing site REFSMMAT.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Good readback. And are you ready for TEI-19? [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: You speak.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. TEI-19, SPS/G&N; 39445; plus 0.61, plus 1.15; 111:31:49.81; plus 2909.4, plus 0785.3, minus 0224.0; 181, 100, 017; Set stars same as DOI, two jets, 17 seconds. Other: burn undocked, assumes circ, LM to Moon at T IG minus 160.09. End of PAD. [Pause.] If you'll give us Accept, we're ready to uplink. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Rog. You have it. And readback TEI-19, SPS/G&N; 39445; plus 0.61, plus 1.15; 111:31:49.81; plus, 2909.4, plus 0785.3, minus 0224.0; 181, 100, 017. Sirius and Rigel; two jets, 17 seconds; burn undock, assumes circ; LM to at T IG minus 166.09.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That was 160.09. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Henry, can I assume that the - the Mission Timer is in sufficient sync and that we don't need to do any updates there and that the REFSMMAT is good as is?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That's affirmative.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Thank you, sir. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Have you got the LM DAP stuff, Hank?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. We've got it and we're uplinking now and we're also loading your EMP 509 and I have your DAP, if you're ready to copy.

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Go ahead.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Correction on that. It's not 509; it's the jet monitor. Okay, LM DAP. LM weight, 36673; CSM weight, 39329. Checklist: DPS gimbal trims are good; no trim required. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Rog. Reading 36673, 39329, and the gimbals are good as is.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: It's a good readback, Charlie. I have a change to your LM Timeline Book on Page 1. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Stand by. Is it the Timeline or Activation?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: The Timeline Book. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: It's a change to your undocking attitude, Charlie. It says Timeline Book. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: O - okay, just had to get it out. Go ahead, Page 1.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, change undocking attitude to 0, 284, 064. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: The reason for this is because of the docking index angle ...

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. That's because of your docking index angle of minus 3½ degrees.

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: Copy. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: And I have some Flight Plan changes for you. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Apollo 16, Houston. We'd like to verify the position of the O 2 Tank 50-Watt Heaters on Panel 226.

a16_0812817.speaker: Duke
a16_0812817.text: They are Open.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. Copy. They're Open. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: What kind of Flight Plan, LM or CSM type?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. They're CSM, if you want to get them, Ken, they're for tomorrow's activities. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, I'm ready.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, the first one is at 96:34. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Go ahead.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, there's a Verb 48 there. Change R-1 to read "10102." [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, "10102" for Verb 48, R-1 at 96:34.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That's correct. At 96:39, write in "Load EMP 509; leave on through gimbal drive check for circ." [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, at 39, "Load 509 and leave through circ gimbal drive check."

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That's correct. The next change is at 97:15. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Go.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Delete the Verb 48. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, deleted the Verb 48 at 97:15; and that's because we'd already set it; affirmative?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That's affirmative. And that also prevents you from activating that Saturn DAP. Okay, at 97:44, right after - right be - prior to the Verb 49 maneuver there, put in "Load DAP, Verb 48 (10101)(X1111)." [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay. You want to "Load Verb 48 (10101) and (X1111)." After the circ burn and ahead of the Verb 49 maneuver.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: That's affirmative and, Ken, the computer's yours; the E-memory program's loaded.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: All right, sir; thank you.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, the next change is at 98:32. Prior to the comm check there, put "Load EMP 509." [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: MCC
a16_0812817.text: Go EECOM.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, prior to comm check, "Load 509."

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. And down about 98:44 after P00, add "Terminate EMP 509, after the P24 is complete." [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, I'll terminate 509 between P00 and loading Verb 48.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. The next change is at 100 hours, 32 minutes, [pause] "Load EMP 509." [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, at about 100:32, "Load 509."

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger. And about 100:43, "Terminate EMP 509, after P24 complete." [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, will terminate 509 after P24.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, Ken, that's it on the Flight Plan changes, I hate to bring this up again, but they've got a change here for your SPS burn cue card. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: All right. What might that be?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Well, we had this - starting this thing 20 minutes early before so that we could help you prior to LOS and we're convinced that you don't really need that much time, and what we think you ought to do is get the gimbal drive test started - you know, the Main Buses on about eight minutes early rather than six minutes. So the change is to - where we had you 40 minutes or minus 20 minutes is to change that to 52 and minus eight. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay. Do I dare use my ink pen this time?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: I hope it's good for the rest of the burns now, if we change that to 52 minutes and minus eight minutes.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, that's no sweat. Thank you.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, and the next one'll become 41 minutes and minus - Correction, 53 minutes and minus seven. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, 53 and minus seven and 52 and minus eight.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Okay, now, earlier we had deleted that "Tape Recorder, High Bit Rate" line there and added it back on the back page, and I guess now we need to - to move it back. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, would you settle for minus eight, so I can just leave it where it is?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger; that's good enough. Just do it there and delete it from the back - back side of the card.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, we'll do that. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Hank, are we going to end up with temperatures that are low enough, or would you like for me to manually set this Temp In valve to a little lower temperature?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Are you talking about the Oxidizer pressure, Ken?

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: No, sir; the manual Temp In and the glycol loop.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Oh, that - EECOM advises that looks pretty good now. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, is it going to get too cold on the - on the dark side? [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Stand by a minute. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Ken, EECOM says that the present setting should keep you in good shape. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Hank, I guess I'd - I would like to run it cooler to get the cockpit a little cooler, if that isn't going to cause any other problems. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Stand by a minute, Ken.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Casper, Houston. We'd like to get the Pan Camera turned off.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, you just want to take - turn the power off, huh?

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger, we were trying to look at - run it, but we got pretty high loads on the spacecraft now, and we're getting close to LOS and there's not going to be time enough to exercise it.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, we'll just turn it off then. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay, Hank, we've got the Pan Camera Power, Off.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger, Ken. And did you happen to notice the retract time on the Mapping Camera.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Yes, sir. I meant to get that in. That was - I thought it was excessive. In fact, I thought it had maybe stuck. It was about three minutes. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger; we copy. [Long pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Go ahead.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Say again.

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: I'm ready to copy, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: Okay. On Magazine Victor, we're up to frame number 8; Sierra Sierra, frame number 13; [pause] Tango Tango, 04. November November, 36. [Pause.]

a16_0812817.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0812817.text: Roger; copy. Victor, 8; Sierra Sierra, 13; Tango Tango, 04; November November, 36.

a16_0812817.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0812817.text: That's correct, sir.

a16_0820401.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820401.text: 16, Houston. To more evenly distribute the - the electrical loads when you get on the back side after LOS, we'd like you to take Telcom Group 2 to AC1.

a16_0820401.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820401.text: Roger; that's after LOS. And in regard to the Mixing Valve, you can adjust that for an Evap Out temperature of 49 degrees, and you ought to be okay.

a16_0820401.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0820401.text: Okay, is that 49 degrees the coldest temperature? Or just how did you -

a16_0820401.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820401.text: If you adjust it right now to an Evap Out of 49...

a16_0820607.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820607.text: Apollo 16, Houston. We'd like to get an E-Mod, if we can. [Long pause.]

a16_0820607.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820607.text: And 16, Houston. Make sure you get the comm set up right in your presleep checklist here, or INCO says they won't be able to command the thing right and we'll have to wake you up next time.

a16_0820607.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820607.text: Roger. They're admonishing me to tell you to be sure you follow the checklist on setting up the comm presleep. [Pause.]

a16_0820607.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_0820607.text: Apollo 16, Houston. We're about two minutes from LOS.

a16_0820607.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0820607.text: This is Apollo Control. We've lost radio contact now with the spacecraft as it passes behind the Moon on the fourth revolution. The crew is scheduled to begin a nine-hour rest period while on the backside of the Moon, and we would expect to hear no further word from them until the end of that rest period. During this frontside pass on the fourth revolution, there were three major items covered. I'll try to run through those three, and summarize what to us appeared to be the major points. On first reacquiring contact, John Young reported that they had seen two Main Bus B undervolt conditions -

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Yeah, if we could [garble] try it.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Looking out that window makes you think you're rotating instead of flying.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: [Garble] going like this. Yeah. I keep looking back at the eight ball to see.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Oh! I didn't check that - that comm.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: How about hitting Telcom, Group 2, AC1?

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Yeah. We're in the attitude I'll be in for - six days. Yep.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Oh, yeah, you can turn it on and look the other way around. Even the real craters turn inside and out on me sometimes [garble].

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: No, but you may have some. (Laughter) The last thing I want you to do, Charlie, is to return the toothpaste.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: You may have that - and my tissues - on a nonreturn basis.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: I'll get the tissues out if that's what you want.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Get out of there, you son of a gun. Can you move? Get my...

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Well, you said you wanted some tissues. They're right in there -right down under there. Yeah.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: I don't think so. I think they should be loose. (Laughter) Right - about where your hand is.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Got your tissues and all that stuff? Okay. Now, are you going to defecate down there? Okay.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Well, I'll do my things after you get done. Well, I'm gonna change the canister, and chlorinate some water, and all that stuff. I'll do it later. Okay? Change the canister and all that crew-sleep bull.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Because it's interconnected with the waste water system.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Not when you - look to see where those vents go together. And those boats really do go upstream. They ain't smart enough to read those check-valve labels.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Okay. We'll bump up the cabin and then get a little - Master Alarm.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: If you think you're grungy, grimy, dirty now, wait until you get out on the surface, then go back in the LM. Man, I bet - I bet that LM looks like a disaster area.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: I suspect you're right. I suspect that - we got a - a sensor that's supersensitive, and when you put loads on it, it - probably triggers at the wrong level. But I ain't gonna run around and troubleshoot it.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Well, let's see, I got to make sure - I got a pair of scissors left with me. Boy, you'd really be in deep trouble around here without your scissors. You got to make - we got to make sure that - There's some things on this transfer checklist that aren't there. What I want to do is make sure you don't transfer two more pair of scissors to the LM. (Laughter) This is...

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: No. In fact, you don't even have to put your headset on. Yeah. Yeah, if you don't want to do that, I'll plug into your hose, and let them correlate the data.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Charlie, did you fill out your menu?

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Okay. John, did you fill yours out?

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: I'll fill it out for you if you'll tell me what you ate. Beef and gravy?

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Huh? Chicken stew? Butterscotch? Chocolate bar?

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Chocolate pudding. Okay, I'll write that down.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: (Laughter) What kind of tape did that bag have on it when you opened it? (Laughter)

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: (Laughter) You had a citrus beverage? How about gingerbread?

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: Oh, man, you is a real hungry one.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0821037.text: The tissues? They're right here. Here you go. Turn around. Ohh. Darn umbilicals! I hate these things.

a16_0821037.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0821037.text: This is Apollo Control at 82 hours, 58 minutes. We're about one minute away from regaining radio contact with Apollo 16, the spacecraft now in it's fifth revolution of the Moon. And we expect the crew is in their sleep period at this time. They're scheduled to have a nine-hour rest period, beginning about 30 minutes ago, while they were on the backside of the Moon. However we will have the circuits up live in case they haven't begun their sleep period and have any last minute items to discuss with Mission Control before beginning the rest period.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: How did you guys decide who was the owner?

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Well, you know, you come equipped with one.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: And network has just called out AOS, Acquisition of Signal, and we see all of the data now suddenly come alive on the television displays here, the telemetry data from the spacecraft. We won't plan to put in a call to the crew, however we will be standing by should we get a call from them.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: And the communications engineer says that the spacecraft appears to be configured for sleep. The High Gain Antenna is in the proper position, the voice subcarrier is turned off, so we'll presume that the crew has begun its rest period.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Huh? In five to ten minutes.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: (Laughter) How about some water? It's chocolate pudding when you get through. (Laughter)

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Is it what? Yeah, we're AOS now. Yeah.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: AOS? Quite a while, I hope.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: It says do that in the morning.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Hey, do you want me to fill them for you?

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Okay. I'll fill them. How much goes in them?

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Oh, you're kidding. Okay. I'll do that right now.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0825800.text: Okay, you decided you wanted to fill those drink bags, John?

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control at 83 hours, 35 minutes. We now have a little under thirty minutes of acquisition time remaining before Apollo 16 goes around the corner on the fifth revolution of the Moon and we lose radio contact. And it has remained quiet, and no calls from the crew, and relatively little activity here in the Control Center - primarily monitoring systems and preparing for tomorrow's activities. We're continuing to watch the spacecraft orbit change gradually. We're now showing an apogee of 58.8 nautical miles [108.9 km], and a perigee, or pericynthion more correctly, of 10.5 nautical

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control at 84 hours, 3 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 16. And nearing the end of the fifth revolution around the Moon. We have about one minute, 45 seconds before we lose radio contact with the spacecraft. We've heard nothing from the crew. They're in their rest period. And all spacecraft systems appear to be functioning properly at the present time. We show Apollo 16 in an orbit 10.4 nautical miles by 58.8 [19.3 by 108.9 km]. And at this time in Mission Control we're in a midst of a shift handover. Flight Director Gene Kranz and his team of flight controllers coming on t

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 84 hours, 52 minutes into the mission. We're a little more than 20 seconds away from scheduled time of acquisition of Apollo 16, now on its sixth revolution around the Moon. We presently show an orbit of 58.8 nautical miles [108.9 km] by 10.6 nautical miles [19.6 km]. Meanwhile in the Mission Control Center, we have had a shift changeover of flight control teams. The White Team of flight controllers headed by Flight Director Gene Kranz is now aboard. Surgeon reports that he has two of the crew members on his biomed. He reported that Lunar Module Pilot Charlie

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 85 hours, 19 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We have some 40 minutes remaining on this front-side pass for Apollo 16. Now on its sixth revolution around the Moon. We've had no communication with the crew, presently in their rest period, however, we will continue to leave the line up during this front side pass. We show Apollo 16 traveling at a velocity of 5,546 feet per second [1,690 m/s]. Current altitude, 11 nautical miles [20.3 km]. The spacecraft is presently in an orbit of 58.8 nautical miles [108.9 km] by 10.5 nautical miles [19.4 km]. Spacecraft weight in

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 85 hours, 59 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. At this time we've had Loss of Signal with the Apollo 16 spacecraft as it passes above the back side of the Moon. We will take down our line at this time. And at 85 hours, 59 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 86 hours, 46 minutes into the mission. We're coming up now on acquisition with Apollo 16 now on its seventh revolution around the Moon. Apollo 16 is presently in an orbit of 58.9 nautical miles [109.1 km] by 10.6 nautical miles [19.6 km]. We expect no conversation with the crew on this front side pass. Young, Duke, Mattingly now well into their rest period. We will leave the line down on this front side pass but we'll bring it up should any conversation developed. We do now have acquisition with Apollo 16 and are receiving data. At 86 hours, 47 minutes Ground

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 87 hours, 52 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 16 has now passed out of acquisition range. We had Loss of Signal with Apollo 16 as it passes above the backside of the Moon on it's 7th revolution. We show orbital parameters of 58.8 nautical miles [108.9 km] and 10.4 nautical miles [19.3 km]. We had no conversation with the crew of Apollo 16 during this frontside pass. The crew is presently in a rest period. We're at 87 hours, 53 minutes and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 88 hours, 40 minutes into the mission. We're standing by now awaiting acquisition with the Apollo 16 spacecraft on its eighth revolution around the Moon. We presently show an orbit of 58.9 nautical miles [109.1 km] by 10.6 nautical miles [19.6 km]. The flight surgeon here in Mission Control reports that Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly and Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke were sleeping very well when he looked at their data through the last pass. We are now receiving data from Apollo 16. The spacecraft has been reacquired. We're at 88 hours, 41 minutes into

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 89 hours, 46 minutes into the flight. We now show Apollo 16 with an orbit of 58.8 nautical miles [108.9 km] by 10.4 nautical miles [19.3 km]. The Apollo 16 spacecraft has passed out of range on its eighth revolution around the Moon. On this past frontside pass, we had no conversation with the crew, still in their rest period. Our wake-up clock here in Mission Control shows that the crew has one hour and 43 minutes of sleep time remaining before the wake-up call. We're at 89 hours and 47 minutes, and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0825800.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0825800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 90 hours, 34 minutes into the mission. We now show Apollo 16 in an orbit of 58.9 nautical miles [109.1 km] by 10.5 nautical miles [19.4 km]. We're coming up on acquisition of the spacecraft on this the ninth revolution. Because we will wake up the crew at some point on this frontside pass, we will leave the line up live. And at 90 hours, 35 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston. We're acquiring data now.

a16_0912400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0912400.text: How you down there this morning, Houston?

a16_0912400.speaker: Peterson
a16_0912400.text: Roger. Got about three short items and a SIM bay status, if you're ready. [Pause.]

a16_0912400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0912400.text: Okay. Can we hold off on the SIM bay status? And I'll copy your three short items.

a16_0912400.speaker: Peterson
a16_0912400.text: Okay. The first one is - based on our evaluation, your potassium levels are running a little low, and we'd like to recommend that you drink some orange juice this morning. [Pause.] Also, you've got a long day ahead of you, so we'd like to recommend that you eat a bit more food. [Pause.] Second item is terminate Battery Bravo charge. The third item is terminate the jet-on monitor. [Long pause.]

a16_0912400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0912400.text: Okay, Don. Number one, I understand your comment about the potassium low and all that jazz. We've just finished up breakfast, and I think we've eaten almost everything that the LMies have to eat. And we - we've been drinking all the drinks every day. And, if we get a chance, well we'll try to get some more - get another juice bag out. We will terminate the Battery B charge and terminate the Jet Monitor, and I understand the way to do the Jet Monitor is - I'll go to - I'll go to the SCS mode and key a Verb 37 Noun 20 and then verify that Noun 26 is all zeros again. And I can go back to P20. is

a16_0912400.speaker: Peterson
a16_0912400.text: There's no requirement to go to SCS, 16.

a16_0912400.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0912400.text: Okay. I can just call [Verb] 37 [Noun] 20 without getting any firings?

a16_0912400.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0912400.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 91 hours, 30 minutes. That's Ken Mattingly aboard Apollo 16 who has been speaking with CapCom Don Peterson here in Mission Control.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: 16, just to be sure we're talking the same thing - to kill the jet-on Monitor, we want to do a Verb 37 Enter, 30 Enter, a Verb 37 Enter, 20 Enter and zero the Noun 26. [Long pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0913110.text: Don, I can't get to the Updates Book where that's written down. Would you read it to me slowly, and I'll do that terminate right now.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: Okay, it's Verb 37 Enter, 30 Enter, Verb 37 Enter, 20 Enter, zero the Noun 26. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: And, 16, you're about one minute to LOS, and you're looking good. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0913110.text: Okay. And we've - we're taking an extra orange with potassium this morning.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Young
a16_0913110.text: Houston, 16. Take a look at that biomed off of me and see how it looks. Over.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Young
a16_0913110.text: I got it reset - from yesterday.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: Ken, still looks a little loose. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Young
a16_0913110.text: Well, it's not loose. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: We'll have to take a better look at it next time around, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Young
a16_0913110.text: Okay. This is John, and the sensors are fixed. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: We've got confusion down here on who we're monitoring, John. [Long pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: John, the lead we're concerned with is the sternal lead - the one on your breastbone. You might jiggle it a little bit. [Long pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0913110.text: Gee, we're doing that. It sure looks like it's all tight.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: John, you might try putting new sponges on that lead. [Pause.]

a16_0913110.speaker: Young
a16_0913110.text: Okay. I did that last night.

a16_0913110.speaker: Peterson
a16_0913110.text: Okay. We'll pick you up next rev and talk about it.

a16_0913110.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0913110.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 91 hours, 37 minutes into the mission. We've had Loss of Signal with Apollo 16. The last conversation aboard the spacecraft was John Young checking on his biomedical sensors. We're at 91 hours, 37 minutes into the mission and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Here you go.

a16_0913110.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Want to change with me now?

a16_0913110.speaker: Crew (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: [Garble].

a16_0913110.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: [Garble].

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Share the drink.

a16_0913110.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: [Garble].

a16_0913110.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Okay. I'm not gonna make you drink it.

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: You want yours, Charlie?

a16_0913110.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: [Garble].

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: There you are.

a16_0913110.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: I got a [garble].

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Okay.

a16_0913110.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: [Garble] to the [garble] very cold.

a16_0913110.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Okay, we're eating.

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Okay, have you got all the - got all the bags filled with tools and all that stuff?

a16_0913110.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Yeah, we're...

a16_0913110.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: You got the pills down there, Charlie?

a16_0913110.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0913110.text: Sure [garble] right there.

a16_0913110.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0913110.text: This is Apollo Control at 92 hours, 15 minutes Ground Elapsed Time and some 13 minutes, 12 seconds until Apollo 16 reappears from behind the Moon in this tenth lunar orbit. Gerry Griffin's Gold Team of flight controllers settled in for the day's activities leading up to powered descent and lunar landing. The offgoing shift of flight controllers have practically all left the room having debriefed their replacements. There will not be a change of shift briefing. Repeat, will not be a change of shift briefing, in as much as the preceding shift was primarily a sleep shift. Apollo 16 still in a 59

a16_0913110.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0913110.text: This is Apollo Control; 92 hours, 27 minutes into the mission of Apollo 16. Less than a minute away from Apollo 16's reappearance around the eastern limb of the Moon on lunar orbit number 10. On this next frontside pass, the main concern of the crew will be transferring quite a few of the pieces of gear and equipment into the Lunar Module, getting the Lunar Module prepared for the descent and landing at the Descartes landing site. Six minutes away, we may be a few moments late getting acquisition because of the apparent position of the High Gain Antenna as seen on the ground by the communicati

a16_0922700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0922700.text: We're in the process of a little suit donning here, and we've got one problem. When I went to retract the mass spectrometer, and the gamma ray boom came in fine, but the mass spectrometer boom indicates barber pole and has stayed barber pole about ten minutes. I went ahead and enabled the jets. And I'd like for you to take a look at the - at the - telemetry talkback on the boom, and see if you can suggest something for me to do.

a16_0922700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0922700.text: Barber pole. It's a total barber pole.

a16_0922700.speaker: Irwin
a16_0922700.text: 16, this is Houston. We're wondering if you've gone through the malfunction procedure for that Boom Retraction on page 1-24 of the Systems Handbook?

a16_0922700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0922700.text: Well, I looked and didn't find one that was appropriate.

a16_0922700.speaker: Irwin
a16_0922700.text: Okay. I guess you're right, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_0922700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0922700.text: We're pretty busy, as you knows Jim: and so I'd really appreciate it if you could talk me through whatever steps you want.

a16_0922700.speaker: Irwin
a16_0922700.text: 16, this is Houston. We'd like you to put the Mass Spec Boom switch to the Off position. That's if it's not there already.

a16_0922700.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0922700.text: Okay. And when I do, it goes to gray.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: 16, this is Houston. We had understood that you had activated all your RCS jets. We show you still in the SIM bay configuration. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay. Thank you. I have the switches with the circuit breakers I had left out.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: 16, this is Houston. You can go normal acquisition procedures on the S-band.

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Jim, what did you want me to do with that High Gain?

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: We wanted you to go through normal acquisition procedures. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: 16, will you go Auto on the High Gain?

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: You have it.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Six - Never mind. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Okay, 16. This is Houston. We have SIM bay data now. Will you go back to Retract on the - on the Boom switch? [Pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay. [Pause.] You have Retract, Jim.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: 16, this is Houston. Will you check the talkback on that boom, and tell us whether it's full barber pole or a partial? [Pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: It's the same as it's been, Jim. It's a barber pole, full.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Okays we copy; a full barber pole. We show it partially retracted within acceptable limits. [Pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: What do you mean partially retracted? Does that mean your telemetry point has cinched closure?

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: That's affirmative.

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay, then I'll put it back into the Off position?

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Stand by, Ken. I think we - we want it in Retract.

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay, I'll leave it in Retract.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Okay, you could put the Retract switch back to the Off position. [Pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay, Retract is Off.

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Roger.

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: If you can watch that thing on telemetry, I can extend it enough to clear it and then try a Retract again. [Pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Irwin
a16_0923500.text: Okay, let's - We're within limits, Ken. Let's hold what we have. [Pause.]

a16_0923500.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0923500.text: Okay.

a16_0924347.speaker: Irwin
a16_0924347.text: Roger. We're ready, Ken. Go ahead.

a16_0924347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0924347.text: Okay, when I look in under the LM umbilical connector cover, the roller cam looks normal, and everything I can see from that side looks correct. When I look under the cover on the right side - that's the probe connector cover - I look at the bungee in the - the little arm that sticks out from the bottom of the cam - when I compare it to another latch, it doesn't stick out as far; in fact, the back of this part - this inner piece of the bell crank - I can get the part number on it, and it's - it's flush; whereas, on the other end, it sticks out and it shows the pin; so it looks like it hasn't c

a16_0924347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0924347.text: If you had a docking latch on the table there, somewhere, you could see what I'm looking at. [Long pause.]

a16_0924347.speaker: Irwin
a16_0924347.text: Ken, this is Houston. Can you see anything that might be obstructing or interfering with that cam action?

a16_0924347.speaker: Irwin
a16_0924347.text: Okay, 16; this is Houston. if you go to P00 and Accept, we'll uplink you. Okay, just Accept. [Pause.]

a16_0924924.speaker: Irwin
a16_0924924.text: Okay, 16; this is Houston. You can go back to Block. [No answer.]

a16_0924924.speaker: Irwin
a16_0924924.text: 16, this is Houston. Did you copy?

a16_0925851.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0925851.text: Houston, we just passed over the good landing site, and you can see the whole area. Stands out very nicely just like the model.

a16_0925851.speaker: Irwin
a16_0925851.text: Very good, Ken. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0925851.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0925851.text: Houston, from my present position I can't be sure exactly where I am because I just looked out the window again but - we passed over a large crater, and it has three little domes in the bottom of it with craters in the top of them; and they look like very subtle cinder cones. I'll try to mark that guy on the way back. It's one of a cluster of two large ones and several smaller ones.

a16_0925851.speaker: Irwin
a16_0925851.text: 16, this is - Houston. Will you give us another reading on that docking tunnel index when you have an opportunity?

a16_0925851.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0925851.text: It's still the same thing: minus 3.5.

a16_0930607.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0930607.text: Okay. John and Charlie got their suits on and they're in the LM. Is there any reason they shouldn't go ahead and power up and get some cooling?

a16_0930607.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0930607.text: This is Apollo Control. Apollo 16 Commander John Young and Lunar Module Pilot Charlie Duke are running almost 40 minutes ahead of the Flight Plan, in as much as they've already donned their pressure suits and they're in the Lunar Module, preparing to power it up. Flight Plan calls for transfer...

a16_0930607.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0930607.text: Houston; Orion on internal power at 93:07.

a16_0930607.speaker: Irwin
a16_0930607.text: And, Ken, this is Houston. The reason for that undervoltage last night was that the - all the heaters just happened to come on at that particular time.

a16_0930607.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0930607.text: Say again, Jim. We were cycling over to relief valve at the time [chuckle].

a16_0930607.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0930607.text: Okay. Did you get my call on the LM power at 93:07?

a16_0930607.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0930607.text: This is Apollo Control. Some 25 minutes remaining now in this frontside pass in the tenth lunar orbit of Apollo 16 before the still docked Orion and Casper go around the corner on the western limb of the Moon. At 93:09, still live on the tenth lunar orbit, this is Apollo Control.

a16_0930607.speaker: Irwin
a16_0930607.text: 16, this is Houston. S-Band Aux Sci switched to Off. Over. [Pause.]

a16_0931925.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0931925.text: Houston, can I give you some torquing angles, or did you copy them?

a16_0931925.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0931925.text: Okay, and we're in the maneuver.

a16_0931925.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0931925.text: This is Apollo Control. The maneuver, referred to just then by Ken Mattingly aboard the Command Module Casper, was the maneuver to the undocking attitude which has a Roll 0, Pitch 104, and Yaw 0; just about on time as called for in the Flight Plan. Some 14 minutes and 8 seconds until Loss of Signal, this is Apollo Control at 93:20.

a16_0931925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0931925.text: Ken, this is Houston. Our plan on the mass spec boom is to leave it where it is, and we're going to ask John and Charlie to check it after undocking, with respect to position. [Pause.]

a16_0931925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0931925.text: And when I was trying to talk to you before, I just wanted to give you the words on that undervoltage which y'all had last night. The reason for that was the fact that all the heaters came on at the same time. Over.

a16_0931925.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0931925.text: Okay, I guess maybe I jumped the gun, but it seemed to me like that - that Master Alarm came on instantly when I hit that switch, and it seemed like the only prudent thing to do was to undo what I just did. [Pause.] I'm glad to hear that, though. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_0931925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0931925.text: And, Ken, if you're - got a few minutes there - I could give you a Flight Plan update, a very short one.

a16_0931925.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0931925.text: Could - could you hold it? I'm in the middle of - suit donning and canister change.

a16_0931925.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0931925.text: This is Apollo Control. We have confirmation that the communications system aboard the Lunar Module is activated. We're beginning to get data out of the LM.

a16_0932357.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932357.text: Ken, will you have Orion select the aft antenna? [Pause.]

a16_0932357.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932357.text: Very good. We're reading you loud and clear.

a16_0932357.speaker: Duke
a16_0932357.text: And you're really beautiful, too. We are on Page 3-6, Step 6. We'd have been a little bit further along, but we had trouble with John's zipper today.

a16_0932357.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932357.text: Orion, will you go Down Voice Backup? [Long pause.]

a16_0932357.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932357.text: Casper, this is Houston. If there's anyth - anything significant from Orion, will you relay, because there is excessive noise down here.

a16_0932357.speaker: Duke
a16_0932357.text: How do you read, Jim? [Long pause.]

a16_0932357.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932357.text: Casper, this is Houston. How do you read?

a16_0932357.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0932357.text: This is Apollo Control. Five minutes away from Loss of Signal as Apollo 16 passes behind the Moon. Lunar Module cabin now showing at 5.02 pounds per square inch pressure [34.6 kPa]. Suit pressure 4.98 [psi - 34.33 kPa] for both men. Cabin temperature 68°F [20°C].

a16_0932925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932925.text: Orion, this is Houston. How do you read?

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0932925.text: You're five by, Jim. How me?

a16_0932925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932925.text: Roger; we're reading you. We still got a lot of noise, but we don't have the big dish up yet.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke
a16_0932925.text: Okay, we got a signal strength of about 3.9 on the Aft Omni.

a16_0932925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932925.text: Roger. Understand 3.9 on the Aft Omni.

a16_0932925.speaker: Irwin
a16_0932925.text: 16, this is Houston. You're two minutes, LOS. [Pause.]

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly
a16_0932925.text: Okay, thank you. You got it.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke
a16_0932925.text: You don't have your audio breaker in, do you?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke
a16_0932925.text: Did you turn on your stuff?

a16_0932925.speaker: Young
a16_0932925.text: That's better. Okay. Thank you. What was that? How did you fix that?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke
a16_0932925.text: I just put my mike closer to my mouth.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke
a16_0932925.text: And talked up a little bit. I've got my Master Volume up full.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young
a16_0932925.text: Okay, where are you at, Charlie?

a16_0932925.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0932925.text: This is Apollo Control. We've had Loss of Signal as Apollo 16, still docked at this time, passed behind the Moon during the end of the 10th lunar orbit. The crew of Apollo 16 considerably ahead of the timeline and getting the Lunar Module manned and checked out. All three crewmen suited at this time. Approximately 46, 47 minutes until acquisition. We'll come back up at acquisition at the start of lunar orbit revolution number 11, lunar orbit number 11, and at 93:35, this is Apollo Control.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Well, at least we got one improvement over the simulators.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: [Garble] How about a - you need a 16 65 before I get away from here, John?

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: No, I - no, I - Tell him no.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I can hear him - I can hear him through your headset.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Go B to Receive and - and then VHF A to T/R.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. Okay. What's those numbers again?

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: We're through with the LM umbilicals, I hope.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: There's a lot of [garble] up here.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Man, this zero gravity is so neat.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I think it's almost as easy to [garble] it was designed [garble] Yes, sir. I'm gonna count them [garble] at least a dozen [garble] Yeah. I'll stow them.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah. You take the umbilicals onto your side? That's new, huh?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. On my checklist, it says verify them stowed.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah. We don't want to - we don't want to leave these up here .... get in the way.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: It says both electrical umbilicals removed. Drogue - Oh, yeah. It does say remove them.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: If you get into Min Dead Band Attitude hold, I can go ahead and do this coarse align.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Wait - Wait a - No, wait a minute. Let - you can't do it without his numbers. And he's doing the tunnel stuff now.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: He wanted you to go - to do the coarse align, but let's do the tun - whatever you think's faster.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah, we're - The only way we'll keep from screwing up is to follow the checklist. Which comes after - comes after the tunnel. Wait a minute. After what? No, sir. I got a coarse align that comes 40 minutes after probe and drogue. If I get out of sync, I'm going to make you run the [garble] Well, you're way ahead of your time line, and I'm just barely hanging on.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay, go ahead. I just didn't see that. Ours just has us at - way ahead of that.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Oh, I see what - Okay, you're right. All I'm supposed to do is verify this stuff. Let him get that end, John. We - we're in Fat City. Man, I'm putting a lot of load on this suit in the back...

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Hey, I don't get much feedback in my mikes. I thought I'd be able to hear myself.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: You know what we need is some orange juice things over here - drinks.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: That water's not leaking, is it?

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Putting all this stuff in here. Trying to put the food on and then do [garble] food [garble].

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. Let's start on the business. You say put the probe in, huh? I'll probe and drogue [garble] probe and drogue [garble].

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I could do the landing gear deploy. You want to do that?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah, that sounds all right to me. They don't have to see that.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. Tell Ken we're gonna deploy the landing gear.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Hey, Ken. If you hear a thump, we're gonna deploy the landing gear.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Circuit Breaker 11, ED Landing Gear Flag, Close.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Master Arm is coming On. System B light.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. Landing Gear Gear Deploys Fire.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: No doubt in my mind. You get a gray?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. ED 11, Logic Power A, Close.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Fire again, huh? Landing Gear Deploy, Fire again.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Hey, it's out, John! I can see the front footpad.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: And then look at the front footpad. Master Arm, Off.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah, Landing Gear Flag. Man, have we got the condensation in here. Looks like you're serious about this.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. You got the - you got some - three capture latches in there? All righty.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Hey, you - Is this your pair of scissors here, Charlie?

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Did you take them out of here?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I took them out of the data card kit.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Last chance to swap seats, Charlie. I got my LOG all ready.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: [Garble] Man, this - this water cooling is so nice, Ken.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Are you in Auto on the Quads? No. Okay. Going to Auto on the Quads, Charlie.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Super. They're already up there, ain't they?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah, I push - those breakers on your side are...

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: ...manual. I mean they're - they cycle on and off by themselves.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Hey, let's get the AOT reticule thing out and put it on.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Oh. I forgot that. That's part of the housekeeping.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I wonder how I forgot that?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I'd look out the - yeah, I'll look out the other way.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: I know it. I just wanted to write it down for the [Apollo] 17 guys.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: My ears have cleared up, John. I mean my sinuses.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: With as much simulator time as we got ... What's the matter, Ken?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah. And it's tight. I can't budge it. You know, I wish I could cut my microphone off on my left side. That way I wouldn't get this drink bag squa - squirted in my face every time.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Pretty exciting, isn't it? [Garble] me another shot of water, Charlie.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Come on. Let's chill it down a little bit.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Can't understand why we're down to 91 percent on the Descent O 2 . Both tanks.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: They never told me they weren't going to.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: That may be what it reads.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: You all finished? I'm gonna close the hatch.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Don't close the hatch until he gets on comm.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: This zero gravity is so neat.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. I've checked the exterior. The capture latches are engaged and locked, I got three good ones. And from my side, they're removed, the lock lever's engaged and flush; so we're all set.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Can you hear me on the comm, Ken?

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah, it is, T.K. If you go to Min Deadband Attitude hold and give me a [Verb] 06 [Noun] 20, I'd appreciate it.

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. I'll get with it right now.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay, Ken. I'm gonna close the hatch. We'll see you in 3 days, babe.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: And don't run off and leave us.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: You want me to check and see if it's sealed? Want me to check the seal and see if there's anything in it before you close it? There was nothing in it, huh ?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Uh-huh. Going Auto, Press Reg A A -

a16_0932925.speaker: Mattingly (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay, John. I'm in Min Dead Band.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Okay. Okay. Plus zero - plus 002.74, plus 109.36, plus 004.57.

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Did you get the docking angle written down, John?

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: Yeah. Just like in the training units. These -

a16_0932925.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0932925.text: These helmet - these helmet bags, the plate - the - the snap caved in over here and you can't get it snapped.

a16_0932925.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
