a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: I don't think that's what it is right now.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: That's [garble] all that stuff? Oh, man. [garble].

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Makes you think that the [garble] valve [garble][garble] landing radar, Ken. Pick me up [garble].

a16_0991703.text: Look at that.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: What?

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Already lost some of it.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: This was pretty good flight.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Going down.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Got time for this [garble]? It has - it's got a main [garble] minus something.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Well, it will be here pretty quick, Charlie. [Garble].

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: That's 20 minutes. I don't think we'll ever agree on that, though; okay?

a16_0991703.text: Okay. Let's try [garble].

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (CM onboard)

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: [Garble] plans.

a16_0991703.text: [Garble] flight [garble].

a16_0991703.text: [Garble] oh, okay [garble] try to [garble].

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: I didn't get a chance to follow all the things [garble]. Do you have any problems or anything?

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: We got a RCS problem, but it's not too bad. And, otherwise, we're okay. We can't get our steerable antenna up.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: You don't need that now, do you?

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: No.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Can you land on omni?

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Yeah, we can land on omni. How does that thing look to you, Ken? Is it unstable everywhere?

a16_0991703.text: Yes, sir. There's no question about it. I - any - any force at all that moves at all makes it go unstable. Looks like feedback in the control.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Is that Main B? Is it run off Main B?

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Yeah. But I don't think that - it's not likely that I wouldn't have done that, I wouldn't think. They - they told me after - I guess it was after you guys had left that they went back and looked at the dumps and found that we happened to hit all the heaters at one time.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Ah so. Well, I never did think it was a good idea to run those gimbal motors that long.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Well, I guess they're having some of those kind of thoughts right now, too.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Yeah. Those once in a million problems like that coarse align, and everybody gets boresighted on it.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Well, I guess we really need to wait and see [garble] really want. You never know, those guys might come through here and find a way to take you down. a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Yeah.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: But if you just count on the external forces not moving it, then I don't know what you do. I was thinking maybe we could use it in Accel Command with - just set the proper trim and immediately go to SCS and Accel Command, point it the right direction.

a16_0991703.text: [Garble] that pulse. [Garble]

a16_0991703.text: You sleeping?

a16_0991703.text: Was I sleeping? I was almost asleep.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: I bet my bride is beside herself.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Yeah.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: We're now passing right [garble] through Scorpio.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Well, we'll be two revs late, but we'll do it.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: I hope you're right.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: We ain't gonna do any EVA today, either.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: You don't want to?

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Not for two revs, Charlie. Let's do it tomorrow and do the full thing.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: What's it do, bend?

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: Probably the first dish, yeah.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0991703.text: He's dropping down out the bottom of the window.

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Yep.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: Did find out that once we got the LM off there that the - we'd be able to see it a lot better. I guess the telescope just wiped out the [garble] the LM.

a16_0991703.text: What's the limitation of how long you can stay before - you can't go down?

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: No, I mean what's the limiting factor? Is it water?

a16_0991703.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: No. We got plenty of water.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: We could - we can land and just do a couple of EVAs.

a16_0991703.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0991703.text: I just wondered what - how they came up with five revs - was it water or what [garble]?

a16_0991703.text: Got no idea.

a16_0991703.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0991703.text: I don't know.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0993100.text: This is Apollo Control, 99 hours, 31 minutes Ground Elapsed Time into the mission of Apollo 16. To recap the current situation here in Mission Control Center, various considerations are underway on whether or not to continue the mission with a later landing or to have the two spacecraft, Orion and Casper, rendezvous, dock and do a Trans-Earth Injection burn using the Lunar Module's Descent Propulsion System. a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Is that sunrise?

a16_0993100.text: Yep.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Did you say you had sunrise, Charlie?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: It's coming up. We can see it glowing beyond the horizon.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: It's gonna be instant sunrise.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: [Garble] doing? Man, looks like [garble] dark as ever.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: It's behind you, Ken.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, it's behind you, boy. When it comes up, we won't be able to see you anymore.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay; I've got you boresighted.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Be kind of hard to get a radar lock. Oh, no.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeow!

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Boy! Did you ever brighten up in a hurry!

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: It was long before we got there, though, that we saw it, right?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Right. Yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Do you reckon light bends?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Huh?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Reckon the light bends?

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Man, are you ever bright!

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Where'd my glove go?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: We were Go for PDI there for a while.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I can't - I can't believe it. I can't believe it (laughter). We'd had no trouble at all picking up the site either.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I know; it's beautiful. I guess you can't win them all.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I'm not getting any cooling at all, Charlie. Are you?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Cooling?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: A little bit out of the suit. Not much.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Why don't you go to LGC on a - for a second or two?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Charlie, we ought to have an eat period is what we ought to do. You ain't hungry?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: No.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: How about something to drink, or something like that?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Back there in the food locker.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I don't want anything, really.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: You don't? Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Unless they got a sandwich or something back there. I'll eat that.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: All they got is those drinks, Charlie. Those orange drinks.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Wait a minute. Open the top, John.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I don't want to get too close to the hatch.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Ain't nothing wrong with the hatch. It's okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Those two on the left come open.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, I know it, if I can get to them.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: See. Those orange drinks.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: What's all that's in there, is orange drinks?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, there's some stuff behind it, but I can't get at it. I'm not - I just can't. I - I could reach it with the moving the orange drinks, but if I do, I don't know what I'm gonna do with them.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Put them in the Flight Data File up here. There's plenty of room up here.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Oh, oh. Excuse me.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Son of a gun, I keep - I keep getting them things.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: In this one?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah. Either one.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Don't think there is plenty of room in there. No, there ain't.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Man, there is more pieces of metal around this spacecraft! You want a food stick?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: It won't go in there?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Might if I fold them in half.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Stick them into the ISA then.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: There we go.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I'd hate for any of that stuff to get loose in zero gravity. It would be a mess.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Charlie, you got me almost to PDI there.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, I tried hard.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: You did good.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: But if the gear don't work. Well, maybe they'll come up with something.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: How about a food stick? Can I have a food stick, Charlie?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Sure.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Don't know where he is now.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, I thought they said that was our closest point of approach, and it sure doesn't look to me like it's gonna be. Looks like we passed it back there about 20 minutes ago.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, I - I agree with you. They want you to be active.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: There is no way they can tell what it is or, these short things; they don't have any idea where we are, Charlie - Ken.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Charlie, I'm going to try reacquire range and make sure I don't have a bad rate.

a16_0993100.text: Okay, I got 0.68 on the...

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I got 0.52. Let me reacquire and we'll try it again.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: That - What is that? That's not 1678.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: No, that's...

a16_0993100.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand what you said, John.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: We should lock on you and give you range and range rate.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, I thought you were saying you didn't have your radar, and I thought that made good sense.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: No. We got plenty.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: We've got plenty of radar. We're going to do it.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I thought you were trying to save on your amps.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: No. No, we got plenty of amps.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay. Well, that would help. That's better than this thing.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Dang right. Where are - Which way should we pitch to get to you?

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Beg your pardon?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Which way should we pitch to get to you?

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Oh. Well, let me see here. All - Oh, boy. It's hard to tell what figures I'm looking at, it's so bright. I think I'm looking at the top of you, though.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: That's what it says, pitch up.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: [Garble], Well, you can't believe that, Charlie. We ain't updated it.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Huh?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: We ain't updated it or nothing.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I said - Oh, you mean the radar?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I don't see him anywhere.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: That's superbright. That must be - maybe I'm looking at the heat shield around your engine. That's probably it, because I can see the four gear. You - you must be pitched 180 to me.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: That's what I thought. He's been going in under us.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, why did you say pitch up?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I didn't say that, Ken did.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: (Laughter) You ain't gonna take credit for it, huh? [Garble] I'd have swore I heard you say pitch up.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, that's what the AGS says, but that ain't right.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, it must have been - You know...

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: ...you can't - Anything less than a mile, these things ain't no good. Because - Well, AGS is okay. But this thing here measures from the center of the Moon. I don't have the foggiest notion where our boy is.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Hear that noise?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: It's in the comm. Oh, that whooooo? Oh, yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: That's what I mean.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: We were back here - It's got something to do with the VHF ranging.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Boy, I don't see him anywheres.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Think we got quite a ways to pitch yet.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Oh, shoot. Do it.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: There he is. Yeah, he's way far away from us. I think what the problem is, Ken...

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: There he is, dead ahead.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: ...is you're opening up.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Dead ahead.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, I got it.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Push the Rendezvous Breakers breakers in.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, that's a good idea.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I agree with you.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: You want to be careful how much velocity you add, because you're too low to add a lot. Or...

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: So far I've just put in two foot per second, but that's - that's even closing [garble]

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0993100.text: It looks like you're looking at me now.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, two foot per second, you should of took out two foot a second on account of you're ahead of us.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Say again?

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Remember Mr. Kepler?

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Say again, John.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Either way, two foot in or out will do it. That'll make him slow down when he goes up over the top of us.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I'd rather have - There we go.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Hey, we got him. Okay. He's still opening.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay. What kind of a range do you read now?

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: 0.66 miles and open, and it's 0.6 foot a second.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, I guess I better put in another couple of foot per second then. Hate using all that gas on it, but I guess that's the only way.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Let me get him boresighted and locked up.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Well, let me get it like this.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay. Thought we might have had a side lobe.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: There you go. Go to LGC.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Got a side lobe.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0993100.text: Okay, what do you show now? ["Tell me when you [garble]" in LM comm]

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Stand by, Ken. We had a side-lobe block. We're getting the main lobe.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: That looks like it, John. Oh, you want to go to -

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_0993100.text: There we go.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay; we close. Show 0.68 miles [1.26 kilometres], 0 feet a second,

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, you're 4200 [feet, 1,280 metres] out. It says here it -

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Okay; we show you -

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Better not add too much.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: No. I'd just hold what you got, Ken.

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0993100.text: Okay.

a16_0993100.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: He'll drop way down. You know, if he - if he fires this way, it's retrograde; it's gonna drop him low - lower his orbit.

a16_0993100.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0993100.text: Yeah, how much did you put in?

a16_0993100.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0993100.text: I put in a total of 3.5 [feet per second or 1.0 metres per second].

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay. Well, that's gonna get you right close to the ground.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Not from over here.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Well, I ain't gonna get very far from you.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0995600.text: This is Apollo Control; 99 hours, 56 minutes Ground Elapsed Time into the mission of Apollo 16. Some seven minutes, 40 seconds away from acquisition on the 14th lunar revolution. To recap again the current situation in the mission, the circularization burn for Command Module Casper was aborted when Ken Mattingly discovered some discrepancies in the backup system which controls the Service Propulsion Engine. We still have a good prime system, that is a Guidance and Navigation system aboard the Command Module. However, we would be one failure away for the very critical Trans-Earth Injection mane

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Am I closing any yet?

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: No. It - it'll take half a rev.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay, I'm not sure - it seemed to me like they gave us bum dope on this 100 hours.

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah, you know they have no idea where we are.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah, but they know where we undocked and we haven't done anything. Think they ought to...

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: No, no. There's no way. Not for short ranges like this.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: I really wanted to get within half a rev. I guess that ought to be a radial burn, shouldn't it?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay. We show you closing slightly now, about a half a foot a second.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah, it shows it took me down to 8.6. But as long as I stick with you, I can't get too far away.

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay. Our Range Rate meter says you're 4,100 foot [1,250 metres] out.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: What do you show for your - perilune?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: The what?

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: What's your perilune?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Ours says 11.0 [miles, 20.4 kilometres], Ken.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay, I'm reading 8.6 [15.9 kilometres].

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: I guess the five revs might have been, John, the - the high gain coverage they got, since our steerable doesn't work. We can go as long as we got the 210.

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah.

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: It's going to be hard to run - He's going to take a lot of gas to get over here.

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Should have took it out.

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Huh?

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: You thrusted toward us 3.5 feet a second. Is that true?

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: I thrusted toward you 3.5. Yeah that was - looks like mostly retrograde.

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah. Looks like to me you're gonna have to go up a little bit now, a couple of feet a second.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Have you got some kind of a chart there I could navigate with?

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: No, we sure don't.

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: No. But, see, that retrograde burn is going to take you down, below us.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Roger. I understand that. It really looks like what I want to do is make a radial burn, you behind me. I really ought to make a radial burn now, shouldn't I?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah. Shouldn't he?

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: How about let's do that?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_0995600.text: What's my range and range rate now?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: 0.680 feet a second [0.21 metres per second].

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay. There's 0.5 foot per second 0.15 metres per second] radial out. ["0.4 foot per sec" in LM tape]

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Okay.

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Man, it's really white into zero phase, isn't it?

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Sure looks to me like I'm opening again.

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Well, we got you about zero, Ken, maybe closing slightly. I think it's gonna take a couple of feet per second radial.

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: He's got to go up like that. But with our mechanics, it may not do anything.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: I guess I'm getting a little concerned about that minus-X I put in there.

a16_0995600.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Guess I don't blame you. I'd have thought you'd have put in plus-X and rose over the top of us.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Yeah, I think I'm gonna take it back out and go the other way. That sound reasonable?

a16_0995600.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_0995600.text: Sure does to me, Ken.

a16_0995600.speaker: Mission Control
a16_0995600.text: This is Apollo Control; 100 hours, 3 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Less than a minute now away from acquisition of Orion and Casper coming around the east limb of the Moon on the 14th lunar revolution. Standing by for acquisition here half a minute away. The atmosphere here in the control room is reminiscent of the period just after the cryogenic oxygen tank incident on Apollo 13. Ten seconds. We're waiting confirmation from the network controller that we've had acquisition.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Okay; here we go.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Okay, there's two - two power.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Okay, now that shows you're opening at 3 and a - that shows you're opening at 3 [feet per second - 0.9 metres per second].

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Here comes Earthrise. See it?

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Yeah.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: That's spectacular.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Yeah. Now according to our mechanics, you're bound to end up behind us, and close to us.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Okay. That shows I got a 59 by 9 [nautical mile, 109 by 17 kilometres orbit].

a16_1000344.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1000344.text: We have AOS, Lunar Module. Let's stand by now for resumption of communications between the control center, Jim Irwin CapCom, and the crew of Casper and Orion.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (CM)
a16_1000344.text: Houston, Orion. How do you read?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Orion, this is Houston. Read you loud and clear.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (CM)
a16_1000344.text: Roger; same-o, Jim. We're about 0.7 of a mile [1.3 km] out from Casper now.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Say again, Charlie. We still have excessive noise down here.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (CM)
a16_1000344.text: I say our range to Casper is about 0.7 of a mile.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (CM)
a16_1000344.text: And he's opening at 2½ [feet per second, 0.8 metres per second]. He put in some posigrade velocity to go up and above and come down and get with us.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: John, I think that total is still slightly retrograde.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (CM)
a16_1000344.text: The total is (slightly retrograde?) [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Yeah, you - I - I'm thinking maybe I ought to go put some more in there. What do you think?

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay, 16. This is Houston. We still do not have an answer, but people are working very feverishly. [Pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1000344.text: Orion. Roger.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Okay; thank you. It'll probably be awhile before we get to station-keeping anyway.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: That only shows 9.2 [2.8 metres per second]. Why don't we get them to get an arc on this? I guess I'd like to know how good my vector was to start with.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: It's no good this close in, Ken.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: How's that?

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: It's not any good this close in.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Say again? I'm sorry; I can't hear you.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Okay. I can't hear you.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: He said it's not any good this close in.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: I know, but my state vector is good. How good is it?

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Oh, okay.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: That's what I'd like to know from Houston.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: You're not locked on them?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Stand by, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Ken - Ken, you should be able to get a lock on with them.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: No, I've been trying that.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Roger. I'm trying now.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Houston, Orion.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Go ahead, Orion.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Okay; we got an RCS System A Reg light. Pressures: Helium is looking like 2300...

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Get the B?

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: The Propellant is at 210; the Fuel Manifold at - and Ox Manifold is - correction, make it 215 - or 220. And everything else looks pretty good. Pressures are holding up - You think the burst disk is gone?

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Houston, do you read Casper?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Roger. That looks that way to us, Charlie.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Houston, do you read Casper?

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Okay.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Yes, Casper. This is Houston. Read you loud and clear.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay. Look like we got a - that 100 hours was a bad time, and I tried to close at him before he realized that it was all minus X. I put in about 3½ foot per second and got to checking. That didn't look like the right thing to do. So I took about 3 of that out, and...

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Hey, Ken, why don't you summarize what you did in the way of thrusters to tell them what to expect. Okay?

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1000344.text: I'm doing that, John.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1000344.text: ...and so I took about three of that out, and I put in a half foot per second radial at about 100 hours and 5 minutes. And I put in the rest, took two foot per second posigrade at about 100 hours and 6 minutes. And at about 100 hours, then I put in three - it was about - roughly retrograde. And my computer now shows 16.5 by 9.2. And I had a good state vector when I started, and that's probably a good value - whenever you get a short arc or something on me.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Roger. We copy, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: That [garble] sound - sounds like all the gears are broken in it.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Orion, this is Houston. We're wondering where you got the estimate of 0.7 nautical-mile range [1.3 kilometres]. [Pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: We got the Rendezvous Radar locked on, if you want us to. Or do you want us to turn it off?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: No, that's fine. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Yeah, I show us now at about 0.9 mile [1.7 kilometres]. Is that correct?

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: That's right, Ken.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM com)
a16_1000344.text: 5500 feet, Ken [1.7 kilometres].

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay. And still opening?

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Yeah.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Houston, Orion. John and I been talking about - If we get to land this thing, we'd like to - probably ought to think about going to sleep first, and we'd get up and do a full EVA tomorrow.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Roger. We - we concur down here.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay, Casper; this is Houston. We're recommending that you null the line-of-sight rates...

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Could you tell me if my range...

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: ...[garble] Go ahead.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: ...and fire five feet per second toward the LM. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay. That's still going to be mostly retrograde, it looks like. That's how I got in this place to start with.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: We copy you, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay, I'm going to hold. Can you guys get a short arc going on my trajectory?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay, Ken. We show you coming up on perilune now, so you'll be affecting your apolune. [Pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: You show me coming up on perilune?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: That's affirm. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Roger. My state vector shows 19 miles up [35 kilometres], and we're not - I'm just passing Smythii. is that - Does that sound reasonable, that we shifted that much in orbital track?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay. That sounds good, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay, I guess I'd like for you to - to summarize again where I stand. I'm a little bit confused now, Jim.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Roger. We were hoping that... [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: [Garble] I'm just passing Smythii, and my altitude according to my computer - Was my state vector a little bit off to start with?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: We think your state vector was fairly accurate, Ken. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1000344.text: Okay. Then there's still a discrepancy in...

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: And you'll be at perilune in 15 minutes. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay, that makes more sense. All right. Because I'm presently at 19 miles, and I think that's probably a good estimate. All right. If I do - Do you want me to thrust towards the LM now, because I'm approaching perilune. Is that affirmative?

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay. Now I'm - This is using up a great deal of RCS which is going to violate the next line. Is this preferable to trying to do a regular rendezvous now?

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Regular what?

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1000344.text: Because if we still have a chance at landing, then I need to [garble] to you...

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Ken, could you give us your position, relative to the LM? [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Yes, sir. I'm ahead of him and slightly below, and I show a - a mile [1.8 kilometres] on the EMS, and I don't know what John has on the radar.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Yeah, he's - he's ahead of us, and I show him about - level and 6,500 feet [2.0 km] out and opening at 3 feet a second [0.9 metres per second].

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay. We copy your position as ahead, below, and about one nautical mile. [Pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: That's affirmative.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1000344.text: And he's opening at 2½ on 16 78.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Roger.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1000344.text: And 3 feet a second on the tapemeter. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Can't unless we terminate this.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Well, let's terminate it.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Can't terminate it, huh? Go to Auto in Track.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay, Jim. To make sure there's no confusion, I haven't done anything yet.

a16_1000344.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: No, you got to...

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Thank you, sir.

a16_1000344.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1000344.text: Okay. On the - on the COAS, I've got him boresighted there, and he's 35559 from local vertical.

a16_1000344.speaker: Irwin
a16_1000344.text: Okay, Casper. This is Houston. We're convinced that we want you to fire directly at the LM about 5 feet per second. We want to get a positive closing rate.

a16_1000344.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1000344.text: Okay. That's in work.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay. Looks like the DAP isn't stable now. How about if I give it a Verb 46?

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Ken, we show you in Free.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: I am now: but I wasn't.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Does that mean I'm clear to do a Verb 46? [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. No, that doesn't work. I think maybe I've had one of those transients. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1001938.text: For some reason, every time I pick up CMC Auto, this thing - starts doing maneuvers. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Orion, let's go Lo Bit Rate.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay. I've got it under control, Jim. I had a bad DAP. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1001938.text: This is Apollo Control at 100 hours, 21 minutes. Still standing by here for a resolution of the apparent problem with the Stabilization and Control System aboard the Command Service Module. Meanwhile the two spacecraft are making the necessary maneuvers for rendezvous. Or I should qualify that to say station-keeping. Right now the Rendezvous Radar display shows a separation of some one nautical mile [1.85 km].

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay; we'll [garble] 5 feet per second directly at the LM. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: He didn't mean to do it.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: No. It's going up and over us right now.

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Casper, this is Houston. Hold up on that RCS maneuver.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay. I've put in 3 foot per second.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1001938.text: The maneuver Mattingly was attempting was a 5-foot-per-second line-of-sight RCS maneuver toward the Lunar Module. Right now, he's ahead and below the Lunar Module by about one nautical mile [1.85 km], straight-line distance. We would like to re-emphasize that this will be strictly for station-keeping. Lunar landing is still not positively ruled out at this time depending on what decision is made on the reliability of the Stabilization and Control System to control the SPS engine on the Service Module. Continuing to monitor air/ground for both spacecraft, this is Apollo Control [at] 100 hours,

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Roll's going off a little bit, John. Not that that's going to hurt you any.

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Say he's drifting down - that says he's drifting down.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Ken, to - to get us, you're going to have to thrust down to null the needles.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Thrust down means towards the Moon or down as you see it?

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. I guess I am. Houston, do you want me to go null line of sight all the way in?

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: We need a range and range rate reading now.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: 7000 feet [2100 metres], closing at 3 feet a second [0.9 m/s], and we have a line-of-site rate. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Ken. If you can kill that line of sight, you're closing.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Roger, Charlie. I'm standing by for instructions for best [garble]

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Yeah, Casper; this is Houston. You should null the line-of-sight rates. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay, do you want me to keep them nulled and go all the way in? Is that the idea?

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Roger. Keep a positive closing rate.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay. It's likely to be expensive, but we'll do that.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay, [not on PAO recording] you're going to have to - Your needles are better than [back to PAO recording] mine, why don't you tell me what to do there, John.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. Thrust down, and I'll tell you which way the needle moves. [Garble].

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, thrust away from the Moon. That's doing it. Little more. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: You didn't get it corrected, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Oh, it's just not moving very much at all.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, that's a good place to stop?

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: No, you - It's gonna be expensive, Ken, to do this, but you - you're gonna have to thrust up.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay, I just need some gauges to when I got it nulled.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. You don't have it nulled.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: You've got it to 2 milliradians. Now you've got it, Ken. You killed it.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Looks to me now like I'm drifting the other way.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay; I'll believe your needles. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Better be something right around here.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Three and a half feet [1.1 metres] a second, and you're at 6300 feet [1900 metres].

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Is the rate starting to build now? I'm trying to calibrate the deadband activity here so I can tell what the rate - when it's really a rate and when it's just deadbanding.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. Your rates are nulled, essentially.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Turn on some more water, Charlie. I don't know if I can stand this or not.

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: I think I might throw up.

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Orion, request you select the Secondary Transmitter and Receiver. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Ken - Ken, tell them I selected that Secondary. It'll be awhile.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Houston. Orion says that they have already selected the Secondary. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Houston. How do you read now?

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Read you loud and clear, Orion.

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. You're five by. How's the problem looking? [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: 16, no answers yet. We're still looking at it. [Long pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: You - you maneuvering, aren't you, John?

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: You - are you - you're pitching up, aren't you?

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1001938.text: Okay. I just wondered. He looks like to me he's moving on out there some.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Ken. You're at 5,600 feet [1,700 metres], closing at 4 feet a second [1.2 m/s].

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Orion. This is Houston. We'd like you to open the Primary Power Amp circuit breaker on [Panel] 16. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Orion, let's go Hi Bit Rate.

a16_1001938.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Rog. You have Hi Bit Rate.

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay, Ken. You're getting a line-of-sight rate. You're going to have to thrust a little toward the Moon. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Okay, we can't hold Hi Bit Rate. Request you go back to Lo Bit Rate, Orion.

a16_1001938.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1001938.text: Okay, that's up for me - it looks like it ought to be down for you. [Pause.]

a16_1001938.speaker: Irwin
a16_1001938.text: Orion, this is Houston. Can you give us a range and range rate read-out?

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: Okay; 4,900 feet [1,500 metres], closing at 5 [feet per second, 1.5 m/s].

a16_1001938.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1001938.text: You got the line-of-sight rates nulled now, Ken.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: They wouldn't want to do it the easy way. We're gonna arrive at the same time, in the dark. They've thrusted toward us at - at perigee at 100 hours. Man, that's really - I mean, he's thrusting at apogee so it'd take effect at perigee. And that's no good.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Rates nulled again, John?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yes, they're nulled right now.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay - They are going to keep building this way, and do we have some - some fuel point at which to cut off and switch over to LM power.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: How much are you using?

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Stand by, Ken.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, well, you're at 4,000 feet [1,200 metres] now, at 5 feet a second [1.5 m/s], Ken.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, hopefully, that's most of it.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: And - and - and your line-of-sight rate is starting to build a little in the other direction. You've got it now. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Orion, this is Houston. Is the CSM above you or below you? We hope he's directly ahead. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: He's at 45 degrees above us.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: : Forty-five degrees above.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Above the local vertical.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: And, he's got a - a 5-foot-a-second closing rate, and his line of sights are nulled on the radar.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: And they look like they're killed completely on the optics too. [Pause.] Going to need your tracker light here in a minute. We're just getting a little glinted sunlight now.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. It's on now?

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Which way was he supposed to thrust to null them?

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: The one that was down - then it was up, he was thrusting -

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Toward the Moon...

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: ...away from the Moon.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: It was down for him.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: It was opposite.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah. They're just opposite of what we're looking at.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Boy, those rates look steady as they can be.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: You've really got them killed. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, and since we are going to get rendezvoused in the dark - I guess we'll just come up alongside and hold stations.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: That seems like a fair thing.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: All right, sir. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Would - would it be easier to thrust down now?

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, Ken. You're going to have to thrust down a hair.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: It looks - it would be up to us, Ken. I think if we thrusted, we'd have to thrust up. I think you have to thrust down a skosh.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: That's down to you, right? [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, that's what I mean, you would thrust - you would thrust up.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. I think I got it killed again.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: It's looking good.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1003514.text: Looks pretty good. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1003514.text: What's that closure rate now?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Still five feet a second. Still off 3½ feet a second [1.1 m/s] now at 3,000 [900 metres].

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: 3½ feet per second.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Roger.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, all I've got's the tracking light; I've lost the rest of your image.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. You've - you're gonna have to thrust a little more to kill that rate the same way. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. That got a lot of it, but not all of it. [Pause.] Okay. You got most of it.

a16_1003514.speaker: CC-CM/LM
a16_1003514.text: Okay, Casper. This is Houston. You might pick up a temperature caution light on your quads, but it's of no consequence.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. Yeah, I see B is up high. Is that due to the thruster activity?

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Affirmative, Ken.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Or is that due to heater fail-on?

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: I think it's thruster activity.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. Rog.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Orion, this is Houston. Will you give us another range and range rate, John?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yep. They're at 3,100 feet [950 metres], at 3½.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Roger. 3,100 at 3½.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Roger. At an angle of 68 degrees to local vertical now.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Understand; 68 degrees. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: I can't believe I'm doing this. I can't believe we're doing this. Turn on some more water.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, Ken. You got a sight rate going to the south according to my needles. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Whoa, Charlie.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Whoa.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. Let's watch that for a minute before I start working on it, because we haven't had any plane component before.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: How's the line-of-sight rate doing now? Holding?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Holding. It's holding - the vertical one is holding right on.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: You're at 3,000 feet [900 metres], at 3 feet a second [0.9 m/s].

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. And range rate?

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1003514.text: 2,800 feet [850 metres].

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Now we must be going in the right direction then.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, you're just get there.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: You now have 2 milliradians to the south.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, I'll take some of that out. That means I go to the south, right?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yep. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: How's that? Right direction?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, that's got most of it. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Unknown speaker
a16_1003514.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: You still got some more to the south you've got to get. Still 2 milliradians. Okay. That's got it, Ken.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: All right. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, it looks like I'm picking up a rate in the opposite direction in the in-plane component.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: No, you're not - you're not - You don't have any rate yet.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: According to my needles.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: This is very much like the simulator where, because of the deadband lags, it looks like it takes a long time to pick up one of those rates. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Orion, this is Houston. We want you to get the Rendezvous Radar and the tracking light off as soon as it's feasible, to conserve power.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Roger. We will. It's not too feasible right now.

a16_1003514.speaker: Irwin
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, we understand. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, it looks like I may be a little more to the south.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Just a hair, Ken. Okay. You're at 2,400 feet [730 metres] at 2 [feet per second, 0.6 m/s].

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: He's going to need to thrust towards us a little bit.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: He thrusts the opposite way we do. We're up down.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: How about that rate to the south? It looks like it's building again. Okay.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Ken, our needles don't show it.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: He never really got it all out.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Better start using their -

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Huh?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Somebody better start using their brains and common sense here.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: What do you mean?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Or it'll blow the whole works.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: You don't think this is right, what he's doing?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: You want me to stick that card back over there?

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Hey, I show quite a drift rate now, John. Do you still show no out of plane?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, I don't show any, and I've got you boresighted in Att Hold, and I don't show any motion there either, Ken. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Where? Our needles say he's drifting south.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Just a little south, Ken.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay. It looks like - I'm going to take some of that out. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1003514.text: This is Apollo Control. Flight Director Gerry Griffin has instructed the CapCom to tell the crew that at Acquisition of Signal on Rev 15 - that's in spite of the next revolution - they'll be given a Go/No-Go for a landing on Rev 16. Hopefully by that time the situation will have resolved itself on the Thrust Vector Control System which drives the SPS. Apparently there is a problem in the yaw gimbal actuator in the Service Propulsion System. The decision has not yet been made, and hopefully will be made prior to the time of Acquisition of Signal on Revolution 15. Some 19 minutes remaining in th

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: He's going off the bellyband.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Can you tell if I'm going to - maybe I put that in the wrong direction, although I'm sure that that was the right - South is to your left, isn't it?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Whoa, Ken. You got it.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: You betcha.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. We're going the right way, then.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Hey, wait a minute, Ken...

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, Ken. You were drifting south. That's right. You have to thrust north. You got it.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: John, we've been going the right direction all along, then.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, you have. Yeah, don't worry about it.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: It appears to be I'm still a little bit out of plane. I guess that's the sensitivity of the Rendezvous Radar. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, don't worry about it.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Down to one foot [0.3 metres] a second. If he'd get a little bit more closing rate in, it'd be less gas.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: I think it would be too.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Huh?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Let's call up Verb 63 again. Can we do that? No, I don't want to - I don't want to break lock.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay; how's my closure rate?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: We're showing a foot a second on the tapemeter. It isn't closing very fast.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Well, that's what I was just wondering. There could be a little more plus-X.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. Say when and how much.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, I'm going to put in a foot plus-X.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay? As long as we are using brute force, we might as well.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, that's about a foot.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. You're at 2,000 feet [600 metres] at 2 [feet per second, 0.6 m/s]. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: There you go. It worked.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: How about that? [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: What was that?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Tunnel light.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Oh.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: I can see the LM in Earthshine now. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay, fine. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: You're getting over behind us, Ken. You're going to have to - to thrust toward us a little more.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, what's my range rate now?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: You're at 2,000 feet, but it's hardly closing at all.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, give me another foot. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, there's another foot per second. [Long pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Now you're starting to build a rate to the north.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: I don't think those needles are as good as we're using them in here.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah, I - I don't think they're quite as good.

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Yeah.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: It looks like I need to start reversing my in-plane direction.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay, do I still have a positive closure rate?

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: Yep, 3 feet a second; 2,000 feet.

a16_1003514.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1003514.text: Okay.

a16_1003514.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1003514.text: 1,800 feet now [550 metres].

a16_1003514.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1003514.text: Old Antares.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. Now, you are moving north definitely.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay, I'm getting you centered back up in the COAS. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young
a16_1005539.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: He's got to put that 05 back in to get - to get his orbit back up.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay, do I still have a closure rate?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Say again?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Do I still have a closure rate?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: That's affirmative; 2 feet a second.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay. Looks like the old EMS is just sort of sitting here looking at itself.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. You do have a line-of-sight rate to north.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay, I'm going to go ahead and use the EMS - I mean the COAS on the sync because that's working out pretty good in here. Seems to be a more sensitive indicator of out of plane.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, you've got 4 milliradians to the north. You're at 1,500 feet [450 metres] now. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay, well. Just barely drifting in my COAS. It's pretty good here. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; well, now, you have... [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Can you see me at all?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Yes, sir, in Earthshine I can see the whole LM now.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1005539.text: I'm afraid we're going to run out of Earthshine here before we get it completed. How's the closure rate now?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, fine.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Still 2 feet a second, Ken. We're about 1,400 feet [430 metres] now.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Man, that Moon in Earthshine is really something.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; And I show you with 4 milliradians to the north, and I see you drifting slowly across the COAS to the north.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Rog. I didn't quite get it stopped. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, you're fixing it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: That looks to me like that's fixed.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: [Garble.] You still show some residuals?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, you're still 3 milliradians to the north.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: Orion, this is Houston. We're showing about ten minutes to LOS, and I have some words for you on our general plan, when it's convenient.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Go ahead.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. [Pause.] Fair enough.

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: And, Casper; this is Houston.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Go right ahead.

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: Roger. We want you to verify that you're in Auto Dump on the water. That's Pressure Relief in the number 2 position. That's vertical. And if you have an opportunity to get away from the controls there, we'd like you to manually dump the water to ten percent on the back side. That should require about 17 minutes. Over.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay. I am in Auto Dump and I'll have to wait until we get in daylight to go down there, I think.

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: Okay, we copy.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: I show about full, but I guess it isn't. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. The line-of-sight rate is starting to - Have to thrust down a little - I mean, up a little. [Pause.] That fixed it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay. [Pause.] How's my closure rate?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Two feet a second. You have it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: You're at a thousand feet [300 metres] now, approaching [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: How's the out of plane?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: It's starting to go to the south of here. Don't worry about it right now.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: You got it, Ken. When you get in - when you get in...

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: Orion, this is Houston. We'd like you to configure for RCS Bravo only. Over.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Roger. We'll open the Cross Feed and pull Main SOV A.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1005539.text: We're configured.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Why don't you turn out some lights, Charlie? I don't know...

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. How's that?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah. Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Let me turn the numerics down a little bit.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. You're about 990 feet [300 metres] now.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: All righty. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: What a time to be closing, pitch black dark.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: 970 [295 metres]. [Pause.] You've got the line-of-sight rate. [Long pause.] Okay; can you see me with the spotlight yet?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: No, that's what I was looking to see, because we're going to lose Earthshine here in just a minute. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. You've got to thrust down just a hair. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You get that thrusting down a hair?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I'm not sure if that was the same [garble] you're talking about. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Does that fix it?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: No.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: It's really strange, it was sitting here in the COAS here, right in the middle. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: You thrust a hair down and a hair to the north.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: You're upside down compared to me, and when you say down you mean you're going - you're going down on me - is that correct?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: I'm doing it from the needles. If you don't ro - if you haven't rolled from the last way you were doing it, we were doing it okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah. That's right, Ken. We're going down with you. We'd have to thrust up, according to the needle.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; it's 820 feet [250 metres] now.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay. [Long pause.] It still doesn't seem like it does much. [Pause.] Okay; I show a line of-sight rate that's essentially killed.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: That's about right.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah. They're about killed for this close in. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: He looks bigger than 800 feet [240 metres].

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Sure does. At night, all cats are black.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble] one of those cycle slips of that radar.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: What's your VHF reading, Ken?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: [Garble] One-four.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Yes, sir.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; we're 750 feet [230 metres] here.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: How much?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay, I can see your image is about 2 degrees, now. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: 16, this is Houston. We're showing about two minutes to LOS, and if you'll give us a range and range rate, and, Ken, perhaps you could repeat it for us.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; 710 feet [215 metres], closing at 2 feet a second, rates essentially nulled.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Did you copy that, Houston? The range is 710 feet, 2 feet per second, rates nulled. [Long pause.] Houston, did you copy Casper?

a16_1005539.speaker: Irwin
a16_1005539.text: Roger; we copied down here. Thank you.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. I can see the whites of your eyes. I can see you every time your light flashes. And every time my light flashes, it flashes off your probe.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Uh huh. Let me turn my spotlight now. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: You ought to have me now. Does it do you any good?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I can tell I got you, but it's a poor competitor for Earthshine. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, we ain't got any Earthshine, old buddy.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Beg your pardon.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I say, we're gonna lose Earthshine here in a minute.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Roger. It will all of a sudden look very nice. [Long pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: You can rendezvous under these conditions very nicely, the problem being that you've got to keep referring to the reticle to get some kind of range, I because there's just no - you still don't have enough good depth perception to tell where you are. [Pause.]

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Right. You're gonna be docking with - you're just slowly drifting to the north. You got the vertical line-of-sight rate killed.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1005539.text: Okay, in order to have good comm, [pause] man, you just disappeared - got the spotlight on. [Pause.] I tell you, the spotlight isn't nearly as good as Earthshine. I'm really surprised.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1005539.text: This is Apollo Control. We have had Loss Of Signal with both vehicles as they pass behind the Moon during the end of revolution number 14. At the start of Revolution 15, the crew of Apollo 16, still at this time station-keeping in the two vehicles, will be given a Go/No-Go decision for powered descent and landing during Rev 16 which will be some 4 hours from now. If the decision is Go, and all of the maneuver timelines will have to be read up to the crew during the front-side pass of revolution number 15. If the decision is [for] no landing, then the crew would proceed to rendezvous, dock, and

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You got the tracking light on?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I tell you, the spotlight isn't nearly as good as earthshine. I'm really surprised.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: We got a tracking light on, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I know. I'm - I'm using that [garble] turned it over.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You're closing at - at 500 [150 metres] - at 2 feet [0.6 metres] a second, 520 feet [160 metres].

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Spotlight is probably good for 300 feet [90 metres] on in, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That sounds like a good number. I can tell that you're out there. I can [garble] three hours [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; you're at 510 feet [155 metres], 2 feet a second.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. I'm really amazed how when you get range [garble] all the way in there. I'm at point - Well, I'm down to 0.09 now.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oscillating between 1 and 0.09.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. Verb 40 should be - You're at 480 feet [145 metres] now, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: All right, sir.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You're going to station-keep, right?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I thought I'd come in to where I can guarantee a good spotlight.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
