a16_1005539.text: Then you can - I'd like to get a little closer before you power down the radar.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Hello. Maybe this is where we ought to stop to keep from burning it out. What do you think?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, I don't know. If - if you want to get closer right now, I don't care. I think that - I would like for you to be in good station-keep position and be sure what you're doing, and then we'll just go on around. Okay? Kind of dark out there.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: We can still see your probe.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I hope that's still there. We've got enough problems without that. Actually, the RCS [garble] doesn't look as bad as I thought it would.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You better [garble] again.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Say again?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble] again.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. You're at 370 feet, 360 - 370 feet [110 metres] at - still at 2.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay [garble]. It'll be daylight by the time we get there, won't it?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Probably. Have you got me good enough to where I can shut off the radar?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yes, sir.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Thank you.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: What me to - want to slow it down?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah. Okay; you're - we still showed you with 2 feet a second. You still got it, man.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: We see you getting a hair bigger.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; I pulled off one foot.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; you can pull the breakers.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: If I knew where they were, there'd be no need to sweat it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Want me to turn those lights on?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I thought I'd leave the tracking light on. Ken, do you need the tracking light?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, you can turn it off and let's see.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: It's off.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Nope, don't need it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble]

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Boy, that landing site and that North and South Ray are really something, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That sure is. I got a good look at them a couple of times.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: It looks just like the LMA.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Sure looks different than it did yesterday.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Guess we better [garble] track [garble]. On the ground [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Boy howdy. That [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble]. Yeah.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Phew! There's no cooling on this thing at all.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Sure looks like a jack-o'-lantern.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oh, me! Give me some water, Charlie. I'm really about to erp.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, just a minute.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, you're in Suit Disconnect. That's why.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Huh?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You're in Suit Disconnect.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oh, no kidding?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: What a [garble]. Okay, you can shut that water off.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, you're holding like a rock out there, Ken. Not using any thrusters, are you?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Beg your pardon?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Huh?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand you.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Not using any thrusters, are you?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I think so. Bound to be some for attitude control.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oh.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: What are you looking at, Charlie?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: The RCS.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: How you like the propellant position?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I just [garble] How about turning your [garble]?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble] over here [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, [garble] little gadget [garble] I think [garble] 101:22:36.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I think you got [garble] pretty bad.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Is that what [garble]?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: [Garble] cut in here [garble]. Seems like it [garble] on the gimbal? [Garble]?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Boy, Ken. You got me there.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Did you understand?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I don't have any idea.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: It's off. How do you read?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear. I got a - a squeal with you. But I got you good and - good and clear.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, how do you read now?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You still got a real bad squeal.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, over.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken, we have Voice/Ranging back on. How do you read?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, it's a little scratchy, but clear.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Charlie, we must not be doing anything right.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, how do you read?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. How do you read VHF B?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, Ken. How do you read?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear. How me?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, if you read, I'm transmitting -

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; are you getting - getting me now?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: How do you read, Ken?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear. How me?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; you're still a little garbled but okay. What are you transmitting?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I'm transmitting on B and receiving on A.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. Why don't we try - I think it's our B Receiver. Why don't you try B Duplex? Transmit B - correction, transmit A and receive B.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well - Okay, just a second. Let's go to something simplex. That worked real nice.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay, B Simplex.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. B Simplex.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: How you read B Simplex?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear. How me?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Still the same. You sound - you're a little garbled is all, but you're okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; you sound good.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. I think it's our B Receiver.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, why don't we use A Simplex then?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Tag back here in 30 seconds.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Say again?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: A Simplex is no good. Tag back B Simplex in 30 seconds.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: VHF A, Ken?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Loud and clear.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That's the best one. It - it's our B Receiver is a little scratchy.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, this in plane may be mighty bad if the Sun comes up and hits you in the eyes. I don't know which way you're pointed.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I don't either.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Find out right quick.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah. Well, if it is [garble] field of view.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I'm pointing...

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: It ought to - I think you're the one that's going to be looking into the Sun, because we're in - in an inertial attitude and I was looking at the Sun at sunset. I think the Sun's going to rise over my back.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That'll be fine. I don't care.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I'm glad to hear that because there's really not much that I can do about it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I knew that there wasn't. You know, if we do PDI from now, it will be a miracle.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I'm afraid you're right. And here comes the Sun. Man, are you bright.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, Ken, at least our urine dump works.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: (Laughter) Well, I guess [garble] you have to have something to do. Have to get down and get that water in a few minutes. I thought about that on the last pass, and I thought I had - had more than enough time to get it squared away.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, we don't see you venting anything.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I'm not. Had a problem [garble]. Afraid I'm gonna - gonna pop that relief valve if they don't [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; well, are you - No. Hey, Ken, if you - you're in great shape. Why don't you go get it, and we'll - watch it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Let's wait until we get - get daylight on the whole spacecraft.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oh, we ain't got day - I got daylight on you.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: We'll do it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Bring that out of there! I can see why that's propulsive.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; I'm back at the capsule to visual.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okeydokey.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Man, we must be over the Sea of Rain.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, you ought to see that dust squirt out of there.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I can see it going past you.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I got a good picture of that.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That's good. Somebody will get something out of all this.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Looks like you're translating your spacecraft.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I've picked up quite a drift here.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard?)
a16_1005539.text: Man, that's a long wench coming over the cold north [garble].

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You guys have another dump going?

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: No. This thing just catches this in a can down there, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oh. There was still something. Maybe it's just - my stuff was bouncing off of you.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Hey, there's an icicle hanging off that dump.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That right?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Is you about to go ahead and terminate?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: I beg your pardon?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: (Vox) popped your dump valve, there.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Did you say something about terminating?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: (Vox)nate your dump?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: If you want me to. Like I'm down to 50 percent.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: It's ice, I guess.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That little door down there that's open, is that the solar door?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, the solar door should be down off my left foot. Yeah, underneath the terminal lines of the urine dump - the water dump, rather. Can you see it from there?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Sure can.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1005539.text: How about that.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: If you'd like to yaw around and get the Sun out of your eyes - you can do that.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: We're in great shape. It's not in our eyes, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Oh, okay.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Ken, your SIM bay is all retracted.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; how about taking a look at that mass spec. You - you know where that one is. That's the one in the - all the way in the aft shell, and it's the one towards the plus-Y axis.

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Cover's silver, right?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Beg your pardon? The cover over it is white. The silver cover goes over the gamma ray.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; it's all - everything's in, and all the covers are closed.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay. That's interesting.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Following us?

a16_1005539.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, he's drifting some.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I was trying to see what this dump did. Looks like it started out giving me Delta-V and then it looked like it quit. Or at least it changed. It could be that it - if it's forming icicles out there, that it's deflecting us up.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: That big chicken's been over on this side again, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah. That sure is a fascinating place down there. [Garble] good-size chicken, though.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: You said it was - once you tried it with the - in Accel Command with the 204. Did that have - It said it looked like it was stable but oscillating. What does that mean?

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Well, it meant that it was pointing about plus or minus one degree. But it seemed to be pointing at one degree about the desired axis.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: We got you about ten minutes on the dump, Ken.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Okay; I'm down to 40 percent. I got my timer running here.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: One for you, too. You know every crater - every one over here shows those lineations, like on 15.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah, I was noticing that. Everywhere I looked, I saw that. In the craters, in the highlands, in the - just the whole surface of the Moon is covered that way. I was about to decide it was an optical illusion, but the last time I came across Theophilus down low, it turned out that those lineations follow the depressions that touch the craters that are along the rim. Where - where there was a crater on the rim, you see these - these little lineations curve around it. They take the same pattern, like there is really a whole bunch of - of fractures there.

a16_1005539.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1005539.text: Yeah.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: But you're right. They're everywhere. I haven't seen any place, except there's a couple of places around Descartes that looked to me like they didn't have it.

a16_1005539.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1005539.text: This is Apollo Control; 101 hours, 44 minutes into the mission of Apollo 16. Fourteen minutes before the start of revolution number 14 [means 15] around the Moon. At which time, shortly after the spacecraft, which now should be nose-to-nose station keeping, will come around the east limb of the Moon. They will be given a Go/No-Go decision from the ground on whether or not to make the landing during the succeeding rev - revolution, or lunar orbit number 16. To recap again, the source of the current situation and delaying the landing, [is] the secondary or back up system, which actually acts as

a16_1005539.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1005539.text: All right. Let's see, if we delay - I bet one of the constraints may even be the Sun angle for me. Just trying to think - looking back at - at how much effect that Sun angle had between looking at that landmark last night and looking at it this morning. Last night you couldn't tell North and South Ray. You could tell that the craters were there, but you couldn't see any rays. And this morning, the rays were very obvious.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: I think the constraint to landing is you.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Well, I'm thinking that, if we get a - if we get a workaround, which right now, I'm fresh out of ideas. But they've given me clever ideas before.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Yeah. Let me say I didn't mean that "you" literally.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: I understand. (Laughter) You don't - well, I guess you do feel worse than I do, but not a lot.

a16_1014400.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: It'd be better. You'd get shadows and - and then the shadow of the LM when it comes down, in case this landing radar does its thing again.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: If we do go, it'll probably be - probably just a two-EVA sequence.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Yeah. Yeah, it seems like the only hope is to get back on the time line and pick it up with the nominal numbers.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Yeah, I don't think we can get a - have the consumables to stay for three EVAs.

a16_1014400.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Not after all this, I don't think. Might not even be a one-EVA, or a one-EVA is about all, I guess.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Well, unless - Your battery power may be down? I bet you could get two. Well, there's no sense in speculating. The numbers will come out of the computer. Man, that [garble] of yours sure is looking clean.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Okay; down to eight percent.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Okay; I'm going to go down and shut it off.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Okay.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Okay; it's off, so it ought to tail off pretty quickly. It'll be [garble].

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Okay, we're looking at it now, Ken. It's still spitting out quite a few particles.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Yeah. On this side, it looks to me like the particles have changed nature, though. They look like snowflakes now, when they looked like rain before.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: That's true.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: And they don't have the appearance of having the same velocity, but I'm not sure about that.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: No, they don't have the same velocity. They just sort of sublimating out of there. The other ones were coming out like a rifle shot.

a16_1014400.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: What time do you have AOS on the Flight Plan, Ken?

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Well, the schedule numbers all went out the window.

a16_1014400.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: You got the dooby [garble] abort? Anybody?

a16_1014400.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1014400.text: Do I have any more what?

a16_1014400.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1014400.text: (Vox) body. Our first CSM active rendezvous, too.

a16_1014400.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1014400.text: This is Apollo Control; 101 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Manned Spacecraft Center Director, Dr. Christopher C. Kraft, Jr., just came back into the Control Center after having attended the meeting by management people in one of the back rooms, and the situation is Go for landing. We - To reaffirm we do have a Go for landing in revolution number 16. That decision will be passed up to the crew at Acquisition of Signal some seven minutes from now as they come around the frontside of the Moon. The new maneuver, timewise, will be read up to the crew for circularization by the Command Modul

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Okay, Charlie, we're at 138 now, so at 155 before we pick up AOS and - Well, no, it should be about 145 at this altitude. That's - that's - it looks like we ought to get it pretty soon.

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Looks like all those little particles there, they're coming out and slowing it down. They look like they're just sort of stopping out there.

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: The thing I haven't figured out is that the particles also look like they're coming out slower.

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Every now and then you get a blizzard. It looks just like you're really drowning in [garble].

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Okay; rough calculation says we should pick up AOS about 102:02 [garble].

a16_1015000.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1015000.text: What's your best guess for P21, say, Ken?

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Where we are right now. We're about 125 degrees, probably about 30 miles high.

a16_1015000.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1015000.text: I don't care. Just wondering when we was going to get acquisition.

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: That's about 100 degrees east and gonna be about 25 miles high. I got that out of our spiffy - spiffy little P29. He's doing longitude now. Get that. That wasn't a bad guess. We're now at a 121 and 33 miles high.

a16_1015000.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Ken, the way that figure looks, we're down to one gimbal motor in yaw then, huh?

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Well, that's right unless they can find something.

a16_1015000.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Well, there's not much that they can find on the ground to fix it, though.

a16_1015000.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015000.text: Well, they may find some crude control mode that you could use in here that would make it oscillatory but not unstable. It's the divergence [garble] it's tracking. If it had been just the [garble] we got to go ahead and burn; then we go [garble] the Moon.

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015652.text: I tell you, that thing is really threatening to whip around to[at?] the back end. Think it'd just be [garble] like that.

a16_1015652.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1015652.text: They've got the data from one that you'd let it do that on a little?

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015652.text: Yeah, I showed it to them on two separate occasions on that last pass. Both times, they had high gain all the way. So there should be no question about it.

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015652.text: I just really didn't follow their comment about what they were trying to duplicate conditions on the simulator.

a16_1015652.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1015652.text: Well, they want to make - make it unstable and see if somebody can fly it. Would you believe?

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1015652.text: Hey, Ken. If they let us go, boy, I'll tell you, if you ask me, you ought to just forget about that MEP - EMP thing, and just leave the gimbal motors on those six minutes.

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1015652.text: Well, I really don't really know if that had anything to do with it or not. It - it would seem that, with this being our first gimbal problem and that's the first time we've done that, that would seem like a reasonable thing to suspect. But if that's what they suspect, then - then the next answer is pull the plug.

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1015652.text: First answer's what - second answer's what?

a16_1015652.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1015652.text: This is Apollo Control; 101 hours, 56 minutes Ground Elapsed Time in the mission of Apollo 16. Less than two minutes prior to Acquisition of Signal with Orion and Casper coming around from the rear face of the Moon on the 15th revolution. As the conversation begins with the crew, the word that we're Go for landing will be passed up to the crew. Apparently, during the simulations here and Downey, California, it has been determined that the oscillations in the backup control system which controls the motion of the large engine on the Service Propulsion System, would present no structural hazard

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: Orion, this is Houston.

a16_1015652.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Hello, Houston.

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: Roger. I have some switches and circuit breakers we want you to take care of to try to improve the comm situation. I'll give them to you as soon as you're ready to copy. [Pause.]

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Go ahead.

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: Okay, we want on Panel 12, Track Mode switch, Off; on Panel 16, Primary Transmitter/Receiver Circuit Breaker, Open; S-Band Antenna Heater Circuit Breaker, Open; S-Band Antenna Comm Circuit Breaker, Open; and Primary S-Band Power Amplifier, Open. Then on panel 11, AC Bus S-Band Antenna, Open. Over. [Pause.]

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Okay. Turn off the Track Mode on 12 - Track Mode, Off. Is that right, Jim?

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: That's right, Track Mode switch, Off, on Panel 12. [Pause.]

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Okay, you'll have to find another name for that switch. Oh, okay, we got it.

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: It's been a long day. And did you copy those circuit breakers, Charlie?

a16_1015652.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Yeah, he's got them; we're getting them now.

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Well, I'm all ears, I don't know about Ken.

a16_1015652.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Go to it.

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: Okay, Orion can always tell Casper what his problem is, but it looks like an open circuit in the rate feedback and your servo loop. We've run exhaustive tests down here on the West Coast and East Coast on controllability aspects and structural aspects, and everything looks satisfactory. On Apollo 9, we ran - a similar test was run, as you probably remember. And if such a - such a problem did occur up there, you could expect oscillations, of course, with the gimbal, but you could expect a steady attitude. It would be a limit cycle. So we're convinced down here that we have a satisfactory contro

a16_1015652.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Understand. [Garble.]

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: And I hope Casper copied.

a16_1015652.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1015652.text: Okay, Jim, one thing...

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1015652.text: Okay, Casper copied that. I - I guess I'd like to know, is that thing going to diverge up to a point and then cease to diverge? Does it become neutrally stable at some - some amplitude, Jim? [Pause.]

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: That's affirmative, Ken.

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1015652.text: Okay, that must be some number bigger than the one I looked at, and the other question - only other question I had is, are there any connection between this, in your mind, and the - and the longer duration gimbal On times? [Long pause.]

a16_1015652.speaker: Irwin
a16_1015652.text: Okay, the answer to that, Ken, is negative.

a16_1015652.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1015652.text: Okay, sounds good. Thank you.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Jim, could you go through that switch list one more time - CB list one more time a little bit slower? [Long pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay, Charlie. On that circuit breaker list, on panel 16, it was Primary Transmitter and Receiver, S-Band Antenna Heater, S-Band Antenna Comm, Primary S-Band Power Amp. And then on panel 11, it was just one, AC Bus S-Band Antenna. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Casper, Houston. We're on two loops now.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, Henry. Thank you.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Hey, Ken, I've got a couple other words about that if you'd like to listen.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Okay. We got them all.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay, understand that's complete.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: I surely would, Stu.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Most of the cases where they appeared to be diverging to you and you shut it off the motor, would short, and some of them was just very close to the point at which it became stable. And on some of the - the longer ones, we did see the stability, but those that you called as diverging were short of reaching this stable point, it appears that the controllability is not going to be any problem when - If you would have to burn with this, according to the stroking tests on [Apollo] 9, you'll get a lot of - of oscillations and you'll feel the spacecraft shaking, but the attitude will not be ch

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: That is complete. Roger.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Let me give you some words on the general plan here in this rev. We want to get the PADs up to you, then we'll uplink, and then we want you to do a P52 Option 1. And then you'll pick up in the Timeline Book at circ. [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Roger; copy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: And some more information, if you'd like to copy it; I have sunset at 102:35:50 and perform a 400 plus 3 after the P52. And for the P52 use the same stars as the P52 in the Timeline Book. And, of course, after the uplinks to you - Verb 47. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Rog. We copy all of that. One thing - you want us to do Option 3 before the Option 1?

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Negative; just the Option 1.

a16_1020343.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Okay.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Okay, we're ready to copy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: That sounds like a good plan. Now, I guess if I'd have been a little smarter, we'd have pressed on on schedule.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay. We're standing by for the PADs. [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: No, I don't think so, Ken. They - they appeared to be diverging and it was a - it was a true divergence as far as you could tell. It - it was just, in most cases, just short of becoming stable.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: And...

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Orion, will you turn S-Band Ranging switch Off? [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Ranging is Off.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Let's go Hi Bit Rate. [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, I tell you - you know the difference in this and the simulator, where you can really feel it move, and this old dog was really wagging its tail.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Yes. You know, Jim was talking about the Apollo 9 test, and he said that - that they really - you really feel it in the spacecraft. But this thing is stable. They have - they've really checked that out, and it'll rattle and roll a little bit, if you have to use it, but it's stable.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: You are Hi Bit Rate. Is Casper going to get a little Sep maneuver here?

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Stand by. Okay. Go ahead.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Lima, 104:42:16.64; 111:03:30.00; T2 at PDI plus 24 plus 54; and then T3, Nectar, 106:25:11.81. Over. [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Sounds good. Once again, the ground earns their pay.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, Hank, I guess I'm in need of a general outline of where we intercept the Flight Plan. And it looks like one of the things I'll be needing is a - some kind of a separation burn from Orion again, so that I'm not setting here blasting it into his face. And then I'll need a certain burn PAD. And after that, I'll - I guess we just sort of stumble along and try to pick up some landmark tracking and things like that.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Rog. Say Lima and Mike again.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Lima is 104:42:16.64. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Copy that. Also Mike.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Mike is 111:03:30.00. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Okay...

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: My fuel is kind of low.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Okay, of course, as you know, we're working the Flight Plan now, and Hank's got the - the PADs for you. And I just wanted to make one other comment now. Do you have any other questions - do you have any reservations about this duty, because we sure want to get - get your concurrence? But everything looks like it's - it's go.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Copy. T2 would be PDI plus 24:54. And we have Lima, 104:42:16.64; 111:03:30.00; November, 106:25:17.81. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Roger; on November there, it's - the seconds, 11.81. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Did somebody fly one of these in the CMS?

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Copy, 11.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Well, But...it's been flown on the hardware evaluator.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: And I have the PDI PAD when you're ready.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, I just want to get - if anyone's...

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Go ahead.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Yeah.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: ... run one of these things in the manual MTVC or something like that.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Okay, yeah. They - it's been flown, in all three - three modes, Ken, G&N, SCS Auto and MTVC. It's also been flown on the...

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Roger.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: ...on the hardware evaluator, and - and, of course, we did have the stroking test on Apollo 9, where it was flown in front, and pretty much duplicated this exact problem as far as cycles per second, so forth.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: All right, sir. I'm happy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Roosa
a16_1020343.text: Very good. And Hank's got some good words here for you here.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Okay, Ken. I have your...

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Thank you very much.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: ...Sep PAD for you. You'll use normal sep procedures. In other words, you'll be below the LM, facing it, and back away with your minus-X thrusters. I'll read you your new PAD, if you're ready to copy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, just a second. I got my PAD book handy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Roger. And now I have the No PDI Plus 12. [Pause.] Orion, we've turned the biomed off.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Okay, go ahead. Okay, you got the old biomed off.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay. And here's No PDI Plus 12. 104:30: all zeros; plus 0102.3; plus all zeros; minus 0050.0; 0138.4, plus 0011.4, 0113.9; 0:35; all zeros, 271; 0870.0; plus 0102.6, all zeros; minus 0049.4; 105, 18, all zeros; 107, 05, 45.00. Throttle profile 10 percent for 26 seconds. Full throttle for remainder. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Roger. Noun 33, 102:30, all zip; attitude 000, 357, 000.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, this is sep. That's at 102:30:00; attitude 000, 357, and 000.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Good readback, Ken.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: And this is to be a - a one-foot-per-second radial inward.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: That's affirmative.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Roger; copy. Give me the Noun 42s again. Over.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Roger. Noun 42. 0138.4, plus 0011.4, 0113.9. Over. [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: And I have your Circ PAD for you now, Ken, if you're ready to copy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Roger. Circ, SPS/G&N; 39095; plus 0.49, plus 1.19; 103:21:42.43; Noun 81, plus 0069.1, all zips, minus 0043.5; 000, 139, 358; 0068.0, plus 0053.1; 0081.6, 0:05, 0070.1. The rest is NA. Sirius and Rigel; 131, 071, 014. Two jets; 16 seconds; quads Alfa and Charlie. And in comments: manually roll 90 degrees from PAD attitude for burn, except the final attitude and trim in P40.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Good readback, Charlie. I have AGS abort constants when you're ready.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Stand by. [Pause.] Okay, I'm ready to copy.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Okay, Orion. We're going to hold up. We've got to get some high bit rate. [Pause.] Orion, select Downvoice Backup. [Long pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Houston, how do you read Downvoice Backup? Over. [Pause.]

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Orion, this is Houston. I read you very, very weak. We want you to go to P00 and Data. We're gonna send you some uplinks, And we do not want you to transmit until the uplinks are complete.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay. Let me ask one question before I read it back. I assume that I would be outsmarting myself if I went through the 90-degree roll in the Verb 49 maneuver rather than going to zero roll. I'm looking for ways to kind of be stingy with the RCS.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Understand. We have P00 and Data.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Stand by one.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Let me read you the PAD back now and then ask you the questions, Hank.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Okay.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okays it's circ, SPS/G&N; 39095; plus 0.49, plus 1.19; 103:21:42.43; plus 0069.1, all zips; minus 0043.5, 000, 139, 358; 0068.0, plus 0053.1; 0081.6, 0:05, 0070.1. Sirius and Rigel; 131, 071, 014. Two jets, 16 seconds; quads Alfa and Charlie. Manually roll 90 degrees for burns.

a16_1020343.speaker: Irwin
a16_1020343.text: Orion, we want you to go to Downvoice Backup.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Good readback, Ken.

a16_1020343.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1020343.text: Roger. You have Downvoice Backup.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: And would you like for me to go to A/C Roll for the normal roll coming up to control?

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Ken, there's too much noise. Can you say it again.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Would you like for me to go to A/C Roll for normal roll control also?

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Stand by. That's affirmative, Ken. Go to A/C Roll.

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay.

a16_1020343.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1020343.text: Ken, we're trying to work in a P52 here, and we're checking that attitude, and then we'll give you what we think is best as far as that maneuver. .

a16_1020343.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1020343.text: Okay.

a16_1021716.speaker: Irwin
a16_1021716.text: Orion, this is Houston with the new Sep PAD and Circ PAD whenever you're ready.

a16_1021716.speaker: MCC
a16_1021716.text: Hey, tell him not to talk now, because they're hitting the data then every time now in Downvoice Backup.

a16_1021716.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1021716.text: Okay, Jim. We're still getting the uplink.

a16_1021716.speaker: Irwin
a16_1021716.text: Okay, no transmissions here. [Pause.]

a16_1021716.speaker: Irwin
a16_1021716.text: You guys should maintain radio silence up there.

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: Casper, Houston. Between now and sep we're not going to do anything. In the meantime, FAO is working on a - whether the burn attitude is going to be good for your P52 or not. So just go ahead, get sep out of the way and we'll have some words for you then.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: Okay, looks like I could use a new state vector, too.

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: Roger. They are working on the vectors now.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: Okay, will it do me any good to load - Yeah, I can go ahead and load this thing and let them put in a new vector later. Is that correct?

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: Say again.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: Is it okay to go ahead and load P30 and then out in a new vector afterwards, or is it best to wait until I get the vectors in?

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: Stand by a minute, Ken.

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: Ken, go ahead and sep. We'll up-link after sep.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: Okay, thank you.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: How about if I do this 90 degrees to that attitude to save - save the maneuver. I'll have to go pretty fast to get there.

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: I guess I didn't understand your question, Ken.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: I'm almost 90 degrees to that attitude and I could do it. Instead of pointing and doing it along the X-axis, suppose I come down and do this 90 degrees out and do it with the B/D thruster? Put in that one foot per second?

a16_1021716.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1021716.text: Stand by, Ken.

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: That'd get me a - a pitch attitude of 085 - or 087, excuse me.

a16_1021716.speaker: Roosa
a16_1021716.text: Okay. Now, he loaded - he loaded his P30 and you're looking at...

a16_1021716.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1021716.text: Stu, you were on air to ground. I've loaded P30, and I have flown to 90 degrees from the attitude in order to save that extra high-speed maneuver to get there. And I'm going to burn it along the Z-axis. It'll be towards the Moon, which is our check, and I'll take it from 1 foot per second to 2 foot per second as per the normal procedures, except I'll be using the Z-translation.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Okay, Orion. We have the uplinks in, and I'm ready to give you the AGS abort constants.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, stand by. Go ahead.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Okay, beginning with 224 plus 60529, plus 29402, plus 60406, plus 00572, minus 32664, minus 54401. And we want you to reload 373 with plus 08574. Change 254 to plus 08817. Over. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Okay, Ken. We concur as long as it's 1-foot down radial.

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay, it'll be 1 foot towards the Moon, and we'll still count from 1 to 2 foot per second on the Noun 85.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Roger.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, Jim. We copy starting with 224, 60529, 29402, 60406, 00572, 32664, 54401. Load 373 with plus 08574; 254 plus 08817. Over.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: That's a good readback, and, of course, 662 and 673 are minus.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: That's affirmative.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Okay, and I have the Sep PAD and Circ PAD if you're ready. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Go ahead.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Okay, Sep PAD is at 102.30, all zeros. And on this Circ PAD; ignition 103:21:42.43, Noun 81s; plus 0069.1, plus all zeros, minus 0043.5. Over. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Casper, you a Go for sep.

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay; go for sep. Thank you, sir.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay. Hopefully, that's a Sep PAD. Ken got 103:21:43; plus 0006.9 - correction, plus 0069.1, minus all balls, minus 0043.5. Over.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Roger. That's the - the Circ PAD. The other - the first one was the Sep PAD.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, just the T IG . Okay, we're gonna get to work - start loading these AGS stuff.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Okay, and after you load those AGS abort constants, you'll be clean to pick up on the Timeline Book at the Circ burn.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Okay; whenever you're ready.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Roger. After the P52. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Ask them for a new DAP load or new DAP weight - it doesn't make any difference.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Just to clarify, Ken. You're going to burn the Noun 85 to zero.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Why don't - why don't you do that, John, while I...

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay.

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Negative; the Noun 85 will go to plus 2. It was loaded so that it would point you in the other direction, and by taking it this way, I'll - the dummy load we put in was a - a minus, and we normally burned it to a plus 2. I'm going to burn towards the Moon, which is going to make this come out to be plus 2.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: ...I think we're all right, but I got to load this stuff.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Houston, do we have a new LM DAP weight?

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Stand by.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Or is that worth fooling with?

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: [Garble] when we pitch up like this, I feel like I'm going backwards - in an orb or in an inertial pull. [Long pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Kind of got your [garble].

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: We originally put in a vector. We wanted to burn radially inward, and we put in a vector that was - would cause you to point radially outward on the calculations and then we just burned it to a larger number. So P40 wouldn't - wouldn't cause you to turn around and point 180 from where you were when you undock.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Roger; copy.

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Do you have any reservations?

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Long as you get a foot toward the Moon.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Orion, this is Houston. We'd like you to open AC Bus A Tape Recorder on Panel 11. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay. We can do that.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay. It's coming open.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: And I have a PIPA bias for you...

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, it's open.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: ...when you're ready to copy.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Stand by. [Pause.] Whew. Go ahead.

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay. Inside of 30 seconds.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Okay. Address 1456. Data, 03141. Over. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay. I'll not do - I'll do the gimbal drive check with the secondary in pitch - unless - Are they in the same package? It seems like they're in separate packages. The secondary in yaw is the one I'll bring on after the gimbal drive check.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, 1456. Say again the data.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Rog; 1456 address, 03141.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Good readback.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: We're entering that now. Verb 21 Noun 0 - Noun 01 Enter, 1456 Enter, load 0314 - 03141. [Long pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Good number, I guess, huh? [Pause.] [Garble].

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay; how's that?

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Looks okay, Ken.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Orion, this is Houston. We'd like you to open the Up Data Link circuit breaker on panel 11 and go to Normal voice configuration.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Rog. Data Link. [Long pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, Houston; Orion. How do you read Normal voice? Over.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Very good. Much better, Charlie.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay. Can you say something about our trajectory now? Are we still 17,000 feet [5,000 metres] south and the same as before?

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Stand by, John. We'll have some words for you.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: And I assume you want to use both systems for PDI, both RCSs.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: We're still talking about that down here, John.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Casper, Houston. If you'll give us Accept, we'll up-link.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Orion, this is Houston. At the present time, it looks like you'll be coming in 16,000 feet [4,800 metres] high and about 20,000 feet 6,000 [metres] south,

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: You have it.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Okay, understand. 16,000 high and 20,000 south.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: And, Casper, when you get through with the up-links I we want to go to an attitude of 000, 060, 000 and do a P52.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Roger.

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Jim, John and I are just laughing. We'd like to go back to the sims, please. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Okay, 000, 060, and 000 and a P52, option 3. And I take it that I should enter 509 just before the P52, and leave it in until after the gimbal drive check in P40. The same procedure we had last time. Is that affirmative?

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: So would we. [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Glad you turned the biomed off. [Long pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: That's affirmative.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Houston, okay to do that P52 now? [Pause.]

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: All righty.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Houston, are we clear to do the P52 now?

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Roger; as soon as you're in darkness, John. Well, just an, advisory, it's Option 1.

a16_1022408.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1022408.text: Understand. Option 1 and we're going to gyro torque it.

a16_1022408.speaker: Irwin
a16_1022408.text: Roger.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Casper, the computers are yours.

a16_1022408.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1022408.text: Thank you.

a16_1022408.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1022408.text: Casper, Houston. We're trying to troubleshoot the LM communications problems and it will help if you go to omni Alfa.

a16_1023906.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1023906.text: Jim, we entered the P52. We've got you on the Aft omni now.

a16_1023906.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1023906.text: That new REFSMMAT was pretty close to the old one - just a couple of degrees, right?

a16_1023906.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1023906.text: Man, when those jets turn on, Jim, nobody had ever commented before, but it really horses this old thing around.

a16_1023906.speaker: Irwin
a16_1023906.text: Okay. Orion, this is Houston. We have another procedure we wanted you to try with the comm problem.

a16_1023906.speaker: Irwin
a16_1023906.text: Okay, we want you to open the Secondary Power AMPs circuit breaker on Panel 11. And, of course, you'll lose comm when you open that; and then after one minute, close it, and then we'll re-establish comm. [Pause.]

a16_1023906.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1023906.text: Roger; copy. [Pause.] We'll do that after John finishes marking.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Orion, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Loud and clear.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Oh, you're loud and clear too. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Roger; could you give us the - your Noun 93s? We'd - had lost data at that point.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Yeah, sorry about that, Jim. Here they are: the star angle difference was 4 balls 1, minus 4 balls 1; our torque angles were minus 0.067, plus 0.108, plus 0.050; torqued at 104:42:25.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Roger. Copied down to Noun 93 is minus 0.067 plus, 0.108, plus 0.050. Over.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Hey Houston, I don't know where Ken is at this point when we missed up into our P52. But I trust he's still keeping an eye on us.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Casper, we have a Noun 93.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: I hope so too.

a16_1024347.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Are you, Ken? [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: And, Ken, what we would like for you to do is pick up in the Flight Plan at 97:07, and with the circ preps, and just step on through that, procedure-wise, and be sure you do the Verb 49 after the circ. I have a change in your PAD attitude...

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: You said Verb 29, what first to take?

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger. Right after the circ burn, want to be sure you do the Verb 49. And, to get it into the landmark tracking attitude, we're going to do the high-altitude landmark tracking. And we've got a change to your PAD attitude for your circ. We're going to go ahead and give you an attitude that has the 90 degrees in it, so the Verb 49 will be more efficient. And the new attitude is 090, 139, 358.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: And, Orion; this is Houston. Just a reminder on the 400 plus 3, and a Verb 47.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Roger; we already did that.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Okay; very good. [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay; 090, 139, and 358. I'm on my way now. And I'll get myself into the proper tracking attitude if we don't get all those things worked out.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger. And we want to make sure you don't bypass the final trim in P40, in that attitude.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: That's affirmative. I will take the final trim.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger. And somewhere in here I need to give you the new abort PADs, whenever you can get the chance to copy them.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay. Let me get the maneuvers started, and let me get myself squared away and get the time line in my head and then I'll give you a call.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Charlie, this is Houston. Could you put your mike a little closer? Your volume seems to be a little lower than - than John's. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay; how's that?

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Much better.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay; I had one of them up. Every time I turn my head I get orange juice.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: It's delicious, Jim, but it's better in your mouth than floating around the cockpit.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: I know what you mean. I wish I had some.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: As a matter of fact, I've already had an orange shampoo with the helmet on. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: I guess that's better than no shampoo. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Yeah, I think you're right. [Pause.] Jim, we were really impressed with that landing site from ten miles, anyway, it sure looks exactly like the LMA.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Okay, Charlie. We're kind of curious about the orange juice problem. Did you have a - a bag failure?

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay, Hank; and one question that comes to my mind is, do you want the secondary yaw gimbal brought on the line or not?

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Well, I think it must be the valve. The Command Module water had a lot of air bubbles in it and when I - of course, when I put my suit on, it sort of compressed everything. And every time my mike comes by and grabs the - the valve, it bends it down just slightly, which is - which is enough to cause some to squirt out due to the pressure from the suit. Over.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Stand by, Ken. I'll get you an answer on that one.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: We copy.

a16_1024347.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1024347.text: I had the same problem all the time in one g. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Yeah, at one g though, you bend over and it's on your visor and you can lick it off. [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Okay, Ken, what we'd like for you to do is leave the secondary gimbal motors off until you have finished the gimbal drive check, then bring the secondary gimbal motors on, and do a normal burn. And if you have to, go ahead and down grade, down mode, if you have to to arrest some kind of a bad rate or something.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Casper, Orion transmitting VHF A Simplex. How do you read? [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: That's okay, Ken.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Or would you rather just not exercise it. It's macht's nicht to me.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Charlie, this is Houston. We're kind of concerned about how much...

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: It's your druthers, Ken. If you want to do it that way, that's fine.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Casper, Orion...

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: ...orange juice might have spilled out. We're concerned about the amount that might have got in the suit loop and its effect on the LiOH canister. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay. It'll just verify that I've got everything else hooked up properly. I'd like to keep as close to the normal procedures as I can. Hey, you did copy the P52 things?

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Jim, most of it, for some reason floated up under my helmet - I mean my Snoopy hat, and I'm pretty sticky around the temples and all; and I don't think anything - most of it stuck right into my helmet. And the suit loop flow is not enough to drive it down under - into the suit. And I don't feel like I'm wet at all down in that area. Over.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger. It looked good. And Orion's trying to call you on VHF.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay, I had turned them off while we were doing our chatter. Let me get to them.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Orion, Casper.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Okay; thank you, Charlie. [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Young (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Yeah, I don't - I don't think there is any of it in the suit loop to amount to anything. [Pause.] Looking at Charlie, I can tell where most of it is. [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Orion, did you call Casper?

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Yeah, Ken, I was just seeing how you read. We're all set to go for your Circ. [Pause.] Okay, what kind of Sep maneuver did you do? [Pause.] All right, thank you. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Orion, let's try Biomed, Left. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay, you got John's arrhythmia.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: And, Ken; in addition to the PADs, I also have you LOS and AOS time.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Houston, Orion. I'd like to confirm that in System A we have enough ullage volume to get all the propellants out of the tank. Over.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: That's not correct, Charlie. We'll give you the exact number here shortly.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay, we're still looking at 2,000 - about 2,100 psi [14,500 kPa] on the helium.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Casper, Houston. How do you read?

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Loud and clear.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Okay, we lost you there a minute.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay. Do you want another omni?

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Stand by.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Orion, this - this is Houston. In answer to your question, Charlie, if you were to lose source pressure right now, you could get 35 percent out. [Pause.]

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay; we only have 50 - 50 percent remaining.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: Understand. And that 35 percent is enough to complete the mission.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Casper, Houston. We're about 9 minutes from LOS, and I sure would like to get these PADs up when I ever - you get a chance.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay. If we - Do we have a double failure here on the two regs and that loop?

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: That's affirmative.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay. Can I catch them when we get AOS, Hank? These are all the abort PADs, right.

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: Okay. So what's holding us is that check valve that unseats at 2 - about 225 and reseats at 212?

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Okay. And - but let me give you the LOS and AOS.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay; go ahead.

a16_1024347.speaker: Irwin
a16_1024347.text: That's correct, Charlie. And really you have - should have about 60 percent in that system. Your gauge has an error in it.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger. LOS is 103:04:54; AOS, 103:51:25. Are you interested in sunrise?

a16_1024347.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1024347.text: We cop... Rog; we copy.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: No, sir. That's all right, thank you. Yeah, let me concentrate on making sure that it all goes well in time, Hank. And I'll pick up those abort PADs at AOS.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Omni Delta, 16, or Casper.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: And, Houston; Casper.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Go ahead.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: One thing on the plus side, Hanks, is Charlie took a look at the mass spec and says that it's all inside and buttoned up.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: He said the mass spec is all inside and buttoned up?

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Yes, sir.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Okay. I'll relay that.

a16_1024347.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1024347.text: Okay, and I took the trim maneuver in P40 and I put that bias to Attitude B, 90 degrees roll, 139 pitch, and 1.7 in yaw, and that's about right, considering the roll.

a16_1024347.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1024347.text: Roger.

a16_1030126.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1030126.text: Houston, Orion.

a16_1030126.speaker: Irwin
a16_1030126.text: Go ahead, Orion.

a16_1030126.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1030126.text: Roger, Jim. We watched Ken's waste water dump, and I can see why that thing really gives FIDO fits. It really comes out of there like a water hose.

a16_1030126.speaker: Irwin
a16_1030126.text: Okay; we copy.

a16_1030126.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1030126.text: And we took a picture of it, or two, and I hope they come out and show you that. We had pretty good lighting.

a16_1030126.speaker: Irwin
a16_1030126.text: Good; we hope you have some good pictures of it. And we're showing about two minutes and a half to LOS.

a16_1030126.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1030126.text: Casper, Houston.

a16_1030126.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1030126.text: Go ahead.

a16_1030126.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1030126.text: Roger. You have a Go for circ, and when you come up on - at AOS next time we'd like you to come up in the landmark tracking attitude that is giving us 98.22. That's a little different from the Verb 49 maneuver that's called out right after the circ burn. It's different in roll. In fact, you should be in attitude 000, 276, 000. And we want you to do your Verb 49 to that attitude: 000, 276, 000, rather than a roll of 060 as it calls for there right after the circ burn.

a16_1030126.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1030126.text: Rog; AOS time, please.

a16_1030126.speaker: Irwin
a16_1030126.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a16_1030126.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030126.text: What time did they say AOS was, Ken?

a16_1030126.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030126.text: Well, the reason I ask, Ken, is, for this P52, I need to be close to the right attitude to pick up your story.

a16_1030126.speaker: Irwin
a16_1030126.text: AOS for Rev 16 is 103:51:25.

a16_1030126.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16_1030126.text: Roger.

a16_1030126.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030126.text: My eight-ball in normal.

a16_1030126.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1030126.text: Okay. I'll pick you up on the best antenna.

a16_1030126.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030126.text: Oh, let's try it and see what happens.

a16_1030126.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1030126.text: Roger. Omni D, Omni Delta.

a16_1030126.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1030126.text: Okay, thank you, Hank.

a16_1030126.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1030126.text: Ken, we'd like to know if you did a purge when you did the waste water dump.

a16_1030126.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1030126.text: A purge? A fuel cell purge? No, sir.

a16_1030126.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1030126.text: Okay, copy. You didn't purge fuel cells.

a16_1030126.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1030126.text: No, that's correct.

a16_1030126.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_1030126.text: Ken, if you can work it in, don't jeopardize the burn. Maybe after the burn you can get a urine dump and purge on all those things so we can get the SIM bay going later. That's okay, but if you can't work it in, don't - don't jeopardize anything

a16_1030126.speaker: Mattingly
a16_1030126.text: Okay, I'll get you a purge in there, anyhow.

a16_1030126.speaker: Mission Control
a16_1030126.text: And we've had Loss of Signal as Apollo 16 spacecraft, Orion and Casper, have passed behind the Moon. They're nearing the end of lunar orbit number 15, some 47 minutes before spacecraft come around for the 16th revolution and subsequent landing which is now scheduled for a Ground Elapsed Time of - actually the ignition for PDI, Powered Descent Initiation, will be at 104:17:23 with the landing some 12 minutes later. The powered descent will have a total velocity change of 6,703 feet [2,043 metres] per second. The crew has been advised - that is the crew of Orion - that they are - will be about 1

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay. Caution/Warning's back to Normal. TVC Servo Power Number 1 and Number 2 are on. RHC is to AC. Direct is Off. The BMAGs are uncaged. I'm in SCS.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Mark it. Seven minutes, the gimbals are coming on. One, Pitch; one, Yaw. Pitch looks good, trimmed at 1.5. Yaw looks good, trimmed at 1.2. MTVC; good in pitch; it's good in yaw. Turn the THC control. Goes back to zero. No MTVC. Going clockwise. No MTVC. Secondary Gimbal; Pitch 1. MTVC is good. Thumbwheels are good. Back to neutral. AC/DC; Main A, Main B. BMAGs are caged.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Gimbal drive check; minus 2 in pitch, plus 2, minus 2 in yaw, zero. And they're trimmed. Trims are good. And P509 is coming out.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Hey, how about going Vox, Ken.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: I am in Vox.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Are you reading me in Vox, Charlie?

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Yeah, your Vox circuit was like a key, but it's fine.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard?)
a16_1030500.text: Okay; 509 is out.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay. I'm strapped in. I'll turn the Vox up [garble] a little if that'll help.

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: It would sure be good.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay. And I'll try to talk to you as loud as I can and good. Burn time is 5 seconds. Two jets for 16 seconds, the ullage. Coming up on three minutes to burn. EMS is in Delta-V; the Delta-V C is set.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: And I'm bringing on the Yaw Gimbal Number 2...

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Mark. And [garble] that's a good sign.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Coming up on one minute. Stand by.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: One minute. EMS is Normal. Translation Power is On. The Delta-V Thrust switch A is coming On -

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Mark.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: DSKY is blank. Average g is on.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Ullage; ullage is good.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Pro.,

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Shutdown. Looks like a good one.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Gonna have to do some trims.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Okay; I'm gonna have to roll to get the - to trim out.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Might know this little guy would be the one that takes the Z-axis trim that you have to roll for.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Why do you got to roll, Ken? Because of jets?

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Yeah.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: The Gimbal Motors are Off.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: You got about a 20-hour charge on those batteries, I bet you.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Yeah. Okay, let me cut this Beta. I have a residual of plus 0.2, plus 0.2, zip. Attitude - 61-

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay, I'm going off Vox. Have a good trip.

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: (Vox) one, Ken.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay, Orion, you don't need any further data for the P56, do you?

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: No, we got it all, Ken. Thank you.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: All right. Sorry we held you up so long.

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: No problem.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: We're just happy to be on our way, babe. That was great. Hang in there.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: I'm gonna have to buy some of those cats a couple of cases of beer when we get home.

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: You can bet.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Like a light to the blind.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay, Ken, I think we ought to go back to the Voice Ranging on the VHF. Is that what your PDI switch list called for?

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay.

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Ken, do you read? Over.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: Loud and clear. How me?

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Ken, do you read? Over.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Loud and clear. Did you copy him on Voice Ranging?

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Houston - Ken. Over.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Yeah, I copy you now.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: I went to Voice Ranging and Duplex Bravo, and I could hear you, but I couldn't receive [means transmit?].

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: (Vox) read now?

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: How about now; do you hear me? Okay, I'm talking to you on the A Simplex but I'm not getting through to you on the B Duplex.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay. You weren't getting through on B Duplex, because I was - I was - had B Receiver Off.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: That'll do it.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay, I'm gonna go Voice Ranging and B Receiver, okay?

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: You can put B to Receive over there, John?

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: [Garble], sir.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay, you're a little scratchy, but okay.

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM comm)
a16_1030500.text: All righty.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: My helmet looks like my training helmet now.

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Yeah.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: What time do you have, John?

a16_1030500.speaker: Young (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: I've got - Well, my clock is wrong.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Ken, what time do you have, Houston time?

a16_1030500.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16_1030500.text: I got - 22 minutes of 8.

a16_1030500.speaker: Duke (LM comm)
a16_1030500.text: Okay, thank you.
