a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Any differences in the terraces?

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: No, Tony, not that I can tell from here. Those terraces could be rays (of ejecta) out of Stubby or something like that.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay. You mentioned two different rock types.

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: I can see (that) Stubby has...Right at the edge of Stone, Stubby has got much steeper walls going off of Stone Mountain than I originally imagined it. It's...(Pause) I don't think Stone Mountain came up to Stubby and stops.

a16a1065806.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1065806.text: Good readback, Ken.

a16a1065806.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1065806.text: Okay. Outstanding.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay. (Helping John verbalize the thought) You think Stubby is punched into the edge (of Stone Mountain)...

a16a1065806.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1065806.text: Okay, we got less than a minute to go. Stu will see you on the other side.

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: (Garbled under Tony) Do y'all have a next...(Listens) [If Stone Mountain is older than Stubby, then the wall of the crater at the bottom of the mountain might be relatively steep, softened only to the extent that material slid into it off the mountain. If the mountain were a volcanic construct younger than Stubby, the crater wall might be relatively worn all around.]

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: Well, that's my guess from here but there again, the thing is so steep that the whole side of Stone Mountain, right now, from...A good half of it is in shadow.

a16a1065806.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1065806.text: All right, Hank. Thank you very much. You've done a good day's work. See you tomorrow evening.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay. (Pause) Go ahead, Charlie. One thing; you mentioned two rock types: the black and white ones and then the all white ones. Do you see anything else?

a16a1065806.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1065806.text: Roger.

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: Yeah, there was one right out in front of the LM here, just to the right of the footpad that looks like a breccia to me, Tony. Either that or an indurated regolith (which is soil compacted in an impact). We'll tell you when we get out.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: Tony, we'll give you an analogy of what that black and white rock looks like. It's really a gray and white and looks like a granitic rock with very large crystals to it, though I kind of doubt that (it is granitic).

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Outstanding! You're really whetting our appetites. (Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: There are really some interesting rocks out here. I see some that are pure snow white. And we've got the whole run of them. It's hard to tell at this sunlight, which is so bright on the surface, just exactly what color these things are, even with the naked eye. You know, it's very deceptive. I swear I see one out there with some pink in it, (chuckles) but we'd better wait until we get out. We'll pick it up and make sure.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Roger. I understand. (Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: What do you call tomato soup made with cold water, Tony?

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Awful. (Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: John says 'cold tomato soup'. (Long Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Hey, Charlie. When you get a chance, could you take a look at that ridge at 12 o'clock, which you described as 50 to 100 meters out, and see if that continues on around to 10 and 9?

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: Yes, it does.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay, could you...

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: It continues on around to my side.

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: John's original observation was that it looked like we're in a big old subdued crater, and that's really what it looks like, Tony.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: Man, those black and white rocks really look interesting, Tony. I just can't wait to grab one of those.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: I tell you, Charlie, we feel the same way. 107:05:28 Duke: In fact, the impression you get is that it almost looks like the color of labradorite.

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: Oh, Charlie! (Long Pause) [Jones - (Chuckling) "Do you have any comment about this little exchange?"] [Duke - "I think John was thinking we were getting too technical."] [Muehlberger, from a 1996 letter - "What caught my eye (while reading a draft of the Apollo 16 Journal), was the early observations (here and at 106:19:07 ) - both from the LM window - that were describing rock types that were alien to the pre-mission photo-geologic interpretation of highlands volcanic rocks. The geological field trips that we took the crew on - primarily into andesite volcanos along Lake Mead a few miles east

a16a1065806.speaker: Duke
a16a1065806.text: Tony, I guess it's really a bluish cast instead of real black to me. But in this Sun it looks bluish.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Right, we understand. (Pause)

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Okay. And if you can pull yourselves away from the window there, we'd like you to hold to the schedule of starting pre-sleep in about 20 minutes.

a16a1065806.speaker: Young
a16a1065806.text: Well, we'll bring you a small one of each. I'll tell you one thing, I'm glad we brought the rake, because we really can do it.

a16a1065806.speaker: England
a16a1065806.text: Very good. [Like the other J-mission crews, John and Charlie will use a geology tool that is rather like a clam rake with tines that are one centimeter apart. We weren't so sure that the regolith would have the rock sizes to be captured by the rake. You know, you could pull it through (the soil) and come up with nothing. And this is true all over the north - excuse me, the northeast and also the southwest sid

a16a1073139.speaker: Duke
a16a1073139.text: Well, that's all you're going to hear from me. Good night.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Okay. I'll get to that in just a minute. I'm flapping right now with some - trying to make up the things we missed here. And I just finished putting most of Sharonov and Mendeleev on magazine November November. And I'll try to pick up the one that [garble] if you'll tell me I can do it on November November.

a16a1073139.speaker: England
a16a1073139.text: (Laughing) Okay, good night. [Long Comm Break]

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Okay, stand by.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: And, Casper. Could you give us a frame number on November November.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Okay. How about - ah - 145?

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Okay, 145. I believe that.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: And, don't let me forget things like this pan camera thing coming up, because I am sitting here getting camera set up. I am going to try to get the earthshine sequence in this trip, too.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Okay. Roger. We'll give you a call.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: And, Ken, it's about time now. Within the next 15 seconds or so, if you want to get the Pan Camera, Standby Stereo on Power.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Okay, thank you, sir. Standby, Stereo, Power. You've got it.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Roger.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Well, I'll tell you. Just a little reminder like that can go a long ways toward getting something done in here.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Jolly good. We'll try to please.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1073139.text: This is Apollo Control at 107 hours and 59 minutes, and at this point, we have caught up with all of the back-log of tapes that was accumulated during the change-of-shift press briefing and which continued to pile up on us as we were replaying the tapes that we had already accumulated. We are up to date now and standing by live, and we believe that third good night, or at least hope that third good night, was the final one. We don't expect to hear from the crew now for about eight hours aboard Orion. We are in contact with Ken Mattingly aboard the orbiting Command Module - Command Service Modu

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Okay, Ken, you're 30 seconds from the T-start time on the pan camera.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Okay.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Ten seconds, Ken.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: And, you've got it.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Okay. Roger...

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Barber pole in gray and away she goes.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Very good and Ion Source, On.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Ion Source, On.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Mark.

a16a1073139.speaker: Roosa
a16a1073139.text: Okay. And, Ken, on those last November November, we'll give you 30 frames on that one.

a16a1073139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1073139.text: Okay. I guess it was scheduled for another magazine, but I just don't have time to change it.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: No Sweat. You got 30.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay. That should be plenty. And, I got the magazine XX loaded in the Hycon, and I am ready to go to work on that as soon as we get in the darkness. Well, maybe that won't work, because I guess you got a P52 and things coming for me.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Stand by on that, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Ken, what we'd like for you to do after this Sunside pass, after you finish up here, is to get a good night's sleep. We're not showing you anything scheduled after that.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I thought there was a P52 or something I was supposed to get as soon as it got dark. I'll - I can sneak that in there, too. I hate to see us miss very much of the things that we almost did.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: No, Ken. This - It's not scheduled. The last thing you need to...

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Well [garble].

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: ... do is 108 plus 50, where you go in to do the activities there in the flight plan; you go right into the pre-sleep checklist and we'll see you in the morning.

a16a1075900.speaker: Young
a16a1075900.text: Tony, you guys missed it by about 10 minutes. The RCS Reg A light just came on. [Readers should note that, unlike the EVA CapComs on the other missions, Tony has chosen to be on duty whenever the crew is on the surface and awake. Like everyone else, he has already had a long day because of the six-hour landing delay. Having signed off for the night, he has gone home to get some sleep but will be back before Charlie calls Houston at 115:49:37 . The overnight CapCom is astronaut Don Peterson.] [The following audio clips are either PAO announcements or cover conversations between Ken Mattingly an

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Oh, okay. Outstanding. Very good. Thank you.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Casper, if we can have the High Gain to Auto; please, sir.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: You've got it.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Can you look in your plot-board me approximately what my longitude is right now?

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Oh, Ken, it's probably about 70 East, something like that. You're just coming across the western rim of Smythii there.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, good enough.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Yes, here comes our old friend, Langrenus.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Ken, we need barber pole [garble]...

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: I guess you need a little barber pole, don't you? Okay, that should be one plus what we have.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Hey, Stu, if I put 30 frames on this Crozier, I won't get that first strip of Kant - Andel. You think about doing away with the intervalometer and taking the pictures with less overlap and try to squeeze it all onto this one mag?

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, stand by. Let's take a look at that, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I got a couple of minutes before I start.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Oh.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Ken, you can go ahead and disregard the intervalometer and try to get them both on that same mag.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, thank you very much. I'm all set up to come up on Crozier.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Well, it looks like I ran out anyhow. I got 165 and the magazine's empty, and I just finished the strip of Crozier.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I copy that.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: That's on magazine November November.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: And I'll go see if I can get Papa Papa out here real fast.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Papa Papa is out and loaded. I'll try to pick up Descartes to Andel with it.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Stu, there is a definite textural similarity between the material or the bright spot by Descartes Crater and the things around Stone Mountain. However, it is a lighter albedo. It's a shade lighter and the line of demarcation seems to come along the long crater.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay. We got that.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1075900.text: This is Apollo Control at 108 hours, 21 minutes. We have heard no nothing further from the crew aboard the Lunar Module Orion, Charlie Duke and John Young since we last said good night. But we do have about 40 minutes of acquisition time left with the Command Module, Casper, which is presently in an orbit 66.8 nautical miles [124 kilometres] by 53 nautical miles [98 kilometres]. And occasionally we are getting bits and pieces drifting through the communications of what sounds like Marshall music that Ken Mattingly is playing on the onboard tape recorder. And as the level reaches the high enoug

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: And another strange sight over here, I think it's Andel, that's where I'm supposed to be ending the strip. But there's another crater here that looks like it's flooded, except this same flooded material seems to run up on the outside. You can see a definite patch of this stuff that's run down inside an old crater. And that material at least lays on top of it, but it lays on top of things that are outside and higher. It's a very strange operation. I guess we'll have to wait and let someone that knows what they're talking about look at the pictures.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: All righty, Ken. Sounds real interesting.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Man, this is unbelievable. It's really something. Everywhere you turn, there's something new. And let's see if we can get in the old SS on Ptolemaeus here.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Well, I'll tell you what. I'm going to have to skip Ptolemaeus. The terminator is still on the rim.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Just for kicks, though, I'm going to show you one on frame SS that is really fascinating. And I'm just on the eastern rim of Ptolemaeus. I mentioned it last time. I'm going to take a little strip of these.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: And then see if I can get - yeah, that ought to be good enough. Okay, I took - I took it up to 20 frames, and I used about five of these on SS. And what I took it of was - This material that's on the eastern rim of Ptolemaeus has the same textural appearance in the - low that we saw in the Descartes formation, that being the stuff coming from the crater Descartes running north yesterday. An entirely different appearance than the rest of the terrain in the low Sun. I think there may be some interesting comparison there.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Ken. Got that. And you're approaching 30 seconds to - the...

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, going to end up pan camera off here somewhere.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger; on my mark, you'll be 25 seconds.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Mark. And, Ken, just turn the cameras off there. Then, before you continue on with those steps, I want to say something about those procedures on down at the bottom. I'm showing 6 - 7 seconds.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And...

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Mark. I show T-stop. That's the pan camera and mapping camera.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, they are Standby and Off. I'll wait 30 seconds before I take the Image Motion, Off. Hey, thank you, Stu, that was a big help.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger. And - I would - We're going to delete, on those procedures there, the Mapping Camera, Retract; and the Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover, Close - We're going to leave those out all night, and we'll have a - a plan tomorrow on how we're going to handle the mapping camera.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay. You do want the Laser, Off, though. Is that correct?

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: That's affirmative.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, the Laser is Off now. The Mapping Camera going to Standby and the Image Motion is coming Off.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Jolly good.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And, Ken, a couple of other items. We're going to let the Bat A charge all night, so we'll just leave that as is.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay. Those batteries kinda put in a day's work, too, today.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I see that we're going to have AOS on the next pass before we get - before the sleep period starts, so I think I'll wait and give you my film summary at AOS, if that's okay. It'll take me that long to sort it all out, I'm afraid.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: That's okay, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: All I was planning to give you was how much was left in each mag.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Say again, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: All I was planning to give you, Stu was, how much is left in each magazine.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Hey, that's jolly.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And Casper, Houston.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay I got a couple of things.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Go ahead.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Ken, one is we would like to delete that film status report. We would like for you to start your rest period just as soon as you can after LOS and let us pick up any talking about the film or anything like that for tomorrow.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Oh, very well. You is the boss.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And another thing, we're noticing indications here that your screens - on your O 2 return hoses and also the suit circuit return valve. You might take a look at those tonight and see if they need a little cleaning.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I've been cleaning the suit circuit return screen every night and it's been getting pretty dirty, so I'll check it again today and the other hoses, I've got a - since I didn't have a screen for the inlets, I capped the inlets and just used the outlets to keep stuff from - We got so much junk here, I didn't want to get stuff inside the hoses down through the suit fans and to clog up the other filters...

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: ... So I put the interconnects on the inlets and just let the air blow out of the hoses and take it all in through the suit circuit return. That might give you a little higher pressure rise.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, we - we concur with the configuration and but we have noticed the O 2 flow creeping up slowly, indicating that it would probably need a little housecleaning on that screen.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Yes, sir; thank you very much. I'll catch that baby.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: I'll tell you, this is - A man shouldn't get paid for doing this.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Yes, it really sounds great, Ken. I think - I think the difference in the Earth crescent sure must make a difference, the way you're talking of earthshine versus the way I saw it.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Oh, it's fantastic. You can see the whole thing. It's really something. I'm going to try that - that's the reason I wanted to try and get these earthshine pictures in this time before the Earth gets any smaller. Because it really isn't nearly as dramatic tonight as it was last night, and I don 't know whether that 's the altitude or what.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: But if I - let's see, we want to run these booms out and what else? Got to turn the Pan Camera, Off. Okay, if you'll give me a call on those.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger. I'm watching for you on the boom deploy, Ken. You got a little less than 5 minutes.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I'll - You know something else that I'm not real sure about. It sure looks to me as though the earthshine is not as bright on this mare. I guess it's just this mare that's over around Fra Mauro and so forth is just darker, and maybe it's my night adaptation that hasn't taken affect yet, but I got the distinct impression that that band's [?] a lot brighter when you get over to the western limb.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, got that, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: I don't think I understand that.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: I tell you, I thought this was kind of appropriate here. A few minutes ago, I was playing Berlioz' Symphonie Fantastique and looking at this fantastic sight and floating along here, and it's just unbelievable it's so much fun.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Yes, it sure sounds like it; in fact, we were catching a little of your music occasionally there. Didn't sound as good as [laughter] "Riding Old Paint", but I guess it'll do.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Well, I've been listening to "Old Paint" kind of music for three days of PTC. But it was good "Old Paint," I'll have to admit. I enjoyed it.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And, Casper; Houston.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Go ahead.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, would - What we'd like to do now, Ken, is go ahead and put out the booms now and, as soon as you have them out, go ahead and start the - start your P20 running right now. It looks like we might be cramped a little bit to get your uplinks in, so we want to make sure that we get - all of the up-links completed here.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay. In other words, you want me to cancel the earthshine ?

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Yes, that's what we are saying, Ken. We're just afraid we might be cutting it kind of tight on the up-link.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: All right, that's in work.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, Ken, and we can take the Pan Camera Power to Off. The lens is stowed.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay. Pan Camera Power is Off.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, and I guess I might as well go ahead and put the booms out, hadn't I?

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger. We'd - we'd like to have those out and, as soon as you complete that, let's go ahead and do the - go into the P20 that we're showing at 108 plus 50. Let's don't wait for that.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I'm already going there.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Oh, okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: I'm doing a manual roll to get over there and spin it around.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, very good.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: And I guess I'd like to have a SIM bay configuration - what - what you think I should have at the end of - while I get ready to go to bed, what mechanical and electrical status, and let me crosscheck it to make sure I haven't forgotten something.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay. We'll get that for you.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Holy smokes.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And Casper, Houston. We've got that SIM bay configuration when you're ready.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, it is your normal sleep configuration, with a change in the first digit of the top line. We're going to change that 0 to a 1. You will now have a configuration, minus 11111; second line is normal, 01222.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, minus all ones; 01222. Thank you, sir.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Roger. And we'd like...

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: And just looked at the inlet screens and you're right, they're - Go ahead.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I copied your - your bit on the screens and we'd like B/D Roll for sleep tonight.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, you'd like to do a B/D Roll. Okay. How does the general RCS picture look?

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: We're in - we're in good shape, Ken. We're down a little on the Flight Plan, but we're riding 168 above the above the red line. We're - On the Flight Plan, we're down a minus 133.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And...

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Eventful afternoon.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: It'll all get done. You're doing a great job, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Well, I'm just real sorry about that delay this afternoon. I wish I had known more about it. I'd already decided that if it was - if it was just oscillatory and stable, I was going to take it.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Yes; well, I tell you, the - the traces on those up to the time that you turned off the gimbal motors were just a classic divergent curve, right out of the textbook.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Yes. Yes, I couldn't believe it when I saw that thing. Thought I was back in Floody's simulator.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Yes, I think there has been a lot of people talking about SimSup today. Wish we could just forget this one.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: But, hey, I got a couple other reminders here while we're chatting. I'd like to remind you on your pre-sleep checklist that we'll not bump up the cabin tonight.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, thank you.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: And, Ken, a couple other - or one other item here, you might get a leg up on your pre-sleep checklist and check the Optics Power, Off, at your convenience.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I'll get that stuff in just a minute.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: Okay, I wasn't trying to hurry you, I just wanted to toss in a little reminder there.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: Yes, thank you. I think I left it on last night.

a16a1075900.speaker: Roosa
a16a1075900.text: That isn't what I was trying to say, Ken.

a16a1075900.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1075900.text: (Laughter) Well, you know what was going on last night and this morning. Everything you said was true. I got a garbage can in here that's bigger than me.

a16a1090200.speaker: Peterson
a16a1090200.text: Go ahead, Casper. This is Houston.

a16a1090200.speaker: Peterson
a16a1090200.text: Casper, Houston. How do you read now?

a16a1090200.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1090200.text: Okay, I'm ready to give you Accept.

a16a1090200.speaker: Peterson
a16a1090200.text: Okay. Go Accept. We're ready to up-link.

a16a1090200.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1090200.text: Okay, standing by. And I'd like to verify the cryo configuration with you and make sure that - I'll leave a Battery A on charge overnight. There's no lithium canister change tonight and it looks like when you get the up-link in and I give you a Verb 74, we'll be through.

a16a1090200.speaker: Peterson
a16a1090200.text: I believe that's right. Stand by one.

a16a1090200.speaker: Peterson
a16a1090200.text: Casper, Houston. We - we concur with Battery A, will stay on charge all night. There's no LiOH change. And on the cryo configuration, the O 2 and H 2 Tanks 1 and 2, Auto; Tank 3, Off.

a16a1123245.speaker: Duke
a16a1123245.text: Hey, you know, a bit ago we had a little MA-RCS problem .... The system A ... now shows a 10 to 15 percent quantity. Is that what you guys were expecting? Over.

a16a1123245.speaker: Duke
a16a1123245.text: Okay. If y'all are happy, we'll see you in a couple of hours and go back to sleep. Over.

a16a1123245.speaker: Peterson
a16a1123245.text: Say again, Charlie. You're very garbled.

a16a1123245.speaker: Duke
a16a1123245.text: Okay. If you guys are happy, we'll go back to sleep.

a16a1123245.speaker: Peterson
a16a1123245.text: All right, Charlie. We've got one circuit breaker we want you to open. Stand by a minute. [Pause] Rendezvous Radar, Operate, panel 11, row 3, under Heaters.

a16a1123245.speaker: Duke
a16a1123245.text: Okay, we got it. Good night.

a16a1123245.speaker: Peterson
a16a1123245.text: Roger. Thank you. [Jones - "If I remember, you talked about this little wake-up in 'Moonwalker'."] [Duke - "If I remember right, it just rattled me right up out of sleep. That Master Alarm goes off in your (Snoopy) helmet, since I was on comm. I've forgot what it sounded like, but 'bong, bong, bong' and, God, it was loud! I went out almost through the top of the...Almost jumped out of my skin!"] [Jones - "But you got it figured out pretty quick."] [Duke - "Well, yeah. Then I saw what the Master Alarm was. 'Cause they said we were going to get it. It was a low quantity light. They told us about

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: There's B.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: We have a tone, a vent flag, and a press flag, and a PLSS O2, greater than 85 (percent).

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. (Garbled) PLSS O2's reading about 98.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Paragraph 6; very faint) And you can't hear Houston. Houston, how do you read the LMP? Over.

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: Ken, in regard to that Davy thing - I was just talking to Spence and he says that the - that was the correct time and that - that - where they call officially the terminator. And the photo setting should have worked. But it sounds like from what you said, it may have been a little too dark.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Say again, Charlie.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Slowly) How do you read? Over.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: We're copying you, but you're weak.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay. We're reading you 5 by. We're pressing on. (Pause) Comm check with the LMP. You do the comm check now.

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: (Laughter) There's nothing but hard shadows down there where Davy is. Maybe - maybe the rim of Ptolemaeus there's - and Alphonsus, and that area is a little higher than we calculated because it wouldn't have to be off by much in order to keep you from - from missing it. I - after we talked about it there - why, looked out the side to the south, and it looked like further south in the mare. The terminator did go out a little further. So, I think we got caught by elevation.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Hello, Houston. How do you read? Over.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Okay, John. You sound good but, again, you're weak also.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay, I'm hollering as loud as I can. And my microphones are right in my mouth.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Right. I can hear it bounce against your tonsils.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: You're loud and clear, Houston.

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: I suspect that's the case, Ken.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. We're going to AR now. How do you read now, Houston?

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Okay, I'll whip into a little P52 here.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Okay, just like before.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Do you read (Houston), Charlie?

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay, Houston. You're coming in beautifully, Tony; 5 by.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Very good. Actually, your comm is better now - for both of you - than it was when it was on the LM (comm).

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay, great. Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (next to last paragraph) Okay, Houston. My O2 quantity is 100 percent.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: So's mine, about 99.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Reading the handwritten change) "Squelch B to full decrease."

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Okay, we copy that.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. "S-Band Mod(ulation) to PM."

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Go. (Pause)

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Not bad. All ready.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay, Houston. You don't...Y'all have telemetry now?

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Hey, Hank.

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Negative; we don't.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Let's get some cooling in here.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay, it says "verify comm and telemetry". There's no way we can do that, is there?

a16a1182843.speaker: England
a16a1182843.text: Okay, no. We don't expect it until you get on the LCRU.

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Well, there's the old Earth, again. And it's getting smaller. I think it's not sanforized.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: (Shouting) Okay, fine. (To Charlie, now at the top of the middle column of Card 1 Side 2 ) Okay, "cold, as required. Circuit breaker (panel) 16: Cabin ECS Repress, closed, verify..."

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: Roger (laughter).

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Go. [John and Charlie have been through these procedures often enough that Charlie is anticipating John's words.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: Ken, in your post-sleep, did you terminate the jet monitor?

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: "...Repress, closed, verify. Suit Fan Delta-P to open."

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Go.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: "Suit Fan Delta-P number 2..."

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Oh, hey - no. Let me write that out on my post-sleep checklist right now. They wrote that in as an extra item yesterday, and I forgot it this morning.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: No, that ain't right. Suit Fan 2?

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: "Suit Fan 2, open."

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay. [They have shut down the fan that moves oxygen through the ECS Suit Circuit and have shut off a differential pressure (Delta-P) sensor that would have warned them that the fan was not running.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: "Suit Fan selector to 2." (Pause) "Verify ECS caution and Water Sep lights come on in about a minute."

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay. [With the fan off, there is no air flow to drive the water separator and, once the centrifuge in the separator spins down, a warning light will come on.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: " Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) , Pull to Egress. Verify."

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Go.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: " Cabin Gas Return (Valve) to Egress. Verify."

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Go.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: " Suit Circuit Relief (Valve) to Auto. Verify."

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: It sure pays to have you guys watching.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Go.

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: Well, I just happened to think of that one, and I got to thinking about your P52, using SCS, and then I wondered about the jet monitor program.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: (Halfway down the middle column on Card 1 Side 2 ) Okay; 102 hours (on 2-9), "OPS connect", LMP first. " Suit Isolation Valves , actuate..." No, we don't have that yet. Want to go to Suit Isol, though. (Garbled) both of them. Okay, let me connect your OPS hose. (Pause)

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: For that one, you get the award for the year. That was smooth.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: It's hot in here.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: There's the Sep light.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. Got a Water Sep light, Houston. [The water separator has spun down.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Garbled) on that.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: "Retrieve purge valve (from purse )."

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: "Verify closed, lock pin in, and in low flow."

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: And, Ken. Whenever you get a chance, Gamma Ray, Shield, On. When you get through with this.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: That's verified. (Garbled) for you, Charlie.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: "Install purge valve in PGA, red on red."

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: "PGA diverter valve to vertical." (Garbled)

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Thank you, Charlie. [As shown in Figure I-23 in the EMU Handbook , the diverter valve is part of the oxygen inflow connector and gives them the option of directing the PLSS oxygen flow entirely into the helmet (the vertical position) or partly into the suit torso (the horizontal position). Generally, the astronauts put the diverter valve to horizontal only when they were in the cabin and were trying to dry the suits out a little. In the hoizontal position, used in the cabin, all the incoming oxygen stream is divided between a duct leading to the helmet vent and a duct leading the vents in the

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Okay, Gamma Ray Shield is coming On -

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Mark it.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: We're in lock.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay. Now we'll repeat it.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. (Pause) [Now they will install John's purge valve.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Hey, why don't you sock us some water. We're still on LM cooling.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Yeah, just a minute. (Pause) [They are probably talking about running water through the LCGs again.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. Hope you're not keying your mike again, Charlie.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: How's that?

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: That's better.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Garbled)

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. (Long Pause) In and locked? (Pause) Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Got it. No? (Garbled). Lock pin isn't in.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: In and locked.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: All righty.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Bottom of the middle column on Card 1 Side 2 ) (Garbled) now let's get a drink and I'll get us some cooling.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. That's pretty smart, Charlie. (Long Pause) Okay. (Long Pause) [John is saying that it was a good idea to run the LCG pump occasionally.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Brace this here for a little bit.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: And he's doing it. (Pause) Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay, I'm turning off the (Descent) water (valve as per the last line in 2-9 prior to "102:06 Helmet/Glove Donning").

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay. (Pause) [In the following transmission, Charlie suggests that they leave the water on for a while.]

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Let's see. We could still do that. Let's do that...Let's keep doing it until we get down here.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (top of right-hand column on Card 1 Side 2 ) Okay, "PLSS fan, on; position mikes". Done.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Fan's on; mike is positioned.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay; Fan is on.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Vent Flag's clear.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Mine isn't yet. (Pause) Mine did. "Don helmet; check drink bag position. Don LEVAs and lower protective visor. Secure tool harness."

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Guess whose helmet's in the very back. (Pause) Nope. (Long Pause) [During this interval, we can hear clacking noises which indicate that one of them, possibly John, is getting his helmet on. I think that John already has his helmet on because the dialog from here to 118:38:55 seems to concern only Charlie's helmet and, after that point, there is no doubt that they both have their helmets on.] [Jones - "Ideally, you each got your own helmet on?"] [Duke - "Uh-huh."]

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: All right. (Pause)

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Want me to get it, Charlie?

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Just the Velcro over here, John.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Yeah. (Pause) Okay, let me try to get it on when...Try to get it on whenever you get it down; I can see it. Oh, man, that's going to get you with the orange juice. (Pause) (Garbled) Give another try. (Pause) 118:37:57 Duke: Nope. Won't do it. (Pause) Make sure the Velcro's down all the way in the back, here.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: That's what it is, right there.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: That's what it feels like; right over there. Same place as yesterday (garbled).

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: Okay, Ken. We got the 93. You are clear...

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Yeah. Yeah. There's another piece (garbled)

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Okay, you folks have the angles.

a16a1182843.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1182843.text: ...to torque.

a16a1182843.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1182843.text: Okay, I'll do it at 10.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: (Garbled) too much. Boy. (Pause) This comm is beautiful, isn't it?

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Yeah. Now try it. Let me put it on for you, so I can see what you...

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay.

a16a1182843.speaker: Young
a16a1182843.text: Just hold your head back. Get it over your head first. Watch out for your mike. There you go. Get that inside.

a16a1182843.speaker: Duke
a16a1182843.text: Okay. (Pause) Felt like you got it, John. 118:38:55 LM Crew: (Helmet lock audible, as usual) Got it. [Although the comm may have been good in the spacecraft, the audio tape in Houston is difficult to understand and I have no doubt that transcription errors remain.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 9 min 38 sec )

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay, now we don the LEVAs .

a16a1183857.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1183857.text: And, Casper; Houston. Got a little update to you there for that dead band test. We'd like to change the 5 degrees to 2½ degrees.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Okay.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay, I'll put yours on first. (Pause)

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Careful we don't drop those gloves.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Yeah, I know it. We'd be in sad shape. [With the suits and PLSS on, it would be all but impossible to get the gloves off the floor.]

a16a1183857.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1183857.text: Okay. Make that 2½.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: I got it. Ah, the old red stripes ! (Long Pause) [John's LEVA has a red strip that runs back from the top-center of the faceplate. The stripe - along with similar red stripes on his arms and legs - make it relatively easy to tell John and Charlie apart in the TV and photographs. Jim Lovell was the first of the Commanders to have red stripes on his suit.]

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: That looks pretty good, John.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Okay. (Pause) 118:39:39 Duke: (To himself) Get it down in back. It is (and it's) Velcroed (in place).

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Okay.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay, the old long arms, here, will get mine out. (Pause) This tool (harness?).

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: All righty. (Pause) Almost got it, Charlie.

a16a1183857.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1183857.text: And, Ken. Since we updated the clock, we need to update the time on the T IG for the TEI-26. The rest of the TEI-26 PAD's good. So, whenever you are ready to copy, I'll read you the new T IG .

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay. Sorry. You're a little top-heavy with this PLSS, aren't you?

a16a1183857.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1183857.text: Okay. Just a second. Let me get my GDC here. This GDC is working a lot better. When we started out, I made a drift check on it, you know - right after insertion, and it was drifting pretty readily. And now, this thing will go for six hours and be off less than ten degrees. I guess it just - maybe once it got warmed up, it just sort of stabilized, and it's really - really doing a good job now.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Not really. I feel a little bit...(Long Pause) There, you got it.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: (Not finished) Hang on. (Pause)

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Okay, can I turn around?

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay. [Evidently, John had turned to face his circuit breaker panel so that Charlie could secure his LEVA in the back.]

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: (Garbled) turned around. (Pause)

a16a1183857.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1183857.text: Hey, that sounds real great.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Oh. Man, is that (LM LCG) water cold! Whoo, whoo!

a16a1183857.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1183857.text: Yeah, it is particularly nice to know (laughter).

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Feels good doesn't it?

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Mm-hmm! Okay, can you get my tool harness straps?

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Yep. (Pause) Okay, there's one.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: (I'll) get the other on.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Got it. 118:41:19 Duke: Okay. Hold on. [Now, Charlie will secure John's tool-harness straps.]

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Got this one. It's Velcroed down. Here's the other one. (Pause) And it's Velcroed down. Okay, "LCG cold" (second paragraph, right-hand column, Card 1 Side 2 ). We got that. And I'm going to open the (LCG) Pump (circuit breaker), and we can disconnect the (LM water) hoses, and then connect up the PLSS (water) hoses.

a16a1183857.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1183857.text: Okay. Why don't you give me a new time for TEI-26?

a16a1183857.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1183857.text: Roger. T ig is 125:26:15.47.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Okay.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay, Pump (breaker) is open.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Okay.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: See if I can get...

a16a1183857.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1183857.text: Okay, that is 25:26:15.47.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Got it.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Got yours, huh?

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: Yep.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Would you throw that back up in there?

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: I'll get it out of the way. [John's LM water hose extends from the ECS behind Charlie over to John's side of the spacecraft and he is probably putting it back on the engine cover.]

a16a1183857.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1183857.text: Roger. That's 125.

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Boy, those things are a bucket of snakes, aren't they?

a16a1183857.speaker: Young
a16a1183857.text: That's alright. They won't bother you, will they?

a16a1183857.speaker: Duke
a16a1183857.text: Okay. No. Uh-uh. It's alright.

a16a1183857.speaker: Young

a16a1195235.text: Okay, John, here comes the (TV) picture. Ah-ha-ha! Man, Tony, I locked it the first time.

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: All righty. In column A, OID 05 change 03773 to read 03521.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Outstanding. That's got to be a first.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: It is for me. (Long Pause) [During the 1992 mission review, Charlie was fairly confident that, here, he was installing the TV camera and connecting the cable. The cable connection had given him trouble in training.]

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Whoop, whoops. I missed that, Hank.

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: Okay.

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: I guess I'm going to have to do one thing or the other. I can't talk and eat at the same time.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Okay, the old bubble person (meaning himself) has got the bubble right in the middle.

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: Okay. Whenever you're ready, we'll - you - If you don't want to do it now, just holler.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay. (Pause) [John is leveling the UV camera as per CDR-10 . With it leveled and, initially pointing down-Sun, he will be able to point at various targets using an elevation gauge near the top and an azimuth gauge at the base. See NASA training photo KSC-71P-628 .]

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Okay, "set target number one". Azimuth 14 and elevation 48, and say again what you want me to make it, Tony.

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Okay. Let me finish this eat period.

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: Okay.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay, we'd like to make the azimuth 98.

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: I got - I got carried away with trying to get ahead.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: (Surprised by the big difference) 98?!

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Right, we're changing targets.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: That ain't even close. (Hearing England) Yeah. (Chuckling) Okay.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: And the elevation is 28. (Pause) And watch the film advance as you turn the power on. (Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: And turning it in azimuth just completely destroyed whatever level it had. 98 and what now?

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Hey, Hank. If you got time while I'm - while I can listen, and - how about telling me if there's - you got any words on the general EVA plan for the surface and - guys are doing.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: (Annunciation carefully) 98 and 28. (Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: Okay. The guys are outside now on the surface. They got the Rover deployed and they're checking it out. And they're going to try to do the nominal number 1 EVA plan. As - about as far as we can predict in the future right now is through - doing the second EVA tomorrow. We don't know how consumables are going to hold out for the - for the thing. We're going to have to take a look at it - whether there's a possibility of the third one or not. Right now, I'm not so sure.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: 98 and 28. Okay. (Pause) [Meanwhile, Charlie is aiming the high gain using the handle and sighting scope shown in Figure 2-13 in the LRV Operations Handbook . Photo AS16-110- 18008 gives a good side view of the sighting scope at Station 5 and AS16-108- 17671 shows John doing an alignment at Station 8.]

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Well, Tony, the old Earth is boresighted in the sight.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Outstanding.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Gonna be right on, babe. I think. Oops. Hey, you really got to bend back to see that beauty (meaning Earth). Y'all are right overhead! Okay, TV. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Could you get your head back far enough to actually see it?"] [Duke - "By leaning back, holding onto the antenna mast or the ladder or something, you could do it. It was difficult, though."]

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: There - there still is some chance, huh?

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: Well, it doesn't look too bright, but they're looking at it.

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Have they got the ALSEP out yet? Or does that come after the Rover?

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: That comes after the Rover.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Okay, Tony, I turned the power switch on...(Correcting himself) When I unstowed it, the power switch was on. I turned the power switch off on the TV.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Okay, Houston, will you go with this bubble just broke off on one side, or do you want to level it every time? [The level bubble is in a small, covered, bowl shaped cavity.]

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Is it off the case (meaning the side of the cavity)?

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Yeah, it's off the case.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay, that's fine. As long as it's off the case.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay. Now, all you want me to do on this first one is turn the power switch on, right?

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Right. Power switch on, and watch the film advance as you come on so you can tell us how many degrees.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Okay, it looked like it was better than 90. That's about all I can say about it. Maybe 100 or 110.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay. (Pause) Let's just leave it there. 119:58:06 Young: Okay. (To Charlie) Hear that VHF (Very High Frequency)?

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Is that what that is?

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Yeah.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Ah, so. I can hear it, John.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Yep. (Pause) (To Houston) Okay, I guess that tells us something about the camera operation.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Right, the mode change works.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: It started, I'm sure, Houston. (Hearing Tony) Yep. Well, I don't know. That'll probably be in a minute or two - like two and a quarter minutes. Okay. I'm gonna...(Pause) [Apparently, some function in the UV camera generates a VHF signal that can be picked up by the comm system. The other possible source of VHF is the Command Module which, however, won't pass over the landing site for about another 16 minutes and, consequently, is well below the local horizon.]

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Boy, is this ever a neat operating environment!

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: (Garbled) (Pause) Okay, Tony, I'm reading, on Internal, S-band (signal strength) is 26, Temp is 14, Power is 22. Over.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay, we copy.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Look at this, Charlie.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Yeah.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: I can carry it over my head. (Chuckles) [As per CDR-10 , John is carrying the Quad III LRV Aft Pallet to the Rover. This pallet was stowed just to the left of the Quad III Payload Pallet compartment where the UV camera is stowed, which is shown empty in a detail from AS16-107- 17436 , a frame from a LM pan Charlie will take at the start of EVA-2. As indicated in Figure 3.4-1 in the Lunar Surface Procedures volume, the LRV Aft pallet contains a variety of geology tools and, also, the penetrometer and the Portable magnetometer. John is at the 1:05 mark in the checklist. The EVA started at 118:53

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: He gets paid double time, Charlie.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: I'll tell you.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: For every strip.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: (Grunts) It's amazing. (Pause) (As per LMP-8 ) the LCRU blankets are 100 percent open.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Going to External. (Pause) Mode switch to 2.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: (Very pleased) I'll be darn if the old Quad III pallet didn't go on like it was supposed to!

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: And, Tony, you ought to have it; you got 4.0 on the signal strength.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Lookit that! (Pause) (Garbled) (Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: You getting a signal, Tony?

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Ah, we're working it.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Okay, you got 4.0; you got External, and your mode switch is 2, and the Power is 2 - correction - I didn't check the power. The S-Band... (Pause) The Power is 12. 14. Over. Correction, make that 18.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Oh, don't tell me.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: What?

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Finally happened.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: What?

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: I pulled a wire loose, Charlie.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Uh-oh. (Long Pause) [Young, from the 1972 Technical Debrief - "On the back end (Rover load-up), the old pallet just fell off (that is, came off easily) the Quad III and fell onto the LRV and went right in place and locked right in place and I don't understand it (why the operation went so smoothly). Just a piece of cake. And the only problem I had was that, on one of the penetrometer pins (at the bottom on CDR-10 ), the wire pulled loose so that, instead of having a loop, I just had a long piece of wire. I was able to wrap the wire around my hand and pull the pin. The pin was pretty hard to pu

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Okay, (Garbled; Long Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1195235.text: Casper, Houston. Just a little reminder - about time for - to open the alpha particle X-ray cover.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Houston, how do you read?

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Stand by a second, Charlie. (Pause) Okay, it's looking pretty good. Don't have a picture here in the (Mission Operations Control) room yet, but we're getting data.

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Okay. I'll - Thank you, sir.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Okay, fine. Okay. (As per LMP-9 ) the DAC (Data Acquisition Camera) is coming out (of its stowage place in the MESA). (Pause) [The DAC is a 16-mm movie camera that Charlie will mount on his handhold as shown in Figure 2-14 from the LRV Operations Handbook . And undated Ed Dempsey training photo shows the DAC mounted on the Rover at the Cape. Scan courtesy Frederic Artner.]

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Alpha cover, Open -

a16a1195235.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1195235.text: Mark. And it's gray.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: (Garbled) as far as keeping an eye on us, you guys would rather be outside than inside, wouldn't you? (Comm clears dramatically)

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Okay, Tony, the TV camera is pointed right down at the ground, forward of the Rover.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Hey, our comm just improved 900 percent. That's beautiful. (Long Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Uh-oh, look at that. (Laughs)

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Did you get that pin out, John?

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Which one, Charlie?

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: The one that you broke the wire on.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: No, I haven't, but I'll work it later.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: What is it to?

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: I don't know. Wait a minute. (Pause) Think it's to the penetrometer. (Long Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Man, I tell you, if my Christmas stocking looked like this ETB, I'd be saved. Okay, (DAC) magazine P, the X is in the middle, and the frame is lined up.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay, magazine Papa. (Pause) Hey, Charlie. Verify the TV power switch is on.

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: (Lost under Tony) all right.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Stand by. (Pause)

a16a1195235.speaker: Young
a16a1195235.text: Got it, Charlie. [John has solved his penetrometer problem.]

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: (To Houston) You mean the LM power switch or the one on the TCU?

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: On the TCU.

a16a1195235.speaker: Duke
a16a1195235.text: Okay, I'll shoot it to On. Okay, momentary On; back to center.

a16a1195235.speaker: England
a16a1195235.text: Okay. (Pause) Hey, we've got a picture!! [TV on.] Video Clip 3 min 15 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 29 Mb MPG ) MP3 Audio Clip ( 14 min 27 sec )

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Yea! 120:05:39 Young: Of the ground, no doubt.

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Of the ground. [Those listening to the audio track may have noticed a high-pitched beep at the start and end of each of Tony's transmissions. Markus Mehring has provided a discussion of these Quindar Tones .]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Let's hear it (for the TV camera).

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Yeah. That's nice looking ground. [The TV camera will be operated from Houston by Ed Fendell . Fendell raises his aim and gives us a view of the WNW horizon. He then pans counter-clockwise.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Okay, the (DAC) camera is running! The 16 millimeter is running!

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Outstanding.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: I don't believe it.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: It's actually...

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Outstanding. (Pause) [The Apollo 15 crew had numerous problems with their DAC because of film magazine jams and got very little usable film during their traverses.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Okay, getting the other DAC (magazine) out (of the ETB).

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: This mission's full of firsts.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Little firsts, but they mean something...

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Oh, is this easy to do in one-sixth gravity....

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: ...personally, anyway.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: ...I really like it. This is about the neatest thing I ever saw. Okay. (Long Pause) [John is loading equipment on the aft pallet. In the meantime, Fendell finds Charlie at the MESA. Charlie turns toward the Rover, carrying the ETB in his right hand and the DAC in his left. The UV camera is at the right side of the TV frame.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Hey, you're looking at me with the big eye!

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Right. The big eye's on you, Charlie.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: (They're) trying to see if you're nervous, Charlie. (Pause)

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Can't just throw those bags over there like I used to (in training); they bounce into the dirt.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Yeah. (Pause) [As per LMP-9 , Charlie has taken the ETB to the Rover. He is standing next to John's seat and has probably just tried to toss the two padded bags listed near the bottom of the checklist page over onto the right-hand, LMP seat. During training, it may have been easy to make the toss so that the bags would stay on the seat. Here, because of the one-sixth gravity, they have probably bounced off and landed on the ground on the other side of the Rover.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: How's the (TV) picture, Tony?

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Very good picture. (Pause) Beautiful; outstanding color.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Super.

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: You're in living color. [Color television had come into widespread use only a few years before, in the mid-1960s.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Okay, I'm putting on magazine Bravo (aka AS16-114)...(Stops to listen) Okay, magazine Bravo is going on the Commander's camera. [Charlie is wearing John's camera. He is holding the film magazine in his left hand and removes a dark slide with his right hand. The magazine is a cube about 3 to 4 inches - 7 to 10 cm - on a side.] 120:07:45 Duke: (Blows) I just tried to blow off the dust (on the magazine), Tony. And it's starting at frame count number 4.

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: Okay, Hank. I'm ready to copy your erasable updates.

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Okay.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: That (trying to blow the dust off) won't work, Charlie. [Charlie inserts the magazine at the back of the camera and then reaches down with his left hand to get the handle-mounted trigger and advances the film by one or two frames.]

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Bravo 4; and keep count of how many times you blow off the dust.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: It didn't get it off, John. (Responding to Tony) Well, it didn't work, so... [Charlie takes the CDR camera off his RCU bracket and puts it on John's seat.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: Say again, Casper.

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: I'm ready to copy the erasables.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: (Pleased) Oh, look, this thing says "Lock" on it, Charlie. [Young, from the 1972 Technical Debrief - "Unlike the training equipment, both the shovel and the rake were very easy to lock on (the extension handles) because it tells you which way to turn the thing to lock it and how to put it on."] [Here, John is attaching the scoop to one of the two extension handles.] [Charlie looks at his cuff checklist.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: Okay. In column A there - column alpha - OID 05.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Okay, this (DAC) goes to the other seat. [Charlie picks up the DAC and reaches across to put it on the LMP seat.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: (Laughing) Oh, boy!

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Okay, (reading LMP-9 ) "three HEDC (Hasselblad Electronic Data Camera film magazines), two DAC (magazines), and 500 under the (CDR) seat". [Charlie's hands are off-camera, but he appears to move the ETB so that he can raise John's seat.] 120:08:16 Duke: And look at all of the little goodies (in the ETB?). Uh-oh. (Pause as he tries to raise the seat) The old Velcro man did it again. Video Clip (2 min 50 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo clip or 26 Mb MPEG )

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Charlie, that thing (a decal) tells you what to do!

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: This is on 9-4.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: How about that? (Laughs) A new first. This is so super.

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: That's affirmative. A...

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: Okay.

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: The old data should read 03773. The new data there should be 03521.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Got you, huh?

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: That's affirmative. Column A again. OID 07 reads now 76747; new data, 76274.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Uh-huh. (Pause) Oops. (Pause) [Although we can't see Charlie's hands or John's seat, it appears that, when Charlie tugs at the Velcro, he starts to fall forward and has to catch himself.] 120:09: Duke: Aw, come on out of there. No. (Grunts) (Pause) [Charlie continues to struggle with the Velcro. The TV camera jiggles in response to his efforts.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: Okay. 07 now reads 76274.

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: Roger. Column Bravo, OID 04. Now reads 13353; new data, 13347.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: I tell you, Houston. I'm just cool as a cucumber, and this Sun is so bright you can't believe it.

a16a1200538.speaker: England
a16a1200538.text: Outstanding. (Long Pause) [Charlie finally gets the Velcro loose.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: Column Bravo, OID 05. Old data, 00041; new data, 65620.

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Okay, as you can tell on the big eye, we're unloading the ETB under the Commander's seat. [A training photo by Ed Dempsey shows the CDR camera in the stowage area under Charlie's seat. Scan courtesy of Frederic Artner.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: Okay. New data, 65620. That's column Bravo, 05.

a16a1200538.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1200538.text: That's correct, Ken, and that's all of that. I hate to go back, but along about 125:06, when we deleted that P52, we should have deleted the P00 that went right ahead of it.

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: Hey, your vise is in, Charlie, (as per Item 7 on CDR-11 ). [John has mounted the vise on the top of the aft pallet behind Charlie's seat. They will use the vise to separate the drill stem sections of the deep core. Because of a design error, the Apollo 15 vise was mounted backwards and was all but useless to Scott and Irwin. Needless to say, that error was corrected for Apollo 16.]

a16a1200538.speaker: Duke
a16a1200538.text: Super. (Pause) John, I don't know if this film is gonna really balance in here; I can't get it wedged in like I did (in training). [Charlie and I were unable to explain this transmission. Obviously, something to do with the under-seat stowage is different than it was in training. The under-seat stowage arrangement is shown in Figure 4-5 from the LRV Operations Handbook .]

a16a1200538.speaker: Young
a16a1200538.text: No, I don't think...I don't think...(Pause) (Garbled)

a16a1200538.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1200538.text: Okay. Let me come back to that in just a second. I'm passing over Madler now; and, if you remember, we talked about that funny - bright ray pattern - how it seemed to have a funny shape that it - it took off in one direction and then it made a straight line in the other. Well, there's a textural difference in the ground that's underneath that bright material. It's a - It looks like it's - more like highlands - kind of overlay that's on top of a regular mare material. And it does, in fact, go along those - that line of demarcation that we see, and it seems to overlay the - the mare-type, and it

a16a1205534.text: Okay; the temperature...The shorting plug is pulled and the temperature (means "ampere") reading is reading about like...Golly! I can't believe it. It's reading (chuckles) about like three-quarter scale.

a16a1205534.text: Tony, let me give you a question here. The down-Sun heat probe is gonna be within 2 meters of about a 5-meter (diameter) crater. Over. That's maybe a meter deep. a16a1205534.speaker: England
a16a1205534.text: Can you move it to a crater-free area?

a16a1205534.text: Yes, I can; but it'll be more towards the portable (magnetometer)...(Correcting himself) I mean the LSM (Lunar Surface Magnetometer).

a16a1205534.text: Okay, we'd like to do that. [In Figure 3.4-3 from the Lunar Surface Procedures volume, the LSM is the three-armed instrument 35 feet northwest of the west (No. 1) heat flow probe. John is working at the Central Station, connecting the RTG cable as per CDR-18 ; and Charlie is closer to the Rover, working with the Heat Flow equipment. a16a1205534.speaker: Duke
a16a1205534.text: Okay. Now the one up-Sun is perfect, straight up-Sun.

a16a1205534.text: Very good. (Pause) [Charlie is sidestepping to his right as he lays out the cable for the up-Sun probe.] Video Clip ( 3 min 07 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG )

a16a1205534.text: Yeah, this is a super place right here for this up-Sun one. Okay, here we go with a big drill coming up! [Fendell reaches the clockwise stop. a16a1205534.text: That sounds good. [Charlie sets the rack down and then hops around to the east side of it.] Video Clip ( 3 min 10 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG )

a16a1205534.text: Well, I don't think...That won't be any problem. The only thing goes down past there is the LSM.

a16a1205534.text: Okay, (reading the bottom of CDR-18 ) "Level and align experiments package, by eyeball." [Charlie removes one drill stem from the bag and then lays the rest on the rack.]

a16a1205534.text: Okay, that's okay, John. We understand you're going to deploy it (meaning the LSM) almost due west of the RTG?

a16a1205534.text: Right. (Long Pause) [Charlie tries to thread the drill stem into the drill but without luck. The stems have a single thread which circles the stem in a rise of about a centimeter and, in shirtsleeves, it is trivial to get them threaded. a16a1210808.speaker: England
a16a1210808.text: (To John) Okay, and we need about 30 feet between that heat flow hole and the LSM. (Pause)

a16a1210808.speaker: England
a16a1210808.text: Very good. (Pause) [Charlie picks up the drill by grabbing the stem just above the chuck, turns the assembly over and positions the bit in the ground next to the probe he laid down previously.]

a16a1210808.speaker: Duke
a16a1210808.text: For a minute there I was worried. Okay. I can stab it into the ground about...(Pause) [Charlie pushes the bit a few inches into the ground, removes a thermal cover from the drill and tosses it off-camera to our left.] 121:09:31 Duke: Okay!! Are you guys ready?! Here we go! (Applying power to the drill) Mark. Hey, that beauty is going right in!

a16a1210808.speaker: England
a16a1210808.text: Outstanding. (Pause) [Charlie gets about a foot of penetration; but, then, the rate slows dramatically. Something similar happened on Apollo 15 when the joint between the first and second drill stems went into the surface but, in that case, the cause was a faulty drill-stem design which prevented the cuttings from flowing upward past the joint. a16a1210808.speaker: Duke
a16a1210808.text: It's not going in. Something hard in there. (Pause) Whatever it was, we got through it, Tony. It's speeding up again.

a16a1210808.speaker: Duke
a16a1210808.text: Right on down now. It's super now. It must have been a rock. I'm sure the regolith is covered with...(Pause) [Charlie is speculating that, because the surface is littered with rocks, there are numerous subsurface rocks as well.] [Charlie finishes the first stem.]

a16a1210808.speaker: England
a16a1210808.text: Very good, Charlie. 121:10:27 Duke: Okay, and first, the long stem is in. [This first stem is about a meter long.]

a16a1210808.text: Golly, Charlie. (Pause) Help me when you get finished. a16a1210808.speaker: Duke
a16a1210808.text: Okay, Tony, the foot mashie is not gonna work.

a16a1210808.speaker: Duke
a16a1210808.text: Gonna have to use the wrench.

a16a1210808.speaker: England
a16a1210808.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Charlie gets into position a meter or more from the drill, leans forward and puts his left hand on the drill to support himself while he reaches down with his right hand and engages the wrench on the drill stem.
