a16a1254008.text: I say getting into this moose (meaning the LM) is the hardest job of the whole EVA.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Okay, and there's the pallet. What did you bring up with you?

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: I brought the pallet. We've got an SCB, the core stems, and the ETB.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Okay. Hardly nothing in the SCB, right?

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: Okay, just a second now. The highest stuff is in the mares [sic] - to best...

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: One big rock is all.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Yeah. (Pause) Whew!

a16a1254008.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1254008.text: Roger. In the west...

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: ...Cognitum, Nubium, and so on.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: That other big muley ( 175k ) we'll get with the big rock bag later on. (Pause) Think you can do that all one-handed, John, huh?

a16a1254008.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1254008.text: Right. And the next highest - is in the central highlands from Midler to Alphonsus.

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: Okay, the - you say the highest readings - highest of - of what? Just - just the highest counts?

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: If I can jump up to the third rung. All I got to do here is jump. (Pause) Ah. There we go.

a16a1254008.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1254008.text: I guess just the highest - highest counting rates in the Gamma Spectrometer.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: He jumps over buildings with a single bound, Houston! Faster than a speeding bullet. [This is another reference to the comic book character, Superman.]

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: Okay.

a16a1254008.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1254008.text: Third highest is Mare Fecunditatis area. And the lowest readings occur in - on the far-side highlands.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Okay, Tony. We're bringing SCB number 5 in with a big rock.

a16a1254008.speaker: England
a16a1254008.text: Okay, we copy that. (Pause)

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: (Garbled) core.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Wait a minute. You're going to have to stick those up in the...

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Oh, don't kick them back out, Charlie...

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: I'm not.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Hold still. I'll get them. I'll give them to you.

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: Well, I can't - I can tell you they sure look different. They're all black over there. That's always intriguing, when you can't see something.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Okay. Can you hand them up?

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: How's that?

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: I say great! Got them. Filthy.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Here you go.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Gimme...No. (Pause)

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Here's your SCB.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Okay.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Okay, let me get you an ETB.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Tony, read out the ETB stuff.

a16a1254008.speaker: England
a16a1254008.text: Okay, Charlie. You...

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Just didn't look quite full to me.

a16a1254008.speaker: England
a16a1254008.text: Right, you have two HEDC mags, B and D; three HEDC mags, A, C, and H; one 500-millimeter mag L; three DAC mags, P, Q, and R; your maps; and six sample contingency bags...(correcting himself) or "containment bags".

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Okay, John. I didn't get that.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: You didn't hear any of it?

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: I did not get those (containment) bags. See, I don't have that on my checklist.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Okay. [Duke - "They were bags for the bags; but I don't remember them."] [ Sample Containment Bags were flown on the J missions to help reduce the amount of dust in the cabin. The Sample Collection Bags were put inside the Containment Bags . Photos of containment bags in the National Air & Space collection courtesy Allan Needell.]

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: And they're on the MESA.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Okay, I'll go get them.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Okay; they're for these cover bags.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Yeah, right.

a16a1254008.speaker: England
a16a1254008.text: Okay. They're in the left front of the MESA, John.

a16a1254008.speaker: Young
a16a1254008.text: Yeah, I know where they're at. Okay, now it doesn't hit the deck anymore. That hit the deck some more. [John notices that, because the pallet and rock box have been removed from the MESA, the bottom of it is no longer touching the ground.]

a16a1254008.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1254008.text: And, Ken, these light-colored markings you reported near King Crater - the west of King? Farouk says those are near the crater Abul Wafa. And these may be similar to the swirls of Ibn Yunus, but they are not identical. And for your information, the markings of Abul Wafa are - he uses the term antipodal or opposite to Riccioli, on the western part of your track.

a16a1254008.speaker: Duke
a16a1254008.text: Tony, I have (an EVA elapsed time of) 6 (hours) 58 (minutes).

a16a1254008.speaker: England
a16a1254008.text: That's right. (Long Pause) [The longest EVA up to this point in Apollo is the second Apollo 15 EVA, which lasted 7 hours 12 minutes. However, John and Charlie were out longer than the 6 hour 33 minute duration of the first Apollo 15 EVA.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 15 min 45 sec )

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: (Laughter)

a16a1254008.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1254008.text: That means it's 180 degrees from there.

a16a1254008.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1254008.text: Tell him that it - it's awfully - Roger; Roger. Tell him it's awful hard to find a place where there - 180 degrees away - there won't be a crater on the Moon.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, I think that (meaning the containment bags) was the only thing I didn't have, John.

a16a1255139.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1255139.text: (Laughter) Roger.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: He'll understand.

a16a1255139.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1255139.text: Casper, High Gain on the Auto - Auto on the High Gain.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Roger. You should have six DAC mags...Correction, six Hasselblad mags and three DAC mags.

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: Sure can.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, I've got all the film.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: These bags are on the left side of the MESA, right, Charlie?

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: I got one that's better for him this time, though. I'm not at all sure that those swirls that I saw north of - northwest of King are - are really - like the others or not. I - I tried to get a look at Ibn Yunus this time, and it's still a little too far to the north.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Left front.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Right where the SWC...I mean, the core stem bags were.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, I've got them up here. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: And, John, maybe you could set the UV...

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: (To Charlie) Right where the core stem bags was?

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: ...before you go up this time.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Is it sample containment bags?

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: That's right.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Oh, okay. And underneath that is a flag for the old whatchacallit. I'm not sure there's any sample containment bags in there, Char...Yeah, I guess maybe there are. (Pause) I'll bring them up separate, Charlie. (To Houston) You want me to reset the UV (as per CDR-42 ) before I go up this time? [The MESA stowage diagram ( 145k doesn't provide an immediate identification of the 'flag for the old whatchacallit'.]

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, it would be a good idea. Then you could just stay up.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: (To John) Why don't you bring the...

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: (Responding to Tony; not looking forward to it) Oh, dear. Okay. (Long Pause) [The UV camera decal, Figure 5.3-1 in the Apollo 16 Lunar Surface Procedures volume, indicates that the planned target for the next sixteen hours is a cluster of galaxies known as NGC 134 at an azimuth of 230 degrees and an elevation of 53 degrees. At 125:16:33 , shortly after John arrived back at the LM, Houston had him point the UV camera at a target with an azimuth of 204 and an elevation of 26. Readers should note that, unlike the Rover Nav system which uses north as zero azimuth, the UV camera uses west as zero a

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: John, when you come up, if you remember to bounce your feet on the struts...

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: ...it'll clean them off. That's what I'm doing up in the...by moving on the floor.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay, (reading CDR-42 ) "ETB, then set the far UV". What's the target, Houston? I'm over at the far UV.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Reset. And then the target is 134 azimuth and 39 elevation. [Note that this is not the target (No. 4) indicated on the checklist. Because the late landing, necessitated deploying the UV camera closer to the LM, the target list is being changed in real time.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, Houston; 3, 2, 1, Mark. Reset. 134 azimuth. (Pause) Houston, can I hit the Reset again? I didn't see the film move. (Pause) No; it did.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay, fine.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Because it's re-moding. Boy. (Long Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay, that azimuth was 134.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: 134 is looking at the lunar module, Houston! You don't want to do that.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Would an elevation of 39 look over it?

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: You know, Henry, one of the things that impresses me is that when you look at the mare surface in very high Sun, like I'm doing now, a lot of the very shallow craters that have just very subtle, sweeping walls and are together maybe in a chain or in groups - when you see this at high Sun, it looks exactly like a swirl pattern. If you didn't know that's what it was, you'd - you probably would wonder about it also.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Heck, no. It's at 26 now (and) it's not clearing it. (Pause) [The LM is 7 meters tall and the horizontal distance from the footpad to the point on the ground directly under the front of the top surface is about 4.0 meters. Consequently, if the UV camera were pointed directly at the LM, any target at an elevation of less than about 60 degrees would be blocked by the spacecraft. However, because (1) the footpad is 4.7 meters from the spacecraft, (2) the UV camera is 2 meters southwest of the footpad, and (3) the horizontal radius of the Descent stage is about 2.2 meters, the LM blocks targets wi

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Well, let me see, it might. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, Houston, I just got a water flag.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: If you want to take a look at Charlie (with the UV camera), yeah, it'll clear it, but that's not any good, Houston. [Readers should note that an azimuth of 134 would leave the camera pointing in the general direction of the LMP window on the north side of the LM, confirming our conjecture that, with regard to UV camera settings only, zero azimuth is west.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1255139.text: Roger.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay, Charlie. What do you have?

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: He has a water flag. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: (Giving John a new target) Okay. Azimuth is 258, elevation is 64.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. I'm going to go to Reset again; will that be all right?

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: That's fine.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Because I can't make it. (Hearing Tony) Okay, Reset; Mark. 258, 64.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Rog. (Long Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: And, Hank, would you give me a warning about 126:18 ?

a16a1255139.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1255139.text: Will do.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Man, that (UV camera) is some contraption, John. (Long Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: 258 and 64, Houston.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay, fine. We'd like you to get on in then.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. That's not looking at anything that I recognize. (Long Pause) [AZ258 and EL64 do not correspond to any of the targets listed on the UV camera decal. Because the lunar surface is so bright, he is probably not able to see any stars and, therefore, would not be commenting on his aim relative to the constellations.] [Young, from the 1972 Technical Debrief - "There's something else I don't really understand about the Far UV camera setup and the alignment that we're doing in real time. Except for the geo-corona and the Earth (Target No. 2 on the decal), we changed every target in real time. I

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay, Charlie. Here I come. Keep cool, man.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: I'm fine. Don't worry. (Pause) [Although Charlie has gotten a warning tone indicating that he is just about out of cooling water, he will end the EVA with about a half pound left out of the original twelve pounds. He is not working very hard at the moment and, if need be, could get hooked up to the LM system relatively quickly.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: Hank, looking in the bottom floor of Messier - I think it's the original Messier, the elongate one - the bottom dark material has a little ropey white material that runs down the length of the crater. And at one end, it looks like - sort of like a high-water mark. On the northern - northern and western end of that, it looks like there had been a high-water mark and then maybe this stuff had dropped down. And you see little blocks of that stuff, kind of like the whole thing had just been floating and it had just sunk a little bit.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Agh. (Pause) Boy. Up to the third rung, Charlie.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Beautiful

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Just like flying.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Put you on...The (Los Angeles) Lakers will want you when you get back. (Pause) [The Los Angeles Lakers professional basketball team was a top-ranked team of the time.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Here are those (containment) bags.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Fine, I've got them. Thank you. Well, I thought I had them. (Garbled) a little bit. I'm not closing you out, John. I'm just (pause) getting some bending room here. (Long Pause) [Charlie is standing behind the hatch and John is still out on the porch.] [Jones - "After you got everything in, you had to get over behind the hatch to let John in."] [Duke - "Yeah. And I was on the right (LMP) side at this point and I swing the hatch open so that he could get in, and that trapped me behind the hatch, and you couldn't bend down; and, at this point, John's still shoving stuff in. I think he's got

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: When I look in the wall of the other one - the round one - it appears that there's a depression in the northwest side where it's kind of pushed in and things may have run down in there. I have the distinct impression that there was an original crater that is not part of the bright one that we see now that's over on the western side.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: (Probably handing the bags in) Okay, Charlie. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Here's the ETB.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. I'd get that (LEC) hook out of the way, if I were you. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay, hook is out of the way. (Pause) [John has probably draped the LEC over the porch railing.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Do anything with that?

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: No, I think you can get in...Wait a minute; I can get it here. (Pause) Okay, I got it.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, enter your humble abode. Okay, you really got to arch your back, John, (and get your stomach low so that the PLSS clears the bottom of the DSKY). There you go; you got it. Okay, come towards me a little bit. Okay. Keep coming towards me. There you go. Okay; now bend over a little bit. Come forward a little bit. There you go; you got it. Your tool harness is hooking up on your...There you go. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, Messier A does show a secondary crater. And I have the impression that that was an old crater that kind of smoothed and darkened and looked like the rest of these older craters, and that it - Messier A then was penetrated on top of that, or at least formed subsequent to that, and it kind of broke into that wall.

a16a1255139.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1255139.text: Roger. The map shows an indication maybe there might be a secondary there.

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, it - I had thought maybe that was a - a terrace - kind of like a slump feature, but apparently that's not the case.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: (Phew), man! (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Now we're back inside (and ready to switch to Lunar Surface Checklist page 3-1).

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Why can't I turn around, Charlie. [After John crawled into the cabin and got his PLSS past the DSKY, he came upright on his knees, facing the left rear of the crew area.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Huh? Can't you go the other way? Okay, you got it.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Hung up on something.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, you're sitting on the hatch!

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Oh.

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: I wish we had some low-Sun pictures of this crater that had the bright splash rays that I took a picture of before, that's about halfway between Messier and Censorinus. I'd swear it's on the top of a - a very shallow rise. And it - appears to me that there is a very slightly darker albedo to the material underneath it - That goes out about the same diameter as the bright rays. Now, it may be that the bright rays are giving it that characteristic just because they're - they may be tenuous enough that they don't show up by themselves, but they may be there.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Don't want to close it (meaning the hatch) all the way and getting all this feedwater in here. [Jones - "The way I understand it is that the sublimator wouldn't work if the hatch was closed. On Apollo 12, Al Bean accidentally swung the door closed and there was enough of a pressure buildup from the water vapor coming off the sublimator that the sublimator quit working - although it certainly wasn't enough pressure to keep him from opening the hatch."] [Duke - "The sublimator needed a vacuum. We'd have to go on through here and look at the checklist. (Pause) We had to close our water before we

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, now come around. There you go. Now we got it. We're back inside.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Reading the top of the righthand column of Card 2 Side 1 ) We've got to close the (PLSS) Primary H2O.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: If you'll turn...There you go.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Get yours closed. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, yours is closed.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay, let me get yours. Get my visor up.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay (garbled). (Long Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Can you swing your (back)pack this way just a little? [The feedwater shut-off valve is one of the three valves on the lower right rear corner of the PLSS. Charlie is probably turning to his left to swing it around so John can reach it.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: How's that?

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: There's another one a little smaller that's about halfway between the one I just described and Censorinus. And if there's one that I'd agree with Stu has black things that drape down inside it - like that might, but maybe when I get closer, it'll look like shadows. It's kind of hard to tell from here. There are an awful lot of blocks around it, it appears.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay, and your water valve is closed.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. And we can close the hatch . (Pause) Okay, (overhead) dump valve going Auto.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: I haven't got the hatch closed, Charlie.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. [As he did during the Depress, Charlie is using the overhead valve and probably can't see what John is doing with the hatch. Charlie is left-handed, so it is relatively easy for him to reach up to get the valve, which is near the center of the ceiling.] 126:02:52 Young: It's closed.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay; can you lock it?

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: No.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause) Probably got to push it to lock it. There you go.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Damn it! (Pause) Ain't locking. Why don't we wait until we get it pressurized. It's closed good and tight.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. [Once the cabin pressure goes above a few tenths of a psi, the hatch will seat itself. After they depressurize the suits, they will be able to bend over much more easily to reach the latch. The latch is really rather superfluous because, at 4.5 psi, the forward hatch would be impossible to open.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Got the dump valves to Auto?

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: No, not yet. I was waiting until you get out of the way.

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: I'm looking now at this bright, depressed crater that's next to it, and I'm going to try to get a picture of that next time I get the camera available because this white stuff runs down the side of a very smooth brown crater. And there's places where you can see it's run out on the floor on the bottom, and it has a very strange appearance. It - it - The white stuff looks like it ran out and then just stopped abruptly. There's no - no toe on it or anything.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, (overhead) dump valve's in Auto. Okay, "PLSS O2 and the press flags may come on during Repress". Okay, I'm going "Cabin Repress, Auto; CB 16, Cabin Repress, Closed".

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Move up (meaning "forward") just slightly. Let me turn around.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause) [Charlie needs to turn around so he can get the valve on the front of the ECS cabinet and then the circuit breaker on the panel on the right bulkhead.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Cabin repress, here we come. (Repressurization audible) (Pause) [Jones - "You've got the Snoopy cap on inside the helmet. Repress is pretty loud in the mike, although not terribly. Could you hear it?"] [Duke - "You could hear this, but it wasn't bad."]

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: (Unintelligible; Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: I got an O flag (as expected).

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: I got an O flag. (Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: How is the (cabin) pressure?

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Two psi, Charlie.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Two?

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Two.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Three?

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Two!

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Oh, okay. Okay, read the checklist. Something happens at 2-1/2.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Where is it?

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: (Garbled)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. "Cabin at 3 1/2 (garbled)" [John is referring to the line 'PLSS O2 - OFF @ Cabin > 2.5 Psia', fourn lines above 109:25 in the righthand column of Card 2 Side 1 .]

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: (Garbled) turn the PLSS O2 off at 2-1/2 (as per Surface 3-1).

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, "PLSS O2 off at cabin 2 1/2".

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay. My thing's going right down. (Repress noise subsidies) Man, it's up there already?

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Yeah.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: That is amazing. Hey, Houston...

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Will you turn off my PLSS O2 Charlie?

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah, (garbled) another hand.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay, very good. You had a 7 hour and 11 minute EVA.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: (Hearing Tony) Super! (Whistles) Master Alarm. It's cabin...Probably. [The Caution and Warning System is telling them that the ECS is not properly configured - and that the warning system is working.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, "PLSS O2, Press Reg A, and Master/Cabin lights are on; verify cabin pressure (increasing). Go to Press Reg A and B to Cabin."

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Press Reg A and B to Cabin , Charlie.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, got them.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Okay, "Cabin warning light off"?

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: It is.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: "Verify cabin pressure stable at 4.6 to 5."

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: "Use Purge Valve to depress PGA (Pressure Garment Assembly) as required."

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, mine's depressed.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Mine seems like it's depressed, too.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Yeah. [They have reached 109:25 in the righthand column of Card 2 Side 1 .]

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: "Verify EVA circuit breaker configuration."

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: White dots out plus EVA decals, plus other contingencies. Power down ones that we're using today. [They are checking the circuit breakers to make sure none were bumped open or closed as they moved around with the PLSSs on. As indicated on 1-4 and 1-5 , they have four circuit breakers open which would be closed were they not trying to conserve power because of the late landing. These open breakers are the S-Band Antenna near the left end of the top row on CB11, Mission Timer near the middle of the second row, LGC DSKY near the right end of the fourth row, and Inverter 2 near the middle of the b

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Hey, Houston, do you have telemetry?

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Rog. We have telemetry.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Okay, how does the cabin ECS look to you? (Long Pause)

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Wow, look at all them footprints out there, Charlie!

a16a1255139.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1255139.text: Casper, Houston. About a minute to go for your UV.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Great.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: John, verify you locked the forward hatch.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: (Lost under Tony) looks tracked.

a16a1255139.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1255139.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: No, I didn't lock it. I will. (Pause) [It is a lot easier to get down to lock the hatch with the suits depressurized.]

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: That got it.

a16a1255139.speaker: Young
a16a1255139.text: Yeah. Now it's locked, Houston.

a16a1255139.speaker: England
a16a1255139.text: Okay.

a16a1255139.speaker: Duke
a16a1255139.text: Got to push that beauty in. That's hard to do, pressurized. In fact, it's impossible. I am so dirty, I can't believe it. Grand Prix Apollo 16 Journal Post-EVA-1 Activities

a16a1260708.speaker: Young
a16a1260708.text: Okay, let's keep going here, Charlie.

a16a1260708.speaker: Duke
a16a1260708.text: Okay, (reading the last items on Card 2 Side 1 .) "doff gloves; stow on comm panel; doff helmets with visors, lower shades, stow in (helmet bags)..." (Pause) [Jones - "Do you remember anything about where the helmets were at various times? The 17 guys had some sort of a web bag they put the helmets in."] [Duke - "Yeah, we did, too. We had the helmet bags. It was like a flying-helmet bag. And then there was a webbing that we had. And, I think, it was generally behind the ascent engine cover."]

a16a1260708.speaker: England
a16a1260708.text: And, Charlie, your cabin ECS looked good.

a16a1260708.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260708.text: And, Ken, you don't have to acknowledge, but John and Charlie just got back into the LM, and they're just repressurized.

a16a1260708.speaker: Young
a16a1260708.text: Okay. I'm going to have some air in here. [John's deflated suit may be pinching him.]

a16a1260708.speaker: Duke
a16a1260708.text: (Garbled) my hand's so tired I can't (unlock my gloves)... (Long Pause) John, can you help me?

a16a1260708.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260708.text: Okay. I show that we're at the time to do this; however, it looks like we're not up to Descartes yet, and the camera's pointing - along towards Kant.

a16a1260708.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260708.text: Okay. The Flight Plan calls for leading it about two minutes, Ken.

a16a1260708.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1260708.text: This is Apollo Control at 126 hours 21 minutes [plan GET, 126:10 actual GET], and we've just had a report - a further report on Ken Mattingly and Casper. Everything continues to go very well. Flight Director Donald Puddy, who is following the actions of the Command and Service Module, said that they have not missed a thing in the Flight Plan. Everything is going very well. At the moment, Mattingly is taking UV photographs of the landing site, Casper passing almost directly over the Descartes site now.

a16a1260708.speaker: Young
a16a1260708.text: I think you may have some pressure in the suit there.

a16a1260708.speaker: Young
a16a1260708.text: Let me get this other glove and I'll get it.

a16a1260708.speaker: Duke
a16a1260708.text: I think my fingers are just tired. (Long Pause)

a16a1260708.speaker: Young
a16a1260708.text: (Probably referring to the dust in the cabin) What a mess, Charlie. (Long Pause) (Garbled). (Pause) There we go. MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 30 sec ) [NASA Public Affairs mentions to the media that Ken Mattingly is currently passing over the landing site.] [Readers should note that the times used at this point in the Journal differ from the GET being used in Houston because of an 11 minute 48 second update made to the clocks in Houston at 118:06:31 .]

a16a1260900.speaker: Duke
a16a1260900.text: (Laughing) Sorry to get you so dusty. Okay. Here, let me do that one. I can do it, I'll just get this one off to...Okay. Thank you.

a16a1260900.speaker: Young
a16a1260900.text: Well, look at that, would you. MP3 Audio Clip ( 6 min 45 sec )

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Boy, mine are tired, too. I'll tell you. [Young, from the 1972 Technical Debrief - "It was after EVA-1 that we noticed the wrist rings were getting clogged with dust. There should be some way to cover those wrist rings - the things that snap in and out - to keep them from getting full of dust, because it (meaning the dust) makes them practically impossible to work."]

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. And, it says to "doff helmets with visors; lower shades; stow in helmet bag". (Long Pause) [Now that they have the gloves off, they will doff the helmets.] [Young, from the 1972 Technical Debrief - "After EVA-1, we experienced a little stickiness with the helmets. Not a great deal, so we didn't pay any attention to it."]

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: Okay, Hank. I got it done, but I guess I made one mistake there. I didn't get the engines off. I didn't hear any firings during the time that I was taking the pictures, but I didn't get to Free.

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: Roger.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: (With his helmet now off) Boy, it feels good to be out of there. Man.

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: And, Ken, the guys are back inside. I don't know whether you heard me a while ago or not, but EVA-1 was a total success. They had a seven hour and 11 minute EVA.

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: Hey, that Moon dust don't taste half bad.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Is that what that is?

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: Yeah.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: I think it is just the ECS. (Long Pause) Whew. [Jones - "This is the first time I've heard anybody comment on taste, rather than on smell."] [Duke - "It was a little of both. To me, it was more of a smell. It had that gunpowder odor to me. I thought it might have been the ECS, you know, just coming up - with that oxygen in the lines. But I think it really was the lunar dust. It had to me a greasy (feel)...It really magnified your skin oils. As you got it on, it felt like it was a real greasy feeling. Oily dust. But what I think it was, it was picking up your skin oils - because there is no moi

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: Outstanding. Did they have anything particularly significant to say or...

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: I didn't catch all of it, let me ask...

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: Did they have any surprises in the things they saw or that they didn't expect?

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: Okay. (Pause) "Stow in the helmet bags. Verify safety on dump valve ." All right.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Get that. [They are now at the top of the lefthand column on Card 2 Side 2 .]

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: First thing I want...

a16a1260935.speaker: LM Crew
a16a1260935.text: Is a drink of water.

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: I'm going to take a break and get me a drink of water.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: (Garbled) I finished mine long ago. (Pause)

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: I guess the big thing, Ken, was they found all breccia. They found only one rock that possibly might be igneous.

a16a1260935.speaker: LM Crew
a16a1260935.text: (Garbled) 126:11:34 Young: Yes. I could have drank all of mine if I had a mouth behind my left ear. That's my only problem. It got lodged back there and I could never get at it. (Long Pause)

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: Is that right? [Laughter.]

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: Yeah. I guess the guys are a little bit surprised by that.

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: Well, that ought to- that ought to call for a session with the - (laughter) yeah, yeah (laughter). Well, it's back to the drawing boards or wherever geologists go.

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: Hey, Ken. Ron's asking what you were wearing last night when you got cold.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Old TELMU, Tony, should have seen the water quantity go down about 10 percent on that drink.

a16a1260935.speaker: England
a16a1260935.text: Okay. We saw it, Charlie.

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: I was just sleeping in my sleeping bag. I mean - All I had to do was get up and put on my - my jacket and trousers. Up to then, just getting in the sleeping bag was almost too hot.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Boy, it tasted good. Okay; "verify safety. Descent H2O valve, Open. Remove Purge Valve; stow in purse . Okay; disconnect OPS O2 hose." (Pause)

a16a1260935.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1260935.text: Roger.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Have any? [Charlie may be asking John if he got anything from the drink bag during the EVA.]

a16a1260935.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1260935.text: Okay, we're at frame 60 on magazine OO.

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: That's why you saw me dogging it (meaning "going slow") out there. (Long Pause)

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Okay, I'm turning my (PLSS LCG) pump off. (Garbled) Okay, now I've got to disconnect your O...(Correcting himself) purge valve.

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: (Have I) still got a purge valve there?

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Yeah, with a connector. (Pause) [Jones - "I had been visualizing just a bare pin falling out on the surface and was amazed that you saw it. But the fact that's it's got that Red Apple on there means it was real easy to see."] [Duke - "And it was real easy to get to in an emergency. Just pull the apple. It was a biggie. That's the only reason I saw it: because of the apple."]

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: Try not to step on that bag. That one's got to go back to the...Okay. I can't believe this is so dirty. (Long Pause) Ah!

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: (Laughing) Well it works good, when you (garbled) get around to it. [John has probably gotten his drink valve back into reach and has finally gotten a drink from it.] 126:14:05 Young: Well, shoot, Charlie, let me get that thing. (Garbled) dusty. (Long Pause) [They may have dropped something.]

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Okay, why don't you turn and face me, and I'll get to your (LM) O2 (hoses connected). (Garbled) I've already got mine.

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: You got yours?

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: You know, John, it would be a lot easier if you could come this way. There we go. Uh-oh.

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: All right, how's that? That's fine, Charlie. I think that one's (garbled).

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Okay. And just...I'll read the checklist. "Disconnect OPS O2 hose; connect LM hoses" - funny that we have to do that. " Suit Isol(ation Valve) , both, Suit Flow; PLSS Pump, Off, and Fan, Off." [Charlie is wondering why they have to connect the LM O2 and H2O hoses when, in about an hour and a half, they will doff the suits. The only explanation that comes to mind is that there is a concern about them overheating while they do the PLSS O2 recharge, the PLSS/OPS doffing, and other tasks on the remainder of Card 2 Side 2 ]

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: Okay.

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: "Disconnect PLSS H2O from PGA; connect LM H2O."

a16a1260935.speaker: Young
a16a1260935.text: (Wanting some LM cooling) Now, that's the best thing we got to do. (Pause) Okay, I got a flag, a press flag (as expected, because his PLSS O2 is off).

a16a1260935.speaker: Duke
a16a1260935.text: Okay, let me get you your (LM) water (hoses). (Long Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 2 min 48 sec ) [Readers should note that the times used at this point in the Journal differ from the GET being used in Houston because of an 11 minute 48 second update made to the clocks in Houston at 118:06:31 . Note also, that there seems to be an inconsistency in the times on either side of this long pause.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 21 sec )

a16a1261600.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1261600.text: Okay. I've got a real good look at the Davy chain now, and they are definitely all rimless. There are some - they run kind of northeast - southwest, and there are a couple of very subtle constructional features that just look like little - little bubbles of material that run north and south. They cross the ch - crater chain, but in fact, when they cross it, it kind of breaks it up. But the - the craters in the chain themselves don't look like they have any rims at all.

a16a1261702.speaker: Duke
a16a1261702.text: I think it is on the wall. Here, wait. (Pause) Come around this way with it.

a16a1261702.speaker: Young
a16a1261702.text: Okay. "Connect LM H2O"; we did. "PLSS mode goes to Off, both."

a16a1261702.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1261702.text: And, Casper; Houston. You're coming up on about 15 seconds to T-stop for the mapping camera.

a16a1261702.speaker: Young
a16a1261702.text: Close. Okay. "Audio: Commander and LMP; VHF, Receive."

a16a1261702.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1261702.text: This is Apollo Control at 126 hours 28 minutes [plan GET, 126:17 actual GET]. Young and Duke will spend about an hour and a half to two hours getting the LM cabin cleaned up, stowed, and getting their suits off. We'll then debrief them on the EVA, and let them get something to eat, they'll recharge the Portable Life Support System, and we're scheduled to begin an 8 hour rest period for the Lunar Module crew at [a] Ground Elapsed Time of 130 hours. We'd like to update the status in regard to the possibility of a third period of extra vehicular activity. There will be a meeting tonight, of proje

a16a1261702.speaker: Duke
a16a1261702.text: Okay. Go. [John mis-read the instruction and should have said "Audio: Commander and LMP; VHF A, Receive".]

a16a1261702.speaker: Duke
a16a1261702.text: Wait a minute. Start over again on that.

a16a1261702.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1261702.text: And the Mapping Camera is Off.

a16a1261702.speaker: Young
a16a1261702.text: Telemetry Biomed...No. Forget that one. [To save power, they are not transmitting biomed data.]

a16a1261702.speaker: Duke
a16a1261702.text: Wait a minute. Aft and Off. Go ahead. [Next, they will do a PLSS O2 recharge, starting with Charlie's PLSS. They are at the top of the middle column on Card 2 Side 2 , PLSS O2 Recharge.]

a16a1261702.speaker: Young
a16a1261702.text: Okay. "Verify Descent O2 greater than 56 percent. LMP first; connect your O2 for 10 minutes...(correcting himself) 4 minutes." It takes 2 minutes and 15...

a16a1261702.speaker: Duke
a16a1261702.text: Yeah, we got 80 percent (in the Descent oxygen tank number 2).

a16a1261702.speaker: Young
a16a1261702.text: Yeah. Well, I hope. Okay, Charlie. I don't know if I can...I keep hanging up on something back there. What...

a16a1261702.speaker: Duke
a16a1261702.text: Watch your hoses. Let me disconnect these because we don't need those dadgum things around like that. MP3 Audio Clip ( 11 min 24 sec )

a16a1261913.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1261913.text: And, Ken, have you done the rest of the things there?

a16a1261913.speaker: Duke
a16a1261913.text: Okay; now can you spin around there?

a16a1261913.speaker: Young
a16a1261913.text: Yeah. Here comes all our checklists and cards.

a16a1261913.speaker: Duke
a16a1261913.text: Okay. 126:19:20 Young: (We) may need that one; it might be an APS card. (Pause) [APS is Ascent Propulsion System, which they will use for the return to orbit.] [I mentioned to Charlie that it was very unusual for the crew to be transmitting during this part of the mission. He noted that, in the next to last paragraph in the lefthand column of They are at the top of the middle column on Card 2 Side 2 , they should have gone to "Mode - ICS/PTT". John did, indeed read that step out at 126:18:14 .] [Duke - "ICS:PTT. That meant, to transmit, you had to use the trigger, but we could talk between our

a16a1261913.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1261913.text: I'm coming up to it now. Thank you. Going to Standby, and Image Motion, Off, and it's barber pole - and gray. And here comes the gamma ray shield. Shield is Off now.

a16a1261913.speaker: Duke
a16a1261913.text: Okay. Can you turn...The other...

a16a1261913.speaker: Young
a16a1261913.text: Which way, Charlie?

a16a1261913.speaker: Duke
a16a1261913.text: Well, your hoses are coming from this side, so...You got to get to that valve behind you. (Pause) There you go.

a16a1261913.speaker: Young
a16a1261913.text: That's the valve I got to get to, it's behind me, Charlie. (Laughs)

a16a1261913.speaker: Duke
a16a1261913.text: Okay, "PLSS Mode (AR)"...Houston, how do you read? Over.

a16a1261913.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1261913.text: And if you'll give us Accept, we'll up-link a state vector.

a16a1261913.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1261913.text: Okay, you've got her.

a16a1261913.speaker: Young
a16a1261913.text: Turn sideways, Charlie, and let me get you some oxygen.

a16a1261913.speaker: Duke
a16a1261913.text: We are still in Down-Voice Backup, (so) we should be hot miked.

a16a1261913.speaker: Young
a16a1261913.text: That's what I figured. [Jones - "You were in down-voice backup because of the lack of steerable (antenna) and that wasn't push-to-talk. Is that right?"] [Duke - "Right.
