a16a1475539.text: Shh. (Conspiratorially) We're sneaking up on it, Tony. (Pause) Ah! Got him! Let me see, John.

a16a1475539.speaker: Young
a16a1475539.text: You can't see, Charlie, that's... [John doesn't want to point the open sample pad toward Charlie.]

a16a1475539.speaker: Duke
a16a1475539.text: From way out here, just point it at me.

a16a1475539.speaker: Young
a16a1475539.text: Oh.

a16a1475539.speaker: Duke
a16a1475539.text: You don't have any (garbled) (Pause) [Fendell finds John and Charlie southwest of the Rover and a few meters north of the meter-sized rock John snuck up on. As shown in Figure 3 in Judy Allton's Tool Book , there is only a small amount of soil on the pad, all of it along the right edge.]

a16a1475539.speaker: Duke
a16a1475539.text: Okay; here's the other one. Give me that one, I'll...(Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 9 min 41 sec )

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Gee! The first lunar Great Rock Hunt and we missed it. [Fendell zooms in. John is trying to remove the Beta-cloth sampler, which he has undoubtedly closed already. Charlie plants the scoop and moves in to help.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Can you still see Lassell?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Tell you something else. I leaned on the rock (laughing), and (I know) we can turn this one over (because it moved).

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Say again, Hank.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Can you still see Lassell?

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: We can. (Pause) [Charlie takes the sampler in his right hand and holds it steady while John frees the handle. Charlie then gives John the second sampling head, the one with the velvet pad.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Just barely, yeah.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Okay. I'm just curious why we don't see that little dark feature that's been reported there near the bright one - up to the west of Lassell C.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Did that (rock movement) disturb the surface on the other side there?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: The picture will show how I disturbed it.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Oh, you do, Hank. I didn't mean to say you didn't see it. I said it doesn't look like what we saw before - what we thought we saw. It's a smooth sided thing. Let me get the binocs on it.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay. It's important that you put this second one down in an area that wasn't...

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: No, we didn't disturb it at all.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, good.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Yeah, we know that. 148:02:11 England: Okay. (Pause) [Charlie helps John free the Velcro strap that is holding the sampler head closed. John turns to face the rock and Charlie backs off to the left.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: There you go. Get it?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Yeah. (To Tony) In an area that that (first sampler) didn't go in, right?

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Right.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Tony, John...(Demonstrating) John was sneaking just like this. He really got up to it before it...It didn't even know he was coming. [Charlie plants the left foot, picks up the trailing foot, brings it forward, well clear of the ground, by rotating his body to the left, and plants his right foot a foot or so in front of the left, and so on. It is a very deliberate, slow walk.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Smooth-sided, but through the binoculars, it doesn't look at all like a cone. It looks like a little dome with one side of it broken out. And there are several other little domes out here now that I hadn't seen before.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Outstanding, Charlie. Thanks for the rerun. [Although John has his back to us, it is apparent that he has been having trouble getting the sampler ready.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Ah!

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Man, that thing flops open. [John is finally ready and approaches the rock carefully, although not with quite the exaggerated motion Charlie demonstrated. Charlie goes around to the east side of the rock to watch. This suggests that PLSS exhaust is not a major concern.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay, John, I'll give you a hint. Man, that's a great sneak. Okay; that's good. Right there. [John leans to his right as he reaches over the rock and tries to lower the pad vertically toward the surface on the far side.]

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Just a little pressure. (Pause) [John stands and swings the sampler head up to his right and rests the bottom part of the handle on his left hand.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: When you say side broken out, do you mean like a - a - a - fractured-out piece, or did it look more like a crater?

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Beautiful! You picked some up on that one. [Charlie now has a view of the pad.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Only on one corner. He got some on one corner, Houston. [Figure 3 from Judy Allton's Tool Book shows the Beta-cloth pad, which has lunar soil along the right edge. Figure 4 shows the velvet pad, which has soil adhering to a relatively large patch at the lower right. Journal Contributor Simon Atkinson notes that the two imprints John will make with the sampler can be seen in photos AS16-107- 17561 and 17562 that John takes at 148:07:43. An enhanced detail of 17561 gives us a view into the shadow. A comparison of the faint marks left by the sampling pads with the post-flight photos of the pads s

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, we'll have to take it that way.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Well, through the - to the visual - just to your eyeball, it looks like a - I'll have to catch that again later, but it looked, to the eyeball, like it had a little crater in it. When I got the binoculars on it, it looked like there was just a section of it that was broken out.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: That's too bad. That's the way the ground is. [John is saying that he wasn't able to find a smooth, level surface on the south side of the rock.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: (Responding to Tony) Okay.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Right. Man, you fellas have outstanding finesse.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: I'd say about 20 percent of it's covered.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Twenty percent is pretty good. That's fine.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: I think 20 percent...(Stops to listen) Okay, 20 percent of one corner is covered. I mean, 20 percent of the whole thing is covered. [After John gets the sampler closed, he turns to his left to face Charlie, who steps in to help. Charlie grabs the sampler head and John removes the handle without difficulty.] 148:03:34 Duke: (To John) These go in your rock bags, don't they? I mean in the SCBs? Yeah.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Any evidence of where it went?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: I don't know. Let me take them back and put them under the seat. I don't know where they go. [Charlie steps to his right so he can open John's SCB. Before opening it, he makes sure the sampler head is securely closed.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: No, sir. That's a loaded question.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: I think they go in the SCBs. Tony, do these go in the SCBs?

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: They'll go in the SCB that doesn't go in the SRC (meaning the Sample Return Container, or rock box, which is on the MESA at the LM). [Charlie tries to open John's SCB.] Video Clip ( 3 min 24 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPEG )

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Roger (laughter).

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Next thing you're going to want to know how it came to be there.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Yeah, okay. We've already got that one collected. (Pause) [As per LMP-21 , the SCB which is currently on the Hand Tool Carrier at the back of the Rover is the one that is supposed to go in the SRC. Charlie is saying that that SCB is already full of samples.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Do the other - Are the other domes similar in appearance to that one?

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay, John, that was beautiful. [Charlie is having trouble getting the SCB open.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Guess what.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Yeah. They're not as large, and I hadn't seen those before just now. They're right in the corner of the window, as usual. It's going to take a little work to find them.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: What?

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: (I can't get the) top open, again. (Pause) [Charlie finally gets John's SCB open, stows the samplers, closes the SCB, and then hops around John to get the scoop. He is going to collect a skim sample on the southeast side of the rock.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay, now we got to go get...After (sample) two, place the gnomon. I'll put the shovel. We got a cross-Sun 'after', and a down-Sun and a locator. [Charlie tries to position the scoop so he can plant it next to the east side of the rock to serve as a gnomon. It takes him a few seconds to get a position he likes and, during that time, it isn't obvious to John what he is doing.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Are they all complete, or do they have pieces missing also?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Well, that's going to be hard to get. Don't put the dirt all over there!

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: I didn't! I missed it.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay. It's going to be hard to get because...(Pause) I need to... [Charlie gets the scoop planted and backs up to get the down-Sun.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Hank, I just saw them at the time I mentioned them. And best I could tell, they are complete.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: You can get a cross-Sun from over on this side. [Charlie waves toward the south side of the boulder.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Okay.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: But I'll have to take another look. You know, I could have been - I could have got caught with a crater that inverted on me too. I am going to have to look carefully to make sure I didn't do that.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: We don't have to sneak anymore. [John runs south between Charlie and the rock, carrying the UHT. Charlie turns to his right to get some light on his camera settings.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: We don't need a UHT anymore, do we, Houston? Are we going to need it for the ALSEP?

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Negative. [Evidently, the sampler handle is one of the ALSEP Universal Handling Tools (UHT).]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: We got one back there.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: You got one back there? 148:05:02 Duke: Yeah, it's sitting in the heat flow. See how far you can throw that beauty. [John was facing the rock and, with the UHT in his right hand, rapidly turns to his left and releases it. It sails out of the field-of-view to the left.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: And, Ken, we're about 15 seconds from T-stop.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Look at that!

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Clean across the crater!! [There is a sizable crater in the middle distance.] 148:05:13 Duke: Beautiful. Okay, I'll go get the down-Sun. There we go. [Charlie's down-Sun "after" is AS16-108- 17740 .]

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Well, at least in the vacuum, it doesn't boomerang. [When John released the UHT, it started rotating rapidly around it's midpoint and Tony's reference is to the behavior of Australian boomerangs which, of course, depend on airflow over their curved bodies to achieve curved flight.] 148:05:20 Duke: (I'll) run around and get a locator. (Long Pause) [While John takes a cross-Sun stereopair from the south, AS16-107- 17558 and 17559 , Charlie runs around behind him and takes a locator, AS16-108- 17741 .]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Standby.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Ah, ha. [Charlie is probably pleased that he got John in the picture.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay, Houston; I'm looking back at the LM. Charlie, you can get a picture of the...I can get a picture if I put it on f/whatchacallit, and it'll show that rock is between us and the LM. [John has backed up about two meters and leans back to raise his camera for AS16-107- 17560 . The LM may be the object just above and to the left of the flat-topped boulder which is on the near horizon above and slightly to the left of the scoop handle.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Sure is.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Hey, good show!

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: You can barely see the LM over there. (Pause) 148:06:03 Young: That fills that square. [John thinks they are finished with the soil sampling.] [Jones - "Can you tell me where the phrase 'that fills that square' comes from?"] [Duke - "Well, in the military, you have a set of requirements you've got to do to, like, stay current in an airplane. a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: How about if I go ahead and put the gamma ray out?

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Yeah, well, wait a minute, we got to get a skim (sample). Okay. [Charlie gets the scoop.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Roger. Go ahead, and the lens is stowed.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Okay. And the Power is coming Off the Pan Camera -

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Can we skim where the pristine sample (that is, the pad sample) was?

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Mark. The Gamma Ray Boom is on its way out with a barber pole. And I guess you'd like to have the Shield Off. While I'm about it, I'll do that. And I'm ready to copy your PADs, or whatever things you said you had there.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, we'd like to skim next to it. [Charlie backs away from the rock to the south a meter or two and then hops sideways to his left around to the west side of the rock.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: No, they want it right beside it, right there ...

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: You can't see any of that, there. [Charlie is getting the sample in the shadow of the rock and John is pointing out that the area won't show up well in the photographs.] 148:06:24 Duke: Yeah, I can see. Okay, here we go. Get me a bag ready.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [John gets a bag ready while Charlie raises the skim sample and starts pouring it in.] [In Houston, Flight is told that Charlie, in particular, isn't using his cooling water and oxygen nearly as fast as during EVA-1 and that a 7-hour 35 EVA can be done comfortably.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Tony, I probably got 5 millimeters (depth) on that skim.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: And, Ken, could you get the mass spec on for us all?

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, that's pretty good.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: That's a pretty good little skim there. What setting should I open this up to show you these (sampler) prints we got in the vacuum here? (Correcting himself) I mean in the shadow?

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: It's on.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Roger.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, I'll get you a number on that. Why don't you go ahead...

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: (Lost under Tony)

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: ...and get the deep sample.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay. I can hardly see in there, again. Okay, I'm going to widen...

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: That's going into bag 376? Did you give them that?

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Yeah. No, I didn't.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Okay, the first change is at 1...

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay, I got to widen this area.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Did we lose an element?

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, 376.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Negative. That was a Flight Plan change we were just getting to. We want to look at it for a rev off, and then we're going to bring it back on.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay, (I'll) get a scoop.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Okay, (laughter) that was the one that we had agreed was a - was a "Don't waste time call." I thought maybe you just watched an element burn out.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: And, John, (f/)5.6 at a 250th. (Pause) [John takes a stereopair from the south, AS16-107- 17561 and 17562 , stepping to his right between frames. Enhanced details of 17561 and 17562 give us views into the shadow.] Video Clip ( 2 min 47 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Negative. I guess I should have warned you before I hollered that. The first change after that comes at 149:39.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: (To Tony) Okay. I'll get you a little flightline of that. [John steps farther to his right and takes a third picture of the area, AS16-107- 17563 . Each pair of successive frames forms a stereopair.] [Next, John gets a bag ready while Charlie gets and raises the sample.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay, and Charlie's scoop is being taken right under the (skim sample as shown on CDR-16 )...(Pause) [John is having trouble getting a bag loose. Note that John still has the skim sample bag in his left hand.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Go ahead.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: Okay. After "Pan Camera - standby (T-stop)," add "Gamma Ray, Deploy; Pan Camera, off (MSFN cue)." And I don't know whether you can squeeze it in 06 there or not, but, we also want to add, "Mass Spec Discriminator, High." Up.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: You got it. (Long Pause) [Charlie pours the deep sample.] [Jones - "It looks like you had to shake the scoop to get the soil to go into the bag. Did it tend to stick?"] [Duke - "Sometimes; yeah. Well, if you'll notice there, that angle where I had it, it wasn't enough gravity to pull it out; so you had shake it. Normally, if you could turn it over (demonstrating by raising an imaginary scoop past vertical) like that, it would all fall out, because there was nothing to cause it to stick; but (there was) surface tension between the soils and the shovel, even though it was polished aluminum. Ther

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay, there you go.

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: That's going in bag 377, Houston. [Charlie presents his SCB and, after sealing bag 377, John stows both 376 and 377.]

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, 377. And you've got about 10 minutes now, and we'd like to get that CSVC (Core Sample Vacuum Container).

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Okay, Tony. We can turn this rock over. If you want us to get that sample in, we need an (time) extension.

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Okay. I got "Gamma Ray, Deploy" after "Pan Camera to standby" at 149:38. And I'll get the "Pan Camera, off" until you tell me or when you tell me. I'll take the "Mass Spec Discriminator to High."

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay, we understand. We'll work on that.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Yeah, I'll go get the CSVC then. [In Houston, Jim Lovell, the Backroom spokesman, tells Flight that they want the CSVC next.]

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: All right. (Pause) We'll go ahead and do the CSVC. 148:09:03 Duke: John, you want to start sampling while I do that? (Listens to Tony) Okay, I'm going. [While Charlie heads for the Rover, John takes a stereopair of the rock from the south, AS16-107- 17564 and 17565 . David Harland has assembled a mosaic consisting of frames 17560, 17564, and 17573. The first two are post-sneak pictures of the rock showing John's footprints and the sampler imprints, and the last shows the boulder after John tips it over.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: That's affirmative. And in the little MSFN update block there, cancel - delete the photo PAD - PC photo PAD, the LTV photo PAD, and the manoeuvre PAD. And change the "TEI-53" to TEI-54."

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Well, I can get...(Long Pause) [John takes a stereopair from the northeast, AS16-107- 17566 and 17567 .]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Okay.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: All righty. At 149:45, "Mass Spec Discriminator to Low." Down.

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: John, can you turn that over by yourself?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Yeah, I was going to give it a go. [John reaches down and gets the hammer out of his shin pocket .]

a16a1480128.speaker: England
a16a1480128.text: Okay. Sounds like (it's) worth trying. (Long Pause) [John takes a position south of the rock and hits the rock at least ten times. While he does so, Fendell zooms in on a rock in background that is sitting on top of nearby ridge.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Okay. "Mass Spec Discriminator, Low" at 149:45.

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1480128.text: On the next page, at 150 hours, change the "SIM Exp Status" code to "(plus 1211) (02222)."

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Ah! Come back here, you rascal. (Pause) [We see the top of John's PLSS as he crosses from left to right, presumably in pursuit of a fragment he chipped off the rock.] [In Houston, Flight tells Fendell that he wants to watch John turn over the rock. Fendell pulls back on the zoom.]

a16a1480128.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1480128.text: Hey. Hey, Hank? What do you want? You're - you're getting into areas where we get AOS next time. How about letting me go ahead and work on this sunrise solar corona setup? That's a time-critical guy that if I don't get it just right, I'll miss it.

a16a1480128.speaker: Duke
a16a1480128.text: Getting a sample off of it, John?

a16a1480128.speaker: Young
a16a1480128.text: Yeah. 148:10:15 Duke: Good. (Long Pause) [John drops to his right knee and grabs the fragment. He nearly loses his balance as he gets up. He grunts with the effort and, then, as he walks forward, the pack of sample bags falls off his camera.] Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

a16a1480128.speaker: Hartsfield

a16a1481956.speaker: England

a16a1490704.text: Yeah. Until it gets back to Houston. [Fendell zooms in on the drill and the drill-stem rack and, then, without pulling back on the zoom, pans right.]

a16a1490704.text: There's the 0.2 (tip on the penetrometer).

a16a1490704.text: Okay. [Charlie crosses the TV field-of-view from right to left to do a penetrometer measurement with the 0.2 tip.] [With the keeper in the upper section rammed into position, John has now disassembled the double core by unscrewing the two sections.]

[As can be seen in AS16-107- 17446 , the LPM is at the back of the Rover on the top right corner of the tool pallet. a16a1490704.text: Boy, I sure don't.

a16a1490704.text: Okay. Right by the LSM, by the LPM, there's a screw on (top end closure that's) just like on the top part.

a16a1490704.text: [Garble] DAC's [garble] here.

a16a1490704.text: Yeah.

a16a1490704.speaker: Duke
a16a1490704.text: Okay. That screws back in the (top of the) bottom part.

a16a1490704.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16a1490704.text: And [garble] Power, On. Okay, put the tone booster back on. And we'll check it. [Tone] Oh, there's my [garble] for the night.

a16a1490704.text: Okay, Tony. Here come the two tenths (measurement).

a16a1490704.speaker: Duke
a16a1490704.text: Okay, Tony. Be advised I'm sorry that I'm spiking this thing out occasionally (by using a number of discrete pushes), but this is the only way we can do it.

a16a1490704.speaker: England
a16a1490704.text: That's fine, Charlie. We see the problem. [Charlie hops sideways toward the drill holes.]

a16a1490704.speaker: Duke
a16a1490704.text: Okay, I'm moving. I've got two more to do, cycling to (drum position) 12. And this is about a fourth of the way (from the Rover to the deep core site). Right here. Okay. (Pause) Okay, number 12. [Charlie positions the penetrometer, puts both hands on the top and, with the first push, gets it more than a half meter. The approximate locations of his penetrometer tests are shown in Figure 6-13 in the Preliminary Science Report and are labeled "Pen 1", "Pen 2", and so on.]

a16a1490704.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16a1490704.text: Sure would like to have that little Hasselblad. That's a nice camera. Had a real one that you could keep as your own. I like that electric feature.

a16a1490704.speaker: England
a16a1490704.text: And, John, we should wait on your pan until Charlie's through there.

a16a1490704.speaker: Young
a16a1490704.text: Understand. [Charlie pushes three more times, making some progress with the first two, and then stands.]

a16a1490704.text: Agh! Okay. That's about the same distance, Tony.

a16a1490704.text: Okay. [Charlie pulls the penetrometer out of the ground.] Video Clip ( 3 min 7 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG )

a16a1490704.text: (Passing on a request from Lovell in the Backroom) Hey, John. While you're sampling...

a16a1490704.text: Okay.

His rotation stops and he falls back onto his hands. Once his hands are on the ground, he lets himself rotate forward until his feet are off the ground. He then kicks his feet up, as they fall, he pushes up with his hands. His

a16a1490704.speaker: England
a16a1490704.text: Okay.

a16a1490704.speaker: Duke

a16a1490704.text: Okay. And, John, stand by for a feedwater tone.

a16a1490704.text: How's that (for a timely call)?

a16a1490704.speaker: England
a16a1490704.text: And go on Aux water. [Charlie pulls the penetrometer out of the ground, slides the plate to the end of the rod, and adjusts the recording drum.]

a16a1490704.text: Okay. Cycling to...(Stops to listen)

a16a1490704.text: Okay, Charlie. (Long Pause) [Charlie is running toward the deep core site, sometimes loping and sometimes skipping. The choice of stride may depend on local variations in slope. He stops a couple of meters south of the drill.]

a16a1490704.text: And I'm right by the double core. I mean the deep core.

a16a1490704.text: Now, that's interesting [garble]. looked at that once.

a16a1490704.text: Good show.

a16a1490704.text: Bet I can't get up. (Pause) [Charlie leans back until the bottom of his PLSS is touching his heels. He uses his leg muscles to push his torso up and as he rises, kicks his feet forward under his body. On Earth, the maneuver would be very difficult. On the Moon, it is relatively easy and was used on numerous occasions by the Apollo 17 crew.]

a16a1491604.text: Boy, is this fun. (Long Pause) [Charlie is using the loping, foot-to-foot stride.] 149:21:08 Young: Okay; that pan completes me up to frame of 89, Houston.

a16a1491604.text: Okay, the ( LCRU ) Mode switch is going to 1. [Charlie reaches the MESA after a 44-second run. a16a1491604.text: Okay. And, John, when you get inside (means "get seated"), we have a (switch/circuit breaker) configuration change in LRV.

a16a1491604.text: Okay. (Pause) Charlie's already back at the LM.

a16a1492244.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1492244.text: Oh, it doesn't do a thing. There's apparently just a little bit of polarizing done by the windows. And as I rotate the filter, why, it brightens and dims the scene just slightly. And I checked it against different types of material - the darker materials and the lighter things. And they all seemed to respond exactly the same way. I can't see any - I can't see any effects of polarizing from the surface reflection at all.

a16a1492244.speaker: England
a16a1492244.text: Okay. Charlie, we can put four...

a16a1492244.text: Looks like the bearing (indicator) is working okay.

a16a1492244.speaker: England
a16a1492244.text: ...core tubes plus the CSVC in the rock box and then plus what documented samples you can get in there.

a16a1492244.speaker: Duke
a16a1492244.text: Okay; four core tube, CSVC, documented sample, gotcha.

a16a1492244.speaker: England
a16a1492244.text: Rog.

a16a1492244.speaker: Duke
a16a1492244.text: Okay. Looking back towards Stone Mountain, Tony...

a16a1492244.speaker: Young
a16a1492244.text: Charlie, let me park the LM right there.

a16a1492244.speaker: Duke
a16a1492244.text: Okay. The LM is already parked; but you sure can park the Rover.

a16a1492244.speaker: Young
a16a1492244.text: All right. Fair enough.

a16a1492244.speaker: Duke
a16a1492244.text: Okay. Looking back towards Stone Mountain, Tony, I don't see the Rover tracks. [Although there is no mention of looking for Rover tracks on the mountain, this is probably something Charlie was curious about before the mission. The human eye can be a lot better than the Hasselblads in picking out detail at a distance.]

a16a1492244.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1492244.text: I believe I would have expected a difference.

a16a1492244.speaker: England
a16a1492244.text: Okay. That's fine. We're a little bit behind the timeline there, Charlie. I think we better get closed out.

a16a1492244.speaker: Duke
a16a1492244.text: Okay, we're doing that right now, as fast as we can.

a16a1492244.speaker: England
a16a1492244.text: Okay. I understand. [The closeout procedures are listed on cuff checklist pages CDR-21 , CDR-22, CDR-23 , LMP-21 , LMP-22 , and LMP-23 .]

a16a1492244.speaker: Duke
a16a1492244.text: John's back at the...John's at the Rover (means LM). I'm going to put you on ( LCRU Mode switch position) 3 (FM/TV). (Pause)

a16a1492244.text: That time as I went by King, I took a look at a little different approach. I started out with the central peak and I tried to follow it to the worth. And it appeared to me that perhaps those central peak three prongs - I was looking at the crater blocks that are on them. And then I looked at the floor, and there's a lot of crater blocks that are laying on the floor in between the two main tongues of that central fork. The - it appears to me now that maybe there were three of those pieces of central peak that run out instead of two and that perhaps they curve a little bit over to the right. Bec

a16a1492244.text: Okay, 3. LRV powerdown...(Burst of static)...(As per CDR-21 , I have to) reset the Far UV, Charlie. a16a1492244.text: Okay. Video Clip ( 2 min 50 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

a16a1492244.text: Okay.

If you see

a16a1493323.text: No problem.

a16a1493323.speaker: Duke
a16a1493323.text: But you want to...Whatever you want to do. (Pause) Okay, let me pull my visor down. (Long Pause) I can't believe it. Tony, do we look as dirty to y'all as we do to each other? Video Clip ( 3 min 44 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

a16a1494558.text: That's a little bright crater with a ray-excluded zone that's just about south of Mädler. And I'm looking at Mädler now, and that stuff that makes the bright ray material going out the - to the east seems to come up to the rim. You can see it - It's brighter in that area along going down the - inside of the rim. Then there's a bright streak that runs across the central area, right across and up the other side. And then it sort of stops when it gets to the other rim. But there's a faint evidence of a - of another continuation of that streak.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Charlie's going in right now.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: We were just dusting off. We're pretty dusty. Can you hand me the pallet when you jump up (to the first rung), John?

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Yeah. Wait. Okay, I sure will. I got to put this ( dustbrush ) on the LCRU ( stowage bracket ).

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay. [John's feet come into view from the right side of the Rover. In his shadow, we see him re-stow the dustbrush.]

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: From the nominal timeline, you're down about 30 minutes now.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Yeah, well, we'll get in right in a hurry.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay, fine. And as you walk past that MESA, make sure the blankets are down. We are seeing a temperature rise.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: The blankets are down on the MESA.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: They are down.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay. Fine. [John goes around the front of the Rover and goes off-camera to the left. He is going to turn the TV off and the controls are on the left side of the LCRU .]

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: How can you see...I didn't know you had any thermometers down there (in the MESA). [TV off. Comm noise increases]

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: And that's in Mädler?

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: That's in Mädler, yes.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: John, could you...

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: And we would like those Rover readouts before you pull those circuit breakers, John.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: (To Charlie) You want the pallet, right?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Yeah. Tony, the MESA's partially in the Sun, and that's probably the reason.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Ah so.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: In fact, the...(To John as he gets the pallet) Got it.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Make it?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Uh-huh. (Pause) Okay, ol'...

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: If you want, I'll take these smaller (thermal) blankets and put over the top of it, Houston.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: We'd like you to just get on in.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay. (Pause) How you coming, Charlie?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: I'm up on the porch.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay, Houston, you want to Reset the UV camera?

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Yep. We got a setting.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay, it's azimuth, 100; and elevation, 77.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay. Going to Reset. That wheel's moved more than 180?

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: That may look pretty close to the LM, but we'll just take it the way it is.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: It's going to be pointing right at the LM, Houston!

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Elevation is 77. [Charlie's breathing is audible as he crawls into the cabin.]

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: All right. Maybe it'll be over the top of it. (Hears Tony) Okay. Azimuth, 100; elevation, 77.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay, Tony, I'm inside.

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: Okay. In this higher Sun, it sure appears that the - the bright things that run down into - come out of the Descartes bright spot and run north, seem to be centered around - that's Dollond - I guess that's Dollond B or A - whatever that thing is. I tried to trace the boundaries and all this material that's in what we call the furrowed Descartes that runs up and it becomes part of Smoky Mountain. That material looks just exactly like most of that stuff on the back side, except it may be a little bit darker, and I think that's the Sun angle. That whole area has that same characteristic to me.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Standing up, Charlie?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Yeah. And I got about a ton of dirt from somewhere. (Pause)

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: (To Tony) Okay, elevation, 100...(Correcting himself) Azimuth, 100; elevation, 77, set and pointed. It misses the LM okay. That's straight overhead. (Lost under Tony)

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay. Good show. You're looking at the geo-corona.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Oh, the geo-corona. Hopefully. (Long Pause) Charlie, are you standing up?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Yeah, I'm standing up.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: You ready for a rock box?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Uh...Yeah. I'd like to get this pallet (unstowed). You can start on up.

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: Roger.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: And, John, have you closed the circuit breakers on the LRV?

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: You remember that northwest-southeast trending we saw in the vicinity of North Ray that looked like it was some offsets in those grabens? Can you see any of that in there?

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: That's affirmative.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay. Fine. (Pause) [John has forgotten to give Houston the readouts they requested.]

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: What happens to it if you don't pull those breakers? (Does it) run off somewhere? (Long Pause) Okay, Charlie. [The following dialog indicates that, at this point, Charlie tosses something small out through the hatch.]

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: Just a second. I'm not sure about that. But it does appear to me as if the - the floor that the LM has landed on is indeed a different unit that sticks in, and it's more part of this Cayley material that's farther out to the - to the west. And it does go back just about the way we had drawn the boundaries. Say again your question?

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: I just remember on a plotter, we looked at what appeared to be some graben that came across Smoky Mountain and down to the southeast of it and going back up the northwest. And they were all offset like they may have been some faulting in that area.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Uh-uh, Charlie.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: What?

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: You're too near the (UV) camera to be slinging stuff out there.

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: Okay. Well, I'm not sure what that all is, Hank. That same texture that has many patterns and linear lines and they make a kind of a hash, but that same thing appears all over the - the surface when you look at it in detail. I think I can probably take a picture of most any one of these places down here and analyze it in depth and come up with a very similar picture. And especially the things on the back side look exactly like that Descartes area. It's just that Descartes area is a very small place. And you see so much on the back side that covers that same kind of thing.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Oh, I'm sorry. It's just that one little old dinky thing. That's all I was going to do.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay, here comes the (empty) pallet to you.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Got it?

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Yeah.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: I'm going to throw it by the...

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay, babe, you got two SCBs and an ETB to come up. You could probably load the...

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: There the SRC right there, Charlie.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: I know it. Well, you still got two ETBs (means SCBs).

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Two ETBs?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Yeah. I mean one ETB and the...(Pause) The two SCBs.

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: John and Charlie reported - I guess it's just south of - between where the LM landed and - and Stone Mountain - what appeared to be subdued crater that was some 300 meters in diameter and maybe 50 meters deep that didn't show on our map. Were you able - Can you detect something like that?

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Right. 149:54:06 Duke: You might put one SCB on that ETB line. It's real light. (Pause) [From the porch, John will use the lanyard to haul up the ETB.] [Duke - "(I was suggesting that he) just put the SCB on top of the ETB with the handles, I believe, and it would just come on up, I think."] [The following dialog suggests that the next thing John does is to haul up the ETB.]

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: (Passing in the ETB) Okay, here you go, Charlie.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Pass her in. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) I should have unhooked it. I got it. [Apparently, John didn't detach the lanyard before passing in the ETB.]

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: You know, there's so much noise down there, Hank, I can hardly understand you. Would you say again? Sounds like you're trying to shout over a football game.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: You want me to unhook it?

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Well, I got it now.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay, don't lock the hook. Just unhook it.

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: Roger. I'll try again, I guess. John and Charlie reported a very large crater, maybe some 300 meters in diameter, that was between the LM site and Stone Mountain. They were on their way back from Station 8, and this thing wasn't on their maps, but it was very obvious to them as they were driving.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: I'm not. It's alright. (Pause) Okay, there it comes.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Okay, I got the hook.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay, two SCBs and we got it.

a16a1494558.speaker: England
a16a1494558.text: Okay, John...(Correcting himself) Charlie. Sounds good.

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: I'll look and see. I really hadn't taken the time to compare features just one by one.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: John, you're not going to believe the dirt on this floor.

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Yeah, I am. (Long Pause) [John probably goes down the ladder at this point to get the SCBs.]

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: Ken, could you give us a barber pole on Image Motion?

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: Okay, barber pole on the IMC.

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: That's one I - slipped by...

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: There it is.

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: ...me when I got to talking.

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: I'm sorry. Say again?

a16a1494558.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1494558.text: I let that one slip by me when I got to talking to you about the landing site.

a16a1494558.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1494558.text: Uh-oh. I think you'd go a long ways before you get very far behind.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: What are you doing?

a16a1494558.speaker: Young
a16a1494558.text: Oh, I'm trying to set something up here.

a16a1494558.speaker: Duke
a16a1494558.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [John may be adjusting the lanyard or, quite simply, he may be dawdling to make sure he and Charlie surpass the Apollo 15 EVA record.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 2 min 15 sec )

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Did you throw something out of there?

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: No.

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: You didn't?

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: No. (Burst of static; Long Pause) (Deadpan) Maybe we've got visitors. (Long Pause) [John brings up the first of the SCBs and tries to put it into the cabin far enough that Charlie can bend down and grab it.]

a16a1495638.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1495638.text: Casper, Houston.

a16a1495638.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1495638.text: Go ahead, Hank.

a16a1495638.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1495638.text: Roger. So far, we haven't seen anything - a smear [?] or anything requesting that urine dump by itself. So that thing is still in question. Your next urine dump would be scheduled for 20 hours from now. But it's also scheduled in conjunction with a water dump, et cetera. So I don't know where that thing stands. We're gonna check into it.

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: I got it.

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Got it?

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: Yeah.

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Okay.

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: Yeah. How do you read, Houston?

a16a1495638.speaker: England
a16a1495638.text: We're copying you, Charlie.

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: Okay. I just heard a little squeal back there (and) I was curious.

a16a1495638.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1495638.text: Okay. It'll probably take me another 20 hours to make it worthwhile.

a16a1495638.speaker: England
a16a1495638.text: All right. We had a (site) hand-off.

a16a1495638.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1495638.text: Roger (laughter).

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Ah so. (Pause) [It is currently about 23:52 hours, April 22, 1972, Universal (Greenwich) Time. The Moon is about to set at the Madrid tracking station and, for the next eight hours or so, communications will come through the Goldstone station in California.]

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: These bags come open...The SCBs come open when you don't want them to and you can't get them open when you want them to.

a16a1495638.speaker: England
a16a1495638.text: Okay. We'll call that Charlie's Law.

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: Yeah. (Pause) [This is a reference to Murphy's Law - "If any thing can go wrong, it will." and its many corollaries. My favorite is O'Toole's Rule: "Murphy was an optimist."] [John has probably gone down the ladder to get the second SCB and is now passing it in.]

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: (Grunting) Okay, John, I can't get it...Can you slide it.

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: You okay?

a16a1495638.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1495638.text: Golly.

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Yeah. I'm fine. I'm just having a problem with...

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: I got it.

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Got it?

a16a1495638.speaker: Duke
a16a1495638.text: Okay, now let me get behind the hatch.

a16a1495638.speaker: Young
a16a1495638.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Charlie is standing on John's side of the cabin and now must close the hatch, move over to his side, and then re-open the hatch so John can get in.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 13 sec )

a16a1495850.speaker: England
a16a1495850.text: Charlie, what's John doing right now?

a16a1495850.speaker: Young
a16a1495850.text: Sitting (more likely kneeling) on the porch waiting for Charlie to move out of the way.

a16a1495850.speaker: England
a16a1495850.text: Okay. MP3 Audio Clip ( 2 min 14 sec )

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay. Come on, John. Here we go. (Long Pause) Okay, you've got to come right, John. You reading me okay?

a16a1495905.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1495905.text: Okay, Hank. I got a better visual on that little thing we called a cone, and I guess it looks like it is a crater in the top of it. And from where I am, it looks like the southern end of it, which is away from me, probably has just about reached down level with the mare floor. The rest of it is just a smooth cone that sticks up. It does have some small craters on it. The rim looks relatively sharp, and there's a couple of fractures go through it. Its texture and albedo do not look significantly different than the mare around it. There is a little expression of perhaps a subtle depression aroun

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Yeah.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Okay, I'm in the house.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay; (reading LMP-23 ) "close hatch and repress".

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: That ain't what you do now. [John has remembered that, as per Surface 5-1, they have to turn off their PLSS feedwater before they close the hatch.]

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Yeah, it is. Look it...Can you get back...Your legs...There we go. Okay. PLSS...Okay, wait a minute.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: (Garbled) are open, Charlie.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Yeah. Okay, we shouldn't have closed that hatch all the way. We've got our water still on.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: That's what I said.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: I'm sorry.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Just a second and I'll get it. (Pause) There we go.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. I'll turn your water off.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Well, I can't reach it. Oh, there you go. You were caught on the...

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: On that thing.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Yeah, on that bracket. Okay, there you go.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Okay.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay.

a16a1495905.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1495905.text: Hey, that does sound more like a little vein or a cone to me.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Turn sideways?

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, go ahead. (Pause) [Charlie's feedwater controls are on the lower right corner and he is turning to face aft so John can reach them.]

a16a1495905.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1495905.text: Well, it just looks so much like all the rest of the things around here, Hank. The texture of the surface looks like it is all the same. The flanks of it are fairly steep though. And it's got one of the sharper rims for a raised rim crater of any that I've seen.

a16a1495905.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1495905.text: This is Apollo Control at 150 hours, 25 minutes. The Lunar Module cabin pressure is back now to about its normal level of around 5 pounds per square inch. During the next hour and half Duke and Young will be getting things clean up, stowed in the cabin, getting out of their suits and that will be followed by a debriefing on the EVA. We'll then allow them about 30 to 45 minutes to eat. They'll recharge the potable life support systems in preparation for the 3rd EVA tomorrow. And get ready for an 8 hour rest period which is scheduled to begin at about 154 hours 30 minutes. During the 2nd EVA whi

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: Okay, your water is off.

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay. Read the next step. Close hatch, I think.

a16a1495905.speaker: Young
a16a1495905.text: "Close hatch and lock."

a16a1495905.speaker: Duke
a16a1495905.text: Okay.

a16a1500124.speaker: Duke
a16a1500124.text: Okay, I think the Cabin Repress is next. Okay, and let me read the next step.

a16a1500124.speaker: Young
a16a1500124.text: It's locked. [They are now 7 hours 22 minutes into the EVA and, even though the EVA won't end until the cabin pressure gets to 3.5 psi, they have already broken the Apollo 15 record.] Geology Station 10 Apollo 16 Journal Post-EVA-2 Activities

a16a1500124.speaker: Young
a16a1500124.text: Okay. I believe I've got a water flag.

a16a1500124.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500124.text: And as we come over here - we're coming up on the Fra Mauro, Bonpland, and Parry combination, and I think that's - that's Parry that has - looks like two - almost right-angle rilles running through it.

a16a1500124.speaker: Young
a16a1500124.text: It's probably because we turned the water off.

a16a1500124.speaker: Duke
a16a1500124.text: Yeah. Okay, go ahead. [The PLSS warning system is telling them that there is no feedwater flow into the sublimator, a confirmation that the warning system is working.]

a16a1500124.speaker: Young
a16a1500124.text: "Circuit breaker (panel) 16: Cabin Repress to close." MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 17 sec )

a16a1500155.speaker: Duke
a16a1500155.text: Coming closed. Mark. [The sound of repressurization becomes audible.] [Jones - "What did the cabin do when you repressurized it? It was a pretty lightweight vehicle. Did it pop and flex?"] [Duke - "No, you didn't hear anything. The only thing you could tell was the gauges. You know you could hear it - pssssss, you know the oxygen going in - and you just watched the cabin pressure gauge and it started climbing."] [Jones - "And the walls didn't do anything."] [Duke - "Well, I'm sure they did. I mean, they popped and they got firm and there was probably some seating of the hatch, you know, and th

a16a1500155.speaker: Young
a16a1500155.text: "Master Alarm (and Cabin) Warning light on. Verify cabin pressure increasing."

a16a1500155.speaker: Duke
a16a1500155.text: Okay. I've got a water flag, too.

a16a1500155.speaker: Young
a16a1500155.text: I've got a water flag and an O flag. Cabin press is up to 1.

a16a1500155.speaker: Duke
a16a1500155.text: Houston, we're repressing. MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 08 sec )

a16a1500212.speaker: Young
a16a1500212.text: Verify Press(ure) Regulators A and B coming to Cabin, Charlie.

a16a1500212.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500212.text: I'm looking at Rima Parry. I don't remember the number. It's the western one that runs out of Fra Mauro. And it seems like it is more than just my imagination that says that the floor of that stuff is indeed smoother than the - has fewer large craters than you see in the surrounding areas, although it's pretty close to being equal in small craters.

a16a1500212.speaker: Duke
a16a1500212.text: Coming to Cabin. MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 33 sec )

a16a1500212.text: I think yours is off. Let me try it again. MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 19 sec ) [The Public Affairs commentator announces an EVA duration of 7 hours 23 minutes 26 seconds.]

a16a1500250.speaker: Young
a16a1500250.text: Okay, "Cabin warning light off. Verify cabin pressure stable at 4.6 to 5."

a16a1500250.speaker: Duke
a16a1500250.text: It's there. Yeah, it is. It's there. MP3 Audio Clip ( 10 min 31 sec )

a16a1500313.text: Isn't that amazing?

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: That's something else. (Lost under Tony)

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: Okay. You guys had a 7-hour 23-minute EVA.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Beautiful.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: That's super! That's a lot of fun. Let's go back out.

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: (Hearty Laugh) Tomorrow, Charlie, tomorrow.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: I mean it. I feel great.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: (To John) PLSS O2 Off?

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: PLSS O2 off and...Okay, "Cabin warning light on. Verify cabin pressure stable at 4.6 to 5. Use purge valve to depress PGA as req'd (sic)". [John playfully pronounced "req'd" (meaning "required") as "rickered".]

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Mine's already depressed. 150:03:52 Young: Okay, "Post-EVA System configuration, 15 minutes."

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay, "verify the EVA CBs".

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Casper, you're coming up on T-stop.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Yep. [They will now verify that the circuit breakers shown as in white ("white dots") on Surface 1-4 and 1-5 are open and the ones shown as black are closed.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: I got Suit Fan 2 and Suit Fan Delta-P going in (as per the third and fourth lines in the first paragraph in the right-hand column on Surface 5-1).

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Now where do you see that one? Okay, Suit Fan 2 and Suit Fan Delta...

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: That's right after ...

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay, power-saving circuit breakers are out, and the old others are out. [John is confirming that the breakers are still out of the systems that were powered down to save power because of the late landing and extended surface operations.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay, it's Off for 30 seconds.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay?

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Why do those circuit breakers go in and out on you like that?

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: I don't know. (Laughing) Why do we do that every time (we get ready to go out and come back in). [The obvious reason is that, while they are wearing the PLSSs, they can accidentally knock some of the breakers.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay, it says "ECS caution and water SEP lights out". That's true. "Suit Fan Delta-P, close. Doff gloves, stow on comm panel."

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay! (Long Pause) Must admit my finger's a little tired, though. Just a skosh. Could you turn up your A-9 numerics lighting when you get a chance, John? Let's look at the caution panel. Okay. That's good. We're in good shape. (Long Pause) [Jones - "You also had quite a bit of forearm fatigue after that first EVA. How about here?"] [Duke - "Same. (And) my fingers were a little bit sore. They did get sore and (I had) the forearm fatigue, just like the first EVA."]

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay. My gloves are off. You need some help? You got yours, huh?

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Yep. 150:05:56 England: And, John. That OPS latch on Charlie's OPS may be hot to touch since that cover was up.

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay, Mapping Camera's going to Standby. The Image Motion is Off. Barber pole and gray. Laser Altimeter is Off.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Let me see. (Pause) Well...(Pause) Okay. (Pause) Okay; It's cool as a cucumber. (Laughing) Thanks for your thermal-dynamicist's advice.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Mass Spec Ion Source, On?

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: And the Ion Source is On.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: And did I hear you say Image Motion, Off?

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: That's affirmative.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay, I guess...

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: And Alpha X-Ray Cover coming to Closed.

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: So much for a thermal analysis.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Yeah. (Laughing) It's about 72 degrees F on the top of that thing.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: (To John) Okay. Go ahead.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay, I guess that about cleans that up...

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: It's hard working from absolute zero.

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: And it's Closed.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay, "Descent Water's Open. Remove..." We're right here.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Yeah. [They probably removed the helmets while John was joking with Tony.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay, "purge valves..."

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Water's open; "remove purge valves; stow in purse ". (Garbled)

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: I'm not either. (Pause) That (EVA) was fun.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Sure was, Charlie.

a16a1500313.text: Okay, Casper. I have a - a - a block data PAD for you and some Flight Plan changes.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Go.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay.

a16a1500313.text: Okay, "disconnect OPS O2 hose". Turn around and I'll get yours.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay, I got yours. (Garbled) (Long Pause)

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Why don't you start with the Flight Plan changes.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. At 151 hours, and - we want to - let's see, 151...

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Hey, Hank. Hey, Hank. Have you got two loops punched up? Have you got two loops punched up? The noise is getting louder and louder. It sounds like I got - I'm trying to listen to you over a football game. And I can hardly hear you over the din of everything else. I don't know whether you need to hold the mike closer to your mouth, or whether you got another loop punched up and I'm getting cross-feed.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: (To himself) The outboard one, huh?. Okay, yours is loose.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay, "disconnect LM O2 hoses, red to blue and blue to red; PGA (diverter valve), horizontal. Suit Flow; PLSS Pump, Off; and Fan, Off." (Pause) Wrong switch. Okay, that's. We don't...We'll bypass that.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay. [By putting the PLSS diverter valve in the horizontal position, they will get some oxygen flow into the suit torso once they get connected to the ECS .]

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Let's try again, Ken. How do you read now?

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: (Grunting) I go to Suit Flow in the (garbled) [Charlie is probably trying to turn around enough that he can reach the Suit Isolation Valves on the front of the ECS cabinet.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: That sounds a little better.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: We're supposed to have stowed these in there. We missed a step.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. I've told them to hold it down a little, too. At 151 hours, the SIM code should be "Plus 1110, 01222."

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Wait, wait, wait...Oh, yeah, we did. Not that one. We sure do. I was thinking about EVA-3. Okay. (Pause) [A comparison of the procedures on Surface 5-1 with the post-EVA-3 procedures on 7-1 and with the post-jettison procedures on 7-4 does not suggest an explanation for Charlie's statement. Evidently, they have not properly stowed their OPS oxygen hoses. There is no discussion of the skipped step in the Technical Debrief.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Thank you. (Long Pause)

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. That's "Plus 1110, 01222."

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Roger. And right at 151, over to the left of that, write "Configure comm per S-band with VHF bistatic."

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Now that's a real long bunch of switch settings there. Do you want me to read them all off? Or your - I can give you a procedure on page...

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Houston, the lunar dust smells like gunpowder. (Pause)

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Yeah, why don't you give me the page that it was on in the old Flight Plan in Volume 1...

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: We copy that, Charlie.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Page 311, at about 202 hours and 37 minutes, if you want to turn to that.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Really, really a strong odor to it.

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: Yeah, remember on hammering on rocks, fresh rock powder does have a strong odor.

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Let's do that. That'll save copying an awful lot, I think.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: I hope it's not the (LM) oxygen (supply) that has the peculiar odor. But it goes away after a little while but...

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. You want to look at that right now? I got one small change.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Well, you can bet this Moon has been hammered on. That's for sure.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: But it is really a strong smell.

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Well, I almost got it. The old - Oh, wait a minute. You - What page did you give me?

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Boy, I'll tell you. [Jones - "Do you have any idea what you meant by 'Hope it's not the oxygen'?"] [Duke - "Well, it could be an oxygen contamination and, when we repressurized, if it was (ECS) oxygen contamination, the odor could have been in the oxygen and not from the dust. So we were hoping, you know, we didn't have any contaminated oxygen."]

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: Okay, and we need a Cabin Gas Return Valve , Open.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Stand by. (Pause) [As per Surface 4-5, they had put the Cabin Gas Return valve into the Egress position prior to the EVA and hadn't planned to change it until they got to the last paragraph on Surface 5-4. Houston may be trying to clean some of the dust out of the air that is producing the gunpowder smell.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Page 311. It's 202 hours and 40 minutes.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Right now, we're in a Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) Pull-Egress; Cabin Gas Return is Open; and my (Suit) Flow is On and John's is in Disconnect. Do you want us to go to Push-Cabin?

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Ah so. It's the same volume I'm in. We passed the other volume and I went back for that. Okay. All right, 311. You're ahead of me. Okay, I got it.

a16a1500313.speaker: England
a16a1500313.text: That's affirmative. Push-Cabin. [Charlie is asking if he should change to Suit Gas Diverter Valve, too. Prior to the EVA, they put the Suit Gas Diverter valve to Pull-Egress. As indicated in the accompanying ECS schematic , by opening the Cabin Gas Return Valve , Charlie was letting oxygen flow from the cabin into the ECS . To complete the circuit, he needed to open the Suit Gas Diverter Valve to let oxygen flow from the ECS into the Cabin. Had he not opened it, oxygen still would have flowed into the cabin, but by going into the suits and then out the neckrings.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay, this is the only bistatic we gonna do. Start where it says, "Configure comm" and end where it says, "S-Band Antenna, High Gain, Manual, Wide." And the only change in there is that the VHF antenna should be "Left" instead of "Right." We're in a different attitude.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay. You got it. Feels nice and cool. Sorry about that step, John.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Well, it's my fault.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: (Pointing at the Prep & Post Card) Okay, we got this, we got that, (garbled)

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: (Garbled)

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: You're cutting out now. "Disconnect PLSS H2O from PGA; connect LM."

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. I start where it says, "Configure comm for S-band." And I stop where - including, I assume, the high gain settings.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: There you go.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: That sounds like a good deal.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: (Eager to get cooling) Now that's just one step right there.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: The trouble is, yours is back under the rock box right now. (John laughs) There you go. [This statement confirms that Charlie put the rock box on the Ascent Engine cover when John passed it in and hasn't yet moved it out of the way.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Negative. We got different high gain settings...

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: [Garble] VHF antenna left instead of right. Okay. You got different high gains. All right; thank you.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Ah, that was great fun. (Long Pause) Never seen anybody sneak as nice.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. If you'll turn back down to 151, I'll give you that high gain. It's "Pitch, 20 - plus 20; YAW, 209."

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: (Hearty Laugh) [This is a reference to John's sneaking up on a boulder at Station 9 to collect a Contact Soil Sample. See the discussion following 147:57:04 in the Station 9 portion of the transcript.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: I don't think you got anything on that Beta-cloth one. [This is a reference to one of two sampler heads John used in the experiment.] [Jones - "It seems to me that you two had a tremendous amount of fun doing this. And I think most of the crews did. Neil and Buzz, maybe because of the pressure of the moment or their personalities didn't joke and laugh and marvel at it quite so much. From my point of view, it's a little bit of a shame that that was the case on Apollo 11 because a lot of people only watched 11 and never became aware of how much fun it was."] [Duke - "Oh, yeah. It was a lot of fu

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. That's "Pitch, plus 20; Yaw, 209."

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Yeah, I'll tell you. That's a problem you have to face with it (meaning the Contact Soil Sampler). You know you don't set it down very hard.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Roger. And verify the DSE as "Low Bit Rate, Forward, Forward, Command Reset."

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Have you got yours hooked up yet? Your water?

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Yep.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay, I gave us some water (by briefly closing the LCG Pump breaker). [Next, they will get hooked up to LM comm as per Surface 5-2.]

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay. (Reading) "PLSS mode, 0, both; and Audio CB, Open."

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. We'll verify "Low Bit Rate" and recording.

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay, did you get your pump Off (as per the bottom of Surface 5-1)? Your fan and pump.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. And on that same page where it says "CSM...

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: (Garbled) (Long Pause)

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: You want me to verify or do you want me to configure?

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Configure.

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: I say, do you want me to verify that DSE or do you want me to configure?

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Configure, Ken.

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Right under that about 151:02, delete all that - that block about the lunar horizon. In other words, starting with the little block with CSM checklist all through - right on down through "Set Omni D."

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. That's all deleted.

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: At 51:10, "P00." And following that, "Alpha Particle/X-Ray Cover, Open."

a16a1500313.speaker: Duke
a16a1500313.text: Okay. Audio, Close.

a16a1500313.speaker: Young
a16a1500313.text: Okay, Charlie.

a16a1500313.text: Ready for the audio check? (Long Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 2 min 33 sec ) [Note, the times mentioned by the PAO Commentators are 11 minutes 48 seconds later than the corresponding transcript times because of a clock update in Houston at 118:06:31 .]

a16a1500313.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1500313.text: Okay. At 151:10, we go to "P00" and "Alpha/X-Ray Cover, Open."

a16a1500313.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1500313.text: At 151:20, "Verb 49 maneuver to bistatic attitude." And that attitude is "221, 138, 000."

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay. At 151:20, we go "Verb 49 to bistatic; attitude, 221, 138, 000."

a16a1501330.speaker: Duke
a16a1501330.text: Okay. Call them out to me.

a16a1501330.text: All right. Delete the UV photo PAD block. Delete the acquire MSFN and all that stuff there - the lunar horizon, that comment. At 151:30, next page -

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: And write small. "P20, Option 2. Noun 78, plus 270.00, minus 040.63."

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Boy, Hank. That comm is just terrible.

a16a1501330.text: Houston, how do you read? Over.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Okay. We're having trouble in here, Ken. Everybody is yelling and hollering. We'll get them quieted down.

a16a1501330.speaker: England
a16a1501330.text: Five by, Charlie.

a16a1501330.speaker: Duke
a16a1501330.text: Okay. Thank you. Tony England has probably gone to the Backroom to discuss the scheduled EVA debriefing. ]

a16a1501330.text: Okay, repeat. "Noun 78 is plus 270.00, minus 040.63. Noun 79, minus 0.0830, plus 000.50. Noun 34, plus 00.151, plus 0.0034, plus all zips."

a16a1501330.text: Okay. That says at 151:30, we go "P20, option 2. Noun 78 is plus 270.00 and minus 040.63. Noun 79, minus 0.0830, plus 000.50. Noun 34 is 151, 34, 00."
