a16a1501330.text: That's correct, Ken. And as you can probably deduce from the Noun 34, right at 151:34, you should say "Start pitch rate." And the attitude for that is "221, 114 underlined slash 138, 000."

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay. That's - that sounds reasonable. Let me ask you one question about this antenna. I've got a - a little discrepancy between the - the set knobs that I have and the feedback read-outs that I get off the instrument panel. This is on the high gain settings.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Roger.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Can anyone tell me if it matters which I use, and which one I should use if it matters.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Okay, I'll get that answered while I read you the next.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay. Read on.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Okay. Delete the rest of the things on that page.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: And, from - next page, 152 to 152:30, delete all of that.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Next page, 152:30. Delete everything down to where it says "GDC align" at about 152:52.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: And at - back up at 152:41, out to the side there, you can write it - add "P00, discontinue Bistatic Radar. VHF Range, Off; VHF A and B, Off." And then "Return your S-Band Mode Ranging to Ranging."

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay. At 152:40, you go to "P00, discontinue the Bistatic, VHF Range, Off; VHF A and B, Off; S-Band Mode to Ranging."

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Roger. And at 152:53, you'll pick up the nominal Flight Plan again. And at - Go to the top of the next page up there, at 153:00. That experiment status code now should be "Minus all 1s and 01222."

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: At 153:15, delete the "Mass Spec, Ion Source, On." It's already On.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: All right.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: And, Ken, back up at the top - at 153 even, right at the top of the page, "Configure DSE to High Bit Rate, Command Reset."

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay. "Configure DSE, High Bit Rate, Command Reset" at 153 even.

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: And I think that's all of it.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: Okay. I guess the thing that seems to me like it might be missing here is where you're gonna get - Well, you've got me setting my DSE to high bit rate over here at 153. I guess we'll get some of that, won't we? Because we - we've had it running with no dump...

a16a1501330.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1501330.text: Roger. We've been running in low bit rate.

a16a1501330.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1501330.text: ...[garble] side, and I didn't stop the bistatic until after - That's right - low bit rate - but I didn't stop the bistatic until after LOS. So you're gonna get about half of this in low bit rate and about half of it in high. Okay?

a16a1502100.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1502100.text: I - I guess I got it straight.

a16a1502100.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1502100.text: Okay, Ken. I got some more words on that question you had about - where I said verify the DSE with the bistatic. That should be - should be "verify" rather than "configure."

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. Let me see where that is now. Okay, that's at 151. That's "verify."

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Roger. Because you're going to configure it here at LOS. And the word is on the - the high gain angles, believe your meter.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. I'll use the meters.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: And some more on this configure. We're coming up here on LOS. Apparently, it's important that the DSE be configured on a - a time. It depends on when they start to rewind. So for this rev, they want you to configure the DSE at 150:45.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. 150:45 as opposed to 43. All righty.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: Houston, Orion.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Go ahead.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. My initial O2 recharge's complete and I got 95 percent.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Roger; 95, Charlie.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: Ed, how are you doing today?

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Pretty good, Charlie. And it went real great. We're real pleased down here.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: We're happy as a clam. We just had a great time, having fun as well as the work. (Long Pause)

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: And, Ken, I got one more thing for you, a TEI PAD, a block data.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. Stand by while I get my other book.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Young
a16_150_22_07.text: You know, Ed, when we got up on top of that mountain and I'd been driving up it all the way, and I turned around and looked down, I thought, man, you've just nearly bit off more than you can chew here.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. I'm ready to copy.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Trying to cut through. You've got a lot of hash and I couldn't read you very well.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay, Ken. And to let you know what's going on here, we were going to give you a TEI-54 PAD, and they're jockeying around - and - because of the plane change. And the plane change is gonna come about 169 hours. So they're gonna give you a TEI-48 PAD now, and give you a TEI-55 PAD at about 164 hours. So this'll be TEI-48, SPS/G&N; 38620; plus 0.59, plus 1.25; 168 -

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Young
a16_150_22_07.text: Just as well.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: That's his beard sticking in the mike.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Well, maybe you're starting late, but you'll catch up in 3 or 4 months with a beard.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: Don't rub it in. (Pause)

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: Hey, Ed, how about a little news from you. Anything going on down there that's interesting?

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Hank, I - I can't hear you again. How about asking - asking the comm guy downstairs if he can patch it differently or something. It hasn't sounded like this until just the last - oh, I've been noticing it the last couple of revs, but this thing - I can't even understand you.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Is that news you're asking for, Charlie?

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Duke
a16_150_22_07.text: Yes, sir.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mitchell
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. Stand by. We'll see if we can get you something. [Comm Break]

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Ken, how do you read now?

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Well, that little burst was good, Hank.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay, let's try it again. There's been a lot of noise in the room...

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: No, you're getting drowned out again.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okays Ken. We'll try it again...

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Hanks it sounds just like the other loops are -

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Can you read me all right now, Ken?

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: No, I can't, Hank. It's - it's - Unkey your mike a second. Let me tell you what it sounds like. It - it sounds like that we've got the other loop - the other air-to-ground or the Flight Director's loop or something like that that's got a Vox key that comes on, and I don't hear it when you make a short statement. But when you're on for - and hold it down for any length of time, then all this other talking comes on, and it sounds like I can probably hear Tony and I'm not sure who all else. Nothing is very clear. It is exceptionally noisy, and it just sounds like - sounds like trying to hold a co

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okays it - it must be coming from somewhere else, Ken. We've got everybody in the room real quiet now.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Yeah, I - I don't think it's possible (laughter) for all that noise to be coming through from your open mike. That's the reason I wanted to see if Comm Tech could chase it out or something.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. We're about 2 minutes from LOS. I don't guess we're going to be able to get this PAD to you, and we're not going to see you for another rev, about 3 hours.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Young
a16_150_22_07.text: (Garbled) 4 Okay, Houston ... about 92 percent ... 92 ... 92 ... Houston, do you read? Over. [No answer. Long Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip at 150:30 ( 1 min 23 sec ) [Houston has LOS from the Command Module and switches back to the LM audio, starting at 150:31:52, below.]

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. Well, I'm not gonna - I'm not gonna burn TEI-48 in the meantime, anyhow. But I can't - I'm not gonna copy you properly if I can't hear you.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. We'll work on this thing and see if we can't have it better when we get comm here in a rev and a half.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: All right. Thank you very much, Hank.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Do you - do you still have the noise while we're talking now?

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: Yes, sir. It doesn't come on immediately as soon as you start to talk. It - it builds up slowly, like you start to talk and then it takes about 1001, 1002, and then it comes on like a big rush. And it just swells up and after a couple of seconds, you're completely drowned out.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay. It must be in the lines. They're checking now.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: All right. Thank you very much. I appreciate it.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mattingly
a16_150_22_07.text: And I promise we won't go anywhere in the meantime.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: Okay.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Hartsfield
a16_150_22_07.text: And, Ken, if you still read, we think we got your Flight Plan squared away until you go to sleep tonight. There won't be any more major changes.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mission Control
a16_150_22_07.text: This is Apollo Control at 150 hours, 33 minutes. We don't expect to hear a great deal from Young and Duke while they're getting the cabin in order, getting out of their suits. We have about 9 minutes of contact left with Ken Mattingly in the orbiting Command Module Casper. We're going to switch over to that conversation and we'll tape record any comments from the lunar module crew Young and Duke aboard Orion on the lunar surface. And we'll switch over at this time to the live conversations with Ken Mattingly.

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mission Control
a16_150_22_07.text: This is Apollo Control at 150 hours, 42 minutes [150:37 GET]. We have about 5 or 6 seconds before we lose radio contact with Ken Mattingly as he goes around the corner of the Moon on the 39th revolution and we'll be switching back to the circuits with Orion on the lunar surface, although we haven't had a great deal of conversation with that crew in the last 35 or 40 minutes. You heard Ken Mattingly describe a communications problem, apparently on the uplink. We were getting good solid noise free communications from the Command Module but he described a situation that sounded as if there were a

a16_150_22_07.speaker: Mission Control
a16_150_22_07.text: This is Apollo Control Houston at 150 hours, 49 minutes [150:37] Ground Elapsed Time. In the Mission Control Center Houston we've just had a change of shift, with Gene Kranz taking over as Flight Director and his White Team of flight controllers coming aboard at this time. Meanwhile aboard Orion, the crew of Apollo 16, astronauts John Young, Ken Mattingly apparently [sic - means Charlie Duke] in the process of performing their stowage duties aboard the spacecraft and doffing their spacesuits. We'll keep the line up and continue to monitor. We're at 150 hours 50 minutes [150:38] Ground Elapsed

a16a1503000.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503000.text: Okay. We're running down some news reports for you right now. And we're not pushing, John, but we would like to stay fairly close to timeline so you can get plenty of sleep tonight. You're going to have a hard day tomorrow.

a16a1503000.speaker: Young
a16a1503000.text: Wait a minute, they said we had 2 hours extra tonight where we could just sit around and talk to each other. [This is another reference to the two hours Houston said, at 128:18:33 , would be added to the timeline prior to the start of the upcoming rest period.]

a16a1503000.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503000.text: Okay, the boss (meaning the Flight Director Gene Kranz, who is just coming on duty with his White Team) just said he wasn't really sure he wanted to do all that talking tonight. MP3 Audio Clip ( 5 min 36 sec )

a16a1503152.speaker: Young
a16a1503152.text: Neither do we. We were going to use it to sleep with. Or at least take it easy on fixing things up. [John is saying that he would prefer to use the extra two hours to go through the remaining procedures at a leisurely pace.]

a16a1503152.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503152.text: John, I'm sorry; you're in the hash again. I missed that last.

a16a1503152.speaker: Duke
a16a1503152.text: He said we're gonna use it for sleeping, Ed.

a16a1503152.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503152.text: Great. Just what we wanted. [Comm Break] [In the following transmission, Charlie reports the OPS tank pressures as per the last paragraph on Surface 5-2.]

a16a1503152.speaker: Duke
a16a1503152.text: Okay, Ed; my OPS source pressure is 6100 (psi) and John's is 5900. Over.

a16a1503152.speaker: Young
a16a1503152.text: Houston, we've finished the initial PLSS recharge. Charlie had 95 (percent) and I had 92. Over.

a16a1503152.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503152.text: Roger, John. Say again your percentage.

a16a1503152.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503152.text: We copy, John. [Long Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip at 150:37 ( 0 min 53 sec ) [Note, the times mentioned by the PAO Commentators are 11 minutes 48 seconds later than the corresponding transcript times because of a clock update in Houston at 118:06:31 . A change-of-shift is underway with Gene Kranz and the White Team taking over.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 9 min 03 sec ) (This clip starts with a 4 minute 42 second interval with no comm.)

a16a1503810.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503810.text: Well, if you're in a position to where you want to listen, I've got a little sports news for you. If you'd like to hold off, let me know when (you'd like to hear the news).

a16a1503810.speaker: Duke
a16a1503810.text: Oh, go ahead. We'll listen, Ed. We're just changing out the batteries and stuff for the PLSS (as per Surface 5-3).

a16a1503810.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503810.text: Okay. Right now, we've got New York (Knicks professional basketball team) won 3 to 1 over the (Boston) Celtics in their series. The (Los Angeles) Lakers have finished up theirs, 4 to 2 over Milwaukee (Bucks). And are standing by to see the outcome of the rest of the New York and Celtics games. And the (Houston) Astros (professional baseball team) have finished up 4 in a row today.

a16a1503810.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503810.text: Now that wasn't a kind question. Won, of course.

a16a1503810.speaker: Young
a16a1503810.text: There goes Charlie's tickets. [Duke - "(Laughing) We used to get free tickets to the Astros. They wouldn't be very pleased when I said 'lost'."]

a16a1503810.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1503810.text: We'll run some more news down here before long. (Pause) And when you get your battery management (which is the last paragraph on 5-3), I'll give you the new procedure, Charlie; just give me a call.

a16a1503810.speaker: Duke
a16a1503810.text: Okay; stand by. MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 35 sec ) [Very Long Comm Break] [At about 150:57, PAO takes down the live feed and records LM comm for later playback.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 20 sec ) (The recorded comm mentioned in this clip is contained in the following clip.) MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 39 sec )

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Orion; Houston. Would you give us a clue as to where you are in the checklist?

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay, we just finished changing out my LiOH and we're stowing the PLSS O2 and the OPS is removed.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Charlie's report indicates that they have completed their work on John's PLSS and are about halfway through the procedures, shown in the left-hand column of Surface 5-3, for Charlie's PLSS.]

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Houston, Orion.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Go ahead. 150:59:30 Duke: Okay, Ed, we had one small...(In) looking over the gear here, we had one small casualty. John's OPS antenna has about 2 inches broken off the top of it. That's the only thing we can see wrong with the gear. Over.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: How much, Charlie?

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: About 2 inches. And I checked the comm when I noticed it. When he came in, I checked the comm and he was still sounding the same to me.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay, he sounds good to us. Do you happen to know when it occurred? Or when you first saw it?

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Well, I think it was during the ingress. We got behind and y'all reminded us of it once (at 149:47:03 ), but we were still working and we didn't do it at that point. When we started dusting, Tony said get on in, and so we forgot it. I got in and then when I saw John coming up the ladder, it was gone then.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay, so we're missing a couple inches of antenna. Understand. (Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay, Ed, we're ready for the battery management (as per the right-hand column of 5-3).

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay, Charlie, I'll give you the overall plan here to put the Lunar Batt on the LMP Bus, take Batts 1 and 2, Off, and Batts 3 and 4, On, and I'll give you the details if you feel like you want them.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Oh, no. We got that. No problem.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay, that's done, Ed. We got Batts 1 and 2; Off, 3 and 4 are on; and Luny Batt is on the LMP Bus.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay, Charlie. (Long Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay, Ed, I don't see the Luny Batt carrying much of a load here. Is TELMU satisfied?

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Stand by, Charlie. We're observing that. (Brief Pause) You're Go.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay. [Long Comm Break] [Charlie is probably seeing proof of the power conservation steps they have taken.] [Jones - "I can't tell from the comm here whether you're pressing or not. Were you in a hustle-hustle mode here?"] [Duke - "No. Just relaxed. We weren't hurrying up. Once we got back inside, I don't believe we ever...You know, we were steady working; but we weren't hurrying. I don't remember being rushed at all."] [Jones - "You had plenty of time to do things, but not much time for sitting around, though?"] [Duke - "Well, not here. No; we had a lot to do. Get out of the suits and charge

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Houston, Orion.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Go ahead, Charlie.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay, Ed. I got some (sample container) weights for you (as per Surface 5-4). You ready to copy?

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Stand by one. [ After weighing the sample containers, John and Charlie record the weights on page 2-2 of the LM Lunar Surface Checklist. and are now ready to read up the numbers.]

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: The SRC number 2...(Stops to listen) Okay. (Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Go ahead.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay, the SRC number 2 weighs 41 pounds (18.6 kg). SCB-3, which is in sample containment bag number 3, weighs 30 pounds (13.6 kg). SCB-1, which is in sample containment bag number 4, weighs 26 pounds (11.8 kg). Over. [ Sample Containment Bags were flown on the J missions to help reduce the amount of dust in the cabin. The Sample Collection Bags were put inside the Containment Bags . Photos of containment bags in the National Air & Space collection courtesy Allan Needell.] [The empty Sample Return Container (SRC or rock box) weighs 14.7 pounds (6.7 kg) and the empty Sample Collection Bags (SCBs

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay, SRC 2 is 41 pounds. SCB number 3, which is the containment bag 3, is 30 pounds. SCB number 1, which is in containment bag 4, is 26 pounds.

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: That's Charlie's. (Pause) 151:09:14 Mitchell: Keep going like that, you may have to throw away "Mully". [Readers should note that Ed pronounces the rock name as "Mull-y", rather than Charlie's "Mule-y", a clear indication that he knows it's been named for Geology P.I. Bill Muehlberger (pronounced "mull-ber-ger"). See the discussion following 127:16:40 .]

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: (Big Muley) isn't on board yet. [Long Comm Break] 151:17:32 Duke: Okay, Ed. John's coming out of his suit now.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okeydoke. [John has started the suit doffing procedures listed in the right-hand column of Surface 5-4. They had planned to reach this point in the checklist 1 hour 20 minutes after starting the Post-EVA System Configuration on Surface 5-1 at 150:03:52 . They have gained about five minutes on the timeline.] [Long Comm Break]

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Houston, Orion. (Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Go ahead, Orion.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: I gather Doc's worked on a metabolic assessment for us. Would you let us know in a little while?

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Charlie, come at me again on that, please.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Roger. We're just curious (about) the metabolic rates today. Could you have the Doc work on that for us, and let us know in a little while.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Yeah. I got it, Charlie. On John, the average ran about 785 (BTU/hr) average; and the LMP, on you, Charlie, ran about 870.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay. John, 785, and me, 870. Thank you.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Yeah, we had predicted, on both of you, 890, so (you're) running to the good there (meaning that they are using less oxygen and cooling water than predicted).

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: That's great. Thank you. (Long Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: And, Orion, the Docs tell me you were running about an 88 average heartbeat today.

a16a1505819.speaker: Duke
a16a1505819.text: Okay. Okay, thank you. Is that both of us?

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: That's affirm. Both of you. [Very Long Comm Break]

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: Hello, Houston; Orion. How do you read? (Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Orion, Houston; did you call?

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: That's affirmative. I'm out of my suit, and Charlie's getting out of his suit now.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Fine. I understand that John's out of his suit and Charlie's coming out now, is that correct?

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: Yes, sir.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Okay. [Long Comm Break]

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Orion, Houston.

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a16a1505819.speaker: Mitchell
a16a1505819.text: Rog. Ken's passing overhead right now. Could you give him a call and verify that he's on left VHF antenna. We're not receiving the VHF downlink on the bistatic radar. (Pause) And come up on Transmitter A - Simplex - (garbled). (Pause)

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: Hey, Ken. How do you receive? Over. (No answer)

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: Ken, this is Orion. How do you read? Over. (No answer)

a16a1505819.speaker: Young
a16a1505819.text: Hey, Casper, this is Orion. Houston, you said VHF A to Transmit, B to Receive, right?

a16a1520647.text: Okay, John. We're ready to go when you're ready. (Long Pause) [John and Charlie have now reached the last paragraph in the left-hand column on Surface 5-5. a16a1520647.text: Okay, you can give me the revs 40 to 45 (times) until Charlie gets on comm. Over. a16a1520647.text: Okay, readback: 41, 154:02:12; then 156:00 plus 41; 157 plus 59 plus 13; 159 plus 57 plus 44; 161 plus 56 plus 16.

a16a1520647.text: 152 plus 20?

a16a1520647.text: Right, and I can give you some times in your Surface Checklist for the different periods if you want them.

a16a1520647.text: Okay, say again when the rest period...Where it goes.

a16a1520647.speaker: England
a16a1520647.text: Okay, the rest period at the bottom of 5-7 is 154 plus 35 and it's for 8 hours. And we're gonna try to get you to bed even early.

a16a1520647.speaker: Young

a16a1520647.text: (Lost under Tony)

a16a1520647.text: Okay. Understand. And we'd like to remind you that you have some ointment in your medical kit if your fingers are sore there. a16a1520647.speaker: England

a16a1520647.text: Okay. (Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 11 min 06 sec )

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Okay. Discussing Station 4 here, we'd like your general impression of the rocks. Especially the bigger blocks. You described mostly breccias and white crystalline rocks. Were there any others; and could you just talk about them a little bit?

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: Well, if we'd seen any that we recognized, we'd have told you about it. I think the big blocks were just big brothers to the littler blocks. That secondary that we were working up there was a classic. It really was. And the pan will show that. Must have come from South Ray. It had a great block land in the middle, and then the fractures...ran off into all kinds of little blocks. (Pause) [John is saying that the Station 4 crater upslope from the Rover was formed by a big block that hit the site and then broke apart into numerous small blocks.]

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: I think that's about the only rock that we saw. You know, we're not really sure. It's our first guess as to what those rocks are up there: whether they're breccias or crystalline rocks. I'm sure you all know that. But most of them were very dust covered. I only saw one clear crystalline in the whole EVA - except for the ones I chipped away - and that was the one I picked up. I think it was Station 5, or 6.

a16a1521304.speaker: Duke
a16a1521304.text: I think, Tony, my view is the same. We had only a predominance of South Ray ejecta all around. Mostly some of the smaller rakes (meaning rocks collected in rake samples) were given to Descartes. It just occurred to me that everywhere we were, there was a boulder field of varying sizes and intensity and you could see eruptive force - you could look back at South Ray - and you could see the rays coming our way and spreading and fanning out as they flow.

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: You know, it just may be that that South Ray Crater is so recent it's mantled everything - or most everything - around here. You know, like we said about the rays at South Ray, some were white and some were black rays and just a little layer of dust. I didn't see hardly a clear surface all day long. I felt right at home like we were back in the United States studying geology and everybody said the rocks would be crystal clear. Well, here it's all covered up. And it is my opinion when you hit one and got a cleavage surface, that made all the difference in the world to a rock description. But a

a16a1521304.speaker: Duke
a16a1521304.text: Does that answer your question, Tony?

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Right. And the Station 4, 5, and 6 area, you mentioned that (at) 5 and 6 the surfaces got progressively firmer. I wonder, could you see any contact or was it a gradual thing?

a16a1521304.speaker: Duke
a16a1521304.text: No, we couldn't. Just when we got off the Rover and you felt it under your feet. The softest spot was up on the top, at Station 4. Progressively firmer as we went out, like you say, went down to 6. And you just noticed it when you got out.

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Okay. Understand.

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: Of course, we were working in a couple of craters on Station 4. Right on the - you know - right on the rim of the craters, where you'd expect it'd be softer, too.

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Okay. And Station 4, 5, and 6 also, we're pretty confident that the rocks at Station 4 were from South Ray. At 5 and 6 in particular, though, was there any indication that the craters - either by their orientation or from the secondary blocks lying around - that the source was, in fact, South Ray?

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: Yeah, I would think the crater at 5 was a South Ray crater. Although the rocks generally looked more rounded, maybe from a different layer (at the South Ray site). (Garbled) pattern, you should be able to see that in the film, but the pattern of rocks were all in the far wall, which was away from South Ray Crater.

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Right. Incidentally, the Backroom is really impressed. They are very excited about your choice of sampling on that inner wall of that crater - I guess it was at 5 or 6 - and think that you had a good chance there of getting real Descartes. In fact, they think they've got it in the box. What they're thinking right now is that the areas where you're able to kick up and see white underneath are (South) ray materials. But you didn't see that (white underlayer) at 5 and 6. So, we think you may have gotten Descartes there.

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: Okay. (Pause) I'll tell you one thing. If this place had air, it'd sure be beautiful. It's beautiful with or without air, but the scenery today up on top of Stone Mountain you'd have to be there to see and to believe it. It's just dazzling. And I hope it showed up good on television...

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: It sure did, John. We're really impressed.

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: ...(Lost under Tony)

a16a1521304.speaker: Young

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Okay. We copy that.

a16a1521304.text: And what our plan is: we've got a lot of Flight Plan changes here - about seven pages worth - and we'll put them in your conference period and if we don't get them all up tonight, we'll send you to bed on time and we'll sneak them in the morning.

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: Okay. Tell everybody in the Backroom "thank you" and we really enjoyed it today. By golly, that view from up on Stone Mountain is something else.

a16a1521304.text: I'm sorry, John, our comm's pretty bad. We missed that. Could you say again...

a16a1521304.speaker: Duke
a16a1521304.text: Hey, Tony...(Stops to listen)

a16a1521304.text: No, I won't say it again. I just wanted to say thank you to the Backroom boys.

a16a1521304.text: Tony, I'd like to say the same thing. "Thanks." I think they did a great job and they kept us thinking and on our toes and came up with the right suggestions at the opportune times and thank you, too, for keeping us going. It was a good job.

a16a1521304.speaker: England
a16a1521304.text: Hey, I went back in the Backroom after the EVA and they're just ecstatic back there. I know we didn't see exactly when we expected to see (meaning evidence of volcanics), but we think you got everything that we went up there for. We're in really good shape.

a16a1521304.speaker: Young
a16a1521304.text: That Rover really...If you could have seen some of the things that that Rover did today, you wouldn't believe it.

a16a1521304.speaker: Duke
a16a1521304.text: You just can't believe the ridges and valleys and rilles, here. I tell you, the local slope might be 2 or 3 degrees, but, man, that Double Spot, whoever picked that place to land, it's the only level spot around here. Any place else, you'd really be in trouble. 152:23:16 England: Okay, in about 50 minutes, we're going to get the 210 here, and then we'll have pretty good comm, so why don't you go eat now and do whatever you want, and we'll give you a call when we get the 210 and see if you're ready for the (checklist) updates.

a16a1532304.text: Okay. We copy that, Ken. just stand by a minute.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay. I'm not proposing you change it. I'm just suggesting you consider the big flap that goes on when three guys have to suit up in here.

a16a1532304.speaker: Duke
a16a1532304.text: Houston, we're going off biomed for a little bit.

a16a1532304.speaker: England
a16a1532304.text: Okay. [Very Long Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip at 153:37 ( 0 min 42 sec ) MP3 Audio Clip ( 10 min 59 sec ) (This clip begins with a 2 minute 36 second interval without comm.)

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Yeah, I guess. We're certainly aware of that, Ken, and the name of the game on this one is going to be dock with the LM and transfer across with just a minimum transfer, bring the rock boxes and your suits and the box, and that's about it. And then the next day, complete the LM transfer and so forth. The name of the game is to get to bed. And that's why the decision is made that way.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay. All right. That's just fine then.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Yeah, they've pretty well set a limit here that we're aiming at, Ken, and that's an 18-hour day, considering the EVAs and your long day. So that's about the only way it would work.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: And along that way tomorrow - we'll of course have the update for you later, but we are going to have to schedule a urine dump with the mass spec. So we'll get that.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: And you got Power and Standby on the Pan Camera.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Okay.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Gamma Ray Shield is Off.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Okay.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: And you said you wanted to give me a PAD of some sort. Let me find a place to write that.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay, that's what Hank was starting to give me when we bombed out last time.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: That's affirmative.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay. All set, go ahead.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: PAD based on loading site REFSMMAT, assumed no plane change.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: All righty, that's TEI-48, SPS/G&N; 38620; plus 0.59, plus 1.25; 168:51:56.94; plus 3052.2, plus 0704.2, minus 0137.4; 182, 117, 014; GDC alignment goes with the circ PAD, two jets, 17 seconds. Lambda ignition, minus 172.00. PAD is based on the descent REFSMMAT, and no plane change.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Okay, that sounds like a good readback. We got that beauty in.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: And, Ken, we'd like Pan Camera Power, Off, now.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay. Pan Camera Power's coming Off. And it's Off now.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Okay.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: I got a chance to go back and look at the telescope on one of the last two revs, and found out the problem was that even after I had gone back and taped the eyepieces back on, they still had the tape on them, but the darned things had slipped out of focus with the telescope. And I guess it was far enough out of focus that it - the stars just weren't bright enough to show up. Because while I was sitting there looking in it I could focus it and then the stars would appear and disappear if I defocused it. So I refocused the eyepiece and the telescope works like you'd expect a telescope to work.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: That little bit of troubleshooting sounds like another first for 16.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Well, I never would have thought about that thing coming off if I hadn't found the eyepiece floating by me one day.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Oh, now why did you blow your image.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: What are the surface guys doing now - are they cleaning up after the EVA?

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Roger. They're going through their cleanup, and they've had their debriefing, and I guess they're looking for them to try and be asleep in a couple of hours, or something like that.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Good show. How long was the EVA today? Seven and a half?

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: It was close to that, Ken, 07:23.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Oh, that's pretty good. Guess the little Rover did a good job.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Yeah, it, I didn't -

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Hank just told me they found their way up to Cinco.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Yeah. I didn't get a chance to watch too much of that, but I did see one, when they were up on the southern point, they put the camera out on South Ray and it was just magnificent.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Oh. Save those tapes, I'd like to see that.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: What kind of funny did you notice on the bistatic? Was it just not getting any VHF signal?

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Well, we didn't have it initially, and then some of the words I heard was that we were getting a signal but it was not reflecting properly. And then we picked it up somewhere passing over the landing site and got some data. So I guess I'll have to get a better recap of - of that pass, but I guess - I guess the signal was there but just - just not hitting the right reflecting point.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Well, I'm just impressed that you can bounce a signal off the Moon that's as weak as this one and catch it back at Earth anyhow.

a16a1532304.speaker: Roosa
a16a1532304.text: Yeah, and it's really not much of a switch, Ken, because we're going to run it through the night here anyway.

a16a1532304.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1532304.text: Okay. Hey, when I turn the waste vent on for an hour here, would it - would it make any difference to the mass spec people or anyone like that if I plugged in the black bag for a few minutes?

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: Okay, Ken, we have a Go from all hands to vent the bag.

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: Okay. We do appreciate that.

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: Roger.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Orion, Houston.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Go ahead. Over.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, we'd like to try to get the bulk of this Flight Plan update up tonight because we won't have the 210-foot dish until 2 hours before lift-off. How you doing up there?

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: What's your prognosis on the Pan Camera? Is it getting us any good data, or is it gonna be kind of sloppy?

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: We're coming right along, Tony.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: We'll be with you as quick as we can. Honest.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Understand.

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: Okay, Ken, we're - as I mentioned yesterday, it looks like we're overexposing about one f-stop, and there's a lot of, you know - we'll take that out in the processing, and everybody feels like the data is real good.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: No, I don't think you do; but it's all right. [Comm Break] [John is telling Flight to relax, that he doesn't want to rush anything and will call when he is ready.]

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: Outstanding.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay, Houston. We've got both PLSSs recharged with water and the ten-minute oxygen topoff.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Hey, Tony. What's your best guess about where we landed?

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: About where you landed? We're just going by what you said. Originally, we had you, I think, 150 meters north and 200 west and you said, today, that you were just north (of the LM). We thought that the first estimate of 150 north and 200 west was compatible with the LRV data that you've got, the nav data, we kind of liked that one, but I haven't seen anything from the planners yet.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay. It's pretty hard to tell. From where we were at Station 4 up at Stone Mountain, it looked like...I could see Double Spot and maybe we're just a little past it (to the west), but not much.

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: And, Ken, as you whip by the site over there, if we could get you to put the Gamma Ray Shield on Center.

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: Okay. Do you want it now?

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: That's affirm.

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: Or did you want me to wait? Okay, here it comes.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, we copy that. Much as I'd like to sit here and talk about the landing site, Deke's here looking over my shoulder, and he's telling us we've got to get on with this Flight Plan update.

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: Sorry about that.

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: It's on now.

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: Okay.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay. Let me get Charlie on comm. I want him to hear it, too.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Rog. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Does John sound tired to you, here?"] [Duke - "No, that's just the way he talks."] [Jones - "You'd had a good night's sleep. And it didn't sound like it had been a particularly tiring day. Just busy."] [Duke - "No, I didn't think it was a tiring day, at all. We're jumping out now, raring to go."]

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay, we're ready. Go ahead.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, in your Surface Checklist, page 5-7.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Go.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, change: "Stow hammocks, roll up with sleep restraints" to - that's on the right-hand column about three or four lines down - change it to "Stow hammocks and sleep restraints in jett bag ." (Pause)

a16a1533728.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1533728.text: I was looking at the little dark halo craters around Mädler, and the one that's directly to the - yeah - east of Mädler has white streaks in it. I guess that's fair if - If light craters can bare dark streaks, I guess dark craters ought to be able to have light streaks in them. I don't know what that means to anybody.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: (Amused) We could probably have figured that out. Go ahead.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay. I'm sure you could have. Okay, on that same column, at the bottom of the page, says "Lift-off time data in book for rev 37 to 43," we'll change that to "46 to 51".

a16a1533728.speaker: Roosa
a16a1533728.text: Copy. That seems fair.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, and right under that on the "Pro Verb 37:06 Enter," we'd like to delete both of those lines.

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: They're deleted.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, on page 5-8. On the left-hand column, it says "Empty ETB as follows." We'd like to delete "1 - HCEX MAG D and LCG compartment."

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: That's deleted.

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, and after "Stow in ETB" at the top of the next column, we'd like to add "1 - HCEX MAG D." (Long Pause)

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay, "1 - HCEX magazine D."

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, that's D as in Delta. And then in the same column down, it says "2 - 16 Mags R and S." We'd like to change that to "1 - 16 Mag S."

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay, " 1 - Mag S."

a16a1533728.speaker: England
a16a1533728.text: Okay, that's S as in Sugar. Okay, on 5-9, left-hand column near the bottom of the page, it says "Stow ICG in ICG bag." (Pause) We'd like to change that to "Stow ICG (empty pockets) in jett bag ." (Long Pause)

a16a1533728.speaker: Young
a16a1533728.text: Okay. MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 26 sec )

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. And then at the bottom of the page after the "Used food in containers," we'd like to add two lines. The first one is "LCG adapters," (pause) and the second line is "Urine receptacle."

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, "LCG adapters, two; and urine receptacle, one." [Jones - "What does 'used food' mean?"] [Duke - "It's uneaten food."] [Jones - "It seems to me that they gave you tons of food."] [Duke - "(Chuckling) Seemed like it. Well, it was a standard meal, but it just seemed like it was just huge! And I think it's probably a little bit bigger than normal because it was two meals a day. And it was a little bit more than normal; they had one or two other things in there that you normally wouldn't have had."] [Jones - "So, is the main thing that each meal is half again as big as a normal meal?"] [Duke

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. On 5-10 (pause) delete all the page, and add: "Battery management at 164 plus 45" in the right-hand column. (Long Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: Here's a little beauty that's just - just to the south of the landing site. It's off a big tall dome, and it's got all this - a great white rayed crater in the top of it.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, "Battery management at 164 hours and 45 minutes."

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay, I'll send up the stuff for your cue cards later. We'll go on to page 7-1. (Pause) And I'd like to know if you'd like the change in times in the Surface Checklist. That's what some of these changes are.

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: I'm looking at North Ray now, and it seems to me that that stuff that runs up on the North Ray comes right around the corner. It comes from out in the area back behind what we used to call the -

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Not particularly.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay, I won't send those, then. (Pause) Okay, we'll have to go on to 7-5, then.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, we're at 7-5.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Fine. Okay, on 7-5, delete "Battery management", "On Houston cue: Telemetry PCM, Lo", "S-Band, Voice and Down Voice Backup". We'd like to delete all that. (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, that's all done.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay, and after "BSLSS/rock bag against hatch," add "Report PRD readings to Houston." (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: Just as I was coming up on the landing site that time, I saw this - little, very soft dome sitting up, and it's got this bright white ray crater right in the top of it. It's just like a - the crater itself looks like South Ray, and the - except it's built up on top of this nice little dome. And I don't know if that's coincidental, or what, but it sure is an interesting thing. The crater is about a third the size of the dome itself.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. "Report the roentgens to Houston."

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay, on 7-5 and 6, delete all of the "Doff suits." (Long Pause) [Note on the digital version of the on-board checklist, John and Charlie crossed out all of the right-hand column. In a moment, they will realize their error and will add the notation "Still in Flight Plan".]

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: Roger. Copy.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. On 7-6, delete "EVA debriefing with Houston", and delete "Eat period" right after it. (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: And change "158:22 pre-sleep and equipment stowage" to "172 plus 32 equipment stowage", and that's 27 minutes. (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: And, Ken, have you been mumbling any geologic terms to yourself the last couple of passes?

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: No, sir. I - during that bistatic, I just kept quiet inside, too.

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: Okay. How were things around on the other side?

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: That was a good chance for me to - Yeah, that was a good chance for me to - to get caught up on all the housekeeping and loose ends, and kind of pick up some stuff here and there. That was a - a well needed break.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, go ahead.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: After "Equipment stowage, 27 minutes" add "Circuit breaker panel 11 ( CB(11) ), Heaters AOT (Alignment Optical Telescope), Closed."

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: (Wondering where this should be written in the paragraph) Okay...

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: (Answering the question before John can ask it) That would be right below the "Solar wind ISA..."

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: ...before the...(Stops to listen) Okay.

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: I certainly agree.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay, and we'd like to...I'll hold. (Long Pause) [Deke Slayton may have told Tony to wait until John confirms they've made the change. Readers should note that, now they are talking about flight procedures, John has perked up.]

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: You ready?

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: (Before he could have heard Tony's "You ready?") Okay. Then what?

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. On the "Stow the ETB against the hatch" in the next line, change to "Stow ETB in ISA (Interim Stowage Assembly) big pocket." (Long Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. "Stow ETB in ISA big pocket." Go ahead.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. On page 7-7, delete everything except the first three lines in the left-hand column. (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: Hey, you know, looking down at this - this material that's to the north of Albatregius - Albategnius, that is - excuse me. That material, if you didn't have all these craters around it, that terrain scene could have been placed on the back side almost anywhere. Got exactly the same characteristics as the scene - everything about it's the same as a big share of what we call Cayley and other stuff.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Understand; delete everything on page 7-7 but the first three lines.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: That's right. And page 7-8, delete the whole page. (Long Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: That's done.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. On page 7-9. we'd like to add at the left top side, "Rendever..." Correction, "Rendezvous Radar Operate, Close (pause) ; Rendezvous Radar Standby, Open (pause); Circuit Breaker Panel 11, LGC/DSKY, Close (pause) ; Circuit Breaker Panel 11 ( CB(11) ), Mission Timer, Close." (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: Okay.

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: And the Cayley floor fill I see in Ptolemaeus. And all of these things look exactly like what you see in Mendeleev. I've been looking for something I could say was different. I don't see a thing.

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: Okay. That sounds like a good observation.

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: Look at Alphonsus. I'm looking at the eastern or the dark gray craters, the one that's almost due east of the central peak, the largest ring deposit there. And to the unaided eye, it stands out quite dramatically. When I put the binoculars on it, the difference is extremely subtle. You really have to look for it, and then it just turns out to be a slightly different color, but I can't say anything at all about any difference in textures or any other thing that's different except that there's a slightly different color to it. But it's more obvious to the unaided eye than it is to the eye with m

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. After the "Gimbal Lock Light, Off," about halfway down the page, write in "Delay Verb 16 Noun 65 Enter, mission timer up" - correction, "Mission timer check until after up-links." (Pause) [Interested readers can find a discussion of gimbal lock in the Apollo 11 transcript at 104:59:35 .]

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay, on 7-9 still. After "Verb 21 Noun 27 Enter, 0 Enter," add "Wait for go-ahead from MSFN." (Long Pause) Okay. First, some information here; you might note that this is about the time we'll be getting the 210, and we'll be able to watch the power-up.

a16a1534813.speaker: Roosa
a16a1534813.text: Okay, Ken. I guess what you're trying to say is when you get too close to the forest you can't see the trees, huh?

a16a1534813.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1534813.text: That must be.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. But we always wait for a go-ahead from MSFN on E(rasable)-memory dumps.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Right. That's correct. But we're adding it here anyway. Okay...

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: On the "Telemetry, Hi, verify," the Telemetry will be in Lo, so we'll add "Telemetry, Hi and Voice to Voice." (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. And we'd like to change the up-links to "Lift-off time update, time increment update, RLS, and CSM state vector." (Pause)

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. Understand MSFN will up-link the lift-off time update, time increment update, the CSM state vector, and the RLS.

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: Okay. Good. After "Updata Link - Off", add - that's at the bottom of the page - "Verb 05 Noun 01 Enter, 1706 Enter", and "Verify T-ephem(eris)".

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay. What is it supposed to be?

a16a1534813.speaker: England
a16a1534813.text: We'll give you a call on that.

a16a1534813.speaker: Young
a16a1534813.text: Okay, is it the same as it was in the Activation Checklist?

a16a1534813.speaker: England
