a16a1701159.text: Yeah, and that's in there, too. Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

a16a1701159.speaker: England
a16a1701159.text: Okay, good show. Sounds like you got it all.

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: Okay, John; your mags go in there, John, and that's it. [John has been turning and reading checklist pages to make sure he hasn't forgotten anything.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Okay. Let me drive this (Rover) up the hill (to the VIP site about 100 meters east of the LM).

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: Okay. [John goes around the back of the Rover to his seat and Carhlie follows him.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Bearing 265. 170:19:51 Duke: Tony, a special salute from me to the United States Air Force on their silver (25th) anniversary this year. (Pause) From one of the boys in blue that's pretty far out right now.

a16a1701159.speaker: England
a16a1701159.text: You bet you, sir. That's outstanding. (Long Pause) [Fendell has panned to the clockwise limit and finds John at at his Rover seat. Charlie comes into view from the right and goes to the back of the Rover.] [Note that Charlie has to have put out the Air Force medallion sometime before he put Mag Foxtrot in the ETB. Perhaps he has just moved it. John puts his Hasselblad on his RCU bracket.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: (Looking at his wristwatch, which has been in stopwatch mode since the start of the EVA) Okay, John. We got 4 hours and 15 minutes or so.

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Okay. [John rubs something on his left wrist. He may be examining an abraded surface.] 170:20:33 Duke: No, my watch stopped. How about that? Hm. Okay. Let's see. (Looking at his checklist) Except for...I'll start taking the...As you turn...The LRV configure, you're gonna do. Let's see. The DAC; driving; SWC; astro actions, we're gonna bypass. Okay. We got to clean the EMUs and stow antennas before you drive off. [The EVA started at 165:31:16 , so they are about 4 hours 50 minutes into the EVA. That suggests that Charlie's watch - or at least the stopwatch function - hasn't been operating for a

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: (After reviewing his own checklist) Okay.

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: I guess.

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Here's the old dustbrush . [John reaches into the cloth-lined enclosure under one of the seats and pulls out the dustbrush.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: I'll tell you what, why don't you park the Rover while I make sure everything's under the LM, and we'll dust when we get back. Okay? [John brushes off his checkist. Charlie is still at the back of the Rover.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Okay. Yeah, I'll bring the dustbrush .

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: Okay. (Joining John) And I'll just take a couple of SCBs and take them in...(Reaching for the dustbrush) Here, I'll bring...Oh, you got to get that, don't you.

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: You got to get that LPM (Lunar Portable Magnetometer) out there.

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: Oh, that's right; yeah. [John will make a final set of magnetometer reading at the VIP site and will need the dustbrush to clean both the LPM and the Rover. Charlie goes toward the LM, out-of-view to the left.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Okay. I'm gonna park the Rover (at the VIP site), Houston. I think we got everything out of it there is to get, okay?

a16a1701159.speaker: England
a16a1701159.text: Okay. It sounds good. We think so, too. [John grabs either the back of his seat or the geopallet behind it with his right hand and starts a series of four jumps, getting higher with each one and letting go of the Rover near the top of each jump after the first. He does the fourth one with his hand completely off the Rover. On this jump, he is off the ground for about 1.85 seconds which, on the Moon, means he reached a height of 0.69 meters or 2.3 feet. Before he finishes his next transmission, he does another jump from a spot a bit closer to the TV and is off the ground for about the same leng

a16a1701159.speaker: England
a16a1701159.text: For a 380-pound guy, that's pretty good. [John has moved behind the Rover and, immediately after saying "They threw that out," does a final jump that may be the highest of the series, although not higher by more than a few centimeters. Because he is mostly hidden by the Rover, timing of this jump is more uncertain that the prior jumps.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: ...they threw that out. Yeah, I jump flat-footed straight in the air, 300...

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: (Commenting on John's jump) About 4 feet. [As John completes his last jump, Fendell pans left and finds Charlie, who does a short jump and then tries a big one.] [In his book, Moonwalker , Charlie says "I decided to join in and made a big push off the moon, getting about four feet high. 'Wow!', I exclaimed. But as I straightened up, the weight of my backpack pulled me over backward. Now I was coming down on my back. I tried to correct myself but couldn't, and as my heart filled with fear I fell the four feet, hitting hard - right on my backpack. Panic! The thought that I'd die raced across my

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: (Doing his own jump and realizing he's going over backwards) Wow! [In a slow-motion replay of Charlie's jump, his backward rotation is clearly visible. He may have reached a height of 0.81 meters or 2.7 feet. As he comes down, he is leaning back as much as 20-30 degrees and, although he lands on his feet, he can do nothing to stop falling backwards onto his PLSS.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Charlie!

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: That ain't any fun, is it?

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: That ain't very smart.

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: That ain't very smart. (Apparently trying to get onto his hands and knees) Well, I'm sorry about that.

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Right. Now we do have some work to do (brushing Charlie's suit). (Pause)

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: (Apparently unable to turn over) Agh! How about a hand, John? There we go. Okay. [Although Charlie is hidden by the Rover while he tries to get up, when John does give him a hand and he rises, it does appear that he was still facing up.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Okay. I want to park the Rover.

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: Okay. I'm gonna start upstairs then.

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Well...No, you're too dirty to go up there.

a16a1701159.speaker: Duke
a16a1701159.text: I'm not going in! I'm just taking some bags up, okay? [We see the Rover shake as John stands beside the Rover, facing forward, grabs hold of something, jumps up, and pulls himself sideways into his seat. The Tv camera is aimed such that we see his right shoulder and part of his PLSS as he settles into the seat.]

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Okay. (Pause) (To Houston, once he's seated) Okay. Do you want the LCRU to switch 1 when we start out there, right Houston? (Pause) [John doesn't wait for an answer but swings his legs out of the Rover, pushing himself upright, possibly off the outboard handhold. Fendell started panning right as John moves but doesn't quite keep up enough to show us the dismount in detail.]

a16a1701159.speaker: England
a16a1701159.text: (Answering John) Yes, that's affirmative.

a16a1701159.speaker: Young
a16a1701159.text: Do you read? Over. (Hears Tony as he goes to the LCR at the front of the Rover) Okay. Going to switch 1. (Static) [TV off.] 170:23:18 Duke: Okay, Tony. I'm going to be taking the SCBs up onto the porch.

a16a1701159.speaker: England
a16a1701159.text: Okay, Charlie. (Long Pause) Station 10' Apollo 16 Journal VIP Site

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Houston, the problem, as you must know, with (parking the Rover at) 085 at 0.1 (as per checklist) is that such a reading puts us through a crater that's about 18, 20 feet deep, and it's too steep to climb in and out of. (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: (To himself) Rats. (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: How far is it to the other side of it, John?

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: It's...Oh, it's only a couple of feet. We'll get here at 085 at 100 meters.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. That'll be fine. (Pause) [We can hear Charlie breathing as he takes equipment up the ladder to the porch.]

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Something on here has reset the range. (Long Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Okay. One bag is up, Tony.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. Did you see the number on that? (Pause) Don't go back to look...

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: I'm sorry I didn't. 6 or 7. We got 6 and 4 down here.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. It must have been 7.

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Thank you (for the reminder). (Long Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: And, Charlie; understand you got the Muley rock and put it in the big rock bag?

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: John did. Rog.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. (Long Pause) And, John; once you get parked out there, we're going to need that whole front end brushed off. If you just want to start on the panel and work back, that's probably the best way. We'd like you to use the...

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Understand. 170:26:53 England: Okay, we'd like you to use the small lens brush on the "gotcha" lens. (Pause) [The "gotcha lens" is, of course, the TV camera lens. Journal Contributor John Pfannerstill notes that the acronym for the Ground Controlled Television Assembly, GTCA, was commonly pronounced "gothcha". In 2000 correspondence, Tony confirms that his use of "gotcha" was probably a play on both the acronym and the crew's feeling that the TV was watching them whenever they made a mistake.]

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Okay, Houston. I'm parked on a slope of about 10 degrees - or 5 or 6 or 7 degrees - (with the downslope) toward the lunar module, and it's my guess that this will help your cooling some, because it (meaning the Rover radiator)'s looking towards deep space a little. And I'm about 100 yards (90 meters) directly aft of the lunar module. Is that where you want this contraption to be? (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. It's heading 165.

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Yep. Heading is 165. [An analysis of mission photographs of the LM taken here at the final parking place and elsewhere indicates that the Rover is a bit closer than John's estimate and is about 81 meters from the LM.]

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. Fine. And before you turn it off, there, we'd like a complete readout. (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Okay. I don't want to do any unnecessary brushing. How about somebody reading the EVA Closeout decal to me. This thing is so dusty, I can't read anything. (Going ahead with the instrument readouts ) Amp-hours...(Starting over in the usual order) Well, bearing is 243, which can't be right; distance (driven) 11.4; range 0.2. Amp-hours (remaining) is 28, and 120 on 2; and amps, of course, are off-scale low (because no power is being used). (Pause) Volts are 65, 65. Forward and rear motor temps are off-scale low. And, of course, battery 1 is off-scale low; and battery 2 is reading 143.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay, we copy that; 43.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: That do it, Houston, for you?

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Right. [On Apollo 16, John and Charlie drove 26.7 km and used 98.2 Ah, for an average of 3.67. This figure is much higher than usage during Apollos 15 and 17, which was 1.67 and 1.59 amp-hours/km, respectively. However, the Apollo 16 Mission report indicates that abnormal drainage from Battery 1 was noted during EVA-2. John and Charlie don't give regular amp-hour readings but the few we have indicate big drops during both EVA-2 and EVA-3.]

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Okay, now. How about reading the Closeout decal to me there, because I can't see it for the dust. Even after I brush it, I can't see it.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. The closeout. "Circuit breakers all open except Auxiliary. Bus A and C should be Closed." (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Okay, Tony; I've got two bags up, and I'm gonna have to wait and let John take in the rest, and I'm policing up the area, and it looks like everything (disposable) is pretty much under the LM.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. And, John, Auxiliary Circuit Breaker Bypass, On.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Okay. Wait a second here.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Okay. The Bypass switch is coming On.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. LCRU Power, External; and Mode 3, TV Remote.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Okay. Let me line up the high gain. (Long Pause) 170:30:52 England: And, John, while you're up in the front end, take the TV lens shade off.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Take the lens shade off?

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Rog. Just take it off and throw it away.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: (Before he hears Tony's reply) What do you want to do with it? (Pause) [A detail from AS16-116- 18719 , which John will take at 170:41:04 , shows the TV with the sunshield removed.] [Although the sunshield has not been seen in the field of view at any time, there may be a concern that it could get in the field-of-view and/or disturb the camera while Fendell pans upward to follow the LM ascent. 170:31:19 Duke: Tony, I tried some Max cooling there for a second, on this PLSS, and it really freezes you.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay.

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: (To John) Okay. How you doing, babe?

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Trying to line the Earth up. (Long Pause; Static)

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay, Charlie. If you're out of things to do there, why don't you go on out where John is and see if you can find an igneous or a hard breccia to put on top of that LPM. Use his camera to document it.

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Okay. I'll do that. I was just standing there. I don't have a camera, though, now, Tony.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay...

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: (Garbled), Charlie.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Just use John's.

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: All right. (Long Pause) [A frame from the 16-mm camera mounted in Charlie's window during lift-off shows, most prominently, tracks between the LM and the LRV at the VIP site. Charlie is running out there now and, later, both he and John will run back. A running astronaut kicks a great deal of dirt as he goes, spraying it in a fan, primarily a forward direction. This can be seen best in the video of Gene Cernan's work east of the Rover at Apollo 17 Station 4 at about 145:48:21 . The video clip by Mick Hyde starts at 145:45:28 .]

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay, John. Verify that the circuit breakers you still have in on the panel are at Aux and circuit breakers A and Charlie (are Closed).

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Roger. We're staying here.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. And if you have a chance to aim the high gain, we'll get our TV back.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Aux Power is in, Bus A is in, Bus B is in, and the rest of them are pulled.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. We would...

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: (Lost under Tony) circuit breakers (garbled) pull. Okay. Wait a minute.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: ... like B out, and Charlie in, and Delta out.

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: That's the way I got it.

a16a1702349.speaker: England
a16a1702349.text: Okay. Fine.

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Where's your camera, John?

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Right here, Charlie. (Pause)

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: Okay. I got it. (Pause) (To himself) Okay. A hard breccia or an igneous rock. (Pause) Here's a TV shade!

a16a1702349.speaker: Young
a16a1702349.text: Charlie, vector me in again. [John is asking Charlie to help him with the high-gain antenna alignment.]

a16a1702349.speaker: Duke
a16a1702349.text: I can't do it from here, John. Looks like to me you got to go right. Or down, to you, I guess it is. (Long Pause) Okay. This one looks pretty good right here, John. MP3 Audio Clip ( 0 min 21 sec )

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Do you want this rock brought back, Tony? That is, for the LPM? MP3 Audio Clip ( 10 min 41 sec )

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Roger. We'd like you to document it before you touch it, and then when you get the LPM first measurement, we'll put it on the LPM, take a picture of it on the LPM, and then we'll get an LPM measurement of it, and then we'll sack it and bring it back. [TV on. Charlie is in the field-of-view on the right.]

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay. It's a pretty good one, but it's too big to sack, unfortunately (Lost under Tony)

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Do you have a smaller one around that we can get in the sack? Video Clip ( 3 min 13 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG )

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Yeah, let me look. That was a good... [Charlie may have already taken a pair of cross-Suns of this rock: AS16-116- 18710 and 18711 .]

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: And we're getting a picture.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: There it is. I tell you, when it gets to be a crescent Earth, that thing is really hard to see. [It is currently 20:30 Universal Time on April 23, 1972. At the Descartes landing site, Earth is very close to the zenith and is less than one-quarter illuminated. The sunlit portion includes all of South America except Argentina and the bulge of Brazil and portions of the Caribbean and the western Atlantic.]

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay. I going to tighten down your little screws there. 170:36:16 Duke: How about one a half-an-orange size, Tony?

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: That would be great. [The sample is 60330/35 which is a 318 gram piece of basaltic impact melt. It is described in detail on pages 97-105 in the Apollo 16 Sample Catalog .]

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: (Static fades) Okay. I'm going to get a couple of cross-Sun stereos is all. Is that all right?

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: That's fine. We've got the (sample) location on TV. And, John, when you start dusting off the panel, we'd like to...

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Oh, yeah.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: ... reset the caution.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay. (Laughs) Does that embarrass you?

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: No. (Laughs) It's just that you got a thermal leak there.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Oh. [With the warning flag in the raised position, the Rover instrument console will absorb more sunlight than normal. As becomes evident in a few moments, Houston is concerned about keeping the console from getting too hot.]

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay, Tony. It's an igneous rock, not a breccia.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Great.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: And it's got that sugary texture to it.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Charlie's cross-Sun stereopair of the LPM rock are probably AS16-116- 18712 and 18713 .]

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Yes, the batteries need dusting.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: John, why don't I do that, and you put the LPM out?

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Hey, there you go.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Here's your rock.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Why don't you set it on the seat, huh?

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Camera, too. Charlie, lay the camera up there.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Yeah. Okay, Tony. That's frame count 156 and 157...

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: (Correcting himself) 155 and 156 for that rock.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. We copy that.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: I'm not sure we got...We got a bag left, John?

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Yeah, I put a bag under the seat.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Oh, good.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Here are the (LPM) power switches coming on, Houston.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: (To himself) Gosh. Dumb-dumb. (To Tony) I dusted the back mirror, and then I dusted the front, and now I got re-dust (the back mirror).

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Right. And, Charlie, we'd like you to dust that panel and the top of the console.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: All right, sir. Just a moment.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: What panel?

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: The control panel on the LRV.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Oh, all right. (Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Why do you want to do that, Houston?

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: We want to keep the temperature of the panel down.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: In case anybody comes back? Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPEG )

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: I guess so. Keep it nice for the next guy.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: (Laughing) Okay. (Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay. The top of the panel is dusted, Tony.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Great.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Sometimes I think I'm (garbled).

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: And we'll need all sides of that console and I guess that panel you just dusted.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: All right. (Pause) Okay. The top and the driver's side is dusted. The left battery's dusted. I'm going to dust the LCRU. (Long Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: And, Charlie, after dusting the LCRU there, you'll have to tear off one of those thermal blankets and put it over the control panel on the LCRU.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay. [This request is another indication that Houston is concerned about the TV and communications gear overheating prior to launch.]

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: The big one, the 65-percent one.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: The which one?

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: The 65-percent blanket. And, John, we saw you get back and we started your clock.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Thank you. (Pause) Let me show you what to do with that one, Charlie.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay. 170:41:01 Young: Do you want a picture of it, don't you, Houston? 170:41:04 England: Yeah, it'd be a good idea. [John may be asking if Houston wants a picture of the front of the Rover with the thermal blanket over the LCRU. At some point, John takes two photos of the LPM across the back of the Rover. These frames are AS16-116- 18714 and 18715 .] [Frame 18716 is a "locator" to the LM taken across the Rover seats. Note that John has put a fist-sized rock on Charlie's seat. He will place it on the magnetometer after the current measurement finishes.] [Next, John takes three pictures showin

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: I think I see how it goes. (Long Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: You know, we sure hope you guys have enjoyed watching this as much as we've enjoyed doing it. If there's one thing that's a real pleasure; it's this (one-sixth-)gravity environment.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. And you've got a minute (on the LPM measurement). And we've sure enjoyed watching, I can tell you.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Well, I hope we got all the rocks, Tony, that are here.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: We got all the rock types that look different from any other rock type.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: John, is that right on the thermal blanket? It covers the thing. That's pretty good.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: No, it folds down, and...Let me show you. (Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Oh, I see.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: (There's) something it attaches to down there.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Yeah.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Agh.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Oh, you got it.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Yeah. 170:42:13 Duke: Super. I got one more battery to go. Video Clip ( 2 min 55 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPEG )

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: And, John, do you want to get that (LPM reading)? And don't walk towards the LPM there, Charlie.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Rog. (Long Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay, I'm going to read the LPM, Houston.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay, Tony. The center mirror on the Rover is a little streaky, but it's...

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Charlie, let me read this? X is 322, Y is 530, Z is 510. Can't turn it on but 10 seconds at a clip. X is 322, Y is 531, Z is 507. (Pause) X is 321, Y is 531, Z is 510.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. We copy that...

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: (Lost under Tony), Houston.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: ...and when you put the rock on...

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay. We'll start with the rock.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: ...we'd like a couple of cross-Suns of it.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Don't forget your camera, John.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Here's the rock. I'll get the camera for you. And I guess I'll go on back and take the brush.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Okay? I'll bring your camera out.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: And leave that lens brush there for John to dust the (TV) lens with.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: You mean you didn't dust the lens, Charlie?

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: No, I forgot it. I'll get it.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: (Laughs) Okay. Dust the lens over the mirror. Then you got to redust the mirrors.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Yeah, I know. That's why I'm going to bring it around this way.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Good plan, Charlie. (Pause)

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Better dust the LCRU. 170:44:30 Duke: I will. Okay. Here's your camera. Okay, Tony. There's your lens dusted. (Pause) Okay. You're pointed about 10 degrees down, out to the Rover...

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Fine.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: ...7 o'clock.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Those mirrors are as clean as we can dust them, Houston. If they don't cool down, then there's a problem with thermal.

a16a1703509.speaker: England
a16a1703509.text: Okay. Video Clip ( 3 min 18 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPEG )

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Going on back, John.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Sir?

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: I say I'm going back (to the LM).

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: I promise not to get in until you dust me.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: Sorry about falling down there, (garbled)

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Okay.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: It's only my fifth time, I think.

a16a1703509.speaker: Young
a16a1703509.text: Five times in how many hours is not too bad, Charlie.

a16a1703509.speaker: Duke
a16a1703509.text: (I was) trying to show off. (Long Pause) Can't get over (meaning that he is still amazed by) this big crater, John, behind us. (Pause) [Charlie is talking about the crater that John overflew by just a few meters just prior to touchdown.] [Off-camera, John puts the rock on top of the LPM and then checks to make sure he hasn't disturbed the instrument.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 05 sec ) 170:46:03 Young: Okay. It's still level and the Sun Shadow is still aligned.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay. [Before he goes back to the Rover, John takes a cross-Sun stereopair of the LPM with the rock on top. These are AS16-116- 18720 and 18721 .]

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Tony, is your TV camera working?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, it is. We're driving it around now.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, I see it moving.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: We'll be around to John in a minute.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay. (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (To himself) Close the Hand Tool Carrier.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Hey, don't forget that mag on that camera.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay, Houston. I'm back at the...

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay. And I started your (one-minute) clock.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: ...at the Rover.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Did you get a picture...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (To Charlie) You got the dustbrush ?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: ...of it while you were out there?

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (To Charlie) You got the dustbrush?

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (Answering Tony) Yeah, a stereopair.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay. Fine.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah. I got the dustbrush, John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay. Go to it, Charlie. You're giving me that minute, aren't you, Houston?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, I sure am. You've got about 20 seconds. 170:47:16 Young: I just got a picture of one of the great moments in history, Houston. [John's picture of the LPM, AS16-116- 18722 taken across the Rover, shows Charlie near the LM. Charlie is probably urinating.]

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: How's that? [John describes the scene without actually saying what he thinks Charlie is doing.]

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (Laughing) Charlie looking down into a crater that's (laughing) 10 feet (laughing) 10 feet ...

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay; Mark, John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: ...10 feet to the rear footpad, and 25 foot deep. (Responding to Tony's "mark") Sir?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Go ahead (with the LPM readout).

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, Houston. 317, 525, 5...(correcting himself) 317, 525, 513. (Pause) 320, 526, 513. (Pause) 321, 526, 513. Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPEG )

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay. We copy those.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Get those, Houston?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay. If you'll bag that one (meaning the rock on top of the LPM)...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: And the Read switch is going off.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: We've got it here, and you can go on in.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: What do you want...(Stops to listen) Okay. What do you want me to do with the LPM, want to get it out of the way so it doesn't flap around and hit the LCRU at lift-off or something? (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: We're not too worried about it, just leave it there.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: All righty. (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: And, John, when you bag that (rock), we'll need a bag number.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (Coughs) Charlie, this is a pretty good rock.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: It is, isn't it?

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: It's got a spectacular little zap pit in it. It's lined and it's all silvery and glassy. Fred Hörz will appreciate this rock.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah. [Charlie selected the rock at 170:36:16 .] [Dr. Fred Hörz an impact mechanics expert at MSC, is shown with back-up LMP Ed Mitchell (left) , John Young, and Charlie Duke at the Lunar Receiving Lab.] [Hörz, from a 29 March 2003 e-mail - " I was in the science 'backroom' during this EVA and needless to say: I was pleased that the crew thought of me in person. The rock itself is one of many glass-draped rocks that were returned from Apollo 16, many more than all other missions combined, most likely because they were fresh, uneroded/uncomminuted ejecta from the very young - only 2 m

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: We'll appreciate them all.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: You can see those sugary-textured ones.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: And we better...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay, Charlie, bag 331.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: ...hustle on back in, we're getting up against it. Bag 331.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Oh, okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: We're getting what, Tony?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: We're getting up against the time limit. We'd like you to get on in.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, I'm standing at the footpad ready...

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: That's not a PLSS time limit.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: ...ready to get dusted and get my antenna...(Stops to listen)

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Say again?

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: That's not a PLSS time limit. That's in time for getting ready for lift-off.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Yeah. Understand. (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: And, Charlie, I interrupted. What were you saying?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Kind of looks...(Stops to listen) Oh, I don't remember. (Chuckles)

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Boy, Houston, the beauty of this place is absolutely incredible! (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: We agree. And there's another spectacular view! The pilot who missed the crater.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Watch out. Watch out, John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Yeah.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: To your left is that crater. [John may be taking two last pictures on his way back to the LM. These are AS16-116- 18723 and 18724 . If he took a stereopair and stepped to his left between frames, the step may have triggered Charlie's warning about the crater.]

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: That'd be pretty good to miss it on landing and fall in on it before taking off, huh?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Well, the way I've been falling, I probably would. That's why I steered way clear. (Pause) Boy, this backpack, once you get it torqued off, you can't stop it.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Not without moving.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: That's right. There. Okay. Yeah, I'll put the rock... (If) you take the camera off, I'll put the (LPM) rock in this SCB over here.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay. Video Clip ( 3 min 4 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPEG )

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay. Did you give them the bag number?

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Yeah. (Pause) Okay, Houston. I'm up to frame count 168 on magazine E.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay, John. (I'm) ready to be dusted.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Boy, that's the last one. It's not going to come out, because...(the film didn't advance?)

a16a1704556.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1704556.text: [Garble].

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, you're going to have to take it off.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: We got to take it off. Just shot 169 of the old Rover sitting there. Boy, that's a good machine.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, it's an incredibly good machine. (Long Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay, there you go. Hang on to this.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Now, we got some work to do here, boy. You're all dirty.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: You ought to see your back. I couldn't have gotten any dirtier than you. (Pause) The only other thing we need, John, is the far UV mag.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Yeah.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: I think this stuff is just ingrained into the suit right now.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, I don't think we're going to be able to get it off.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: A little bit's coming off your arm when I whack it. There we come. (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Well, the message is clear.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: What?

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Don't lose the fender off the Rover.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, you ought to see the top of your helmet. (Pause) Looks like it's little mud drops. [Ron Creel has provided a summary ( 1.3 Mb PDF ) of the fender extension losses that occurred on all three Rover missions.]

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Get a little farther away, Charlie?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) I'll kick off my legs (when I get up on the ladder), John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Could you close that (thigh-mounted, strap-on) pocket so the dirt...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Want to get the pockets off?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Well, I don't think we have time. Let's get...I just want to get the thing (meaning the cover flap on the pocket) closed.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: There we go. I got it. There, that's great. That's where all that dust came in from yesterday, was...Yours is closed. Video Clip ( 2 min 52 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay, let me try (to dust) you now. Some off your helmet. (Pause) Uh-oh, did I turn your comm? No, it's on. Golly, that Rover, really...Okay. Let me get under here. There we go a little bit, it's working.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Boy, I tell you, Houston, if we just had some air up here, we could plow this.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Turn around, John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Sure is good-looking dirt, I'll tell you that.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Well, maybe some day. (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay. Spin.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Man, it is brand new.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Yeah, I think I got most of that stuff off that Rover wheel because your (Static) ... on my side...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Is the worst?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Is the worst. Yeah. Can you put your arm over your helmet? There we go. Okay. (Static fades) Let me spend some time here. Okay. That's probably about as good as we're gonna do, John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay; (stow the PLSS/OPS) antennas , and I guess I'm ready to climb in.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Well, you know, I don't think we need to worry about the antennas, but let me get yours. Golly! Look at the top of your...Let me worry about that; let me get the top of your PLSS cleaned off.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Here, come on by the ladder.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: (Garbled) (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Is it on the OPS?

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: All over it.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Oh, yours is dirty, too, I couldn't reach it though; gonna bypass it. It might be a good idea to let me...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Well, we're gonna keep the OPSs, Charlie.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: I know it. We better...You better lean over and let me get yours. (Pause) That rock bag is filthy.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: I heard of dusting off, but I didn't know we were going to have to go from the top down. Stand up, Charlie, and let me get the back of it. Video Clip ( 2 min 24 sec 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 21 Mb MPEG )

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: You know that engine bell didn't even blow out that big old rock over there.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: I know it.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Well...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: There you go.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: ... foot-sized anyway.

a16a1704556.speaker: England
a16a1704556.text: Okay, fellows. We should be pressurized in about 5 minutes.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: There you go.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Oh, that's great. Boy, is that dirty up there. Can you...

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: My knee on your antenna.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay, spin around just a little bit. Whoa.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: You want me to get down?

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: No, you're great. Right there's fine. (Pause) Okay, that's the best I can do, John.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: Well, boy, that's about it, Charlie.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Okay.

a16a1704556.speaker: Young
a16a1704556.text: That's about the best we can do.

a16a1704556.speaker: Duke
a16a1704556.text: Let me...Bend over and I'll get your antenna. (Pause) I'll put my visor down. (Long Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 9 min 29 sec )

a16a1705844.speaker: Duke

a16a1705844.speaker: Duke
a16a1705844.text: Boy.

a16a1705844.text: Okay, we copy that. (Pause)

a16a1705844.text: Okay.

a16a1705844.text: Man, that's a big rock right there. Thanks, babe. (Pause) Okay. (Pause)

a16a1711207.text: Okay.

a16a1711207.text: Me, either. (Pause)

a16a1711207.text: And, John, verify you locked the forward hatch .

a16a1711207.text: Okay.

Item 4: be ready to close out the LM at 179:20; that's (second orbit) AOS plus 10 minutes, the next pass after docking. a16a1754643.text: Yeah. It was a good update.

a16a1754643.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1754643.text: Okay, Ken, if you'll go to Accept, we'll send an up-link for you.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. The Engine Arm is Off; Stop pushbutton is going to Reset.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. You don't have to worry about that, really. Okay. Ten, set Det. Look at all that dirt. 303 is 25 degrees, the AGS says, John.

a16a1754801.speaker: Hartsfield
a16a1754801.text: Roger. Should be on its way.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Roger. Should be on its way. (Long Pause)

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. We got one set of marks already. Okay. I guess we could do a Verb 83 to set the Ordeal.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Let's hold off until we get to the next...

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Hope that cabin fan works. Look at that beautiful sunset, would you?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Boy, Jim, the sunset is spectacular.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke
a16a1754801.text: Boy, Jim, the sunset is spectacular.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Bet it is. [Jones - "But they did bring you home a day early."] [Duke - "Yeah, that's because they got nervous, I think, because, if the engine didn't work and we had a problem it gave them another, extra day, of consumables and stuff to try to figure out what was what. The more you waited up there - if you did have a problem - the less time you had to think of something brilliant to fix it. They got a little nervous and brought us home a day early, I think, just to make sure we could have some ample time to fix any problems."] This concludes the Apollo 16 Lunar Surface Journal. Post-EVA-3 Act

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay; we must have it, John. Okay, P34. Okay, load TPI time of 176:37:52.00.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Orion, there will be no PIPA update.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Well, we got a couple of marks, and I destroyed our solution. None out of plane. 81...

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: ... that's probably a pretty good number. Plus 81 plus 14.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Charlie, why don't we get a - whatever it is you do to get a Verb 86.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: And, Orion, I've got about 2.2 volts on the signal - on the radar. Can you give me a better reading?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: And I have you visually opposite the bright star.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I see his beacon! It's flashing at us. Down a little bit.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Okay. We need to try to reacquire. I'm several miles off from you. We'll reacquire on the A Channel.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. A discussion between the two spacecraft indicated a distance of 113 miles. We show a closure rate now of 424 feet per second.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Five marks in, John. Okay. You can - can I get a Verb 83?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: You can touch my computer today.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: How about another range check when you get a chance to, please.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. We're at 106.5 miles on the tapemeter. That could be a couple miles off, Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. A Verb 83 says we're at 105.72 miles, with five marks in.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That cabin fan is cleaning it out in here.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: No. The power is on Lunar. It's in Slew, Down. Here you go.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: There we go. Okay, 23. Stop. That's good. That's 24. That's close enough.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Let's see what we're in.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. The AGS says 315. It says a 410. (Cough) By 76. That's probably biased with some marks. Okay, Ken. We see your tracker - your light's flashing.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. 41 by 77. Okay. We need a Verb 48, John. There's some food. Did you get a Verb 32?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: No, I didn't do a Verb 32. I Pro'ed on that thing. Verb 48 Enter, 21 Enter, what?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Jim, we got 5988 on the weight. Does that look okay?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. Think that must be him, that bright star up there.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That's him, Charlie. He'll be at - he'll disappear in a second when he goes into night-time.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. Okay. Coming up on 30 minutes for my chart R and R-dot.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: This is Apollo Control Houston at 176 hours 6 minutes ground elapsed time. We show the two spacecraft at a distance of 103 nautical miles apart and a closure rate of 402 feet per second.[PAO is 11 minutes ahead of true GET].

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: The COAS is doing pretty good, Charlie. I got it right in the middle of the COAS. Look at the needle.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Do you have your tracking light on [garble]?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Yes, sir. I'll cycle it - cycle it, but it was on. I can't tell whether it's working, though, Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I don't see nothing. I don't see any fla...

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I - I could barely see it on the footpad - even on - just on the footpad, the only way I could tell it was working, the...

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Orion, this is Houston with TPI solution.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Delta-V x , plus 77.6; Delta-V y , plus 3.8; Delta-V z , plus 3.1; for a total of 77.7. TPF is 29. Over.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Roger. Copy plus 77.6, plus 3.8, plus 3.1, TPF 29.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: Apollo Control, Houston. We now show the two spacecraft at a distance of 79 nautical miles apart and a closure rate of 330 feet per second.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Man, that lift-off was something, wasn't it?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: For a while there, I did - I did - I thought we - I heard it go poop and it sort of - it sort of sat. Before it lifted off.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: It's a sweet little flying machine.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: See how much dirt has disappeared so far?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. I'm going to break out the -

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, we Verb 32 it right here somewhere.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Fifteen marks it says, John, but -

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I don't need that. Verb 32 it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, Houston. Okay, Houston. We're Verb 32, and we ought to have pretty good numbers.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Ah, this is a sweet flying machine, I'll tell you.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: We'll read it down here, John. We can't read you very well. It's just excessive noise on the loop.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Pro. Noun 58 coming up. Okay; 40.2, 78.1, 27.7. Noun 81s, plus 78.0, plus 2.7, minus 0.2.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: The ground says minus 77.6 - plus 77.6, plus 3.8--

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: Apollo Control Houston. About 10 minutes away now from Loss of Signal with Casper. We show a range between the two spacecraft of 74 nautical miles. Closure rate 313 feet per second.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: And the ACS says plus 70 - 78.4, plus 2.0 plus 2.6. It's got a good solution also, John.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: It's closer to the ground than we are.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, Ken. We did a recycle. We're looking at 78.0, plus 2.7, and minus 0.2 on the ...

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, Ken. We did a recycle. We're looking at 78.0, plus 2.7, a minus 0.2 on the PGNS.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, Charlie. Tell me again what ...

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Tell me again what the AGS - AGS says in regards to the ground.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: It's - the AGS says 78.4 versus 77.6. It says 2.0 versus 3 point - 8, and it says 2.6 versus 3.1.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Seventy miles out, John. Get on the chart at 25 degrees. Seventy miles and 25 degrees. We're right on the line. Golly, what is that? Want some tears ?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: You notice our 40-g [?] bags didn't come out with two snaps on them?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: It's all in one eye. That doesn't bother you?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. I had to close it. Uh-huh.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: What a heck of a time for something like that to happen to you.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I know it. I see his tracking light, John. Flashing. 12 o'clock. Hope that wasn't a dadgum - Oh, that might have been a little particle.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, that's a particle floating by us that we're lighting with our -

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: With our - we're lighting it with our strobe.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Matter of fact, I think that's what we were tracking the other day when we first saw Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: Apollo Control Houston. 176 hours 17 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We show a range of 65 nautical miles between the two spacecraft and a closure rate of 277 feet per second.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Hey, Houston; Orion. How do we look for an APS TPI?

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Orion, you're Go for an APS TPI.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: All right, what's your estimate of the burn time?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Check the RCS. Looking good. EPS is looking good.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Orion, are you requesting burn time? Over.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That - John, that fan's giving a lot of circulation. Look at - Watch this.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. It was supposed to have cleaned the place out. Man, we already done more work today than I do in a month normally, Charlie. I can't believe it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Okay, Orion. Burn time for TPI should be about 2.5 seconds.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Trouble is my eyes was tearing so bad I couldn't look out and watch it. Dadgummit!

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Oh, that was a - that was some lift-off. There was a piece of the MESA blanket went out there about 300 meters. I'm glad we put the ALSEP over where we did. That thing would have - could have wiped it out. And it hit the ground with a big - ton of bricks.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I didn't even see the ALSEP.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: [Laughter.] We're going to have lots of marks.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I'm not so sure I shouldn't Verb 93 it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, give them - That might be a good idea.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Hey, Houston. With 21 marks and 17 minutes, you want to just keep marking as opposed to Verb 93ing, right?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: The answer to that, Jim, is yes, I'm sure. Just want to make sure somebody thunked [sic] about it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Okay, you're coming up on two minutes to LOS, and you're looking good.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: Apollo Control Houston. We show a range, now, of 52 nautical miles, a closure rate of 215 feet per second. Less than two minutes, now, from Loss of Signal, as Orion and Casper's pass behind the Moon.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We used about - we haven't used hardly any RCS.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I'm just trying to keep your needles close enough to get good marks, Charlie.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That's great, John; thank you. Okay; 50 miles at 28 degrees.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay; riding slightly inside, but not much. Excuse me.

a16a1754801.speaker: Irwin
a16a1754801.text: Orion, you could do your final comp at 10 instead of eight. Your preference.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That might be a good idea.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We're probably gonna break lock. With all of this Z.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, we are gonna break lock.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: All this X and no Z.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, my comm is set. There they go.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Hey, Ken, how are you doing?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Orion, this is Casper on Victor Hotel. How do you read?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Read you loud and clear, Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Hey, this stuff is working pretty good today, isn't it?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: The ground - MSFN says all solutions are converging.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Man, I could see that thing - light of yours at 70 miles on the telescope, even.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, I could see you visually right after liftoff, when we were supposed to be like 150 miles away.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mission Control
a16a1754801.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We've had Loss Of Signal, now, with both spacecraft - Orion now in hot pursuit of Casper as they both pass behind the Moon. We heard at least half of the conversation as the two spacecraft were talking before we had LOS with Casper. We're at 176 hours, 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Charlie and I both saw you.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That's a good data point. We been asking and nobody has the answer. You can't see it through the COAS, but you can if you look around the side.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly (CM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Well, you got to be in the - ... down ... here; that'll ... it up.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, that's right. That's the answer.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: John, why don't you give me a mark at 12 minutes to go or something ....

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Man, Ken, we got a load of rocks.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Well, that's fine. We got lots of room for them.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Man, we got the world's two biggest trash cans you've ever seen.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Well, you ought to see the two pig pens over here. You ain't gonna let us in!

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: It was - it was - Geez, it's a lot of fun, Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: I never had so much fun in all my life, Ken. And old FDO put us right on the spot. Did you ever see the LM - tracking?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: I never had a tracking pass on you.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly (LM)
a16a1754801.text: I saw - I saw a glint off the - the LM once, and I saw a glint off the Rover when you were over on Stone Mountain - with the binoculars.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: [Garble] I don't know whether it's this - this VHF comm or the [garble].

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, you're a little garbled over here, but I think it's our receiver.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Well, you know, you've had one rendezvous, now we need one.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Okay. I just [garble] you do this one.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: [Laughter.] Well, after we got through with that first fiasco, we've been - rather meager - meager in our usage.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: This is like Gemini X. A dual orbit - a dual - no, I don't want to talk about it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: You want to Pro at 10, John?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: I don't think we're going to need a chart solution, but I'll take the numbers down anyway.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Standby numbers are the same as the ground numbers.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Okay, Ken, we're gonna break lock here when we pitch around, because of this - all of this Z we got. I mean X.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Okay, why don't you just copy my finals?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: And I got a control mode so I'm going to set my computer now.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: In other words, you got plenty of marks. All righty.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: We got plenty. We're gonna - we're gonna start ours, too.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Okay, I'll stop updating on the AGS.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay; 40.2, 78.0, 27, 0.7. That hadn't changed a bit. Okay, Noun 81's a plus 78.0, plus 2.7, plus 0.7. Okay, there's a Pro.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, John. The only one we're off on is in Z. Minus - that'd be plus -

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: About 2 feet a second. And you're about 3 - about 2.5 feet a second from the ground. And the Z comparison is 9 feet a second, so AGS and PGNS are both good.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Well, we're righter than they are, I'm sure of that.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. Well, the AGS says - the only one we're really bad on is - the AGS is minus 3.7.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, Ken, we're gonna burn the PGNS solution; we're within a foot a second.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We didn't break lock. We haven't pitched.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We ain't maneuvered to the attitude, Charlie.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Oh, that's why, huh? Okay, 404 is going to zero.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We may not break it as it is. Are you ready for this maneuver, Charlie?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We're not either. Look at that!

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Well, we might. We're right on the ragged edge, I think.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Tried that before. It worked on the ground. You know something?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I feel like we're still in one-sixth gravity with these restraints.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, John, I'm set up over here. We got Noun 86, let's see, check Noun 86- 410 plus 5, and I'm not gonna load the Delta-Vs.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: No, they're all right. It's just - see, they want me to keep my solution independent here. See how it does. 35, 104; it's pretty close. Is that okay with you? Or you want me to load Noun 86?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That's okay, we can burn anyway. Who want - who wanted you to do that? Are you doing this for Jerry Thomas?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: No. It's just in the procedures. It's been that way. They said that - that if the solutions agree close enough to pass the test, to keep them independent.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: How about a little shot of aqua?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Man, that's the best idea I ever heard of.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Did they tell you that they changed our schedule a little bit?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, we get to keep the Lunar Module.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, they also said we're going home a day early.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Well, I didn't get any answers as to why. I just got this cryptic "No [garble} P62." No - no shaping burn and come home a day early.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: I - I thought they [garble] to do something about it, but I guess there's [garble] been any reason to talk to anybody about it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: We ought to Pro, John, get on to the ...

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Okay, I [garble] you [garble] and I'm all set.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. Okay, at one minute, John, we go to AGS Mode Control to Auto -

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: 10; uh-uh. And I'll get the Pro. (Cough) about a 2-½, one-potato, two-potato, shutdown-type thing.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Make sure that's in there. I'm trimming the residuals.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: I think it's the day after.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: The day after tomorrow? Is that a day early?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Let's - we'll worry about it later.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Is that your orb rate, Charlie?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay - without the angle. That's right on.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: What was ours? PGNS solution? I forgot...

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: PGNS was 78.0, 2.7; point - plus 0.7; AGS was 78.3, 2.9, minus 3.7.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, 50 seconds AGS Mode Control is going to Auto; stand by on Abort Stage.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, I'll get the Manual Ullage; then you Pro.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay. And I get the Pro. Okay?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Well, we (cough) we've only been at it 14 hours. (Cough) Okay, Abort Stage. Stand by for 10 seconds.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Shut - Wow! Burn complete, Ken. Pro. Okay, we're trimming. Great, John!

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Dadgum. Okay, great. That thing really - that's great, John.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, we can Pro out of there. AGS has got minus 0.3 - minus 4 - plus 39. That's right. Okay. Stop that. Turn the page. Okay. AGS Mode Control, ATT Hold. P37 - Max Noun 49's a 0.8 and 0.5 - and 5.0. Okay, do you want to do a Verb 67?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Do I want to do a Verb 67?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I will in a second, hear?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Wait until we get pointed at you, Ken; it'll be 2 seconds.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, we're about there, go ahead.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: All right. And I'll tell you when I've got it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: Okay, I got you at 27 miles.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, we haven't got a lock-on yet.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Come on, radar. There it goes.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: It was taking a long time to designate.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Wonder what that noise is? That sounds like the evil winds blowing.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: I thought that was just on this side.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: It comes in - it must be the VHF [garble].

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: It probably picked up when you [garble] lock.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Hey, look up in the G&N Dictionary, how to Enter that thing.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Verb 67, and just Load it and Enter.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah, that's what I did. Then I had to Pro out of it.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I never had to Pro out of it before.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, wait a minute; let me look.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Yeah. "Verb 67 Load." That's all it says.

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: [Garble] again with the [garble] values in there. And then after that [garble] zero on it, I think.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: You ought to Verb 34 on that.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: What do you do on that? Verb 34?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: [Garble] too many zeros, or do you have another one?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Boy, this is neat. That APS is a pretty big boot, isn't it?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay; at nine minutes, I need a theta.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Ken, you should have seen old Percy Precision, here, plant this beauty down! I'm tellin' you!

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: I do one precision at a time. See if you really got -

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Trying to see if I really got drift up there.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: That - that spot's been in the same place flashing. Is that what you said?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Wish that cabin fan would suck all this dirt out of here.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: It's doing a pretty good job.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: But what happened when we lit the engine?

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: I know it. It came all off the floor; that's the Velcro down.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Ken, we're gonna need that vacuum cleaner something bad.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: You won't even want to put on these OPSs, Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: I only fell down six times.

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Charlie - Charlie was laying down more than he was standing up.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM onboard)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, coming up on - final comp.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Okay, we'll give you a mark countdown of final comp, Ken.

a16a1754801.speaker: Duke (LM)
a16a1754801.text: Can you imagine that, 18 more hours of consumables with three revs of high power?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: You could have gone 18 more hours?

a16a1754801.speaker: Mattingly
a16a1754801.text: How long was your EVA today?

a16a1754801.speaker: Young (LM)
a16a1754801.text: 05:30. They wouldn't let us do a full one.
